entries.title: Listening Practice 1
entries.text: Complete the table. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. 完成表格。每題只可填寫一個單字及／或一個數字。 Restaurant recommendations · 餐廳推薦 Name of restaurant Location Reason for recommendation Other comments 餐廳名稱 地點 推薦原因 其他評語 The Junction Greyson Street, near the station Good for people who are especially keen on Expensive; the is a good place for a drink Paloma Bow Street, next to the cinema food, good for sharing Friendly staff; £50 deposit; limited selection of food The At the top of a Famous chef; all the are very good; only ingredients are used Set lunch costs £ per person; portions are probably of size The Junction Greyson Street，近車站 適合特別喜愛 的人 價錢較高； 是喝飲品的好地方 Paloma Bow Street，戲院旁邊 料理，適合分享 員工友善；訂位需付 £50 訂金； 食物選擇有限 The 位於一間 的頂層 名廚主理；所有 都很好；只使用 食材 套餐每人 £ ；份量大概屬於 Good for people who are especially keen on ____. 適合特別喜愛____的人。 The ____ is a good place for a drink. ____是喝飲品的好地方。 ____ food, good for sharing. ____料理，適合分享。 Limited selection of ____ food. ____食物的選擇有限。 The ____. The ____ 餐廳。 At the top of a ____. 位於一間____的頂層。 All the ____ are very good. 所有____都很好。 Only ____ ingredients are used. 只使用____食材。 Set lunch costs £____ per person. 套餐每人價錢為 £____。 Portions are probably of ____ size. 份量大概屬於____。 You will hear a woman asking a friend for restaurant recommendations. 你會聽到一位女士向朋友詢問 餐廳推薦。 First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 4. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 1 至 4 題。 WOMAN: I've been meaning to ask you for some advice about restaurants – I need to book somewhere to celebrate my sister's 30th birthday and I liked the sound of that place you went to for your mum's 50th. 女士：我一直想問你一些關於餐 廳的建議——我需要訂一個地 方來慶祝我妹妹的 30 歲生日， 而且我覺得你之前去慶祝你媽 媽 50 歲生日的那家聽起來不 錯。 MAN: The Junction? Yeah, I'd definitely recommend that for a special occasion. 男士：The Junction 嗎？是啊， 如果是特別場合，我絕對會推 薦那裡。 We had a great time there. Everyone really enjoyed it. 我們在那裡玩得很開心。每個 人都很喜歡。 WOMAN: Where is it again? I can't remember. 女士：它在哪裡來著？我不記得 了。 MAN: It's on Greyson Street, only about a two minute walk from the station. 男士：它在 Greyson 街，從車站 走路大概只要兩分鐘。 WOMAN: Oh, that's good. I'd prefer not to have to drive anywhere. 女士：哦，那很好。我比較不想 開車去任何地方。 But I don't want to have to walk too far either. 不過我也不想走太遠。 MAN: Yes, the location's perfect but that's not necessarily why I'd recommend it. 男士：是啊，地點很完美，但那 不一定是我推薦它的原因。 The food's amazing. If you like fish it's probably the best restaurant in town for that. 那裡的食物非常棒。如果你喜 歡魚類料理，那它可能是城裡 最好的餐廳。 It's always really fresh and there are lots of interesting dishes to choose from. 食材總是非常新鮮，而且有很 多有趣的菜色可以選擇。 But all the food is good there. 不過那裡所有食物都很好吃。 WOMAN: Is it really expensive? 女士：它真的很貴嗎？ MAN: It's certainly not cheap but for a special occasion I think it's fine. 男士：它當然不便宜，但如果是 特別場合，我覺得可以接受。 It's got a great atmosphere and before dinner you can go up on the roof and have a drink – it's really nice up there but you need to book. 那裡氣氛很好，晚餐前你可以 到屋頂上喝一杯——那上面真 的很不錯，但需要預訂。 It's very popular as the views are spectacular. 因為景色非常壯觀，所以很受 歡迎。 WOMAN: Sounds good. So that's definitely a possibility then. 女士：聽起來不錯。那這家肯定 可以考慮。 Is there anywhere else you can think of? 你還能想到其他地方嗎？ MAN: If you want somewhere a bit less formal then you could try Paloma. 男士：如果你想找比較不正式一 點的地方，可以試試 Paloma。 WOMAN: Where's that? I haven't heard of it. 女士：那在哪裡？我沒聽說過。 MAN: No, it's quite new. It's only been open a few months but it's got a great reputation already. 男士：嗯，它很新。才開業幾個 月，但已經很有名氣了。 It's in a really beautiful old building on Bow Street. 它在 Bow 街一棟非常漂亮的老 建築裡。 WOMAN: Oh, I think I know where you mean – right beside the cinema? 女士：哦，我想我知道你說的是 哪裡——就在電影院旁邊嗎？ MAN: Yes, that's it. I've only been there a couple of times but I was really impressed. 男士：是的，就是那裡。我只去 過幾次，但真的印象深刻。 The chef used to work at Don Felipe's, apparently. 聽說那位主廚以前在 Don Felipe's 工作。 I was really sorry when that closed down. 那家店關門的時候，我真的很 難過。 WOMAN: So is all the food they serve Spanish, then? 女士：那他們供應的都是西班牙 菜嗎？ MAN: Yeah. You can get lots of small dishes to share – which always works really well if you're in a group. 男士：是的。你可以點很多可以 分享的小菜——如果是一群人 一起去，這種方式總是很合適。 WOMAN: Mmm. Worth thinking about. 女士：嗯，值得考慮。 MAN: Yeah. There's a lively atmosphere and the waiters are really friendly. 男士：是啊。那裡氣氛很熱鬧， 服務員也很友善。 The only thing is that you need to pay a £50 deposit to book a table. 唯一一點是，訂位需要付 50 英 鎊訂金。 WOMAN: A lot of restaurants are doing that these days. 女士：現在很多餐廳都這樣做。 I should have a look at the menu to check there's a good choice of vegetarian dishes. 我應該看看菜單，確認是否有 不錯的素食選擇。 A couple of my friends have stopped eating meat. 我有幾個朋友已經不吃肉了。 MAN: Not sure. I'd say the selection of those would be quite limited. 男士：不太確定。我會說那方面 的選擇可能相當有限。 MAN: I've just thought of another idea. 男士：我剛想到另一個主意。 Have you been to The Audley? 你去過 The Audley 嗎？ WOMAN: No, don't think I've heard of it. How's it spelt? 女士：沒有，我想我沒聽說過。 它怎麼拼？ MAN: A-U-D-L-E-Y. You must have heard of it – there's been a lot about it in the press. 男士：A-U-D-L-E-Y。你一定聽 說過——媒體上有很多關於它 的報導。 WOMAN: I don't tend to pay much attention to that kind of thing. So where is it exactly? 女士：我通常不太注意那類事 情。那它到底在哪裡？ MAN: It's in that hotel near Baxter Bridge – on the top floor. 男士：它在 Baxter 橋附近那家 酒店裡——在頂樓。 WOMAN: Oh, the views would be incredible from up there. 女士：哦，從那裡看出去景色一 定很棒。 MAN: Yeah. I'd love to go. 男士：是啊。我很想去。 I can't think of the chef's name but she was a judge on that TV cookery show recently. 我想不起那位主廚的名字，但 她最近是那個電視烹飪節目的 評審。 And she's written a couple of cookery books. 她還寫過幾本烹飪書。 WOMAN: Oh, Angela Frayn. 女士：哦，Angela Frayn。 MAN: That's the one. Anyway, it's had excellent reviews from all the newspapers. 男士：就是她。不管怎樣，各家 報紙都給了很好的評價。 WOMAN: That would be a memorable place for a celebration. 女士：那會是個很適合慶祝、令 人難忘的地方。 MAN: Definitely. Obviously it's worth going there just for the view but the food is supposed to be really special. 男士：絕對是。光是為了景色就 值得去，但聽說食物也非常特 別。 WOMAN: She only likes cooking with local products, doesn't she? 女士：她只喜歡用當地食材烹飪 ，對吧？ MAN: Yes. Everything at the restaurant has to be sourced within a short distance and absolutely nothing flown in from abroad. 男士：是的。餐廳裡所有食材都 必須在附近採購，絕對沒有任 何從國外空運來的東西。 WOMAN: I imagine it's really expensive though. 女士：不過我想那一定很貴。 MAN: Well, you could go for the set lunch. 男士：嗯，你可以選午間套餐。 That's quite reasonable for a top class restaurant: £30 a head. 對一家頂級餐廳來說，這價格 相當合理：每人 30 英鎊。 In the evening I think it'd be more like £50. 晚上的話，我想大概要 50 英鎊 左右。 WOMAN: At least that, I should think. But I'm sure everyone would enjoy it. 女士：我想至少也要那個價錢。 不過我相信大家都會喜歡。 It's not the kind of place you leave feeling hungry though, is it? With tiny portions? 不過那不是那種分量很小、讓 人吃完還覺得餓的地方吧？ MAN: No, the reviews I've read didn't mention that. I imagine they'd be average. 男士：不是，我看過的評論沒有 提到這一點。我想分量應該是 正常大小。 WOMAN: Well, that's all great, thanks … 女士：嗯，這些都很棒，謝謝……

entries.title: Listening Practice 1
entries.text: Choose the correct letter. For Questions 17–20, choose TWO letters. 選擇正確字母。第 17–20 題每組需選擇兩個答案。 Heather says pottery differs from other art forms because Heather 說陶藝與其他藝術形式不同，因為 it lasts longer in the ground. 它在地下能保存得更久。 it is practised by more people. 更多人從事陶藝。 it can be repaired more easily. 它更容易修復。 Archaeologists sometimes identify the use of ancient pottery from 考古學家有時會根據以下哪一項判斷古代陶器的用途 the clay it was made with. 製作它的黏土。 the marks that are on it. 它上面的痕跡。 the basic shape of it. 它的基本形狀。 Some people join Heather's pottery class because they want to 有些人參加 Heather 的陶藝班，因為他們希望 create an item that looks very old. 製作一件看起來很古老的物品。 find something that they are good at. 找到自己擅長的事。 make something that will outlive them. 製作一件比自己存在得更久的東西。 What does Heather value most about being a potter? Heather 最重視陶藝家這份工作的哪一點？ its calming effect 它令人平靜的效果 its messy nature 它容易弄髒的特性 its physical benefits 它對身體的好處 Most of the visitors to Edelman Pottery 大多數到訪 Edelman Pottery 的人 bring friends to join courses. 會帶朋友一起參加課程。 have never made a pot before. 以前從未做過陶器。 try to learn techniques too quickly. 急於過快學會技巧。 Heather reminds her visitors that they should Heather 提醒參加者應該 put on their aprons. 穿上圍裙。 change their clothes. 更換衣服。 take off their jewellery. 取下首飾。 Which TWO things does Heather explain about kilns? Heather 解釋了關於陶窯的哪兩件事？ what their function is 它們的功用 when they were invented 它們何時被發明 ways of keeping them safe 如何安全保管它們 where to put one in your home 在家中應放在哪裡 what some people use instead of one 有些人用什麼代替陶窯 Which TWO points does Heather make about a potter's tools? Heather 對陶藝工具提出了哪兩點？ Some are hard to hold. 有些很難握持。 Some are worth buying. 有些值得購買。 Some are essential items. 有些是必需品。 Some have memorable names. 有些名稱很容易記。 Some are available for use by participants. 有些可供參加者使用。 You will hear a potter, Heather McCallum, speaking to a group of people who are visiting a pottery, a place where people make pots and other objects from clay. 你會聽到一位名叫 Heather McCallum 的陶藝家，正在對一 群參觀陶器工作坊的人說話。陶 器工作坊是人們用黏土製作陶罐 和其他物品的地方。 First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 11 至 16 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 11 至 16 題。 Hello and welcome. 大家好，歡迎你們。 My name's Heather McCallum and I'm one of the potters who work here at Edelman Pottery. 我叫 Heather McCallum，是 Edelman Pottery 這裡工作的陶藝 家之一。 Before we go into the workshop, I just want to say a bit about the craft of pottery. 在我們進入工作室之前，我想先 簡單介紹一下陶藝這門工藝。 Then we'll have a look at the equipment, and you can try making a pot of your own. 然後我們會看看設備，你們也可 以試著自己做一個陶罐。 Like many people, I'm sure you know that pottery as an art form is tens of thousands of years old, and we know this because it stands the test of time. 和很多人一樣，我相信你們都知 道，陶藝作為一種藝術形式已有 數萬年的歷史。我們之所以知道 這一點，是因為陶器經得起時間 的考驗。 Things like baskets and pictures don't survive in the earth in the same way that pots do. 像籃子和圖畫這類東西，無法像 陶罐那樣在土壤中保存下來。 And even if ancient pots are found in small pieces, they still provide a lot of information about the past. 即使古代陶罐被發現時只是小碎 片，它們仍能提供大量關於過去 的資訊。 There's no doubt that pottery has given archaeologists a fascinating insight into how ancient humans lived. 毫無疑問，陶器讓考古學家對古 代人類的生活方式有了非常有趣 的了解。 The shape of an artefact may have been lost, but archaeologists can tell whether the pots were for, say, storage or cooking by examining the impressions on the clay, the scratches from tools; and the clay itself can reveal where the pots came from. 一件器物的形狀可能已經無法辨 認，但考古學家可以透過觀察黏 土上的印痕、工具留下的刮痕， 判斷這些陶罐是用來儲存東西還 是烹煮食物；而黏土本身也能顯 示陶罐的來源地。 When I ask people why they want to take a pottery class with me, they sometimes talk about these things. 當我問人們為什麼想來上我的陶 藝課時，他們有時會談到這些事 情。 Like our ancestors, they hope that something they create will also last longer than they do, that their work – whether it is good or not – might say something about humanity many years after their death. 就像我們的祖先一樣，他們希望 自己創作的東西能比自己存在得 更久；希望自己的作品——不論 好壞——在他們去世多年後，仍 能傳達某些關於人類的訊息。 Of course, you will all have your own reasons for coming here. 當然，你們每個人來這裡都有自 己的理由。 As far as I'm concerned, what I love most is the concentration you need to make a good pot. 就我而言，我最喜歡的是製作一 個好陶罐所需要的專注力。 That focus takes you away from the stresses of everyday life. 那種專注能讓你暫時遠離日常生 活的壓力。 If you're elderly, it's also good exercise for hands and wrists and helps with arthritis and, of course, it's a fun activity for children because it's so messy! 如果你年紀較大，這也是對手部 和手腕很好的鍛鍊，還有助於緩 解關節炎；當然，對孩子來說，這 也是一項有趣的活動，因為它非 常容易弄得一團糟！ Here at Edelman Pottery, we show you some of the basic pottery techniques so that you can use these to create whatever you wish – a gift for a friend, perhaps. 在 Edelman Pottery，我們會教你 們一些基本陶藝技巧，讓你們可 以用這些技巧創作任何想做的東 西——也許是一份送給朋友的禮 物。 Like nearly everyone who comes here, I'm sure this is the first time you will have tried the art, so we'll keep things simple today. 和幾乎所有來這裡的人一樣，我 相信這是你們第一次嘗試這門藝 術，所以今天我們會保持簡單。 Now, before we move on, can I just say a word about what you're wearing. 現在，在我們繼續之前，我想先 說一下你們的穿著。 As we said in our email, please remove any watches, necklaces, etc. and put them somewhere safe. 正如我們在電子郵件中提到的， 請取下手錶、項鍊等物品，並把 它們放在安全的地方。 If you have long hair, do tie it back now. 如果你是長頭髮，現在請把頭髮 綁起來。 We'll provide aprons later, but I trust your clothes are old but comfortable – not your favourite T-shirt or jeans! 稍後我們會提供圍裙，但我相信 你們穿的是舊而舒適的衣服—— 不是你們最喜歡的 T 恤或牛仔 褲！ Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20. 在你聽接下來的內容之前，你有 一些時間閱讀第 17 至 20 題。 Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20. 現在請聆聽並回答第 17 至 20 題。 So now we're in the workshop. Have a look around – there's a lot going on. 現在我們來到了工作室。請環顧 四周——這裡有很多東西正在進 行。 To make pottery that will last, you need a potter's wheel, a kiln – which is basically a very hot oven where you fire the pottery – and some tools. 要製作能長久保存的陶器，你需 要陶輪、窯爐——基本上就是一 個用來燒製陶器的高溫烤爐—— 以及一些工具。 So first, the kiln. If you look over in the far corner, you'll see one of ours. 那麼首先來看窯爐。如果你看向 遠處的角落，就會看到我們的一 座窯爐。 Since their invention, kilns have changed very little, though in the past 20 years, a lot of progress has been made in temperature control. 自從窯爐被發明以來，它們的變 化很小，不過在過去 20 年裡，溫 度控制方面有了很大的進步。 Basically, a kiln removes the water from clay at temperatures of around a thousand degrees Celsius. 基本上，窯爐會在大約攝氏 1000 度的高溫下去除黏土中的水分。 This allows anything you've made to set permanently in shape. 這樣你所製作的東西就能永久定 型。 It's a pretty ugly, heavy object that's hard to keep in a house or flat so most people don't have one. 它是一個相當笨重又不太美觀的 東西，很難放在房子或公寓裡， 所以大多數人家裡都沒有。 You may think, ‘Can't I use my oven?' Well, that's possible but domestic ovens don't really get hot enough and eventually the clay will crack and fall apart. 你可能會想：「我不能用家裡的烤 箱嗎？」嗯，這是可能的，但家用 烤箱溫度通常不夠高，最後黏土 會裂開並碎掉。 Some people fire pottery in a fire pit outside – but bear in mind that can be dangerous. 有些人會在戶外火坑裡燒製陶器 ——但請記住，這可能很危險。 You also need to know about safety procedures for kilns as they release toxic compounds into the air. 你也需要了解窯爐的安全操作程 序，因為窯爐會向空氣中釋放有 毒化合物。 Every potter needs a potter's wheel. 每位陶藝家都需要陶輪。 This machine is used to shape the clay into an object with circular walls or sides – such as a bowl. 這台機器用來把黏土塑造成具有 圓形壁面或側面的物品，例如 碗。 Its invention revolutionised the pottery industry, allowing multiple items to be produced in a day. 它的發明徹底改變了陶器產業， 使人們一天之內能製作出多件作 品。 Lastly, there are a number of different tools that potters use, depending on what they want to make. 最後，陶藝家會根據自己想做的 東西，使用各種不同工具。 When you start, your hands can make all kinds of shapes and curves without relying on a sculpting tool. 剛開始時，你的雙手就能做出各 種形狀和曲線，不需要依賴雕塑 工具。 However, there are some basic tools that you will need to handle the clay on the wheel. 不過，在陶輪上處理黏土時，你 還是需要一些基本工具。 Some look very strange and have even odder names that you may find hard to remember. 有些工具看起來很奇怪，名字甚 至更奇怪，你可能會覺得很難記 住。 Rather than go through them all now, I'll just name a few tools as we go along. 與其現在逐一介紹，我會在操作 過程中順便說出幾種工具的名 稱。 We can provide these and I wouldn't recommend spending money on them yet. 我們會提供這些工具，所以我暫 時不建議你們花錢購買。 So let's try making a pot of your own … 那麼，讓我們試著自己做一個陶 罐吧……

entries.title: Listening Practice 1
entries.text: Choose the correct letter. For Questions 21–26, choose TWO letters. 選擇正確字母。第 21–26 題每組需選擇兩個答案。 Which TWO things do the students both believe are responsible for the increase in loneliness? 兩位學生都認為哪兩項因素造成孤獨感上升？ social media 社交媒體 smaller nuclear families 規模較小的核心家庭 urban design 城市設計 longer lifespans 平均壽命延長 a mobile workforce 流動性高的勞動人口 Which TWO health risks associated with loneliness do the students agree are based on solid evidence? 兩位學生認同哪兩項與孤獨有關的健康風險有充分證據？ a weakened immune system 免疫系統變弱 dementia 失智症 cancer 癌症 obesity 肥胖 cardiovascular disease 心血管疾病 Which TWO opinions do both the students express about the evolutionary theory of loneliness? 兩位學生對孤獨感的進化理論共同表達了哪兩個看法？ It has little practical relevance. 它的實際意義不大。 It needs further investigation. 它需要進一步研究。 It is misleading. 它具誤導性。 It should be more widely accepted. 它應被更廣泛接受。 It is difficult to understand. 它很難理解。 When comparing loneliness to depression, the students 把孤獨感與抑鬱症比較時，兩位學生 doubt that there will ever be a medical cure for loneliness. 懷疑孤獨感是否會有醫學治療方法。 claim that the link between loneliness and mental health is overstated. 認為孤獨感與心理健康的關係被誇大。 express frustration that loneliness is not taken more seriously. 對孤獨感未被更認真看待感到不滿。 Why do the students decide to start their presentation with an example from their own experience? 為何兩位學生決定以自身經驗的例子開始匯報？ to explain how difficult loneliness can be 解釋孤獨感可以有多難受 to highlight a situation that most students will recognise 突出大多數學生都會認得的情況 to emphasise that feeling lonely is more common for men than women 強調男性比女性更常感到孤獨 The students agree that talking to strangers is a good strategy for dealing with loneliness because 兩位學生同意，與陌生人交談是應對孤獨感的好方法，因為 it creates a sense of belonging. 它能建立歸屬感。 it builds self-confidence. 它能建立自信。 it makes people feel more positive. 它令人感覺更正面。 The students find it difficult to understand why solitude is considered to be 兩位學生難以理解，為何獨處被視為 similar to loneliness. 與孤獨相似。 necessary for mental health. 心理健康所必需。 an enjoyable experience. 一種愉快的經驗。 You will hear two sociology students, called Tamara and Dev, discussing their research for a presentation on loneliness. 你會聽到兩位社會學學生 Tamara 和 Dev，正在討論他們 為一場關於孤獨的簡報所做的 研究。 First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 21 至 26 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 21 至 26 題。 TAMARA: Shall we go through the notes we've made from our research into loneliness now, Dev? Tamara：Dev，我們現在來看一 下關於孤獨研究所做的筆記， 好嗎？ DEV: OK, Tamara. It's been a real eye-opener. Dev：好的，Tamara。這真的讓 人大開眼界。 I had no idea that loneliness has been increasing steadily for the last twenty years. 我完全不知道在過去 20 年裡 ，孤獨感一直在穩定增加。 TAMARA: I know. And it's the same all over the world – the downside of a modern lifestyle I guess. Tamara：我知道。而且全世界 都是這樣——我想這是現代生 活方式的負面影響。 DEV: Did you come to any conclusions about what the reasons for the increase are? Dev：你對孤獨感增加的原因 有得出什麼結論嗎？ TAMARA: Well, I'd assumed it was mainly an issue for the elderly – but in fact it's something which affects young people just as much. Tamara：嗯，我原本以為這主 要是老年人的問題——但事實 上，年輕人受到的影響也一樣 大。 DEV: Mmm. So nothing really to do with longer lifespans. Dev：嗯。所以其實和壽命變 長沒有太大關係。 What about social media? 那社群媒體呢？ In my case, far from making me feel isolated, it actually does the opposite. 就我而言，社群媒體不但沒有 讓我感到孤立，反而起了相反 的作用。 TAMARA: It definitely does more good than harm. Tamara：它確實是利大於弊。 I'd say loneliness has a lot to do with the way cities are designed – people living in high-rise flats with not much opportunity to speak to their neighbours. 我認為孤獨感和城市設計方式 有很大關係——人們住在高層 公寓裡，沒有太多機會和鄰居 說話。 DEV: I think you're right. Dev：我覺得你說得對。 TAMARA: Another possible reason is that people are having fewer children and don't live in large extended family groups. Tamara：另一個可能原因是人 們生的孩子變少了，也不再住 在大型大家庭裡。 DEV: But, in this country anyway, that all changed decades ago and yet loneliness is a more recent problem. Dev：但是，至少在這個國家， 這些改變幾十年前就已經發生 了，而孤獨感卻是比較近年的 問題。 TAMARA: I suppose so. A more plausible explanation is that people are having to move around for work and often end up living miles away from their family and friends. Tamara：我想也是。更合理的 解釋是，人們因為工作不得不 到處搬遷，最後常常住得離家 人和朋友很遠。 DEV: That's true. Dev：這是真的。 TAMARA: Looking at the studies on health risks and loneliness, there are claims that loneliness has as much impact as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Tamara：看看關於健康風險和 孤獨的研究，有人聲稱孤獨對 健康的影響相當於每天抽 15 根香菸。 DEV: Or similar to the risks caused by obesity. But I'm not sure there's enough evidence for some of these claims. Dev：或者類似於肥胖所造成 的風險。不過我不確定其中一 些說法是否有足夠證據支持。 TAMARA: Well – what about that one in Finland which showed that loneliness increased the risk of cancer by about ten per cent? Tamara：嗯——那芬蘭那項研 究呢？它顯示孤獨會使罹患癌 症的風險增加大約 10%。 And those findings have been supported by other studies too. 而且這些發現也得到了其他研 究的支持。 DEV: You're right about that one. I was actually thinking of the studies on dementia. Dev：那一點你說得對。我其實 想到的是關於失智症的研究。 Some found no association between loneliness and dementia and others found the opposite. 有些研究發現孤獨和失智症之 間沒有關聯，另一些研究則得 出相反結論。 TAMARA: Not exactly reliable then. Tamara：那就不算很可靠了。 There's been a lot of research on cardiovascular disease and whether loneliness contributes to that. 關於心血管疾病以及孤獨是否 會造成這類疾病，已有很多研 究。 DEV: Yes, I read that it was hard to reach a judgement as the definition of loneliness varied quite a lot and the responses from participants were too subjective. Dev：是的，我讀到過，由於孤 獨的定義差異很大，而且參與 者的回答太主觀，因此很難得 出判斷。 But there's no doubt that loneliness contributes to a weakened immune system. 但毫無疑問，孤獨會導致免疫 系統變弱。 TAMARA: Unquestionably. The data on that is sound. Tamara：毫無疑問。這方面的 數據是可靠的。 DEV: What did you think about the evolutionary theory of loneliness? Dev：你怎麼看孤獨的演化理 論？ TAMARA: Well, I thought the idea that loneliness evolved because it motivated people to be with other people quite convincing. Tamara：嗯，我覺得這個觀點 很有說服力：孤獨之所以演化 出來，是因為它會促使人們和 其他人在一起。 Survival often depended on group cooperation. 生存往往依賴群體合作。 DEV: But I don't think there's enough evidence to claim that there must be a group of neurons in our brains which influence social behaviour, by making us feel bad when we're alone. Dev：但我不認為有足夠證據 可以說，我們大腦中一定有一 組神經元，會透過讓我們獨處 時感到難受來影響社交行為。 TAMARA: There are a few studies which support the theory but not conclusively enough. More evidence is needed. Tamara：有一些研究支持這個 理論，但還不夠確定。還需要 更多證據。 DEV: Mmm. And anyway, this theory's not really useful when it comes to solving the problem of loneliness today. Dev：嗯。而且不管怎樣，這個 理論在解決當今孤獨問題方面 並沒有真正的幫助。 TAMARA: True. Tamara：沒錯。 Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30. 在你聽接下來的討論之前，你 有一些時間閱讀第 27 至 30 題。 Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30. 現在請聆聽並回答第 27 至 30 題。 DEV: Should we look at the relationship between loneliness and mental health now? Dev：我們現在要來看孤獨和 心理健康之間的關係嗎？ TAMARA: OK. So, loneliness and depression are clearly related and that's been recognised by various governments around the world. Tamara：好的。孤獨和憂鬱顯 然有關，這一點已經受到世界 各國政府的認可。 But unlike depression, loneliness has no recognised clinical form. 但與憂鬱不同，孤獨沒有公認 的臨床形式。 DEV: There's no available diagnosis or effective treatment – and that's not likely to change. Dev：目前沒有可用的診斷方 式，也沒有有效治療方法—— 而且這種情況不太可能改變。 TAMARA: I don't think so either. I was thinking we should start our presentation with an example from our own experience. Tamara：我也這麼認為。我在 想，我們應該用自己的經驗作 為簡報的開頭。 I'd like to talk about how lonely I was when I started university. 我想談談我剛上大學時有多孤 獨。 Being away from home for the first time and all that. 第一次離開家之類的經歷。 DEV: Good idea. Everyone will be able to relate to that – although a lot of students were probably too embarrassed to admit to it. Dev：好主意。每個人都能有共 鳴——雖然很多學生可能太不 好意思承認。 TAMARA: Yeah. We could discuss ways of dealing with loneliness as well. Like just talking to strangers. Tamara：是啊。我們也可以討 論應對孤獨的方法，比如和陌 生人聊天。 DEV: Loads of studies have shown that interactions with shop assistants and bar staff make people feel more optimistic and relaxed. Dev：大量研究顯示，和店員或 酒吧工作人員互動，會讓人感 到更樂觀、更放鬆。 TAMARA: I don't know about that but it must make people feel more connected with their community. Tamara：這個我不太確定，但 它肯定會讓人覺得和自己的社 區更有連結。 DEV: True. Although you need to be a certain kind of person to be able to just strike up a conversation. Dev：沒錯。不過你得是某種性 格的人，才能隨意開啟一段對 話。 TAMARA: Good point. We should say something about solitude and how being alone and being lonely aren't the same thing. Tamara：說得好。我們應該談 談獨處，以及「獨自一人」和 「感到孤獨」並不是同一回事。 It's strange the way some people can't stand being by themselves while others love it. 很奇怪，有些人完全受不了獨 處，而有些人卻很喜歡。 DEV: Yeah. The research shows a certain amount of solitude is beneficial for well-being, which I appreciate – but being alone isn't something I actually like. Dev：是啊。研究顯示，適量獨 處對身心健康有益，這點我能 理解——但我其實並不喜歡一 個人待著。 I'd never choose to go on holiday alone, for example. 例如，我絕不會選擇一個人去 度假。 TAMARA: Me neither. Tamara：我也是。 DEV: Well let's not … Dev：那我們就別…… That is the end of Part 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3. 第三部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第三部分的答 案

entries.title: Listening Practice 1
entries.text: Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. 完成筆記。每題只可填寫一個單字。 Pollution from ____ on the river bank. 河岸的____造成污染。 In 1957, the River Thames was declared biologically ____. 1957 年，泰晤士河被宣布在生物學上已____。 Seals and even a ____ have been seen in the River Thames. 泰晤士河曾出現海豹，甚至一條____。 Riverside warehouses are converted to restaurants and ____. 河畔倉庫被改建成餐廳和____。 In Los Angeles, there are plans to build a riverside ____. 洛杉磯計劃在河邊建造一個____。 In Los Angeles, there are plans to display ____ projects. 洛杉磯計劃展示____項目。 In Paris, ____ are created on the sides of the river every summer. 巴黎每年夏天都會在河邊建造____。 Over 2 billion passengers already travel by ____ in cities around the world. 全球城市已有超過 20 億乘客乘搭____出行。 Goods could be transported by large freight barges and electric ____. 貨物可由大型貨運駁船和電動____運輸。 In future, goods could be transported by ____. 未來，貨物可由____運輸。 You will hear part of a presentation by an urban planning student about the role of rivers in cities around the world. 你會聽到一位城市規劃學生所 做簡報的一部分，主題是世界 各地城市中河流的作用。 First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 31 至 40 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 31 至 40 題。 It's quite hard to think of a city that doesn't have a big river running through it. 很難想到一座沒有大河流經的 城市。 If you think about the major cities in the world, Shanghai, New York, Mumbai, London, they're nearly all built on rivers. 如果你想想世界上的主要城市 ——上海、紐約、孟買、倫敦 ——它們幾乎都是依河而建 的。 When these cities were established hundreds or even thousands of years ago, the rivers were a big part of people's lives. 當這些城市在數百年甚至數千 年前建立時，河流是人們生活 中非常重要的一部分。 In 16th-century London, the quickest way to get from one part of the city to another was by river. 在 16 世紀的倫敦，從城市的 一個地方到另一個地方，最快 的方式就是走水路。 But people also used the river for fishing, as the water then was relatively clean, and they would also go on boat trips up and down the river just for pleasure, as a relaxing escape from the noise and bustle of the city streets. 但人們也會在河裡捕魚，因為 當時的河水相對乾淨；他們也 會乘船沿河來回遊覽，只是為 了娛樂，作為一種遠離城市街 道喧囂與忙碌的放鬆方式。 But as industries developed and populations increased, city rivers suffered. 但是，隨著工業發展和人口增 加，城市河流受到了損害。 The rising number of people meant there was a huge increase in the amount of sewage discharged into the rivers. 人口數量上升，意味著排入河 流的污水量大幅增加。 Rivers had always been used for this purpose, but when the number of inhabitants was so small that wasn't such a problem. 河流一直被用於這種用途，但 當居民人數很少時，這並不算 太大的問題。 However, as cities grew to over a million inhabitants, the impact on the rivers became more serious. 然而，當城市人口增加到超過 一百萬時，對河流的影響就變 得更加嚴重。 In addition, other types of pollution increased as factories were built beside the river and discharged their waste materials into the water. 此外，隨著工廠建在河邊，並 把廢料排入水中，其他類型的 污染也增加了。 This got worse over time. 情況隨著時間變得越來越糟。 As recently as 1957, scientists at London's Natural History Museum declared that the River Thames was ‘dead' in biological terms, as the water was too filthy to support any kind of life. 直到 1957 年，倫敦自然歷史 博物館的科學家還宣布，從生 物學角度來看，泰晤士河已經 「死亡」，因為河水太污濁，無 法支撐任何生命。 But in recent years, as rivers lost their industrial function, cities have begun to recognise their true value and to take steps to clean them up. 但近年來，隨著河流失去工業 功能，城市開始認識到河流的 真正價值，並採取措施清理它 們。 For example, the River Thames is now cleaner than it's been for a hundred and fifty years. 例如，泰晤士河現在比過去 150 年中的任何時候都更乾 淨。 These days you can see seals swimming in the water and recently people had to try to rescue a whale which had got lost and swum up the river from the sea by mistake. 如今，你可以看到海豹在水中 游泳；最近，人們還不得不試 圖拯救一頭迷路的鯨魚，牠誤 從海裡游進了河中。 Unfortunately they didn't succeed, but the problem was disorientation rather than the quality of the water. 不幸的是，他們沒有成功，但 問題在於鯨魚迷失方向，而不 是水質。 Then, all around the world, riverside areas are now seen as prime sites for development. 如今，在世界各地，河岸地區 都被視為開發的黃金地段。 Warehouses that were once used for storing goods are now being converted into expensive restaurants and also into apartments with river views, which are in great demand and sell for astronomical prices. 曾經用來儲存貨物的倉庫，如 今被改造成高級餐廳，也被改 造成能欣賞河景的公寓；這類 公寓需求很高，售價也高得驚 人。 In Los Angeles, on the west coast of the USA, an architect has plans to revitalise the banks of the river and to make a park there which can provide facilities for sports as well as a natural environment for relaxing in. 在美國西岸的洛杉磯，一位建 築師計畫活化河岸，並在那裡 建造一座公園，既提供運動設 施，也提供可供放鬆的自然環 境。 It's also hoped that the riverside can be used for other purposes – it's been proposed that facilities could be provided for displaying projects related to various kinds of art that have been produced by local people, for example. 人們也希望河岸能有其他用途 ——例如，有人提議提供設施 ，展示當地人創作的各類藝術 相關項目。 In the city of Paris, during the summer months of July and August, all the traffic is banned from the roads by the sides of the river and the banks are transformed into beaches, where people can relax in deckchairs under potted palm trees, sunbathe, or buy a drink or a snack while enjoying the view. 在巴黎，每年夏季的 7 月和 8 月，河兩旁的道路會禁止所有 車輛通行，河岸則被改造成沙 灘。人們可以在盆栽棕櫚樹下 的躺椅上放鬆、曬太陽，或是 一邊欣賞景色，一邊買飲料或 小吃。 But to make the most of our rivers in our increasingly crowded cities, we need to allow them to regain their original purpose and be used as a means of transport, reclaiming our streets from cars and lorries. 但是，為了在越來越擁擠的城 市中充分利用河流，我們需要 讓它們恢復原本的用途，作為 交通工具，從汽車和卡車手中 奪回我們的街道。 To do this we'll have to shift more traffic back to the river, but this time cleanly and silently, making the most of modern technology. 要做到這一點，我們必須把更 多交通運輸轉回河上，但這一 次要利用現代科技，讓它乾淨 而安靜地進行。 Already more than two billion passengers use the ferry to travel in cities around the world like Istanbul, San Francisco and New York. 目前，全球像伊斯坦堡、舊金 山和紐約等城市，已有超過 20 億名乘客使用渡輪出行。 And these numbers are set to rise further. 而這些數字預計還會進一步上 升。 Admittedly, it's not a fast way of travelling, but neither is a car when it's stuck in traffic. 誠然，這不是一種快速的出行 方式，但汽車堵在車陣中時也 同樣不快。 Of course, passenger traffic on roads might decrease as more people start working from home. 當然，隨著更多人開始在家工 作，道路上的客運流量可能會 下降。 But another recent development, the huge rise in online shopping, has meant that 但另一項近年的發展——網路 購物的大幅增加——意味著另 another form of urban traffic just keeps on growing, and that's deliveries. 一種城市交通仍在持續成長， 那就是配送。 Trucks and vans in the city pollute and double park while dropping off parcels. 城市中的卡車和廂型車在投遞 包裹時會造成污染，還會雙排 停車。 Imagine using the immense capacity of shipping to take these trucks off the road. 想像一下，如果利用水運巨大 的運載能力，讓這些卡車離開 道路。 One freight barge can replace 44 large trucks, uses far less energy and causes less pollution. 一艘貨運駁船可以取代 44 輛 大型卡車，消耗的能源少得多 ，造成的污染也更少。 When the barge docks at the riverside, the parcels could be taken the last few kilometres to their final destination on cargo bikes – electric ones, of course. 當駁船停靠在河岸時，包裹可 以由貨運自行車完成最後幾公 里的配送——當然，是電動貨 運自行車。 This is already happening in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. 這已經在荷蘭城市阿姆斯特丹 發生了。 And in future, the final stage could even be carried out by drone, although at present this isn't allowed. 未來，最後一段配送甚至可以 由無人機完成，雖然目前這還 不被允許。

entries.title: Listening Practice 2
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Question 1-10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Help for carers Local councils can arrange practical support to help those caring for elderly people at home. This can give the carer: • time for other responsibilities • a 1 ___________________ Assessment of mother's needs This may include discussion of: • how much 2 ___________________ the caring involves • what types of tasks are involved, e.g. − help with dressing − helping her have a 3 ___________________ − shopping − helping with meals − dealing with 4 ___________________ • any aspects of caring that are especially difficult, e.g. − loss of 5 ___________________ − 6 ___________________ her − preventing a 7 ___________________ Types of support that may be offered to carers • transport costs, e.g. cost of a 8 ___________________ • car-related costs, e.g. fuel and 9 ___________________ • help with housework • help to reduce 10 ___________________ • a 1 ___________________ • how much 2 ___________________ − helping her have a 3 ___________________ − dealing with 4 ___________________ − loss of 5 ___________________ − 6 ___________________ her − preventing a 7 ___________________ • transport costs, e.g. cost of a 8 ___________________ • car-related costs, e.g. fuel and 9 ___________________ • help to reduce 10 ___________________ You will hear a woman who is caring for her elderly mother talking to a friend. 你會聽到一位正在照顧年邁母親的女士和朋友交談。 First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 4. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 1 至 4 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 4. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 1 至 4 題。 CAROL: It's really good to see you, Tom. Carol：見到你真的很高興， Tom。 Since I had to give up work, I feel I'm losing touch with my friends and colleagues. 自從我不得不辭去工作後，我覺得自己正逐漸和朋友及同事失去聯繫。 TOM: We really miss you in the office – we were all so sorry you had to leave. Tom：辦公室裡大家都很想念你——你不得不離開，我們都覺得很難過。 But you must be relieved to have more time to look after your mother. How is she? 不過你現在有更多時間照顧你母親，應該也鬆了一口氣吧。 她怎麼樣？ CAROL: Well, she's very cheerful but she needs a lot of help. Carol：嗯，她很開朗，但她需要很多幫助。 TOM: Have you tried to get any support from the local council? Tom：你有試著向地方議會尋求支援嗎？ CAROL: No. I didn't know I could. Carol：沒有。我不知道可以這樣做。 TOM: Yes, they offer different kinds of practical support. Tom：可以的，他們提供各種實際支援。 They realise that carers sometimes need time for all the other responsibilities they have apart from the person they're caring for, and also that they sometimes need a break. 他們了解照顧者除了照顧對象之外，還有其他責任需要時間處理，而且有時也需要休息一下。 CAROL: Absolutely. OK, so tell me more. How do I go about getting this support? Carol：完全沒錯。好，那你再跟我說說。我該怎麼申請這些支援呢？ TOM: Well, you'd have to have an assessment of your mother's needs. Tom：嗯，你需要先讓人評估你母親的需求。 That means someone would come round and talk to you about the situation and what you need. 也就是會有人到你家，和你談談目前的情況以及你需要什麼。 So for a start they'd want to know the amount of time you spend looking after your mother every day. 首先，他們會想知道你每天花多少時間照顧你母親。 CAROL: OK. Carol：好的。 TOM: Then they'll probably ask you what sorts of tasks you do for your mother during the day. Tom：然後他們可能會問你白天都為你母親做哪些事情。 Things like if she needs help with getting dressed, for example. 例如，她是否需要別人幫忙穿衣服。 CAROL: Right. I help her with that, and also I help her get into the shower in the morning. Carol：對。我會幫她穿衣服， 也會在早上幫她進浴室洗澡。 TOM: Yes, that sort of thing. Tom：是的，就是這類事情。 They'll probably ask you if you do the shopping for her, and help her at mealtimes. 他們可能也會問你是否替她購物，以及是否在用餐時幫助她。 And whether she can cope using money. 還有她是否能自己處理用錢的事情。 CAROL: Yes, that's becoming a bit of a problem. Carol：是的，這正在變成一個小問題。 She used to be very good at it, but not any more. 她以前很擅長處理這些事，但現在不行了。 Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 5 to 10. 在你聽接下來的對話之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 5 至 10 題。 Now listen and answer questions 5 to 10. 現在請聆聽並回答第 5 至 10 題。 TOM: And be ready to tell them about anything you find particularly difficult about caring for your mother. Tom：你也要準備好告訴他們，在照顧你母親時有哪些事情讓你特別覺得困難。 CAROL: So recently I've noticed she's started to have quite bad problems with her memory … if I wasn't there, I think she'd forget to eat, for example. Carol：最近我注意到她的記憶力開始出現相當嚴重的問題 ……例如，如果我不在，她可能會忘記吃飯。 And often she doesn't seem quite sure what day it is. 而且她經常似乎不太確定今天是星期幾。 TOM: Yes, tell them about that. And are there any physical difficulties you have caring for her? Lifting her, for example? Tom：是的，把這些告訴他們。 那你在照顧她時，有沒有遇到身體上的困難？例如扶她起身之類的？ CAROL: Yes. She's quite heavy, and I'm afraid of hurting my back – I'd be in real trouble if that happened. Carol：有。她挺重的，我擔心會傷到背——如果真的那樣， 我就麻煩大了。 TOM: They can give you advice about that, and also about how to avoid the possibility of your mum having a fall. Tom：他們可以就這方面給你建議，也可以告訴你如何避免你媽媽跌倒。 CAROL: Great. So once they've done this assessment, if I'm eligible, what happens next? Carol：太好了。那麼，一旦他們完成評估，如果我符合資格，接下來會怎樣？ TOM: Well, they might support you financially. Tom：嗯，他們可能會給你經濟上的支援。 So they might help you with transport costs, like if you have to get a taxi to take your mother for an appointment, for example. 例如，如果你必須叫計程車帶你母親去赴約，他們可能會幫你支付交通費。 CAROL: I usually drive her myself actually. So could I claim for the petrol? Carol：其實我通常都是自己開車送她。那我可以申請汽油費補助嗎？ TOM: You could, and you can claim for the insurance too. Tom：可以，而且你也可以申請保險費補助。 CAROL: Oh, right. Carol：哦，好的。 TOM: And if you need help with the housework, they can arrange for someone to come along once or twice a week. Tom：如果你需要有人幫忙做家務，他們可以安排人每週來一兩次。 And one other thing, I hope you don't mind me saying this, but it's important you look after yourself, and it seems to me you're under quite a bit of stress. 還有一件事，希望你不介意我這麼說，但你也要好好照顧自己，這很重要。我看得出來你承受了不少壓力。 CAROL: I am, yes. Carol：是的，確實如此。 TOM: Well, tell the council, because they may be able to give you some advice on how to minimise it. Tom：那就告訴議會吧，因為他們也許能給你一些建議，幫你減輕壓力。 CAROL: Really? Though actually I feel so much better having talked to you. Carol：真的嗎？不過其實跟你談過之後，我已經覺得好多了。 I'll get in touch with the council straight away. Now shall we … 我會馬上聯絡議會。現在我們是不是…… That is the end of Part 1. You now have one minute to check your answers to Part 1. 第一部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第一部分的答案。

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11-16 What is the role of the volunteers in each of the following activities? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A-I, next to Questions 11-16. What is the next annual event for volunteers? a boat trip a barbecue a party You will hear a man who works for Elmley Town Council talking to some people who want to join the small town's volunteer scheme. 你會聽到一位在 Elmley 鎮議會工作的人，正在和一些想加入這個小鎮志工計畫的人談話。 First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 11 至 16 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 11 至 16 題。 Good morning everyone. I'm Steve Wainwright, from Elmleigh Town Council, and I organise the town's volunteer scheme. 大家早安。我是 Steve Wainwright，來自 Elmleigh 鎮議會，負責組織鎮上的志工計畫。 I'm delighted you're all interested in joining the scheme. 我很高興你們都對加入這個計畫感興趣。 Our volunteers help to create a sense of community among the many people who live in our historic town of Elmleigh, and make residents and visitors feel welcome at local events. 我們的志工幫助生活在歷史悠久的 Elmleigh 鎮上的居民建立社區歸屬感，也讓居民和遊客在當地活動中感到受歡迎。 First I'll mention just a few of the activities that volunteers carry out. 首先，我會簡單介紹幾項志工會做的活動。 One is to walk around the town centre streets wearing our volunteer T-shirt. 其中一項是在鎮中心的街道上穿著我們的志工 T 恤巡走。 Tourists often ask how to get to a particular shop, and they might also be grateful for recommendations about what to visit. 遊客常常會詢問某家商店怎麼走，也可能會很感謝有人推薦值得參觀的地方。 The town holds a large number of concerts each year, and part of the volunteers' role is to get everyone in the audience to the right place as smoothly as possible. 這個小鎮每年舉辦許多音樂會，志工的部分工作是盡可能順利地把觀眾帶到正確的位置。 You'd be surprised how many people buy tickets then don't check them, and head for the wrong section of the hall! 你會驚訝地發現，有很多人買了票卻沒有檢查，結果走到音樂廳錯誤的區域！ Volunteers may get involved with community groups, such as sports clubs or gardeners' associations. 志工也可能參與社區團體的工作，例如運動俱樂部或園藝協會。 Here the volunteers talk about how groups can help each other. 在這方面，志工會和各團體討論它們如何互相幫助。 For instance, a writing group might want to travel to another town to hear a talk by a well-known author, but may not know that another club has a coach they could travel in. 例如，一個寫作小組可能想去另一個城鎮聽知名作家的演講，但可能不知道另一個俱樂部有一輛他們可以搭乘的巴士。 The town produces a monthly magazine, and anyone who lives in the town can send in articles. 這個小鎮會出版一本月刊，住在鎮上的任何人都可以投稿。 It's free to residents, and is paid for by local businesses – that's the responsibility of the council's advertising department. 這本雜誌對居民免費，由當地商家支付費用——這是議會廣告部門負責的事。 We depend on volunteers, though, to find out what people think of events they've attended, and any suggestions they have for the future. 不過，我們需要依靠志工去了解人們對參加過的活動有什麼看法，以及他們對未來有什麼建議。 The volunteers then send a summary to the editors. 然後志工會把摘要送給編輯。 There are a number of clubs for retired people, and every year, the council arranges lunch for all the members. 這裡有一些退休人士俱樂部， 每年議會都會為所有會員安排午餐。 The volunteers welcome the guests, and when everyone's sitting down and relaxing after the meal, some volunteers put on a show – usually around half an hour of songs and short plays. 志工會迎接賓客，等大家用餐後坐下來放鬆時，一些志工會表演節目——通常是大約半小時的歌曲和短劇。 The club members really welcome the chance to chat to the volunteers at these events. 俱樂部會員非常歡迎在這些活動中和志工聊天的機會。 The town council has a website, of course, and volunteers are asked to help by making sure residents know about it. 當然，鎮議會有一個網站，志工需要協助確保居民知道這個網站。 It's updated every day with information about future activities, and we want as many people as possible to use it. 網站每天都會更新未來活動的資訊，我們希望盡可能多的人使用它。 Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20. 在你聽接下來的演講之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 17 至 20 題。 Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20. 現在請聆聽並回答第 17 至 20 題。 OK, now you know some of the things our volunteers do, I'll go on to some practical matters. 好了，現在你們已經了解志工會做的一些事情，接下來我會談談一些實際事項。 As you probably know, the town arranges three major festivals every year, and they all depend on a large number of volunteers. 你們可能知道，這個小鎮每年會舉辦三個大型節慶活動，而它們都需要大量志工協助。 The book festival lasts three days, and uses several venues, which all need volunteers. 書展持續三天，使用好幾個場地，每個場地都需要志工。 More are needed for the music festival, because that lasts a whole week, and even more help is required for the science festival, even though it's only two days long. 音樂節需要更多志工，因為它持續整整一週；科學節雖然只有兩天，卻需要更多協助。 It involves quite a lot of venues, though. 不過，它涉及的場地相當多。 It's a good idea to help at the festival you're most interested in, because you can attend most of the events for free. 在你最感興趣的節慶活動中幫忙是個好主意，因為你可以免費參加大部分活動。 We try to use volunteers who are flexible, though, because some festival events are held outdoors, and the weather may affect the size of the audience, and even whether the event can take place; so there can be changes at short notice. 不過，我們會盡量安排比較有彈性的志工，因為有些節慶活動在戶外舉行，天氣可能會影響觀眾人數，甚至影響活動是否能舉辦；因此可能會臨時變動。 What's essential, though, is being able to get on well with other people, and also to deal with someone who's behaving badly – as occasionally happens. 不過，最重要的是能和他人相處融洽，也能應對偶爾出現的行為不當者。 Our plan is to get you all working in September, after a week's training starting on the 2nd. 我們的計畫是讓你們在 9 月開始工作，在 2 日開始的一週培訓之後上工。 So we'll be timetabling you for duties the following week, from the 9th onward. 因此，我們會安排你們在接下來那一週，也就是從 9 日起的值勤時間。 Later, in the week beginning September 23rd, we have a chat with each of you, to find out how you feel about being a volunteer, and what extra support you need. 之後，在 9 月 23 日開始的那一週，我們會和你們每個人談談， 了解你們對擔任志工的感受， 以及你們需要哪些額外支援。 As a thank you to the volunteers, we arrange an annual event. 為了感謝志工，我們每年都會安排一項活動。 In recent years we've had a party in the town hall, and last year a barbecue in Chamber Park. 近年來，我們曾在市政廳舉辦派對，去年則在 Chamber Park 舉辦烤肉活動。 Our forthcoming event is a trip along the canal from here to Dewhurst and back. 我們即將舉辦的活動，是沿著運河從這裡到 Dewhurst 再返回的旅行。 It's on Saturday September the 28th, and if you'd like to attend, you can sign up once you start work. 活動在 9 月 28 日星期六舉行， 如果你想參加，可以在開始工作後報名。 Now this is the volunteers' T-shirt… 現在，這就是志工的 T 恤…… That is the end of Part 2. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 2. 第二部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第二部分的答案。
