You will hear two students, called Rosie and Colin, discussing their human geography assignment. 你會聽到兩位學生 Rosie 和 Colin 討論他們的人文地理作業。 First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 21 至 25 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 21 至 25 題。 ROSIE: Colin, I'm really struggling to think of a topic for our human geography assignment. Rosie：Colin，我真的很難想出我們人文地理作業的題目。 COLIN: Me too, Rosie. I'll tell you what, let's think about the different aspects of human geography, and see if we can narrow the topic down a bit to help us decide. Colin：我也是，Rosie。這樣吧，我們先想想人文地理的不同面向，看看能不能把題目範圍縮小一點，幫助我們決定。 ROSIE: OK. So one aspect is population. Rosie：好。其中一個面向是人口。 That would be all about population density and migration and so on. 那會涉及人口密度、遷移等等。 Lots of facts and statistics … Maybe a bit boring? 會有很多事實和統計資料……也許有點無聊？ COLIN: Yeah, but quite straightforward to find on the internet. Colin：是啊，不過在網路上很容易找到資料。 ROSIE: Suppose so. How about health? Rosie：也許吧。那健康呢？ I'd never thought about the links between that and geography until Professor Lee gave us that lecture on cholera. 在 Lee 教授給我們講霍亂那堂課之前，我從來沒想過健康和地理之間的關聯。 How in the nineteenth century a physician used street plans and plans of water supplies to find the source of a cholera epidemic. 那位醫生如何在 19 世紀利用街道圖和供水規劃圖，找出霍亂疫情的源頭。 COLIN: Yes – fascinating, wasn't it? Or we could do something more general – like economies. Colin：是啊——很有趣，不是嗎？ 或者我們可以做比較廣泛的主題 ——比如經濟。 ROSIE: So how financial and commercial factors are linked to the physical environment? Rosie：也就是財務和商業因素如何與自然環境相關聯？ COLIN: Yeah. Colin：對。 ROSIE: I thought that had been taken off the syllabus for this year. Rosie：我以為今年的課程大綱已經把這部分刪掉了。 COLIN: Has it? Colin：是嗎？ ROSIE: I'm not sure. But it might be best to avoid it. Rosie：我不確定。不過也許最好避開它。 COLIN: OK. Maybe we could do something on culture. Colin：好。也許我們可以做文化方面的題目。 We had that lecture about culture and geography last week. 上週我們有一堂關於文化和地理的課。 ROSIE: I didn't get much out of that. Rosie：我從那堂課裡沒學到太多。 It was all so general and the lecturer didn't give any useful examples. 內容都太籠統了，講師也沒有給出任何有用的例子。 COLIN: Yeah, I hardly took any notes, it didn't seem worth it. Colin：是啊，我幾乎沒做筆記，感覺不太值得。 ROSIE: Me neither. Rosie：我也是。 COLIN: We could focus on poverty. Colin：我們可以聚焦在貧窮問題上。 That's something that's a global problem … 那是一個全球性的問題…… ROSIE: The trouble is, Dr Lee was saying, that you have to be careful with some of the figures relating to poverty – they're sometimes deliberately manipulated. Rosie：問題是，Lee 博士說過，處理一些和貧窮相關的數據時要很小心——它們有時會被刻意操控。 COLIN: You mean the information gets changed for political reasons? Colin：你的意思是，資料會因政治原因而被改動？ ROSIE: That sort of thing, yes. Rosie：差不多就是那樣，是的。 Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30. 在你聽接下來的討論之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 26 至 30 題。 Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30. 現在請聆聽並回答第 26 至 30 題。 ROSIE: So what are we going to do our assignment on? I'll tell you what, one of the possibilities we haven't discussed is urbanisation. Rosie：那我們的作業到底要做什麼主題呢？這樣吧，我們還沒討論到的一個可能題目是城市化。 And now over half the world's population lives in cities, that's really important. 現在世界上超過一半的人口住在城市裡，這真的很重要。 COLIN: OK, good idea, Rosie. Let's do that. Colin：好主意，Rosie。我們就做這個吧。 ROSIE: I love living in a big city, but of course there are problems. Rosie：我喜歡住在大城市裡，但當然也有一些問題。 COLIN: Things like theft and robbery? Colin：像偷竊和搶劫這類問題嗎？ ROSIE: Yes, but where I come from, that's linked to another more serious issue, which is that a lot of people don't have jobs. Rosie：是的，但在我來的地方，這和另一個更嚴重的問題有關，那就是很多人沒有工作。 That's getting worse and worse. 情況正變得越來越糟。 And we also still have quite a lot of people who are homeless, though that's not quite so bad as it was. 而且我們那裡仍然有相當多人無家可歸，雖然情況不像以前那麼嚴重。 COLIN: It'd be nice to talk about some positive developments. Colin：能談談一些正面的發展也不錯。 Like some of the new developments on the outskirts of cities. 例如城市郊區的一些新建設。 ROSIE: Yeah. They've opened some massive new shopping centres outside my city. Rosie：是啊。我們城市外面開了幾個大型新購物中心。 COLIN: Yeah, the same with mine – but it's meant a lot of the shops in the city centre are closing down. Colin：是啊，我那裡也是——但這意味著市中心很多商店正在倒閉。 But the outskirts are ideal for buildings that need a lot of space, like for conferences. 不過郊區很適合需要大量空間的建築，例如會議中心。 They've opened a couple of big ones. 他們已經開了幾個大型的。 ROSIE: Yes, we've got some too. Rosie：是的，我們那裡也有一些。 It'd be nicer to have more facilities for things like football too. 如果能有更多像足球這類活動的設施就更好了。 But that's not happening where I live. 但在我住的地方，這並沒有發生。 COLIN: Same in my area. Colin：我那裡也是一樣。 ROSIE: We could include something about developing disused industrial sites. Rosie：我們可以加入一些關於開發廢棄工業用地的內容。 It seems like a good idea, because you're not doing any harm to the natural environment. 這看起來是個好主意，因為不會對自然環境造成傷害。 COLIN: Yeah, but aren't the buildings architecturally significant? Colin：是啊，但那些建築難道不具有建築上的重要性嗎？ ROSIE: Not really. And what people forget is that they often used quite dangerous materials – chemicals and things – which haven't been properly cleared away, so the whole site has to be made safe. Rosie：其實不太是。而且人們常常忘記，那些地方以前經常使用相當危險的材料——像化學品之類 ——這些東西還沒有被妥善清除， 所以整個場地都必須先變得安全。 COLIN: Mm. That can't be cheap. And I bet it's often not budgeted for. Colin：嗯。那肯定不便宜。而且我敢說，這通常沒有被列入預算。 ROSIE: You're right. Rosie：你說得對。 COLIN: Have you read about Masdar City? Colin：你讀過 Masdar City 的資料嗎？ ROSIE: In Abu Dhabi? Yes, it was designed to be a green city, wasn't it? Rosie：在 Abu Dhabi 的那個嗎？ 有，它被設計成一座綠色城市，對吧？ That might be a good example of a city which set out to depend entirely on renewable energy. 那可能是一個很好的例子，展示一座城市如何以完全依賴再生能源為目標。 COLIN: Yes, we should say something about that. Colin：是的，我們應該談一下這個。 It was designed to be totally pedestrianised too, wasn't it, with the transport underground. 它也被設計成完全行人化，交通系統則設在地下，對吧？ ROSIE: Yes, and they had big plans for recycling to reduce waste to the lowest possible level. Rosie：是的，而且他們有大型回收計畫，希望把廢棄物降到最低。 But let's stick to talking about power sources. 不過我們還是專注談能源來源吧。 COLIN: Then there's that ecotown in England, Greenhill Abbots. Colin：還有英格蘭那座生態小鎮 Greenhill Abbots。 It set out to conform to the usual principles – sustainability and so on. 它一開始就是按照一般原則來規劃——例如永續性等等。 A lot of people were against it at first; they said the plans were unrealistic. 一開始很多人反對，說那些計畫不切實際。 I'm not sure how far they've got with it – I'll check. 我不確定他們目前進展到什麼程度——我會去查一下。 ROSIE: Right. So it looks as … That is the end of Part 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3. Rosie：好的。所以看起來…… 第三部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第三部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 2
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Developing food trends · The growth in interest in food fashions started with 31 _____________ of food being shared on social media. · The UK food industry is constantly developing products which are new or different. · Influencers on social media become 'ambassadors' for a brand. -Sales of 32 _____________ food brands have grown rapidly this way. · Supermarkets track demand for ingredients on social media. -Famous 33 _____________ are influential. Marketing campaigns · The avocado: - 34 _____________ were invited to visit growers in South Africa. - Advertising focused on its 35 _____________ benefits. · Oat milk: - A Swedish brand's media campaign received publicity by upsetting competitors. - Promotion in the USA through 36 _____________ shops reduced the need for advertising. - It appealed to consumers who are concerned about the 37 __________ · Norwegian skrei: - has helped strengthen the 38 _____________ of Norwegian seafood. Ethical concerns · Quinoa: - Its success led to an increase in its 39 _____________. - Overuse of resources resulted in poor quality 40 _____________. · The growth in interest in food fashions started with 31 _____________ -Sales of 32 _____________ food brands have grown rapidly this way. -Famous 33 _____________ are influential. - 34 _____________ were invited to visit growers in South Africa. - Advertising focused on its 35 _____________ benefits. - Promotion in the USA through 36 _____________ shops reduced the - It appealed to consumers who are concerned about the 37 __________ - has helped strengthen the 38 _____________ of Norwegian seafood. - Its success led to an increase in its 39 _____________. - Overuse of resources resulted in poor quality 40 _____________. You will hear part of a food science lecture on fashions in food. 你會聽到一段食品科學講座，主題是食品潮流。 First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 31 至 40 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 31 至 40 題。 There are trends in food, much as there are trends in clothing. 食品也有潮流，就像服裝也有潮流一樣。 Interest in food fashions has risen rapidly since the birth of the smartphone when people first began taking photos of their food and instantly sharing them with their friends. 自從智慧型手機問世、人們開始拍攝食物照片並立即分享給朋友後，大家對食品潮流的興趣迅速上升。 The food industry in the UK, in particular, is obsessed with finding and exploiting the next big food trend. 尤其是英國食品業，特別熱衷於尋找並利用下一個重大的食品潮流。 Marketeers aim to create a huge demand for a food item, which was previously unknown, or not needed. 行銷人員的目標，是為一種先前不為人知或並非必要的食品創造巨大需求。 One of the most effective ways of promoting a new food product is by using social media influencers as brand ambassadors. 推廣新食品產品最有效的方法之一，是讓社群媒體網紅擔任品牌大使。 In return for free samples, many influencers will post content about a product, although there are influencers with hundreds of thousands of followers who can command large fees for their services. 許多網紅會因收到免費樣品而發布產品相關內容；不過，有些擁有數十萬粉絲的網紅，也能為服務收取高額費用。 Companies which sell vegan produce were pioneers in being able to increase sales really quickly in this way. 銷售純素食品的公司，是以這種方式快速提升銷售量的先驅。 For a food item to become really popular it has to be readily available, so supermarkets have a role to play in creating a new food trend. 一種食品若要真正流行，就必須容易買到，因此超市在創造新食品潮流方面扮演著一定角色。 They have dedicated teams closely following which new products or ingredients are trending on social media and are particularly interested in what well-known chefs are putting on their menus. 它們有專門團隊密切關注哪些新產品或食材正在社群媒體上流行，也特別關注知名主廚把哪些東西放進菜單。 I'd like to look at a few examples of marketing campaigns which were really successful in launching a new fashion trend. 我想看看幾個非常成功地帶動新潮流的行銷活動例子。 Starting in the 1990s with the avocado. 先從 1990 年代的酪梨說起。 A British PR company was hired to raise its profile and stimulate demand. 一家英國公關公司受聘來提高酪梨的知名度並刺激需求。 They paid for a group of journalists to travel out to South Africa to meet avocado farmers. 他們出資讓一群記者前往南非，去見酪梨農民。 Articles written following this visit helped to educate the British public about the avocado, which at this time was certainly not the daily staple it's since become. 這次拜訪後撰寫的文章，幫助英國大眾認識酪梨；當時酪梨當然還不像後來那樣成為日常主食。 Advertisements were designed to promote the avocado as a 'superfood': rich in nutrients and therefore beneficial for health. 廣告把酪梨包裝成「超級食物」來推廣： 營養豐富，因此有益健康。 Avocados became hugely fashionable and within a few years UK avocado sales had grown from 13 million pounds annually to around 150 million, making it one of the most successful fresh produce campaigns in UK history. 酪梨變得非常流行，短短幾年內，英國酪梨年銷售額從 1300 萬英鎊增長到約 1.5 億英鎊，使其成為英國歷史上最成功的新鮮農產品行銷活動之一。 Oat milk is a recent example of a new product which became fashionable very quickly. 燕麥奶是一個近年的例子，顯示一種新產品如何迅速流行起來。 Now there are many brands available, but one company which had early success was the Swedish brand, Oatly. 現在市面上有很多品牌，但早期取得成功的其中一家，是瑞典品牌 Oatly。 They attracted a lot of attention with a media campaign which used provocation as a way of getting their message across effectively. 他們透過一場使用挑釁手法來有效傳達訊息的媒體活動，吸引了大量關注。 The fact that this campaign aggravated competitors producing milk from dairy cows was seen as a plus, as it helped to make oat milk seem cool. 這場活動激怒了生產牛奶的競爭對手， 而這被視為加分，因為它讓燕麥奶看起來很酷。 In the USA, the brand decided against a big retail launch in favour of getting the product into coffee chains, which removed the need for a big advertising budget. 在美國，該品牌沒有選擇大規模零售上市，而是把產品推進咖啡連鎖店，這樣就不需要龐大的廣告預算。 This proved far more effective than offering samples in supermarkets. 事實證明，這比在超市提供試用品有效得多。 Oat milk had an advantage over other alternative milk products such as almond milk. 與杏仁奶等其他植物奶替代品相比，燕麥奶具有優勢。 Many consumers prefer it because it has less of an impact on the environment. 許多消費者更喜歡它，因為它對環境的影響較小。 It requires significantly less water to produce than other alternative milk products and it also has a relatively low carbon footprint. 生產燕麥奶所需的水明顯少於其他植物奶產品，而且它的碳足跡也相對較低。 Norwegian skrei, a rarely available seasonal fish delicacy, otherwise known as Arctic cod, is now found on the menus of Michelin starred restaurants throughout Europe. 挪威 skrei 是一種稀有的季節性魚類珍饈，又稱北極鱈，如今已出現在全歐洲米其林星級餐廳的菜單上。 The demand for skrei has been used by a food marketing agency to build the reputation of Norway's fisheries in general. 一家食品行銷機構利用人們對 skrei 的需求，來提升挪威漁業整體的聲譽。 Marketing surveys have shown that a significant number of shoppers now associate Norway with excellent seafood. 行銷調查顯示，現在有相當多消費者會把挪威和優質海鮮聯想在一起。 Food trends can be considered a good thing in some ways as they can benefit farmers and food producers enormously. 從某些方面來看，食品潮流可以被視為好事，因為它們能讓農民和食品生產者大大受益。 The public can also be encouraged to buy things which are more sustainably produced. 大眾也可以因此被鼓勵購買以更永續方式生產的產品。 But ethical concerns have been raised about the effects a surge in demand can cause. 但是，需求激增可能造成的影響也引發了倫理方面的擔憂。 Quinoa is a classic example. 藜麥就是一個典型例子。 This plant is native to Peru, and when demand peaked some years ago, the price soared, making it unaffordable for local people. 這種植物原產於秘魯，幾年前當需求達到高峰時，價格飆升，使當地人買不起。 While the popularity of quinoa has benefitted farmers financially, there have been other negative consequences. 雖然藜麥的流行讓農民在經濟上受益， 但也帶來了其他負面後果。 As demand grew, farmers began working the land all year round in order to produce more quinoa. 隨著需求增加，農民為了生產更多藜麥，開始全年耕作土地。 One issue has been that the fertility of the soil decreased dramatically, which could potentially lead to desertification in some areas. 其中一個問題是土壤肥力大幅下降，這可能會導致某些地區沙漠化。 Another example would be the case of… 另一個例子則是…… That is the end of Part 4. You now have one minute to check your answers to Part 4. 第四部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第四部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 3
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Practice 3, source question diagram/table, PDF page 4 =Furniture Rental Companies Name of company Information about costs Additional notes Peak Rentals Prices range from $105 to $ 1 __________ per The furniture is very 2 __________. room per month. Delivers in 1–2 days. Special offer: free 3 __________ with every living room set. 4 __________ and Mid-range prices. Also offers a cleaning service. Oliver 12% monthly fee for 5 __________. Larch Furniture Offers cheapest prices for renting furniture and Must have own 7 __________. 6 __________ items. Minimum contract length: six months. 8 __________ — See the 9 __________ for the most Rentals up-to-date prices. 10 __________ are allowed within 7 days of delivery. Peak Rentals Prices range from $105 to $ 1 __________ per The furniture is very 2 __________. Peak Rentals Prices range from $105 to $ 1 __________ per The furniture is very 2 __________. Special offer: free 3 __________ with every 4 __________ and Mid-range prices. Also offers a cleaning service. 12% monthly fee for 5 __________. 6 __________ items. Larch Furniture Offers cheapest prices for renting furniture and Must have own 7 __________. 8 __________ — See the 9 __________ for the most 8 __________ — See the 9 __________ for the most 10 __________ are allowed within 7 days You will hear a woman phoning the owner of a house she is going to rent about companies that she could rent furniture from. 你會聽到一位女士打電話給她即將租住房子的屋主，詢問可以租用家具的公司。 First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 1 至 5 題。 Now, listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5. 現在，請仔細聆聽並回答第 1 至 5 題。 MAN: Good morning. 男士：早安。 SHELLEY: Hi. This is Shelley Mayer. Shelley：你好，我是 Shelley Mayer。 I'm renting your house on Archwood Avenue. I'm due to move in next week. 我租了你在 Archwood Avenue 的房子，預計下週搬進去。 MAN: Oh yes, hello Ms Mayer. What can I do for you? 男士：哦，是的，你好，Mayer 女士。有什麼我可以幫忙的嗎？ SHELLEY: When I viewed the house, I told you I'll most probably need to rent some furniture – at least until I know whether my temporary work contract is going to be made permanent. Shelley：我看房時跟你說過， 我很可能需要租一些家具—— 至少在我知道臨時工作合約是否會轉為永久合約之前。 MAN: Yes of course, I remember. And I said I could give you some information about furniture rental companies in the city. 男士：是的，我當然記得。我也說過可以給你一些市內家具租賃公司的資訊。 SHELLEY: That's right. Shelley：沒錯。 MAN: Well, the biggest company is called Peak Rentals. 男士：嗯，最大的一家公司叫 Peak Rentals。 I've recommended them to other people and have always heard positive reports about them. 我曾向其他人推薦過他們，而且一直聽到不錯的評價。 SHELLEY: Could you give me an idea of their costs? Shelley：你能大概告訴我他們的收費嗎？ MAN: Sure, I actually have one of their brochures here. 男士：當然，我這裡剛好有一本他們的小冊子。 It says the monthly price per room starts at a hundred and five dollars and goes up to two hundred and thirty-nine dollars – that depends on which rooms you need furniture for, of course. 上面寫著每個房間每月的價格從 105 美元起，最高到 239 美元——當然，這取決於你哪些房間需要家具。 SHELLEY: Sure. It's just to get a general idea of how much it's gonna cost. Shelley：明白。我只是想大概了解一下會花多少錢。 And you said you had some positive feedback about this company. 你剛才說這家公司有一些正面的評價。 MAN: Yes, people have mentioned that the furniture from Peak Rentals is more modern than any of the other companies. 男士：是的，有人提到 Peak Rentals 的家具比其他公司的都更現代。 And also, once you place an order, the furniture will be delivered to you in just one or two days. 而且，一旦下單，家具只要一兩天就會送到。 SHELLEY: That would be really helpful. Shelley：那真的很方便。 MAN: Oh, and the brochure says that there's a special offer at the moment. 男士：哦，還有，小冊子上說目前有一項特別優惠。 If you rent living room furniture – I believe that's a set of chairs and a TV table, you'll also get a lamp at no extra cost. 如果你租客廳家具——我想是一組椅子和一張電視桌——你還可以免費獲得一盞燈。 SHELLEY: OK. But, you know, that price range you gave is more than I was hoping to pay. Shelley：好的。不過你知道，你剛才說的價格範圍比我原本希望支付的還高。 MAN: Then you could try Aaron and Oliver. 男士：那你可以試試 Aaron and Oliver。 SHELLEY: Sorry, what and Oliver? Shelley：抱歉，什麼 and Oliver ？ MAN: Aaron. Double-A-R-O-N. 男士：Aaron。兩個 A，R-O-N。 SHELLEY: OK. Are they cheaper? Shelley：好的。他們比較便宜嗎？ MAN: I'd say they're a mid-price company. 男士：我會說他們是中等價位的公司。 But if you chose them, you need to be aware that they charge an extra twelve per cent every month in case of damage. 但如果你選他們，要注意他們每月會額外收取 12% 的費用， 以防家具受損。 SHELLEY: Oh I see. I'd have to do the math carefully then. Shelley：哦，我明白了。那我得仔細算一下。 MAN: Right. But one helpful thing is that they also do cleaning for customers. 男士：對。不過有一點很方便， 他們也為顧客提供清潔服務。 SHELLEY: For the furniture? Shelley：清潔家具嗎？ MAN: For the house. 男士：是清潔房子。 SHELLEY: Oh I see. I probably won't need that. Shelley：哦，我明白了。我大概不需要那個。 Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10. 在你聽接下來的對話之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 6 至 10 題。 Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10. 現在請聆聽並回答第 6 至 10 題。 MAN: There's another company called Larch Furniture. 男士：還有另一家公司叫 Larch Furniture。 It's quite new, and it has the lowest prices in town. 它相當新，而且價格是城裡最低的。 That's for both furniture and also electronic equipment. 這包括家具，也包括電子設備。 SHELLEY: Well that would be good. Shelley：那挺好的。 I'm not bringing much with me, and I won't have much time to go shopping after I start my job. 我不會帶太多東西過來，而且開始工作後也沒有太多時間去購物。 MAN: There are two things you need to know about Larch Furniture. 男士：關於 Larch Furniture， 有兩件事你需要知道。 First of all, you have to take out insurance on the furniture, and you need to organise that yourself. 首先，你必須為家具購買保險，而且需要自己安排。 SHELLEY: That wouldn't be too hard. Shelley：那應該不會太難。 MAN: Also, you can't take out a contract for less than six months, but I figure that might not be a problem for you. 男士：另外，你不能簽少於六個月的合約，不過我想這對你來說可能不是問題。 You're renting the house for twelve months after all, aren't you? 畢竟你要租這棟房子 12 個月，對吧？ SHELLEY: Yes. OK, well I … Shelley：是的。好的，那我…… MAN: … sorry to interrupt. I just thought of another furniture rental company. 男士：……抱歉打斷你。我剛想到另一家家具租賃公司。 It's called Space Rentals. And it's located very near to the house. 它叫 Space Rentals，而且離這棟房子很近。 SHELLEY: OK. Shelley：好的。 MAN: I don't have any information about their charges, so it's best to use their app to find out what it would cost you to use them. 男士：我沒有他們收費的資料，所以最好使用他們的應用程式查看使用他們服務需要多少費用。 SHELLEY: OK thanks. I'll do that. Shelley：好的，謝謝。我會這麼做。 MAN: One good thing about that company is that if you don't like the furniture once it's delivered, you can request exchanges – as long as you do that within a week of receiving it. 男士：那家公司有一個好處是，如果家具送到後你不喜歡， 可以要求更換——只要你在收到家具後一週內提出。 SHELLEY: That sounds really great. OK. Well thanks very much. That's so helpful … Shelley：聽起來真的很棒。好的，非常謝謝你。這太有幫助了…… That is the end of part one. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part one. 第一部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第一部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 3
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–16 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Bidcaster Community Archaeology Project 11. Who was responsible for starting the community project? A. the castle owners B. a national charity C. the local council 12. How was the gold coin found? A. Heavy rain had removed some of the soil. B. The ground was dug up by wild rabbits. C. A person with a metal detector searched the area. 13. What led the archaeologists to believe there was an ancient village on this site? A. the lucky discovery of old records B. the bases of several structures visible in the grass C. the unusual stones found near the castle 14. What are the team still hoping to find? A. everyday pottery B. animal bones C. pieces of jewellery 15. What was found on the other side of the river to the castle? A. the remains of a large palace B. the outline of fields C. a number of small huts 16. What do the team plan to do after work ends this summer? A. prepare a display for a museum B. take part in a television programme C. start to organise school visits Practice 3, source question diagram/table, PDF page 8 17. bridge foundations __________ 18. rubbish pit __________ 19. meeting hall __________ 20. fish pond __________ Who was responsible for starting the community project? the castle owners a national charity the local council How was the gold coin found? Heavy rain had removed some of the soil. The ground was dug up by wild rabbits. A person with a metal detector searched the area. What led the archaeologists to believe there was an ancient village on this site? the lucky discovery of old records the bases of several structures visible in the grass the unusual stones found near the castle What are the team still hoping to find? everyday pottery animal bones pieces of jewellery What was found on the other side of the river to the castle? the remains of a large palace the outline of fields a number of small huts What do the team plan to do after work ends this summer? prepare a display for a museum take part in a television programme start to organise school visits bridge foundations A B C D E F G H I rubbish pit A B C D E F G H I meeting hall A B C D E F G H I fish pond A B C D E F G H I You will hear an archaeologist who is part of a community project to excavate an ancient village, talking to members of the public who are visiting the site. 你會聽到一位參與社區考古計畫的考古學家，對參觀遺址的民眾介紹發掘古代村莊的工作。 First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 11 至 16 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 11 至 16 題。 Hello, I'm Hayden. I'm one of the archaeologists investigating the site here at Bidcaster. 大家好，我是 Hayden。我是正在調查 Bidcaster 這處遺址的考古學家之一。 This is the third summer for this community project, and most of the people digging here are volunteers. 這是這個社區計畫進行的第三個夏天，而在這裡發掘的大多數人都是志工。 I'm a full-time archaeologist for the town council, but I was asked to join the project by NHA, a charity which sets up projects like this up and down the country. 我是鎮議會的全職考古學家， 但我是受 NHA 邀請加入這個計畫的。NHA 是一個慈善機構，在全國各地設立這類計畫。 As you can see, we're next to Bidcaster Castle, which is great because the owners let us use their facilities. 如你所見，我們就在 Bidcaster Castle 旁邊，這很棒，因為城堡主人讓我們使用他們的設施。 So, how did we get to where we are today? Many archaeology projects happen when an ancient object is found, and in our case, that object was a gold coin. 那麼，我們是怎麼走到今天這一步的呢？很多考古計畫都是因為發現古代物件而展開的； 在我們的案例中，那件物品是一枚金幣。 Coins are often found by people using metal detectors to look for things buried in the ground – or coins are uncovered when wild animals like rabbits have been digging tunnels. 硬幣常常是人們用金屬探測器尋找地下埋藏物時發現的，或者是像兔子這類野生動物挖洞時把硬幣翻出來。 Here, a walker found it on the ground after a rainstorm washed away some of the earth and sand. 在這裡，是一位行人在暴雨沖走部分泥土和沙子後，在地面上發現了它。 When the story of the gold coin hit the news, Peter Swift, an amateur historian, contacted me to say he believed there had been a village on this site, centuries before the castle was built. 當這枚金幣的消息登上新聞後，業餘歷史學家 Peter Swift 聯絡我，說他相信在城堡建成前幾個世紀，這裡曾經有一座村莊。 Just by chance, the team found some old maps and documents in our library which showed five-hundred-year-old drawings of ruined buildings on the grassy area between the outer stone walls of the castle and the river. 純屬偶然，團隊在我們的圖書館裡找到一些舊地圖和文件， 上面有 500 年前的圖畫，描繪了城堡外石牆和河流之間草地上的廢墟建築。 We knew then we were onto something. 那時我們就知道，我們找到了重要線索。 Over the three summers the team has been here, we've found the remains of several buildings, and more broken pots than you can count! 在團隊來到這裡的三個夏天裡，我們發現了幾棟建築的遺跡，以及多到數不清的陶罐碎片！ Normally you'd expect to find brooches and other jewellery, but we're still waiting to uncover any such items. 通常你會期待找到胸針和其他首飾，但我們目前還在等待發現這類物品。 The people who once lived here were skilled at making tools from animal bones, as you'll see when you visit the exhibition. 曾經住在這裡的人很擅長用動物骨頭製作工具，這點你們參觀展覽時會看到。 Besides the discovery of the village, we've also found evidence of human activity on the other side of the river – no other houses or huts so far, but we can see the borders of an ancient field system. 除了發現這座村莊外，我們也在河對岸發現了人類活動的證據——目前還沒有發現其他房屋或小屋，但我們能看到古代田地系統的邊界。 At one point we found a long wall and thought it was an ancient palace, but it turned out to be a modern wall. 有一次我們發現一堵長牆，原以為是古代宮殿，結果證明它是一堵現代牆。 This summer's work will end soon, but we'll be back next summer. 今年夏天的工作很快就會結束，但我們明年夏天還會回來。 In the meantime, we're putting on a series of guided tours for school groups this autumn. 在此期間，我們今年秋天會為學校團體安排一系列導覽活動。 Oh and, maybe you saw the TV documentary about our project. 哦，還有，也許你們看過關於我們這個計畫的電視紀錄片。 That suggested the objects we've found are going to the town's museum, but we don't know that for sure yet. 那部節目暗示我們發現的物品會送到鎮上的博物館，但我們目前還不能確定。 Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20. 在你聽接下來的演講之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 17 至 20 題。 Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20. 現在請聆聽並回答第 17 至 20 題。 When you enter the site, please make sure you keep to the paths at all times. 進入遺址時，請務必始終沿著小路行走。 There are a few other things – the highlights of the site, if you like – that I want to mention. 我還想提幾個地方——你也可以說是這處遺址的亮點。 Take a look at the map; our present location is marked at the bottom. 請看一下地圖；我們目前的位置標在底部。 This year we've identified the foundations of an ancient bridge. 今年我們確認了一座古橋的地基。 And it's really exciting today because a team of divers are in the river searching for lost objects. 今天特別令人興奮，因為有一隊潛水員正在河裡尋找遺失的物件。 To reach the bridge, take the main path ahead of you, go straight on and keep going till the path bends to the left. 要到橋那裡，請沿著前方主路直走，一直走到小路向左彎。 You'll see a smaller track leading off to the right. 你會看到一條較小的小徑向右延伸。 Follow that to take you to the river, where the divers are. 沿著那條路走，就會到達河邊，也就是潛水員所在的地方。 You might be interested to see the rubbish pit. 你們可能會有興趣看看垃圾坑。 This is very near the castle walls in the northwest corner of the site. 它非常靠近遺址西北角的城堡牆。 It actually dates to the time of the castle and not the ancient village. 它其實屬於城堡時期，而不是古代村莊時期。 We found oyster shells and fish bones, and we assume they were thrown from the castle kitchen above. 我們發現了牡蠣殼和魚骨，推測它們是從上方的城堡廚房丟下來的。 One area we excavated in the first summer uncovered the site of a meeting hall. 第一年夏天，我們發掘的一個區域揭露了一座會議廳的遺址。 We knew it was an important building because it had two rows of post holes, deep enough to support a large roof. 我們知道那是一座重要建築， 因為那裡有兩排柱洞，深度足以支撐大型屋頂。 It's the largest structure in the central area of the site, next to the current excavation area. 它是遺址中央區域最大的結構，就在目前發掘區旁邊。 Last year we discovered a fish pond in the ancient village. 去年，我們在古代村莊中發現了一個魚塘。 Normally these were beside a river. 通常這類魚塘會在河邊。 The pond here is further away, but it's possible the river has moved slightly. 這裡的魚塘離河較遠，不過也有可能是河道稍微移動過。 Anyway, to get there from here, you turn right at the first information board you come to, and follow the path into the trees. 總之，從這裡去那裡時，在你遇到的第一塊資訊牌處右轉， 然後沿著小路走進樹林。 Before you come out of the trees, you'll see it on your right. 在你走出樹林之前，你會在右手邊看到它。 If you reach the river, you've gone too far. 如果你走到河邊，那就走太遠了。 So, does anyone… 那麼，有沒有人…… That is the end of part two. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two. 第二部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第二部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 3
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–26 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Project on Theatre Programmes 21. Finn was pleased to discover that their topic A. was not familiar to their module leader. B. had not been chosen by other students. C. did not prove to be difficult to research. 22. Maya says a mistaken belief about theatre programmes is that A. theatres pay companies to produce them. B. few theatre-goers buy them nowadays. C. they contain far more adverts than previously. 23. Finn was surprised that, in early British theatre, programmes A. were difficult for audiences to obtain. B. were given out free of charge. C. were seen as a kind of contract. 24. Maya feels their project should include an explanation of why companies of actors A. promoted their own plays. B. performed plays outdoors. C. had to tour with their plays. 25. Finn and Maya both think that, compared to nineteenth-century programmes, those from the eighteenth century A. were more original. B. were more colourful. C. were more informative. 26. Maya doesn't fully understand why, in the twentieth century, A. very few theatre programmes were printed in the USA. B. British theatre programmes failed to develop for so long. C. theatre programmes in Britain copied fashions from the USA. Questions 27–30 What comment is made about the programme for each of the following shows? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 27–30. Comments about programme A. Its origin is somewhat controversial. B. It is historically significant for a country. C. It was effective at attracting audiences. D. It is included in a recent project. E. It contains insights into the show. F. It resembles an artwork. Shows 27. Ruy Blas __________ 28. Man of La Mancha __________ 29. The Tragedy of Jane Shore __________ 30. The Sailors' Festival __________ Finn was pleased to discover that their topic was not familiar to their module leader. had not been chosen by other students. did not prove to be difficult to research. Maya says a mistaken belief about theatre programmes is that theatres pay companies to produce them. few theatre-goers buy them nowadays. they contain far more adverts than previously. Finn was surprised that, in early British theatre, programmes were difficult for audiences to obtain. were given out free of charge. were seen as a kind of contract. Maya feels their project should include an explanation of why companies of actors promoted their own plays. performed plays outdoors. had to tour with their plays. Finn and Maya both think that, compared to nineteenth-century programmes, those from the eighteenth century were more original. were more colourful. were more informative. Maya doesn't fully understand why, in the twentieth century, very few theatre programmes were printed in the USA. British theatre programmes failed to develop for so long. theatre programmes in Britain copied fashions from the USA. Ruy Blas Its origin is somewhat controversial. It is historically significant for a country. It was effective at attracting audiences. It is included in a recent project. It contains insights into the show. It resembles an artwork. Man of La Mancha Its origin is somewhat controversial. It is historically significant for a country. It was effective at attracting audiences. It is included in a recent project. It contains insights into the show. It resembles an artwork. The Tragedy of Jane Shore Its origin is somewhat controversial. It is historically significant for a country. It was effective at attracting audiences. It is included in a recent project. It contains insights into the show. It resembles an artwork. The Sailors' Festival Its origin is somewhat controversial. It is historically significant for a country. It was effective at attracting audiences. It is included in a recent project. It contains insights into the show. It resembles an artwork. You will hear two theatre studies students, Maya and Finn, discussing their project on theater programs. 你會聽到兩位戲劇研究學生 Maya 和 Finn 討論他們關於劇場節目單的專題。 First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 21 至 26 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 21 至 26 題。 MAYA: So Finn, I've done as much as I can for our project on theatre programmes. How's your research coming along? Maya：Finn，我已經盡力完成我們關於劇場節目單專題的部分了。 你的研究進行得怎麼樣？ FINN: OK, Maya. I didn't know theatre programmes are called playbills in the USA till I started looking into the topic. Finn：還可以，Maya。我開始研究這個題目後，才知道劇場節目單在美國叫 playbills。 Even though I struggled to find many useful websites, I'm glad we picked this subject. 雖然我很難找到很多有用的網站，但我很高興我們選了這個主題。 No one else on the course is doing the same as us, although it is one of the research areas of the module convenor. 課程裡沒有其他人做和我們一樣的題目，雖然這是該模組負責人的研究領域之一。 MAYA: That might actually put some people off. Maya：那其實可能會讓一些人卻步。 FINN: I suppose so. Anyway, I hadn't realised there are actually companies specialising in creating theatre programmes. Finn：我想也是。不管怎樣，我之前沒意識到其實有專門製作劇場節目單的公司。 MAYA: Yes, they're quite common nowadays. Maya：是的，現在相當常見。 Contrary to what many people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes, in fact companies buy the rights to publish programmes on the theatre's behalf – and then make their money selling advertising space within the programme booklet. 和許多人以為的相反，劇院並不是雇人製作節目單；事實上，公司會購買代表劇院出版節目單的權利，然後透過出售節目冊中的廣告版面賺錢。 FINN: It must be easier for theatres to do it that way. Finn：對劇院來說，這樣做一定比較容易。 MAYA: Yes. Maya：是的。 FINN: I remember reading something about programmes in early British theatre. Finn：我記得讀過一些關於早期英國劇場節目單的資料。 It said that the cast was always very important. 裡面說演員陣容一直非常重要。 MAYA: Yeah, audiences were very familiar with leading actors, and big names would draw huge crowds. Maya：是啊，觀眾對主要演員非常熟悉，而知名演員會吸引大量人潮。 FINN: But I hadn't realised that if the programme named a famous actor, that's who the public expected to perform. Finn：但我之前沒意識到，如果節目單上列出某位知名演員，觀眾就會期待那個人上台演出。 And if that didn't happen, people accused the theatre of breaking their agreement with the audience. 如果沒有發生，人們就會指責劇院違反了和觀眾之間的約定。 They would demand refunds, and, if they didn't get them, there were riots! 他們會要求退款；如果拿不到退款，就會發生騷亂！ MAYA: Outrageous. That'd never happen now. Maya：太誇張了。現在絕不會發生這種事。 FINN: No, people are too polite, even when they're disappointed if the star of the show misses a performance. Finn：不會，現在的人太有禮貌了，即使主演缺席演出讓他們失望也是如此。 MAYA: We should definitely include that information about early audiences in our project. Maya：我們絕對應該把早期觀眾的這些資訊放進專題裡。 I also think it's important to mention that lots of ordinary people at that time were illiterate, so theatre programmes were of limited value in advertising plays. 我也覺得有必要提到，當時很多普通人不識字，所以劇場節目單在宣傳戲劇方面的價值有限。 When a company of actors arrived in a town, they'd parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances. 當一個劇團來到城鎮時，他們會穿著戲服在街上遊行、敲鼓，並宣布即將上演的劇目。 FINN: Interesting. I couldn't imagine that happening now either. Finn：真有意思。我也無法想像現在還會發生這種事。 MAYA: There's also an interesting comparison to make between eighteenth and nineteenth-century programmes. Maya：18 世紀和 19 世紀的節目單之間也有一個有趣的比較。 FINN: Wasn't it in the nineteenth century that theatre programmes started to resemble programmes today? Finn：劇場節目單不是在 19 世紀開始變得像今天的節目單嗎？ MAYA: Yes. And, unlike programmes from the eighteenth century, they always used colour. Maya：是的。而且和 18 世紀的節目單不同，它們總是使用色彩。 FINN: And there was a greater variety of designs. Finn：而且設計種類也更多。 But personally, I think eighteenth-century programmes were superior because they told the theatre-goers so many things, including about the actors. 但就我個人而言，我認為 18 世紀的節目單更好，因為它們告訴觀眾很多資訊，包括演員方面的內容。 MAYA: And about the writer, the plot, and sometimes the history of the play. Maya：還有作者、劇情，有時也包括這齣戲的歷史。 FINN: That's right… What should we say about theatre programmes in the twentieth century? Finn：沒錯……那我們該怎麼談 20 世紀的劇場節目單呢？ MAYA: I reckon the most important thing is the dramatic change they underwent during World War Two. Maya：我覺得最重要的是，它們在第二次世界大戰期間經歷了巨大的變化。 FINN: When the government imposed restrictions on the use of paper. Finn：也就是政府限制紙張使用的時候。 MAYA: Yeah, but that was only in the UK. In the USA, programmes – or rather, playbills – continued to be published in the same format ... Maya：是的，但那只發生在英國。 在美國，節目單——或者更準確地說，playbills——仍然以相同形式出版…… FINN: … while here in the UK, programmes became merely a single sheet of paper folded to create four pages for text. Finn：……而在英國，節目單只剩下一張紙，對摺後形成四頁文字。 MAYA: What I don't really get is that, after the war, they didn't go back to being more than one sheet, or change in any way for over twenty-five years. Maya：我真正不明白的是，戰後它們沒有恢復成多張紙，也在超過 25 年的時間裡沒有任何變化。 I know there were paper shortages after the war, but only for five or ten years. 我知道戰後曾有紙張短缺，但那只持續了五到十年。 FINN: Strange. Finn：真奇怪。 Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30. 在你聽接下來的討論之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 27 至 30 題。 Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30. 現在請聆聽並回答第 27 至 30 題。 MAYA: I've got some pictures of programmes we could include on the slides for our presentation. Maya：我有一些節目單的圖片，可以放進我們簡報的投影片裡。 FINN: I found a couple too, Maya. Let's go through and see what we think. Finn：我也找到幾張，Maya。我們一起看一下，看看想法如何。 MAYA: Erm …, this is an old one, for a play called Ruy Blas. Maya：嗯……這是一張舊的，是一齣叫 Ruy Blas 的戲的節目單。 FINN: Never heard of that, but the programme looks very decorative. Finn：我從沒聽過那齣戲，但這張節目單看起來很有裝飾性。 MAYA: Good enough to put in a frame on the wall. The images are just beautiful. Finn, what did you find? Maya：漂亮到可以裝框掛在牆上。 那些圖像真的很美。Finn，你找到什麼？ FINN: I've got some pages from a programme for Man of La Mancha. Finn：我找到幾頁《Man of La Mancha》的節目單。 I thought this was a good programme to show, not because of the pictures, but because it contains articles written by members of the theatre company. 我覺得這是一份很值得展示的節目單，不是因為圖片，而是因為裡面有劇團成員寫的文章。 So we can learn how the production was created, and the thoughts and feelings of the cast. 所以我們可以了解這部作品是如何創作的，以及演員們的想法和感受。 MAYA: Good. I've got a copy of a programme that's now in a museum. Maya：很好。我有一份目前收藏在博物館裡的節目單副本。 It's for The Tragedy of Jane Shore and it's said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press. 它是《The Tragedy of Jane Shore》 的節目單，據說是澳洲第一台印刷機印出的、現存最早的文件。 FINN: Fantastic. Finn：太棒了。 MAYA: Another programme to talk about is for The Sailors' Festival. Maya：另一份可以談的是《The Sailors' Festival》的節目單。 It comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago. 它來自大英圖書館幾年前開始建立的節目單數位化館藏。 It already comprises over two hundred thousand programmes, which is amazing. 這個館藏已經包含超過 20 萬份節目單，真的很驚人。 FINN: Wish I'd known about it while I was doing my research! Finn：真希望我做研究時就知道這個！ That is the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three. 第三部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第三部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 3
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Inclusive Design Definition ● Designing products that can be accessed by a diverse range of people without the need for any 31 __________. ● Not the same as universal design: that is design for everyone, including catering for people with 32 __________ problems. Examples of inclusive design ● 33 __________ which are adjustable, avoiding back or neck problems. ● 34 __________ in public toilets which are easier to use. ● To assist the elderly: ○ designers avoid using 35 __________ in interfaces. ○ people can make commands using a mouse, keyboard or their 36 __________. Impact of non-inclusive designs ● Access: ○ Loss of independence for disabled people. ● Safety: ○ Seatbelts are especially problematic for 37 __________ women. ○ PPE jackets are often unsuitable because of the size of women's 38 __________. ○ PPE for female 39 __________ officers dealing with emergencies is the worst. ● Comfort in the workplace: ○ The 40 __________ in offices is often too low for women. without the need for any 31 __________. catering for people with 32 __________ problems. ● 33 __________ which are adjustable, avoiding back or neck problems. ● 34 __________ in public toilets which are easier to use. ○ designers avoid using 35 __________ in interfaces. ○ people can make commands using a mouse, keyboard or their 36 __________. ○ Seatbelts are especially problematic for 37 __________ women. ○ PPE jackets are often unsuitable because of the size of women's 38 __________. ○ PPE for female 39 __________ officers dealing with emergencies ○ The 40 __________ in offices is often too low for women. You will hear a design and technology lecturer talking about inclusive design. 你會聽到一位設計與科技講師談論包容性設計。 First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 31 至 40 題。 Now, listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40. 現在，請仔細聆聽並回答第 31 至 40 題。 It's only relatively recently that designers have become aware of the need to be inclusive when designing products. 直到相對近年，設計師才開始意識到在設計產品時需要具備包容性。 But what does that mean exactly? Well, it simply means designing products that span economic, social and cultural barriers. 但這到底是什麼意思呢？簡單來說，就是設計能跨越經濟、社會和文化障礙的產品。 It means making sure products are accessible – so that as many different types of people as possible can use them without any type of adaptation having to be made to the original design. 這意味著要確保產品易於使用，讓盡可能多不同類型的人都能使用，而不需要對原始設計進行任何改造。 Inclusive design is often linked with universal design, although they are not quite the same thing. 包容性設計常常和通用設計聯繫在一起，雖然兩者並不完全相同。 Universal design aims to make products that work for everyone and that includes considering the needs of people who have cognitive difficulties, which can present quite a challenge. 通用設計旨在製作適合所有人使用的產品，其中包括考慮有認知困難者的需求，而這可能相當具有挑戰性。 Today, examples of successful inclusive design can be seen all around us. 如今，我們周圍到處都可以看到成功的包容性設計案例。 In workplaces it is common to see desks which can be adjusted to suit people of different heights or for wheelchair users. 在工作場所，常可以看到可調整高度的桌子，以適應不同身高的人或輪椅使用者。 This still isn't always the case, however, and is one reason why office workers often suffer from back or neck problems. 不過，情況並不總是如此，這也是辦公室工作者常常出現背部或頸部問題的原因之一。 You'll find another example in the public toilets of countless hotels, airports and offices. 你也可以在無數飯店、機場和辦公室的公共廁所裡看到另一個例子。 Taps that you activate by sensor require no pressing or twisting movements. 感應式水龍頭不需要按壓或旋轉動作。 These are not only more hygienic, they're also easier for people with dexterity or mobility issues. 它們不僅更衛生，對手部靈活度或行動能力有困難的人來說也更容易使用。 The tech industry has been criticised in the past for focusing too much on young consumers but this is changing. 科技產業過去曾因過度關注年輕消費者而受到批評，但這種情況正在改變。 Many products are now designed with the elderly in mind. 現在許多產品在設計時都會考慮老年人的需求。 For example, it's well known that vision declines with age, and that we also become worse at distinguishing between similar colours; in particular, shades of blue, which is why software designers rarely create interfaces with this colour. 例如，眾所周知，視力會隨著年齡增長而下降，而且我們分辨相近顏色的能力也會變差； 尤其是藍色系，因此軟體設計師很少使用這種顏色來設計介面。 Motor skills also decline with age and some people have difficulty doing everyday things like picking up a cup or opening a door. 動作能力也會隨年齡下降，有些人在做日常事情時會遇到困難，例如拿起杯子或開門。 This can also affect their ability to use a mouse or keyboard. 這也可能影響他們使用滑鼠或鍵盤的能力。 So voice access is now a routine way of making commands. 因此，語音控制現在已成為發出指令的一種常見方式。 It's worth looking at the problems non-inclusive designs cause when not enough consideration is given to a range of users, as it can have a serious impact on people's lives. 當設計沒有充分考慮不同使用者時，非包容性設計會造成許多問題，這點值得關注，因為它可能對人們的生活造成嚴重影響。 Access is one obvious example because it has such a huge impact on disabled people's independence. 使用權就是一個明顯例子，因為它對身心障礙者的獨立生活有巨大影響。 Not being able to access public transport because buses or trains are not wheelchair-friendly means many disabled people can't go out unless someone goes with them. 如果公車或火車不適合輪椅使用者，導致無法搭乘公共交通，這就意味著許多身心障礙者除非有人陪同，否則無法外出。 Safety is another issue. 安全是另一個問題。 Inexplicably, most cars are still crash-tested using a dummy based on an average-sized male. 令人難以理解的是，大多數汽車在碰撞測試時，仍使用以平均身材男性為基準的假人。 This has safety implications for all women, particularly those who are pregnant, as the seatbelts worn by the dummy are not adapted to accommodate them. 這對所有女性都有安全影響， 尤其是孕婦，因為測試假人使用的安全帶並未調整到能適合她們。 Over the past 100 years, workplaces in the UK have, on the whole, become considerably safer. 過去 100 年來，英國工作場所整體而言已變得安全許多。 Employers are legally required to provide well-maintained personal protective equipment or PPE – anything from goggles to full body suits – to workers who need it, free of charge. 法律要求雇主免費為有需要的員工提供維護良好的個人防護裝備，也就是 PPE，範圍從護目鏡到全身防護服都有。 But most PPE is designed to fit men. 但是，大多數個人防護裝備都是依照男性身形設計的。 A recent report found that employers often think that when it comes to female workers, all they need to do to comply with this legal requirement is to buy jackets, for example, designed for a small man. 最近一份報告發現，雇主常常認為，對女性員工而言，要符合法律要求，只需要購買例如為小個子男性設計的外套即可。 The problem with this is that women can be tall and still have much smaller shoulders than the average man. 問題在於，女性即使身材高挑，肩膀仍可能比一般男性窄得多。 Ill-fitting PPE such as hi-vis jackets, vests and body armour can put women at risk. 不合身的個人防護裝備，例如高能見度外套、背心和防彈護具，可能會讓女性處於危險之中。 The report found that 95% of women said that their PPE often hampered their work and that this problem was worst in the emergency services, particularly the police. 報告發現，95% 的女性表示，她們的個人防護裝備經常妨礙工作；這個問題在緊急服務部門最嚴重，尤其是在警察部門。 Another problem is related to comfort at work. 另一個問題與工作時的舒適度有關。 A very common scenario in offices in summertime is to see women wrapped in blankets or wearing sweaters while the air conditioning is on high. 夏天的辦公室裡很常見的一幕是，空調開得很強，女性裹著毯子或穿著毛衣。 Meanwhile the men are in shorts and T-shirts. 與此同時，男性則穿著短褲和 T 恤。 This is due to differences in metabolic rates for men and women. 這是因為男性和女性的新陳代謝率不同。 There is a standard setting for air conditioning to be at a temperature of 21 degrees, designed to suit men, and in most modern offices it's not possible to turn the air conditioning up or down. 空調有一個標準設定溫度是 21 度，而這是為了適合男性；在大多數現代辦公室裡，空調也無法自行調高或調低。 This means that many offices which mainly employ women are wasting energy by having the air conditioning set too high. 這意味著許多主要雇用女性的辦公室，因為空調設定過強而浪費能源。 As you can see from the examples I've just mentioned, there are serious consequences for designs which don't consider the needs of all users. This is … 從我剛才提到的例子可以看出，沒有考慮所有使用者需求的設計會帶來嚴重後果。這是…… That is the end of part four. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part four. 第四部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第四部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 4
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Advice on Family Visit Accommodation ● 1 __________ Hotel on George Street ● cost of family room per night: £2 __________ approx. Recommended trips ● a 3 __________ tour of the city centre, starts in Carlton Square ● a trip by 4 __________ to the old fort Science Museum ● best day to visit: 5 __________ ● see the exhibition about 6 __________, which opens soon Food ● Clacton Market: ○ good for 7 __________ food ○ need to have lunch before 8 __________ p.m. Theatre tickets ● save up to 9 __________ % on ticket prices at bargaintickets.com Free activities ● Blakewell Gardens: ○ Roots Music Festival ○ climb Telegraph Hill to see a view of the 10 __________ ● 1 __________ Hotel on George Street ● cost of family room per night: £2 __________ approx. ● a 3 __________ tour of the city centre, starts in Carlton Square ● a trip by 4 __________ to the old fort ● best day to visit: 5 __________ ● see the exhibition about 6 __________, which opens soon ○ good for 7 __________ food ○ need to have lunch before 8 __________ p.m. ● save up to 9 __________ % on ticket prices at bargaintickets.com ○ climb Telegraph Hill to see a view of the 10 __________ You will hear a man asking a friend for advice on things to do in the city with a family of visitors. 你會聽到一位男士向朋友詢問，有親戚一家來訪時在城裡可以安排哪些活動。 First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 1 至 6 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 1 至 6 題。 MAN: Sandra – I seem to remember you had some family visitors staying with you recently. 男士：Sandra——我記得你最近好像有家人來你那裡住過。 SANDRA: Yeah that's right. My brother and his family were here a couple of months ago. Sandra：是的，沒錯。我哥哥和他的家人幾個月前來過。 MAN: OK good. Well I wanted to ask your advice – I've got my cousin and her family visiting next month and as I don't have kids I've no idea where to take them. 男士：好，那太好了。我想問問你的建議——我表妹和她一家下個月要來，因為我沒有小孩，所以完全不知道該帶他們去哪裡。 SANDRA: Right. What about accommodation? Are they going to stay with you in your flat? Sandra：明白。那住宿呢？他們會住在你的公寓裡嗎？ MAN: No, thankfully – there wouldn't be room – my cousin wants me to recommend a hotel. Do you know anywhere? 男士：不會，幸好不會——我那裡沒有空間。我表妹想讓我推薦一家酒店。你知道哪裡合適嗎？ SANDRA: Yes, I do actually. I always recommend people stay at the Kings Hotel. Sandra：知道，其實我知道。我總是推薦大家住 King’s Hotel。 MAN: Where's that near? 男士：那附近有什麼？ SANDRA: It's about five minutes' walk from Murray Station – so nice and central. It's actually on George Street. Sandra：從 Murray Station 走路大約五分鐘，很方便，也在市中心。 它就在 George Street 上。 MAN: Oh yes I know. I think they're on quite a tight budget – so how much roughly is it to stay there? 男士：哦，是的，我知道。我想他們預算挺緊的——那住那裡大概多少錢？ SANDRA: If you book a family room it's about £125 per night. Sandra：如果訂家庭房，每晚大約 125 英鎊。 My brother paid for two double rooms in the end and I think that was around £95 for each room. 我哥哥最後訂了兩間雙人房，我記得每間大約 95 英鎊。 MAN: Oh that's not too bad. 男士：哦，那還不算太糟。 SANDRA: So how old are your cousin's kids? Sandra：那你表妹的小孩多大？ MAN: Twelve and nine. So I want to organise some trips while they're here. 男士：12 歲和 9 歲。所以我想在他們來的時候安排一些行程。 I was thinking of doing a bus tour of the city centre – as none of them have been here before. 我原本想安排市中心巴士遊，因為他們以前都沒來過這裡。 SANDRA: Those bus tours are quite expensive. I think it's better to do a walking tour – it gives you a much better feel for the city. Sandra：那些巴士遊挺貴的。我覺得步行導覽更好，能讓你更好地感受這座城市。 There's one that starts from Carlton Square. It takes a couple of hours and doesn't cost that much. 有一個導覽從 Carlton Square 出發，大約需要幾個小時，而且費用不高。 MAN: Sounds good. I'll look that up – thanks. 男士：聽起來不錯。我會查一下，謝謝。 SANDRA: If the weather's nice, one thing you could do is visit the old fort. Sandra：如果天氣好的話，你可以去參觀那座古老堡壘。 You can get there by boat. The whole trip takes half a day. 可以搭船去。整個行程需要半天。 MAN: That's a really good idea. I'd like to do that myself. 男士：這真是個好主意。我自己也想去。 And if the weather's bad I was thinking they could go to the Science Museum. But maybe they could do that when I'm at work. 如果天氣不好，我想他們可以去科學博物館。不過也許可以在我上班時讓他們去。 SANDRA: Yeah – don't forget it's closed on Mondays. Sandra：是啊——別忘了它星期一休館。 MAN: They're here from Saturday for four nights – so Tuesday would be best, I think. 男士：他們從星期六開始來住四晚，所以我想星期二最合適。 SANDRA: Mmm, and it won't be so crowded then. Saturdays are terrible. Sandra：嗯，那時也不會那麼擁擠。 星期六人非常多。 I took my kids to the exhibition on old computers there and it was far too crowded. 我之前帶孩子去看那裡的舊電腦展，結果太擁擠了。 I wanted to go back but it's finished now. 我本來還想再去一次，但現在展覽已經結束了。 MAN: That's a shame. My cousin's kids would have enjoyed that. 男士：真可惜。我表妹的小孩應該會喜歡那個。 SANDRA: There's another one starting soon on space which looks really good too. Sandra：很快會有另一個關於太空的展覽，看起來也很不錯。 MAN: OK, well I'll mention that to my cousin. 男士：好，我會跟我表妹提一下。 Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10. 在你聽接下來的對話之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 7 至 10 題。 Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10. 現在請聆聽並回答第 7 至 10 題。 SANDRA: Have you thought about where to take them to eat? Sandra：你有想過帶他們去哪裡吃飯嗎？ MAN: Well I really like all the food stalls at Clacton Market. My cousin's vegetarian – I know it's one of the best places for that kind of food. 男士：嗯，我很喜歡 Clacton Market 的那些食物攤位。我表妹吃素，我知道那裡是最適合吃這類食物的地方之一。 SANDRA: Definitely, and there'll be loads of choice for the kids, too. Sandra：絕對是，而且孩子們也會有很多選擇。 You need to get there quite early though – at the weekend most of the stalls stop serving lunch at 2.30. 不過你們得早點到——週末大多數攤位下午 2:30 就停止供應午餐了。 MAN: Good point. It's all going to need careful planning! 男士：說得好。這一切都得仔細規劃！ My cousin said she'd love to take the kids to a show at the theatre – but tickets are so expensive! 我表妹說她很想帶孩子們去劇院看演出，但票太貴了！ SANDRA: I know. But you can get some good deals if you book online with bargaintickets.com for the following day – on some seats there's a 75% discount. Sandra：我知道。不過如果你在 bargaintickets.com 上預訂隔天的票，可以找到一些很划算的優惠 ——有些座位有 75% 的折扣。 MAN: Really?! I must try and get some. 男士：真的嗎？！我一定要試著買幾張。 SANDRA: Yeah. There are lots of things you can do for free as well – no need to spend a fortune. Sandra：是啊。也有很多免費活動可以做，不需要花一大筆錢。 MAN: Like what? 男士：比如什麼？ SANDRA: They're coming next month, right? Sandra：他們下個月來，對吧？ Well, check and see if it's the same weekend as the Roots Music Festival in Blakewell Gardens. 那你查查看，是不是剛好和 Blakewell Gardens 的 Roots Music Festival 在同一個週末。 MAN: R double-O-T-S? 男士：R，兩個 O，T-S？ SANDRA: Yeah. Check it out online. It's always a family-friendly event and there's no entry charge. Sandra：是的。你可以上網查一下。 那一直都是很適合家庭參加的活動，而且不收門票。 MAN: That sounds perfect. 男士：聽起來很完美。 SANDRA: And if you're in Blakewell Gardens – climb Telegraph Hill – you'll be able to look right down on the port. Sandra：如果你們在 Blakewell Gardens，可以爬上 Telegraph Hill， 就能直接俯瞰港口。 Everyone's always really impressed because it's so huge. 大家總是印象很深刻，因為它實在太大了。 MAN: Oh yeah – I've been meaning to do that for ages. I've heard the view's amazing. 男士：哦，是啊——我一直想去那裡很久了。我聽說景色很棒。 SANDRA: Yeah. It's really worth the effort. Sandra：是啊，真的很值得。 MAN: Well that's given me loads of ideas. Thanks so much … 男士：嗯，這給了我很多想法。非常感謝…… That is the end of part one. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part one. 第一部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第一部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 4
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11 and 12 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO things does the speaker say about visiting the football stadium with children? A. Children can get their photo taken with a football player. B. There is a competition for children today. C. Parents must stay with their children at all times. D. Children will need sunhats and drinks. E. The café has a special offer on meals for children. Questions 13 and 14 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO features of the stadium tour are new this year? A. VIP tour B. 360 cinema experience C. audio guide D. dressing room tour E. tours in other languages Questions 15–20 Which event in the history of football in the UK took place in each of the following years? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 15–20. Events in the history of football A. the introduction of pay for the players B. a change to the design of the goal C. the first use of lights for matches D. the introduction of goalkeepers E. the first international match F. two changes to the rules of the game G. the introduction of a fee for spectators H. an agreement on the length of a game Year 15. 1870 __________ 16. 1874 __________ 17. 1875 __________ 18. 1877 __________ 19. 1878 __________ 20. 1880 __________ Choose TWO letters, A–E. Parents must stay with their children at all times. Children will need sunhats and drinks. The café has a special offer on meals for children. Choose TWO letters, A–E.
