pay for the players a change to the design of the goal the first use of lights for matches the introduction of goalkeepers the first international match two changes to the rules of the game the introduction of a fee for spectators an agreement on the length of a game You will hear a Guide talking to members of the public who are visiting a football stadium in the UK. 你會聽到一位導遊向正在參觀英國一座足球場的民眾介紹資訊。 First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 11 至 14 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 11 至 14 題。 Good morning, and welcome to City Football Club. 早安，歡迎來到 City Football Club。 I'd like to give you some useful information about your visit to the stadium today, and then we'll start the tour of the areas of the stadium that are open to visitors. 我想先提供一些關於今天參觀球場的實用資訊，然後我們會開始參觀球場中對遊客開放的區域。 I can see lots of children here today, so just to let mums and dads know a few things before we start. 我今天看到有很多孩子在場，所以在開始前，先讓各位家長了解幾件事。 The stadium has lots of stairs, and the players' tunnel is very dark. 球場裡有很多樓梯，而且球員通道非常昏暗。 Please don't let your children wander off on their own, even for a minute. 請不要讓孩子自己走開，即使只有一分鐘也不要。 We don't want any accidents or anyone getting frightened. 我們不希望發生任何意外，也不希望有人受到驚嚇。 Cameras are permitted everywhere, and you can take pictures of your child shooting a penalty. 這裡到處都可以拍照，你們也可以拍下孩子踢點球的畫面。 Assistants are helping to organise this, and hopefully the queue won't be too long – it's very hot and sunny out on the pitch today. 工作人員會協助安排這項活動， 希望排隊不會太久——今天球場上非常炎熱，而且陽光很強。 You can get food and drink at the café, and I really recommend the healthy lunch boxes for children. 你們可以在咖啡館買食物和飲料，我非常推薦給孩子們的健康午餐盒。 Also in the café, children are invited to do a football-themed drawing. 另外，在咖啡館裡，孩子們也可以參加足球主題繪畫活動。 We'll pick the best one at the end of the afternoon, so don't forget to put your name and contact details on the back. 我們會在下午結束時選出最佳作品，所以別忘了在背面寫上姓名和聯絡方式。 That way, if you've left the stadium before then, we'll send your prize, but sadly we can't return drawings. 這樣，如果你們那時已經離開球場，我們會把獎品寄給你；不過很遺憾，畫作無法退還。 I'd like to mention some features of the tour. 我想介紹一下這次導覽的一些特色。 We'll start with the three-sixty cinema experience, which has been very popular over the years, and then I'll take you to the players' dressing rooms before going outside to the seating area and the pitch. 我們會從 360 度影院體驗開始， 這項體驗多年來一直很受歡迎； 之後我會帶你們去球員更衣室， 然後再到外面的座位區和球場。 I should say, if you’d prefer your visit to be self-guided, please collect headphones from the reception and then you can listen to the pre-recorded information at your own speed. 我也要說明一下，如果你們比較喜歡自助導覽，可以到接待處領取耳機，然後按照自己的速度收聽預錄資訊。 We've only just introduced this feature, and would appreciate your feedback. 我們剛推出這項功能，所以很希望得到你們的回饋。 We're thinking of offering tours in other languages in future so if you have any thoughts on that, we'd welcome those too. 我們正在考慮未來提供其他語言的導覽，如果你們對此有任何想法，也歡迎提出。 If you plan to return another time, you might like to book one of our VIP tours – we've only just started offering these, and they can be booked online. 如果你們打算下次再來，也許可以預訂我們的 VIP 導覽——這是我們剛開始提供的服務，可以在線上預訂。 Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20. 在你聽接下來的演講之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 15 至 20 題。 Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20. 現在請聆聽並回答第 15 至 20 題。 Now, the stadium you see today was built in 1989, as part of a three-year redevelopment project – while that project was going on, the team had to play its matches at the ground of another club – apart from that, the club has been here on this site since 1870. 現在你們看到的這座球場建於 1989 年，是一項為期三年的重建工程的一部分。工程進行期間， 球隊不得不在另一家俱樂部的場地比賽；除此之外，這家俱樂部自 1870 年以來一直就在這個位置。 As some of you may know, that was the start of a really important decade in the history of football in this country. 你們有些人可能知道，那是這個國家足球史上一個非常重要十年的開始。 For example, 1870 was also the year that football teams started to include a player whose role it was to guard the goal. 例如，1870 年也是足球隊開始設置一名負責守門的球員的年份。 It's hard to imagine what the game must have been like without someone in that position, isn't it? 很難想像沒有這個位置的比賽會是什麼樣子，不是嗎？ In 1872 and 73, many other clubs were established, both here and abroad, and the following year, in 1874, referees were allowed to send players off if they committed certain offences. 在 1872 年和 1873 年，國內外成立了許多其他俱樂部；接下來的 1874 年，如果球員犯下某些違規行為，裁判可以將他們罰下場。 And also in that year, teams started having to swap ends at half-time. 同樣在那一年，球隊開始必須在中場休息時交換場地。 One fact I was interested to discover was that in early football games, the aim was for the scorer to get the ball between two flag posts, and later between sticks joined at the top with a piece of tape. 我覺得很有趣的一點是，在早期足球比賽中，得分的目標是把球踢進兩根旗桿之間；後來則是在兩根頂端用膠帶連起來的木杆之間。 In 1875, that tape was replaced with the solid crossbar that we're familiar with today. 到 1875 年，那條膠帶被我們今天熟悉的實心橫樑取代。 1877 saw the founding of further new clubs, and the history books tell us that in the same year, all the clubs decided to set a limit of ninety minutes for each match. 1877 年又有更多新俱樂部成立， 歷史書告訴我們，同年所有俱樂部決定把每場比賽時間限制為 90 分鐘。 Before that, it was a more casual arrangement, and this sometimes caused huge arguments – and sometimes fights – during matches, when one team called the end of the game and the other team wanted to play on to try and score a winning goal. 在那之前，比賽時間安排比較隨意，這有時會在比賽中引發激烈爭論，甚至打架；例如一隊宣布比賽結束，而另一隊想繼續比賽以爭取致勝進球。 By 1878, the number of teams in the football league increased again. 到 1878 年，足球聯賽中的球隊數量再次增加。 In addition, referees started using whistles, and electric lamps were installed on certain pitches. 此外，裁判開始使用哨子，有些球場也安裝了電燈。 This was a significant change, as games could then be played in the evenings all year round. 這是一項重大改變，因為這樣一來，全年晚上都可以進行比賽。 In 1880, clubs began to charge fans for admission to games, even though players were still amateurs and had other 'proper' jobs. 1880 年，俱樂部開始向球迷收取比賽入場費，雖然當時球員仍是業餘球員，並且有其他「正式」工作。 That's hard to imagine in the modern professional game where top players earn significant sums of money from both playing and commercial activities. 在現代職業足球中，頂級球員能從比賽和商業活動中賺取巨額收入，這一點很難想像。 That is the end of part two. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two. 第二部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第二部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 4
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21 and 22 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO benefits for children of learning to write did both students find surprising? A. improved fine motor skills B. improved memory C. improved concentration D. improved imagination E. improved spatial awareness Questions 23 and 24 Choose TWO letters, A–E. For children with dyspraxia, which TWO problems with handwriting do the students think are easiest to correct? A. not spacing letters correctly B. not writing in a straight line C. applying too much pressure when writing D. confusing letter shapes E. writing very slowly Questions 25–30 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Teaching handwriting 25. What does the woman say about using laptops to teach writing to children with dyslexia? A. Children often lack motivation to learn that way. B. Children become fluent relatively quickly. C. Children react more positively if they make a mistake. 26. When discussing whether to teach cursive or print writing, the woman thinks that A. cursive writing disadvantages a certain group of children. B. print writing is associated with lower academic performance. C. most teachers in the UK prefer a traditional approach to handwriting. 27. According to the students, what impact does poor handwriting have on exam performance? A. There is evidence to suggest grades are affected by poor handwriting. B. Neat handwriting is less important now than it used to be. C. Candidates write more slowly and produce shorter answers. 28. What prediction does the man make about the future of handwriting? A. Touch typing will be taught before writing by hand. B. Children will continue to learn to write by hand. C. People will dislike handwriting on digital devices. 29. The woman is concerned that relying on digital devices has made it difficult for her to A. take detailed notes. B. spell and punctuate. C. read old documents. 30. How do the students feel about their own handwriting? A. concerned they are unable to write quickly B. embarrassed by comments made about it C. regretful that they have lost the habit Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO benefits for children of learning to write did both students find surprising? improved fine motor skills improved memory improved concentration improved imagination improved spatial awareness Choose TWO letters, A–E. For children with dyspraxia, which TWO problems with handwriting do the students think are easiest to correct? not spacing letters correctly not writing in a straight line applying too much pressure when writing confusing letter shapes writing very slowly What does the woman say about using laptops to teach writing to children with dyslexia? Children often lack motivation to learn that way. Children become fluent relatively quickly. Children react more positively if they make a mistake. When discussing whether to teach cursive or print writing, the woman thinks that cursive writing disadvantages a certain group of children. print writing is associated with lower academic performance. most teachers in the UK prefer a traditional approach to handwriting. According to the students, what impact does poor handwriting have on exam performance? There is evidence to suggest grades are affected by poor handwriting. Neat handwriting is less important now than it used to be. Candidates write more slowly and produce shorter answers. What prediction does the man make about the future of handwriting? Touch typing will be taught before writing by hand. Children will continue to learn to write by hand. People will dislike handwriting on digital devices. The woman is concerned that relying on digital devices has made it difficult for her to take detailed notes. spell and punctuate. read old documents. How do the students feel about their own handwriting? concerned they are unable to write quickly embarrassed by comments made about it regretful that they have lost the habit You will hear two education students discussing an assignment on teaching handwriting to children. 你會聽到兩位教育系學生討論一項關於教孩子書寫的作業。 First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 21 至 24 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 21 至 24 題。 MAN: How are you getting on with the assignment on handwriting? 男士：你關於書寫的作業進行得怎麼樣？ WOMAN: Not too bad. You know, I hadn't realised that children benefit in so many ways from learning to write. 女士：還不錯。你知道嗎，我以前沒有意識到孩子學習書寫能有這麼多方面的好處。 It's such an important skill and yet most people think handwriting is less important than in the past because people hardly ever write by hand these days. 這是一項非常重要的技能，但大多數人認為手寫不如過去重要，因為現在人們幾乎不再手寫了。 MAN: Yes. And all the evidence suggests children should learn to write by hand before they learn to type. Not least because it helps their memory. 男士：是啊。而且所有證據都表明，孩子應該先學會手寫， 再學打字。這尤其是因為手寫有助於記憶。 WOMAN: That's right. The physical act of writing helps children to remember letters. 女士：沒錯。書寫這個身體動作能幫助孩子記住字母。 That seems pretty obvious when you think about it. 仔細想想，這似乎很明顯。 MAN: What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration. 男士：比較不明顯的是，它如何幫助培養專注力。 They have to sit still and focus on one thing. 他們必須坐好，專注在一件事上。 WOMAN: Yeah. That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before. 女士：是啊。我以前從沒想過手寫的這一面。 MAN: Same here. I'm not sure I understand how it improves children's imagination though. 男士：我也是。不過我不太確定自己是否理解它怎麼提升孩子的想像力。 WOMAN: Well, there was that study which showed that primary aged children generated more ideas when they were writing by hand than using a keyboard. I would've guessed that would be the case. 女士：嗯，有一項研究顯示，小學年齡的孩子手寫時，比使用鍵盤時能產生更多想法。我本來就猜會是這樣。 MAN: Mmm, yeah. I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either. 男士：嗯，是啊。我以前也從沒把空間感和手寫聯想到一起。 I thought spatial awareness was more to do with knowing where you are in relation to objects or other people. 我以為空間感更多是指知道自己相對於物體或他人的位置。 WOMAN: I thought that too. But good spatial awareness is essential for writing because you have to space words correctly. 女士：我也這麼以為。但良好的空間感對書寫很重要，因為你必須正確安排單字之間的距離。 It's not just fine motor skills that improve through writing as I'd always assumed. 書寫能提升的不只是我一直以為的精細動作能力。 MAN: Handwriting is so much harder for children with dyspraxia, who have problems coordinating movement. 男士：對於有動作協調障礙的孩子來說，手寫困難得多，因為他們在協調動作方面有問題。 It's good there are lots of things you can do in the classroom to help them. 好在課堂上有很多方法可以幫助他們。 They need so much more support with letter formation – you need to play lots of games to help them distinguish letter shapes. It takes a lot of patience. 他們在字母成形方面需要更多支持——你需要透過很多遊戲幫助他們區分字母形狀。這需要很大的耐心。 WOMAN: Yeah. I liked the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard. 女士：是啊。我很喜歡那種如果用力過大就會亮起來的筆。 That seems like a really simple solution. 這看起來是個非常簡單的解決辦法。 MAN: Yes, absolutely. I'm not sure there's much you can do about children with dyspraxia writing very slowly. 男士：是的，完全同意。至於有動作協調障礙的孩子寫得很慢，我不確定能做什麼。 It's more important to focus on accuracy and as they get more confident I think they eventually speed up. 更重要的是先注重準確性；等他們更有信心後，我想最終速度會提高。 WOMAN: One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper. 女士：有一個相當簡單的方法，就是使用方格紙。 So they write each letter in a box and that trains them to space the letters correctly. 讓他們把每個字母寫在一個格子裡，這樣可以訓練他們正確安排字母間距。 MAN: Indeed, that's more important for legibility than trying to get them to write in a straight line. 男士：確實，這比試著讓他們寫成一直線更能提升可讀性。 Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30. 在你聽接下來的討論之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 25 至 30 題。 Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30. 現在請聆聽並回答第 25 至 30 題。 MAN: For some children it might be better to teach them to write on a laptop rather than by hand. 男士：對某些孩子來說，教他們用筆電寫作可能比手寫更好。 Like children with dyslexia. They often really struggle with handwriting and some just give up. 例如有閱讀障礙的孩子。他們常常在手寫方面非常吃力，有些甚至直接放棄。 WOMAN: Yeah. It's not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong – on a keyboard they can be more willing to have a go. 女士：是啊。如果寫錯了，他們不會那麼沮喪——用鍵盤時， 他們可能更願意嘗試。 But I read that developing fluency isn't any faster. 但我讀到過，這樣培養流暢度並不會更快。 MAN: That's right. Did you read that article on the benefits of teaching print rather than cursive handwriting, where the letters are joined up? 男士：沒錯。你有讀那篇關於教印刷體而不是草寫體的文章嗎？草寫體就是字母連在一起的那種。 WOMAN: Yes. Well in the past cursive writing was certainly considered more stylish and educated. 女士：有。以前草寫確實被認為更有風格，也更有教養。 But not anymore. Teachers' attitudes have changed because it's been proved that cursive is more difficult to learn – especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging. 但現在不是了。教師的態度已經改變，因為事實證明草寫更難學——尤其是對有學習困難的孩子來說，把字母連起來非常有挑戰性。 MAN: I agree. I was always worried that my poor handwriting affected my exam results. 男士：我同意。我以前一直擔心自己糟糕的字跡會影響考試成績。 And now research shows that I was right to worry. 現在研究顯示，我的擔心是有道理的。 I'm sure a lot of students think it's unfair that they're being judged on their handwriting not just their knowledge. 我相信很多學生都覺得，考試不只評估知識，還評估字跡， 這很不公平。 WOMAN: Marks are definitely affected if examiners can't read the script. 女士：如果考官看不懂答卷， 分數肯定會受到影響。 That's why it's always been so important to teach children to write legibly… 這就是為什麼教孩子寫得清楚易讀一直都很重要…… Do you think the role of handwriting will change in the future? 你覺得手寫在未來的作用會改變嗎？ MAN: I can't see that changing much. 男士：我看不出會有太大變化。 Touch typing still isn't taught in most schools, which is a shame. 大多數學校仍然沒有教觸控打字，這很可惜。 But maybe that won't be necessary in the future because people will also be able to write by hand on digital devices. Anyway, teachers understand the value of handwriting. It's a basic life skill. 但也許未來這不會那麼必要， 因為人們也能在數位裝置上手寫。不管怎樣，老師們理解手寫的價值。它是一項基本生活技能。 WOMAN: True. However, the fact is that people are writing by hand less and less and relying on digital devices. That does cause some problems. 女士：沒錯。不過事實是，人們越來越少手寫，越來越依賴數位裝置。這確實造成了一些問題。 MAN: You mean like note taking? There are lots of apps for that. 男士：你是指像記筆記嗎？有很多應用程式可以做這個。 WOMAN: And for reading historical documents apparently. 女士：顯然也有用來閱讀歷史文件的。 But my mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent. 但我媽媽對我糟糕的拼字和非常不一致的標點使用感到震驚。 I think you can put that down to lack of practice. 我想這可以歸因於缺乏練習。 MAN: I expect so. Personally, I miss writing by hand. I hardly ever write anything now. 男士：我想是這樣。就我個人而言，我很懷念手寫。我現在幾乎不寫任何東西了。 I remember my grandparents had such beautiful handwriting and it was so individual. 我記得我的祖父母字寫得非常漂亮，而且很有個人特色。 Nobody I know would be able to identify my handwriting now. It's a shame. 現在我認識的人大概沒有人能認出我的字跡了。真可惜。 WOMAN: I know. I feel the same way. 女士：我知道。我也有同感。 I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally. 我以前手寫日記，現在則用數位方式寫。 It just seems less effort to do it that way. So it's not just a problem… 那樣似乎比較省力。所以這不只是個問題…… That is the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three. 第三部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第三部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 4
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Research in the Area Around the Chembe Bird Sanctuary The importance of birds of prey to the local communities ● They destroy 31 __________ and other rodents. ● They help to prevent farmers from being bitten by 32 __________. ● They have been an important part of the local culture for many years. ● They now support the economy by encouraging 33 __________ in the area. Falling numbers of birds of prey ● The birds may be accidentally killed: ○ by 34 __________ when they are hunting or sleeping ○ by electrocution from contact with power lines, especially at times when there is a lot of 35 __________ ● Local farmers may illegally shoot them or 36 __________ them. Ways of protecting chickens from birds of prey ● clearing away vegetation from the area, unhelpful ● providing a 37 __________ for chickens, expensive ● frightening birds of prey by: ○ keeping a 38 __________ ○ making a 39 __________, e.g. with metal objects ● A 40 __________ of methods is usually most effective. ● They destroy 31 __________ and other rodents. ● They help to prevent farmers from being bitten by 32 __________. ● They now support the economy by encouraging 33 __________ in the ○ by 34 __________ when they are hunting or sleeping when there is a lot of 35 __________ ● Local farmers may illegally shoot them or 36 __________ them. ● providing a 37 __________ for chickens, expensive ○ keeping a 38 __________ ○ making a 39 __________, e.g. with metal objects ● A 40 __________ of methods is usually most effective. You will hear part of an environmental science lecture about the impact of birds of prey on a farming community in Africa. 你會聽到一段環境科學講座，內容是關於猛禽對非洲一個農業社群的影響。 First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 31 至 40 題。 Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40. 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 31 至 40 題。 We've been looking at different types of conflicts that may arise between wildlife and humans at the boundaries of protected areas such as national parks and animal sanctuaries. 我們一直在研究野生動物與人類在保護區邊界可能產生的不同衝突，例如國家公園和動物保護區。 I'd like to illustrate this by telling you about some research that I've been involved in recently in the central African country of Zambia in the area around the Chembe Bird Sanctuary, which contains over three hundred of the listed birds of Zambia. 我想透過我最近參與的一項研究來說明這一點。這項研究位於中非國家尚比亞的 Chembe Bird Sanctuary 周邊地區，該保護區包含超過 300 種尚比亞列名鳥類。 These include a number of birds of prey, such as eagles, hawks and owls, that live by hunting and killing other birds and animals. 其中包括一些猛禽，例如鷹、隼和貓頭鷹，牠們以捕獵其他鳥類和動物為生。 Now, most of the people living in the local communities near to the bird sanctuary are small-scale farmers, and these birds of prey provide important social and ecological benefits to them. 現在，住在鳥類保護區附近社區的大多數人都是小規模農民，而這些猛禽為他們提供了重要的社會和生態益處。 For example, a lot of damage can be caused to farmers' crops by rodents such as rats, which would consume the crops as they grow in the fields as well as after harvesting if they weren't hunted and killed by the birds. 例如，像老鼠這樣的囓齒動物會對農民的作物造成大量損害；如果沒有被鳥類捕食，牠們會在作物生長期間以及收成後吃掉作物。 And the predatory habits of these birds also protect farmers in other ways. 這些鳥類的捕食習性也在其他方面保護農民。 For example, a major danger to rural workers is snakes, whose bite may be dangerous or even fatal, and birds of prey have a major role in keeping their populations under control. 例如，蛇是農村工作者面臨的一大危險，蛇咬傷可能很危險，甚至致命；而猛禽在控制蛇的數量方面發揮了重要作用。 Local people have always been aware of these benefits and for years, even before the sanctuary was opened in 1973, the birds played a key role in the culture of the region. 當地人一直知道這些好處。 多年來，甚至在保護區於 1973 年開放之前，這些鳥類就在該地區文化中扮演關鍵角色。 However, more recently, the sanctuary and its birds have also become increasingly important to the community in economic terms, because at present, after a relatively slow start, tourism has become an important source of revenue for them. 然而，近年來，這個保護區及其鳥類在經濟層面上對社區也越來越重要，因為目前在起步較慢之後，旅遊業已經成為他們重要的收入來源。 However, although these birds of prey are protected by the government, their numbers are falling. 然而，雖然這些猛禽受到政府保護，牠們的數量卻正在下降。 Some of these deaths are accidental. Fatalities occur when birds alight on roads to catch and eat their prey, and are hit by fast-moving traffic. 其中一些死亡是意外造成的。當鳥類降落在道路上捕捉並食用獵物時，可能會被高速行駛的車輛撞死。 Drivers in Zambia have to take special care at night, as birds may regard the quieter roads as safe places to sleep. 尚比亞的駕駛人在夜間必須特別小心，因為鳥類可能把較安靜的道路視為安全的睡覺地點。 Accidental deaths may also occur if these birds fly close to high-voltage power lines, as they may be electrocuted. 如果這些鳥飛近高壓電線， 也可能發生意外死亡，因為牠們可能會觸電。 This is a particular danger in the heavy rain which can occur in the region in the months from December to April. 這在該地區 12 月至 4 月可能出現的大雨期間尤其危險。 And local farmers also pose a threat to these birds. 當地農民也對這些鳥類構成威脅。 As well as growing crops, small-scale farmers in the area also rear chickens. 除了種植作物外，當地小規模農民也飼養雞。 These provide food for the farmers' families, as well as being an important source of income. 這些雞既為農民家庭提供食物，也是重要的收入來源。 But they're also an easy target for birds of prey, and so farmers may shoot these birds, which is illegal but understandable, or they may poison the birds, which again is illegal and can have negative effects on the ecosystem. 但雞也很容易成為猛禽的獵物，因此農民可能會射殺這些鳥，雖然這是非法的，但可以理解；或者他們可能會毒殺鳥類，這同樣非法，並且可能對生態系統造成負面影響。 So how else can farmers protect their chickens from birds of prey? 那麼，農民還能如何保護雞不受猛禽攻擊呢？ Some people believe that to prevent the predators from settling near the area where the chickens are kept it's best to keep this area free from vegetation. 有些人認為，為了防止捕食者停留在養雞區附近，最好清除該區域的植被。 But in fact this is counter-productive as it means the chickens have no cover to hide in and they'll be easier for the birds to see. 但事實上，這樣做適得其反，因為雞沒有遮蔽物可以躲藏，反而更容易被鳥類看到。 Another possibility would be to prevent the chickens from going outside at all, and to keep them safe from predators inside a building, but this would cost far too much to be a practical solution. 另一種可能是完全不讓雞到戶外，而是把牠們關在建築物裡以避免被捕食者攻擊， 但這成本太高，無法成為實際可行的解決方案。 Nearly all the farmers reported that they spent a lot of time and effort trying to frighten off the birds of prey without actually harming them. 幾乎所有農民都表示，他們花了很多時間和精力試圖嚇走猛禽，而不是實際傷害牠們。 Most of the farmers had at least one dog, and said this was a big help at scaring away the predators. 大多數農民至少養了一條狗，並說這對嚇走捕食者很有幫助。 Some of the farmers also reported that during the breeding season, when the chickens were particularly vulnerable, they encouraged their children to watch over the chickens and to hit pans with a metal spoon so that the resulting noise would succeed in driving away birds that were trying to seize the young chicks. 一些農民也表示，在繁殖季節，小雞特別脆弱時，他們會鼓勵孩子看顧雞群，並用金屬湯匙敲打鍋子，讓產生的噪音趕走試圖抓走小雞的鳥類。 None of these methods was a hundred per cent effective, so as a result, the village people told us that rather than just using one method, they were forced to use a combination for them to have any effect. 這些方法沒有一種百分之百有效，因此村民告訴我們， 他們不能只用一種方法，而是必須結合多種方法才會有效。 And even so, these birds of prey remain a major threat to the chickens' survival and cause considerable economic loss to farmers. 即便如此，這些猛禽仍然是雞群生存的一大威脅，並給農民造成相當大的經濟損失。 So we looked at the possibility of a longer-term solution to ... 因此，我們開始研究是否有可能找到更長期的解決方案 …… That is the end of part four. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part four. 第四部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第四部分的答案。

entries.title: Listening Practice 5
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Hinchingbrooke Country Park The park ● Area: 1 __________ hectares ● Habitats: wetland, grassland and woodland ● Wetland: lakes, ponds and a 2 __________ ● Wildlife includes birds, insects and animals Subjects studied in educational visits include ● Science: Children look at 3 __________ about plants, etc. ● Geography: includes learning to use a 4 __________ and compass ● History: changes in land use ● Leisure and tourism: mostly concentrates on the park's 5 __________ ● Music: Children make 6 __________ with natural materials, and experiment with rhythm and speed. Benefits of outdoor educational visits ● They give children a feeling of 7 __________ that they may not have elsewhere. ● Children learn new 8 __________ and gain self-confidence. Practical issues ● Cost per child: £9 __________ ● Adults, such as 10 __________, free ● Area: 1 __________ hectares ● Wetland: lakes, ponds and a 2 __________ ● Science: Children look at 3 __________ about plants, etc. ● Geography: includes learning to use a 4 __________ and compass ● Leisure and tourism: mostly concentrates on the park's 5 __________ ● Music: Children make 6 __________ with natural materials, and experiment ● They give children a feeling of 7 __________ that they may not have elsewhere. ● Children learn new 8 __________ and gain self-confidence. ● Cost per child: £9 __________ ● Adults, such as 10 __________, free SALLY: Good morning. Hinchingbrooke Country Park, Sally speaking. I'm one of the rangers. Sally：早安。這裡是 Hinchingbrooke Country Park，我是 Sally。我是這裡的巡護員之一。 JOHN: Oh hello. My name's John Chapman, and I'm a teaching assistant at a local primary school. John：哦，你好。我叫 John Chapman，是當地一所小學的助教。 I've been asked to arrange a visit to the park for two of our classes. 我被安排為我們學校的兩個班級籌劃一次公園參觀活動。 SALLY: OK. What would you like to know? Sally：好的。你想了解什麼呢？ JOHN: Well, I'm new to this area, so perhaps you could tell me something about the park first, please. John：嗯，我剛來這個地區，所以也許你可以先跟我介紹一下這個公園。 SALLY: Of course. Altogether the park covers 170 acres, that's 69 hectares. Sally：當然可以。整個公園占地 170 英畝，也就是 69 公頃。 There are three main types of habitat: wetland, grassland and woodland. 這裡主要有三種棲地：濕地、草地和林地。 The woods are well established and varied, with an oak plantation, and other areas of mixed species. 這裡的林地已經相當成熟，而且種類多樣，包括一片橡樹林，以及其他混合樹種區域。 JOHN: Right. John：好的。 SALLY: The wetland is quite varied, too. Sally：濕地也相當多樣。 The original farmland was dug up around 40 years ago to extract gravel. 大約 40 年前，原本的農地被挖開， 用來開採礫石。 Once this work was completed, the gravel pits filled with water, forming the two large lakes. 這項工程完成後，礫石坑積滿了水，形成了兩個大湖。 There are also several smaller ones, ponds and a stream that flows through the park. 這裡還有幾個較小的湖、池塘，以及一條流經公園的小溪。 JOHN: OK, so I suppose with these different habitats there's quite a variety of wildlife. John：好的，我想有了這些不同棲地，野生動植物種類應該相當豐富。 SALLY: There certainly is – a lot of different species of birds and insects, and also animals like deer and rabbits. Sally：確實如此——這裡有很多不同種類的鳥類和昆蟲，也有像鹿和兔子這樣的動物。 JOHN: And I understand you organise educational visits for school parties. John：我知道你們也會為學校團體安排教育參觀活動。 SALLY: That's right. We can organise a wide range of activities and adapt them to suit all ages. Sally：沒錯。我們可以安排各式各樣的活動，並根據不同年齡層進行調整。 JOHN: Can you give me some examples of the activities? John：你能舉幾個活動例子嗎？ SALLY: Well, one focus is on science, where we help children to discover and study plants, trees and insects. Sally：嗯，其中一個重點是科學，我們會幫助孩子發現並研究植物、樹木和昆蟲。 They also collect and analyse data about the things they see. 他們也會收集並分析自己所觀察到的資料。 JOHN: Uhuh. John：嗯。 SALLY: Another focus is on geography. Sally：另一個重點是地理。 The park is a great environment to learn and practise reading a map and using a compass to navigate around the park. 這個公園是學習和練習看地圖、使用指南針在公園中導航的絕佳環境。 JOHN: Do you do anything connected with history? John：你們有安排和歷史相關的活動嗎？ SALLY: Yes, we do. For instance, the children can explore how the use of the land has changed over time. Then there's leisure and tourism. Sally：有的。例如，孩子們可以探索土地用途如何隨時間改變。還有休閒與旅遊方面的內容。 JOHN: That focuses on your visitors, I would imagine. John：我想那主要是關於公園遊客的吧。 SALLY: Yes, mostly. The children find out about them, their requirements, the problems they may cause and how we manage these. Sally：是的，大多如此。孩子們會了解遊客、他們的需求、他們可能造成的問題，以及我們如何管理這些情況。 And another subject we cover is music: here the children experiment with natural materials to create sounds and explore rhythm and tempo. 我們涵蓋的另一個主題是音樂：孩子們會嘗試用天然材料創造聲音， 並探索節奏和速度。 JOHN: That must be fun! John：那一定很有趣！ SALLY: Most children really enjoy it. Sally：大多數孩子都非常喜歡。 SALLY: And of course, all the activities are educational, too. Sally：當然，所有活動也都具有教育意義。 Learning outside the classroom encourages children to be creative, and to explore and discover for themselves. 課堂外學習能鼓勵孩子發揮創意， 並親自探索和發現。 JOHN: I would imagine they get a sense of freedom that might not be a normal part of their lives. John：我想他們會感受到一種自由感，而這可能不是他們日常生活中常有的體驗。 SALLY: That's right. And very often the children discover that they can do things they didn't know they could do, and they develop new skills. Sally：沒錯。而且孩子們常常會發現自己能做到以前不知道自己能做的事，並發展出新的技能。 This gives them greater self-confidence. 這會讓他們更有自信。 JOHN: It sounds great. So, what about the practical side of it? John：聽起來很棒。那實際安排方面呢？ How much does it cost for a full-day visit? We would expect to bring between 30 and 40 children. 全天參觀的費用是多少？我們預計會帶 30 到 40 名孩子。 SALLY: If there are over 30, it costs £4.95 for each child who attends on the day. Sally：如果人數超過 30 人，當天每位參加的孩子收費 4.95 英鎊。 We invoice you afterwards, so you don't pay for children who can't come because of sickness, for example. 我們會在活動後開立發票，所以如果有孩子因病無法參加，你們不需要為他們付費。 There's no charge for leaders and other adults – as many as you want to bring. 領隊和其他成年人免費——你們想帶多少都可以。 JOHN: That sounds very fair. Well, thanks for all the information. John：這聽起來很合理。好的，謝謝你提供這些資訊。 I'll need to discuss it with my colleagues, and I hope to get back to you soon to make a booking. 我需要和同事討論一下，希望很快能回覆你並預訂。 SALLY: We'll look forward to hearing from you. Goodbye. Sally：期待你的回覆。再見。 JOHN: Goodbye, and thank you. John：再見，謝謝你。

entries.title: Listening Practice 5
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–15 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Stanthorpe Twinning Association 11. During the visit to Malatte, in France, members especially enjoyed A. going to a theme park. B. experiencing a river trip. C. visiting a cheese factory. 12. What will happen in Stanthorpe to mark the 25th anniversary of the Twinning Association? A. A tree will be planted. B. A garden seat will be bought. C. A footbridge will be built. 13. Which event raised most funds this year? A. the film show B. the pancake evening C. the cookery demonstration 14. For the first evening with the French visitors host families are advised to A. take them for a walk round the town. B. go to a local restaurant. C. have a meal at home. 15. On Saturday evening there will be the chance to A. listen to a concert. B. watch a match. C. take part in a competition. Questions 16–20 Label the map below. Write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 16–20. 16. Farm shop __________ 17. Disabled entry __________ 18. Adventure playground __________ 19. Kitchen gardens __________ 20. The Temple of the Four Winds __________ Practice 5, source question diagram/table, PDF page 8 During the visit to Malatte, in France, members especially enjoyed going to a theme park. experiencing a river trip. visiting a cheese factory. What will happen in Stanthorpe to mark the 25th anniversary of the Twinning Association? A tree will be planted. A garden seat will be bought. A footbridge will be built. Which event raised most funds this year? the film show the pancake evening the cookery demonstration For the first evening with the French visitors host families are advised to take them for a walk round the town. go to a local restaurant. have a meal at home. On Saturday evening there will be the chance to listen to a concert. watch a match. take part in a competition. Farm shop A B C D E F G H I Disabled entry A B C D E F G H I Adventure playground A B C D E F G H I Kitchen gardens A B C D E F G H I The Temple of the Four Winds A B C D E F G H I It's great to see so many members of the Twinning Association here tonight. 很高興今晚看到這麼多友好城鎮協會的成員在場。 Since the twinning link between our two towns, Stanthorpe here in England and Malatte in France, was established, the relationship between the towns has gone from strength to strength. 自從我們英格蘭的 Stanthorpe 和法國的 Malatte 建立友好城鎮關係以來，兩鎮之間的關係越來越密切。 Last month, 25 members of the association from Stanthorpe spent a weekend in Malatte. 上個月，來自 Stanthorpe 的 25 名協會成員在 Malatte 度過了一個週末。 Our hosts had arranged a great programme. 我們的接待方安排了很棒的活動。 We learned how cheese is produced in the region and had the chance to taste the products. 我們了解了該地區起司的製作方式，並有機會品嚐這些產品。 The theme park trip had to be cancelled, but we all had a great time on the final boat trip down the river – that was the real highlight. 主題公園之旅不得不取消，但最後的河上乘船之旅讓大家都玩得很開心——那才是真正的亮點。 This is a special year for the Association because it's 25 years since we were founded. 今年對協會來說很特別，因為今年是我們成立 25 週年。 In Malatte, they're planning to mark this by building a footbridge in the municipal park. 在 Malatte，他們計畫在市政公園建造一座人行橋來紀念這個日子。 We've been discussing what to do here and we've decided to plant a poplar tree in the museum gardens. 我們一直在討論這裡該做什麼，最後決定在博物館花園裡種一棵白楊樹。 We considered buying a garden seat to put there, but the authorities weren't happy with that idea. 我們曾考慮買一張花園長椅放在那裡，但主管單位不太贊成這個想法。 In terms of fundraising to support our activities, we've done very well. Our pancake evening was well attended and made record profits. 在為活動籌款方面，我們做得非常好。煎餅晚會出席人數很多，而且收益創下紀錄。 And everyone enjoyed the demonstration of French cookery, which was nearly as successful. 大家也很喜歡法式料理示範， 這項活動也幾乎同樣成功。 Numbers for our film show were limited because of the venue so we're looking for somewhere bigger next year. 由於場地限制，我們的電影放映活動人數有限，所以明年我們會尋找更大的場地。 We're looking forward to welcoming our French visitors here next week, and I know that many of you here will be hosting individuals or families. 我們期待下週在這裡迎接法國訪客，我也知道在座許多人會接待個人或家庭。 The coach from France will arrive at 5 pm on Friday. 來自法國的長途巴士會在星期五下午 5 點抵達。 Don't try to do too much that first evening as they'll be tired, so have dinner in the house or garden rather than eating out. 第一晚不要安排太多活動，因為他們會很累，所以建議在家裡或花園吃晚餐，而不是外出用餐。 The weather looks as if it'll be OK so you might like to plan a barbecue. 天氣看起來應該不錯，所以你們也許可以安排烤肉。 Then the next morning's market day in town, and that's always a good place to stroll round. 第二天早上鎮上有市集，那一直是很適合散步逛逛的地方。 On Saturday evening, we'll all meet up at the football club, where once again we'll have Toby Sharp and his band performing English and Scottish country songs. 星期六晚上，我們會在足球俱樂部集合，到時 Toby Sharp 和他的樂團會再次演唱英格蘭和蘇格蘭鄉村歌曲。 Toby will already be well known to many of you as last year he organised our special quiz night and presented the prizes. 很多人應該已經很熟悉 Toby， 因為去年他組織了我們的特別問答之夜並頒發獎品。 Now on Sunday, we'll be taking our visitors to Farley House. You may not all be familiar with it, so here's a map to help you. 星期天，我們會帶訪客去 Farley House。你們可能不是所有人都熟悉那裡，所以這裡有一張地圖可以幫助你們。 You can see the car park at the bottom of the map. 你可以在地圖底部看到停車場。 There's an excellent farm shop in the grounds where our visitors can buy local produce – it's in the old stables, which is the first building you come to. 園區內有一家很棒的農場商店，訪客可以在那裡購買本地農產品——它位於舊馬廄裡，也就是你首先會看到的建築。 They're built round a courtyard, and the shop's in the far corner on the left. There's also a small café on the right as you go in. 這些建築圍繞著一個庭院而建，商店在左側最遠的角落。進去後右手邊還有一家小咖啡館。 I know that one or two of our visitors may not be all that mobile. 我知道我們有一兩位訪客行動可能不太方便。 The main entrance to the house has a lot of steps so you might want to use the disabled entry. This is on the far side of the house from the car park. 房子的正門有很多台階，所以你們可能會想使用無障礙入口。它位於房子遠離停車場的另一側。 Children will probably be most interested in the adventure playground. 孩子們可能最感興趣的是冒險遊樂場。 That's at the northern end of the larger lake, in a bend on the path that leads to the lake. There's lots for children to do there. 它在較大湖泊的北端，位於通往湖邊小路的一個彎道處。那裡有很多適合孩子玩的設施。 There are a number of lovely gardens near the house. 房子附近有幾座漂亮的花園。 The kitchen gardens are rectangular and surrounded by a wall. 廚房花園呈長方形，四周有牆圍繞。 They're to the north-east of the house, quite near the smaller lake. They're still in use and have a great collection of fruit and vegetables. 它們位於房子的東北方，離較小的湖很近。這些花園仍在使用，裡面種有許多水果和蔬菜。 The Temple of the Four Winds is a bit more of a walk – but it's worth it. The Temple of the Four Winds 要多走一段路，但很值得。 Take the path from the car park and go past the western sides of the stables and the house. 從停車場沿著小路走，經過馬廄和房子的西側。 Then when the path forks, take the right-hand path. Go up there with the woods on your left and the temple is right at the end. 然後在小路分岔處走右邊那條路。往上走時，樹林會在你的左手邊，而神殿就在路的盡頭。 There are great views over the whole area. 從那裡可以俯瞰整個區域，景色非常好。 OK, so that's… 好的，那麼……

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21 and 22 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO things did Colin find most satisfying about his bread reuse project? A. receiving support from local restaurants B. finding a good way to prevent waste C. overcoming problems in a basic process D. experimenting with designs and colours E. learning how to apply 3-D printing Questions 23 and 24 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO ways do the students agree that touch-sensitive sensors for food labels could be developed in future? A. for use on medical products B. to show that food is no longer fit to eat C. for use with drinks as well as foods D. to provide applications for blind people E. to indicate the weight of certain foods Questions 25–30 What is the students' opinion about each of the following food trends? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 25–30. Opinions A. This is only relevant to young people. B. This may have disappointing results. C. This already seems to be widespread. D. Retailers should do more to encourage this. E. More financial support is needed for this. F. Most people know little about this. G. There should be stricter regulations about this. H. This could be dangerous. Food trends 25. Use of local products __________ 26. Reduction in unnecessary packaging __________ 27. Gluten-free and lactose-free food __________ 28. Use of branded products related to celebrity chefs __________ 29. Development of ‘ghost kitchens’ for takeaway food __________ 30. Which TWO things did Colin find most satisfying about his bread reuse project? receiving support from local restaurants finding a good way to prevent waste overcoming problems in a basic process experimenting with designs and colours learning how to apply 3-D printing Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO ways do the students agree that touch-sensitive sensors for food labels could be developed in future? for use on medical products to show that food is no longer fit to eat for use with drinks as well as foods to provide applications for blind people to indicate the weight of certain foods Use of local products This is only relevant to young people. This may have disappointing results. This already seems to be widespread. Retailers should do more to encourage this. More financial support is needed for this. Most people know little about this. There should be stricter regulations about this. This could be dangerous. Reduction in unnecessary packaging This is only relevant to young people. This may have disappointing results. This already seems to be widespread. Retailers should do more to encourage this. More financial support is needed for this. Most people know little about this. There should be stricter regulations about this. This could be dangerous. Gluten-free and lactose-free food This is only relevant to young people. This may have disappointing results. This already seems to be widespread. Retailers should do more to encourage this. More financial support is needed for this. Most people know little about this. There should be stricter regulations about this. This could be dangerous. Use of branded products related to celebrity chefs This is only relevant to young people. This may have disappointing results. This already seems to be widespread. Retailers should do more to encourage this. More financial support is needed for this. Most people know little about this. There should be stricter regulations about this. This could be dangerous. Development of ‘ghost kitchens’ for takeaway food This is only relevant to young people. This may have disappointing results. This already seems to be widespread. Retailers should do more to encourage this. More financial support is needed for this. Most people know little about this. There should be stricter regulations about this. This could be dangerous. Use of mushrooms for common health concerns This is only relevant to young people. This may have disappointing results. This already seems to be widespread. Retailers should do more to encourage this. More financial support is needed for this. Most people know little about this. There should be stricter regulations about this. This could be dangerous. COLIN: I haven't seen you for a bit, Marie. Colin：我有一陣子沒見到你了， Marie。 MARIE: No. I've been busy with my project. Marie：是啊。我一直在忙我的專題。 COLIN: You're making a vegan alternative to eggs, aren't you? Something that doesn't use animal products? Colin：你是在做純素雞蛋替代品，對吧？就是不使用動物產品的東西？ MARIE: Yes. I'm using chickpeas. I had two main aims when I first started looking for an alternative to eggs, but actually I've found chickpeas have got more advantages. Marie：是的。我用的是鷹嘴豆。 我一開始尋找雞蛋替代品時有兩個主要目標，但其實我發現鷹嘴豆有更多優點。 COLIN: Right. Colin：明白。 MARIE: But how about your project on reusing waste food – you were looking at bread, weren't you? Marie：那你關於廚餘再利用的專題怎麼樣？你研究的是麵包， 對吧？ COLIN: Yes. It's been hard work, but I've enjoyed it. Colin：是的。過程很辛苦，但我很享受。 The basic process was quite straightforward – breaking the stale bread down to a paste then reforming it. 基本流程相當簡單——把變乾的麵包打成糊狀，然後重新塑形。 MARIE: But you were using 3-D printing, weren't you, to make the paste into biscuits? Marie：但你是用 3D 列印把糊狀物做成餅乾，對吧？ COLIN: Yeah, I'd used that before, but in this project, I had time to play around with different patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a more appetising colour, and I was really pleased with what I managed to produce. Colin：是的，我以前用過 3D 列印。不過在這個專題裡，我有時間嘗試不同的餅乾圖案，也研究如何加入水果和蔬菜，讓顏色看起來更有食慾。我對自己做出來的成品真的很滿意。 MARIE: It must've been a great feeling to make something appetising out of bits of old bread that would've been thrown away otherwise. Marie：能把原本可能被丟掉的舊麵包做成看起來美味的東西， 那感覺一定很棒。 COLIN: It was. And I'm hoping that some of the restaurants in town will be interested in the biscuits. I'm going to send them some samples. Colin：確實是。我也希望鎮上一些餐廳會對這些餅乾感興趣。我打算寄一些樣品給他們。 MARIE: I came across something on the internet yesterday that might interest you. It was a company that's developed touch-sensitive sensors for food labels. Marie：我昨天在網路上看到一個你可能會感興趣的東西。有家公司開發了用於食品標籤的觸覺感應器。 COLIN: Mmm? Colin：嗯？ MARIE: It's a special sort of label on the food package. When the label's smooth, the food is fresh and then when you can feel bumps on the label that means the food's gone bad. Marie：那是食品包裝上的一種特殊標籤。當標籤是光滑的，表示食物是新鮮的；如果你摸到標籤上有凸起，就表示食物已經變質。 It started off as a project to help visually impaired people know whether food was fit to eat or not. 它最初是一個幫助視障人士判斷食物是否還能食用的專案。 COLIN: Interesting. So just solid food? Colin：有意思。所以只用在固體食物上嗎？ MARIE: No, things like milk and juice as well. But actually, I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and pharmacies. Marie：不是，也包括牛奶和果汁之類的東西。不過其實我覺得它也很適合用於醫院和藥房的藥品儲存。 COLIN: Right. And coming back to food, maybe it'd be possible to use it for other things besides freshness. Like how many kilograms a joint of meat is, for example. Colin：對。回到食品方面，也許除了新鮮度之外，它還能用於其他資訊。比如一塊肉有多少公斤。 MARIE: Yes, there's all sorts of possibilities. Marie：是的，有各種可能性。 COLIN: I was reading an article about food trends predicting how eating habits might change in the next few years. Colin：我讀了一篇關於食品趨勢的文章，預測未來幾年飲食習慣可能會如何改變。 MARIE: Oh – things like more focus on local products? That seems so obvious, but the shops are still full of imported foods. Marie：哦——比如更重視本地產品嗎？這聽起來很明顯，但商店裡還是充滿了進口食品。 COLIN: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that. Colin：是的，商家需要更積極地處理這個問題。 MARIE: And somehow motivate consumers to change, yes. Marie：是的，也需要想辦法促使消費者改變。 COLIN: One thing everyone's aware of is the need for a reduction in unnecessary packaging – but just about everything you buy in supermarkets is still covered in plastic. The government needs to do something about it. Colin：大家都知道的一件事是， 需要減少不必要的包裝——但你在超市買到的幾乎所有東西仍然都包著塑膠。政府需要採取行動。 MARIE: Absolutely. It's got to change. Marie：完全同意。這一定要改變。 COLIN: Do you think there'll be more interest in gluten- and lactose-free food? Colin：你覺得人們會對無麩質和無乳糖食品更感興趣嗎？ MARIE: For people with allergies or food intolerances? I don't know. Marie：給有過敏或食物不耐症的人嗎？我不確定。 Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now. 我認識的很多人已經買這類食品很多年了。 COLIN: Yes, even if they haven't been diagnosed with an allergy. Colin：是啊，即使他們沒有被診斷出過敏。 MARIE: That's right. One thing I've noticed is the number of branded products related to celebrity chefs – people watch them cooking on TV and then buy things like spice mixes or frozen foods with the chef's name on . . . I bought something like that once, but I won't again. Marie：沒錯。我注意到的一件事是，和名廚相關的品牌產品越來越多——人們在電視上看他們做菜，然後購買印有那位廚師名字的調味料或冷凍食品……我曾經買過一次那種東西，但不會再買了。 COLIN: Yeah – I bought a ready-made spice mix for chicken which was supposed to be used by a chef I'd seen on television, and it didn't actually taste of anything. Colin：是啊——我買過一款現成的雞肉調味料，說是我在電視上看過的一位廚師使用的，但它其實完全沒什麼味道。 MARIE: Mm. Did the article mention ‘ghost kitchens' used to produce takeaway food? Marie：嗯。那篇文章有提到用來製作外送餐點的「幽靈廚房」 嗎？ COLIN: No. What are they? Colin：沒有。那是什麼？ MARIE: Well, they might have the name of a restaurant, but actually they're a cooking facility just for delivery meals – the public don't ever go there. Marie：嗯，它們可能掛著餐廳的名字，但其實只是專門製作外送餐點的廚房——一般民眾根本不會去那裡。 But people aren't aware of that – it's all kept very quiet. 但人們並不知道這一點——一切都非常低調。 COLIN: So people don't realise the food's not actually from the restaurant? Colin：所以人們沒有意識到食物其實不是從那家餐廳來的？ MARIE: Right. Marie：沒錯。 COLIN: Did you know more and more people are using all sorts of different mushrooms now, to treat different health concerns? Things like heart problems? Colin：你知道嗎？現在越來越多人使用各種不同的蘑菇來處理不同的健康問題，例如心臟問題。 MARIE: Hmm. They might be taking a big risk there. Marie：嗯。他們那樣可能是在冒很大的風險。 COLIN: Yes, it's hard to know which varieties are safe to eat. Colin：是的，很難知道哪些品種可以安全食用。 Anyway maybe now . . . 不管怎樣，也許現在……
