Which TWO reasons does the speaker give for recommending Alive and Kicking? It will appeal to both boys and girls. The author is well known. It has colourful illustrations. It is funny. It deals with an important topic. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO pieces of advice does the speaker give to parents about reading? Encourage children to write down new vocabulary. Allow children to listen to audio books. Get recommendations from librarians. Give children a choice about what they read. Only read aloud to children until they can read independently. PRESENTER: The children's book festival is coming up again soon and here to tell us all about it is the festival's organiser, Jenny Morgan. 主持人：兒童圖書節很快又要到了，今天來為我們介紹的是圖書節組織者 Jenny Morgan。 So tell us what we can expect this year, Jenny. Jenny，請告訴我們今年會有哪些活動。 JENNY: Well, as usual we've got five days of action-packed exciting events for children, with writers coming from all over the country getting involved. Jenny：嗯，和往年一樣，我們為孩子們安排了五天精彩豐富的活動，來自全國各地的作家都會參與。 Just to give you an idea of what's on offer in the workshops, first of all, there's a very special event called Superheroes. 為了讓大家了解工作坊有哪些內容，首先有一個非常特別的活動，叫做 Superheroes。 This is a chance for deaf children to share their reading experiences with author Madeleine Gordon, who is herself hearing impaired. 這是讓聽障兒童與作家 Madeleine Gordon 分享閱讀經驗的機會，而她本人也有聽力障礙。 “Just do it” is a practical workshop led by the well-known illustrator Mark Keane. “Just do it” 是由知名插畫家 Mark Keane 主持的實作工作坊。 He'll take participants on a magical journey to faraway lands with an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role play. 他會帶領參與者踏上一段通往遠方國度的奇幻旅程，並讓有志成為演員的孩子有機會進行角色扮演。 “Count on me” is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13–14-year-olds. “Count on me” 是針對 13 至 14 歲孩子設計的活動，以鼓舞人心且有趣的方式探討友誼問題。 It looks at some of the friendships described in popular books and asks participants to compare these with their own experiences. 活動會探討一些流行書籍中描寫的友誼，並請參與者把它們與自己的經驗作比較。 “Speak up” is part of a series of workshops on the subject of mental health. “Speak up” 是心理健康主題系列工作坊的一部分。 This is a creative writing workshop encouraging children to describe situations where young people experience loneliness. 這是一個創意寫作工作坊，鼓勵孩子描述年輕人經歷孤獨的情境。 A recent survey revealed that children can be lonely even when they're at home with their families. 最近一項調查顯示，即使孩子和家人在家中相處，也可能感到孤獨。 “Jump for joy”, as many of you will know, is the heart-warming, best-selling story by Nina Karan about a young girl's trip to visit her relatives in India. 很多人應該知道，“Jump for joy” 是 Nina Karan 創作的一本溫馨暢銷故事，講述一名小女孩前往印度探親的旅程。 It recently received the gold medal at the Waterford Awards. 它最近在 Waterford Awards 中獲得金獎。 Nina will get children to celebrate the word “joy” by writing a poem. Nina 會讓孩子們透過寫詩來歌頌 “joy” 這個詞。 “Sticks and stones” is the beautifully illustrated picture book for young readers about a community who organise an African-Caribbean festival to help local children learn about their Jamaican roots. “Sticks and stones” 是一本為小讀者創作、插圖精美的繪本，講述一個社區舉辦非洲加勒比節， 幫助當地孩子了解自己的牙買加根源。 This will be a musical event where children will have the chance to play steel drums. 這會是一場音樂活動，孩子們將有機會演奏鋼鼓。 This is bound to be very popular, so please book as soon as possible. 這個活動一定會很受歡迎，所以請盡快預訂。 PRESENTER: Thanks Jenny. That all sounds really interesting. 主持人：謝謝 Jenny。這些聽起來都很有趣。 I'm just wondering if you have a favourite book you could recommend for our readers? 我想知道你是否有一本最喜歡的書可以推薦給我們的讀者？ JENNY: It's hard to choose, but Alive and Kicking is definitely worth mentioning. Jenny：很難選，但 Alive and Kicking 絕對值得一提。 You won't have heard of the writer as it's her first book – which is really impressive. 你們可能沒聽過這位作者，因為這是她的第一本書——真的很令人印象深刻。 It's basically the teenage diary of a boy from Somalia who comes to live in the UK. 它基本上是一本日記，講述一個來自索馬利亞、搬到英國生活的男孩的青少年生活。 It deals with the serious issue of immigration and all the challenges the boy has to face at school and with the language barrier, etc. 它處理了移民這個嚴肅議題，以及男孩在學校和語言障礙等方面必須面對的各種挑戰。 Usually, books like this are quite sad, but this one actually made me cry with laughter. 通常這類書會相當悲傷，但這本書其實讓我笑到流淚。 On each page, there are simple but hilarious black and white stick drawings of the boy with his friends and teachers. 每一頁都有簡單但非常搞笑的黑白火柴人插圖，畫的是這個男孩和他的朋友及老師。 At the end of each diary entry, there are new English words the boy learns each day, which may help develop some children's vocabulary. 每篇日記的最後都有男孩每天學到的新英文單字，這可能有助於擴展一些孩子的詞彙量。 PRESENTER: I think my kids would enjoy that. 主持人：我想我的孩子們會喜歡那本書。 What about any advice for parents on how to encourage their children to read more? 那麼，對於父母如何鼓勵孩子多閱讀，你有什麼建議嗎？ JENNY: Well, this is something I get asked about a lot. Jenny：嗯，這是我常被問到的問題。 There are so many distractions for kids these days that it can be hard to find time for reading. 如今孩子們有太多分心的事物， 所以很難找到時間閱讀。 One thing I'd say is to make time to sit down with your child and share books with them. 我會建議的一件事是，抽出時間和孩子坐下來，一起分享書籍。 A lot of parents give up reading aloud to their children as soon as they learn to read independently, but this is a mistake. 很多父母在孩子學會獨立閱讀後，就停止朗讀給孩子聽，但這是個錯誤。 It's good to read more advanced books to them as it helps to develop their vocabulary. 讀較進階的書給孩子聽是有益的，因為這能幫助他們發展詞彙量。 If you don't have time for this, then let them listen to audio books. 如果你沒有時間這樣做，那就讓他們聽有聲書。 Often, they'll want to read books they've listened to for themselves. 通常，他們會想自己閱讀曾經聽過的書。 I think it's a good idea to make a mental note of the type of books your child is reading – often they just read the same genre all the time, which can get a bit boring. 我認為可以在心裡記下孩子正在讀哪類書——他們常常一直讀同一類型，這可能會有點無聊。 You can introduce new authors and genres to them. 你可以向他們介紹新的作者和類型。 Librarians should be able to help you with this. 圖書館員應該能在這方面幫上忙。 PRESENTER: Well Jenny, I think that's really useful... 主持人：Jenny，我覺得這些真的很有用……

entries.title: Listening Practice 7
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–25 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Science Experiment for Year 12 Students 21. How does Clare feel about the students in her Year 12 science class? A. worried that they are not making progress B. challenged by their poor behaviour in class C. frustrated at their lack of interest in the subject 22. How does Jake react to Clare's suggestion about an experiment based on children's diet? A. He is concerned that the results might not be meaningful. B. He feels some of the data might be difficult to obtain. C. He suspects that the conclusions might be upsetting. 23. What problem do they agree may be involved in an experiment involving animals? A. Any results may not apply to humans. B. It may be complicated to get permission. C. Students may not be happy about animal experiments. 24. What question do they decide the experiment should address? A. Are mice capable of controlling their food intake? B. Does an increase in sugar lead to health problems? C. How much do supplements of different kinds affect health? 25. Clare might also consider doing another experiment involving A. other types of food supplement. B. different genetic strains of mice. C. varying amounts of exercise. Questions 26–30 Complete the flowchart below. Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 26–30. A. size B. escape C. age D. water E. cereal F. calculations G. changes H. colour 26. 27. 28. 29. 30. How does Clare feel about the students in her Year 12 science class? worried that they are not making progress challenged by their poor behaviour in class frustrated at their lack of interest in the subject How does Jake react to Clare's suggestion about an experiment based on children's diet? He is concerned that the results might not be meaningful. He feels some of the data might be difficult to obtain. He suspects that the conclusions might be upsetting. What problem do they agree may be involved in an experiment involving animals? Any results may not apply to humans. It may be complicated to get permission. Students may not be happy about animal experiments. What question do they decide the experiment should address? Are mice capable of controlling their food intake? Does an increase in sugar lead to health problems? How much do supplements of different kinds affect health? Clare might also consider doing another experiment involving other types of food supplement. different genetic strains of mice. varying amounts of exercise. 27. size escape age water cereal calculations changes colour 28. size escape age water cereal calculations changes colour 29. size escape age water cereal calculations changes colour 30. size escape age water cereal calculations changes colour Question 30 — refer to the original question paper above. size escape age water cereal calculations changes colour CLARE: Hi Jake. How are you getting on with the practical teaching? Clare：嗨，Jake。你的實習教學進展如何？ JAKE: It's harder than I expected, but I've got some great classes. How about you? Jake：比我想像中難，但我有幾個很棒的班級。你呢？ CLARE: Not brilliant. I'm really struggling with my Year 12 science class. Clare：不太好。我在 12 年級科學課上真的很吃力。 JAKE: Are they hard to control? Jake：他們很難管理嗎？ CLARE: Well, I don't have discipline problems as such. Clare：嗯，倒不是紀律問題。 It's just that they don't seem to think that science has anything to do with their lives. It's depressing. 只是他們似乎不覺得科學和他們的生活有任何關係。這讓人很沮喪。 They listen to what I say, and I gave them a test last week and the results weren't too bad, but there's no real engagement. 他們會聽我講，我上週也給他們做了測驗，成績不算太差，但他們沒有真正投入。 JAKE: Right. Jake：明白。 CLARE: And as part of my teaching practice, I have to design an experiment for them to do. Clare：而且作為教學實習的一部分，我必須設計一個實驗讓他們做。 I was wondering about something on the children's diets... you know, asking them to record what they eat and maybe linking it to their state of health. 我在想是否可以做和孩子飲食有關的東西……比如讓他們記錄自己吃了什麼，也許再和健康狀況聯繫起來。 JAKE: Mmm. Let's think. So your methodology would involve the children recording what they eat. Jake：嗯。讓我們想想。所以你的方法會包括讓孩子們記錄他們吃了什麼。 OK, but you'd also need to have access to the children's medical records and I don't think people would be happy about that; confidentiality would be an issue. 好，但你還需要取得孩子們的醫療紀錄，我想大家不會願意； 保密性會是個問題。 If you could get the right data, the conclusions might be significant, but I suspect it's not going to be easy. 如果你能取得正確資料，結論可能很有意義，但我覺得這不會容易。 CLARE: Right. Clare：對。 JAKE: Have you thought about doing an experiment using animals? Jake：你有想過用動物做實驗嗎？ CLARE: Wouldn't that be upsetting for the children? Clare：那不會讓孩子們難過嗎？ JAKE: Well, the animals don't have to be harmed in any way. Jake：嗯，動物不必受到任何傷害。 It could just be an experiment where they're given a certain diet and the effects are observed. 可以只是給牠們某種特定飲食，然後觀察效果。 CLARE: Would I have to get permission to use animals? Clare：使用動物需要取得許可嗎？ JAKE: Yes, you'd have to submit an outline of the experiment and fill in a form, but it's quite straightforward. Jake：需要，你得提交一份實驗概要並填表，但流程相當簡單。 CLARE: But if we found out that, say, a particular diet affects the health of animals, the same thing wouldn't necessarily be true for people, would it? Clare：但如果我們發現某種特定飲食會影響動物健康，同樣情況不一定適用於人類，對吧？ JAKE: No that's true, but the findings for any experiment are going to be limited. It's inevitable. Jake：對，這是真的，但任何實驗的結果都會有局限性。這是不可避免的。 CLARE: I suppose so. So what animals could I use to investigate the effects of diet? Mice? Clare：我想也是。那我可以用什麼動物來研究飲食影響？小鼠嗎？ JAKE: Yes. You'd need experimental mice – ones that have been specially bred for experiments. Jake：是的。你需要實驗小鼠 ——也就是專門為實驗培育的小鼠。 OK, so what will your experiment be investigating exactly? 好，那你的實驗具體要研究什麼？ CLARE: Well, something to do with nutrition. Clare：嗯，和營養有關的東西。 So maybe we could look at food supplements... things like extra iron and extra protein, and their impact on health. 也許我們可以研究食品補充劑 ……像額外的鐵、額外的蛋白質，以及它們對健康的影響。 JAKE: Mmm. That might be rather broad. Maybe just look at the effects of one supplement, like sugar, on the health of the mice? Jake：嗯。那可能太廣了。也許只研究一種補充物，例如糖，對小鼠健康的影響？ CLARE: In fact, maybe the focus could be on whether mice can control their own diet... Clare：其實，也許重點可以放在小鼠是否能控制自己的飲食 …… JAKE: So, what happens when they have access to more sugar, that they don't really need? Jake：也就是說，當牠們可以取得更多其實不需要的糖時，會發生什麼？ CLARE: Exactly. Do they eat it or do they decide to leave it? Clare：沒錯。牠們會吃掉，還是會選擇不吃？ JAKE: Great. Then later on, you could do a follow-up experiment adding another variable. Jake：太好了。之後你可以做後續實驗，加入另一個變項。 Like, you could give some of the mice the chance to be more active, running on a wheel or something, and the others just sit around and don't do much. 比如，你可以讓部分小鼠有機會更活躍，例如在滾輪上跑，而其他小鼠只是待著，不做太多活動。 CLARE: Or I could repeat the experiment but change the type of food I provided... or use mice with a different genetic structure. Clare：或者我可以重複這個實驗，但改變提供的食物種類…… 或者使用不同基因結構的小鼠。 But I think your idea would be more interesting, I might think about that some more. 不過我覺得你的想法更有趣， 我可能會再多考慮一下。 CLARE: So can I talk through a possible procedure for the experiment where mice are given a sugar supplement? Clare：那我可以說一下讓小鼠攝取糖補充物的可能實驗流程嗎？ JAKE: Sure. I did a similar experiment in college actually. Jake：當然。其實我在大學時做過類似的實驗。 CLARE: Great. So how many mice would I need? Clare：太好了。那我需要多少隻小鼠？ JAKE: I'd say about 12. And all young ones, not a mixture of old and young. Jake：我會說大約 12 隻。而且都要年輕小鼠，不能老鼠和幼鼠混在一起。 CLARE: OK. And I'd need two groups of equal sizes, so six in each group. And how would I tell them apart? Clare：好的。我需要兩組大小相同的組別，所以每組六隻。那我要怎麼區分牠們？ I suppose I could put some sort of tag on one group... or just mark them in some way? 我想可以在其中一組身上放某種標籤……或者用某種方式做標記？ JAKE: You could use food colouring, that wouldn't hurt them. Jake：你可以用食用色素，那不會傷害牠們。 CLARE: Perfect. Then each group would go into a separate cage, and one group, let's call them group A, would be the control group. Clare：太好了。然後每組放進不同籠子，其中一組，我們叫它 A 組，作為對照組。 So they'd just have ordinary mouse food. I suppose you can buy that? 所以牠們只吃普通小鼠飼料。 我想那買得到吧？ JAKE: Yes, it comes in dry pellets. Jake：買得到，是乾顆粒狀的。 CLARE: And the other group would have the same as the first group, but they'd also have the extra sugar. Clare：另一組則和第一組吃一樣的東西，但另外有額外的糖。 JAKE: Would you just give them straight sugar? Jake：你會直接給牠們糖嗎？ CLARE: It might be better to give them something like cereal with it. Clare：也許給牠們像麥片這類東西會比較好。 JAKE: Mmm. Then you'd need to weigh the mice, I should think once a week. And you'd need an electronic balance. Jake：嗯。然後你需要給小鼠稱重，我想每週一次。你還需要一個電子天平。 CLARE: But we can't hold them on the balance, or it'd affect the reading. Clare：但我們不能抓著牠們放在天平上，否則會影響讀數。 JAKE: Exactly. So you need something called a weighing chamber to stop the mice from running away. Jake：沒錯。所以你需要一個叫稱重室的東西，防止小鼠跑掉。 It sounds complicated, but actually you can just use a plastic box with holes in the top. 聽起來很複雜，但其實你只需要用一個頂部有洞的塑膠盒。 CLARE: OK. So once we've measured the weight gain of each mouse we can work out the average for each group, as well as the standard deviation. Clare：好的。一旦我們測量了每隻小鼠的體重增加量，就可以計算每組平均值，以及標準差。 And then see where we go from there. That sounds cool, I think the students will enjoy it. 然後再看看接下來怎麼做。這聽起來很棒，我覺得學生們會喜歡。 JAKE: Yes. One thing... Jake：是的。還有一件事……

entries.title: Listening Practice 7
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Microplastics Where microplastics come from ● fibres from some 31 __________ during washing ● the breakdown of large pieces of plastic ● waste from industry ● the action of vehicle tyres on roads Effects of microplastics ● They cause injuries to the 32 __________ of wildlife and affect their digestive systems. ● They enter the food chain, e.g. in bottled and tap water, 33 __________ and seafood. ● They may not affect human health, but they are already banned in skin cleaning products and 34 __________ in some countries. ● Microplastics enter the soil through the air, rain and 35 __________. Microplastics in the soil — a study by Anglia Ruskin University ● Earthworms are important because they add 36 __________ to the soil. ● The study aimed to find whether microplastics in earthworms affect the 37 __________ of plants. ● The study found that microplastics caused: ○ 38 __________ loss in earthworms ○ fewer seeds to germinate ○ a rise in the level of 39 __________ in the soil. ● The study concluded: ○ soil should be seen as an important natural process. ○ changes to soil damage both ecosystems and 40 __________. ● fibres from some 31 __________ during washing ● They cause injuries to the 32 __________ of wildlife and affect their ● They enter the food chain, e.g. in bottled and tap water, 33 __________ cleaning products and 34 __________ in some countries. ● Microplastics enter the soil through the air, rain and 35 __________. ● Earthworms are important because they add 36 __________ to the soil. 37 __________ of plants. ○ 38 __________ loss in earthworms ○ a rise in the level of 39 __________ in the soil. ○ changes to soil damage both ecosystems and 40 __________. In today's lecture, I'm going to be talking about microplastics. 在今天的講座中，我要談談微塑膠。 Microplastics are tiny pieces of plastic smaller than five millimetres in size. 微塑膠是指尺寸小於五毫米的微小塑膠碎片。 Recently there's been a greater awareness that there are large quantities of plastic waste – big and small – in the environment. 近年來，人們越來越意識到環境中存在大量塑膠廢棄物，不論大小。 The amount of plastic waste in the oceans has received widespread attention, but far less is known about the effects of microplastics in freshwater and particularly in soil. 海洋中的塑膠廢棄物數量已受到廣泛關注，但人們對淡水中，尤其是土壤中微塑膠的影響了解得少得多。 Microplastics can enter the environment via a number of different sources. 微塑膠可以透過多種不同來源進入環境。 Threads and microfibres detach from synthetic clothing every time they're put in a washing machine, and these find their way into the water system. 合成衣物每次放進洗衣機清洗時，都會脫落線頭和微纖維，而這些會進入水系統。 Other sources include big pieces of plastic waste that are already in the environment, and these break down into microscopic particles over a period of time. 其他來源包括已存在於環境中的大型塑膠廢棄物，這些會在一段時間後分解成微小顆粒。 On a larger scale, factory waste is another route, as are tyres which wear down as cars, lorries and so on travel along road surfaces. 從更大規模來看，工廠廢棄物是另一個來源；汽車、卡車等在路面行駛時磨損的輪胎也是來源之一。 We already understand some of the impacts of microplastics from studies involving fish and other animals. 透過涉及魚類和其他動物的研究，我們已經了解微塑膠的一些影響。 There is evidence that microplastics harm small creatures in a variety of ways, such as by damaging their mouths, or by impairing their ability to feed, for example when microplastics get lodged in their digestive system. 有證據顯示，微塑膠會以多種方式傷害小型生物，例如損傷牠們的口腔，或影響牠們進食的能力，例如微塑膠卡在消化系統中時。 Surprisingly perhaps, it is likely that humans consume microplastics, as these have been detected in a wide range of food and drink products, including bottled water, as well as in water that comes direct from the tap. 或許令人驚訝的是，人類很可能也攝入微塑膠，因為在多種食物和飲品中都檢測到了微塑膠，包括瓶裝水以及直接來自水龍頭的自來水。 What's more, salt and many kinds of seafood have also been found to contain microplastics. 此外，鹽和多種海鮮也被發現含有微塑膠。 However, it's important to underline that there is not yet conclusive proof that microplastics cause significant harm to people. 不過，必須強調的是，目前尚無確鑿證據證明微塑膠會對人體造成重大傷害。 In many countries, including here in the UK, there is legislation which prevents manufacturers from adding plastic microbeads to shower gels, facial cleansers and toothpaste. 在許多國家，包括英國，都有法律禁止製造商在沐浴乳、洗面乳和牙膏中添加塑膠微珠。 It is very difficult to accurately estimate the total amount of microplastic particles in the soil as they can be hard to detect, but we do know they are carried in the air and deposited in the soil by rain. 要準確估計土壤中微塑膠顆粒的總量非常困難，因為它們很難被檢測到；但我們知道它們會透過空氣傳播，並被雨水帶入土壤。 What's more, many of the fertilisers used by both farmers and gardeners contain microplastics. 此外，農民和園丁使用的許多肥料也含有微塑膠。 A team from the Anglia Ruskin University in Cambridge has carried out a study of the effects of microplastics on the digestive tracts of earthworms. 劍橋 Anglia Ruskin University 的一個團隊進行了一項研究， 探討微塑膠對蚯蚓消化道的影響。 These worms, which live in topsoil, are an essential component of our agricultural system. 這些生活在表土中的蚯蚓，是我們農業系統的重要組成部分。 By feeding on soil, they mix nutrients into it, thereby making it more fertile. 牠們以土壤為食，並把養分混入土壤中，使土壤更加肥沃。 The researchers set out to discover whether the introduction of microplastics into the soil – and the subsequent ingestion of these by earthworms – would impact soil quality and ultimately inhibit plant growth. 研究人員試圖了解，將微塑膠引入土壤，以及蚯蚓隨後攝入這些微塑膠，是否會影響土壤品質，並最終抑制植物生長。 The short answer was, yes, it did. 簡短答案是：會。 After placing three different types of microplastic particles into the soil, they planted perennial rye grass. 他們將三種不同類型的微塑膠顆粒放入土壤後，種下多年生黑麥草。 The particles of microplastic, which included biodegradable PLA and conventional high-density polyethylene, or HDPE, were then ingested by the earthworms in the soil. 這些微塑膠顆粒包括可生物降解的 PLA，以及傳統高密度聚乙烯，也就是 HDPE；它們隨後被土壤中的蚯蚓攝入。 The result was that the worms lost weight rapidly. 結果是蚯蚓體重迅速下降。 What's more, a lower percentage than normal of the rye grass seeds germinated, and the researchers concluded that this was a direct result of the earthworms being unable to fulfil their normal role in making soil more fertile. 此外，黑麥草種子的發芽比例低於正常水平，研究人員認為，這是蚯蚓無法正常發揮使土壤更肥沃作用的直接結果。 The team also discovered that there was an increase in the amount of acid found in the soil, and this was attributed mainly to the microplastic particles from conventional HDPE plastic. 團隊還發現土壤中的酸含量增加，這主要歸因於傳統 HDPE 塑膠中的微塑膠顆粒。 The conclusions of the study make for very interesting reading – I've included the reference in the notes to give you at the end of this session. 這項研究的結論非常值得一讀——我已把參考資料放進課程結束時會發給你們的筆記裡。 To summarise, the authors proposed the idea that we need to regard soil as we would regard any other process in nature. 總而言之，作者提出一個觀點：我們需要像看待自然界中其他過程一樣看待土壤。 This means we should accept the implications of soil being dependent on decaying and dead matter constantly being passed through the bodies of earthworms. 這意味著我們應該理解土壤依賴腐爛和死亡物質不斷通過蚯蚓身體這一過程所帶來的意義。 That is, when soil becomes impoverished by the presence of microplastics, not only ecosystems but also the whole of society are negatively impacted. 也就是說，當土壤因微塑膠存在而變得貧瘠時，不僅生態系統，整個社會也會受到負面影響。

entries.title: Listening Practice 8
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Part 1 Questions 1–6 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. First Day at Work ● Name of supervisor: 1 __________ ● Where to leave coat and bag: use 2 __________ in staffroom ● See Tiffany in HR: ○ to give 3 __________ number ○ to collect 4 __________ ● Location of HR office: on 5 __________ floor ● Supervisor’s mobile number: 6 __________ Questions 7–10 Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Practice 8, source question diagram/table, PDF page 5 ● Name of supervisor: 1 __________ ● Where to leave coat and bag: use 2 __________ in staffroom ○ to give 3 __________ number ○ to collect 4 __________ ● Location of HR office: on 5 __________ floor ● Supervisor’s mobile number: 6 __________ Bakery section — Use _____ labels Sushi takeaway counter — Re-stock with _____ boxes if needed Meat and fish counters — Collect _____ from the cold-room Must wear special _____ KAEDEN: Hello Charlotte. I'm Kaeden, one of the supervisors. Welcome to the team. Kaeden：你好，Charlotte。我是 Kaeden，這裡的主管之一。歡迎加入我們的團隊。 CHARLOTTE: Hi Aiden. Charlotte：你好，Aiden。 KAEDEN: It's Kaeden. Kaeden：是 Kaeden。 CHARLOTTE: I'm so sorry. Charlotte：真的很抱歉。 KAEDEN: Don't worry. People often get my name wrong; they never know how to spell it. Kaeden：別擔心。大家經常把我的名字弄錯，也不知道怎麼拼。 It's K-A-E-D-E-N, in case you ever need to write it. 是 K-A-E-D-E-N，以防你之後需要寫下來。 CHARLOTTE: I'll try and remember. Charlotte：我會努力記住。 KAEDEN: So, there are a few practical things you need to sort out this morning. Kaeden：那麼，今天早上你需要先處理幾件實際事項。 Then I'll show you what you're going to do today. 然後我會告訴你今天要做什麼。 CHARLOTTE: The email I received said to go to the front desk, to show my letter of appointment and pick up my badge. Charlotte：我收到的電子郵件說， 要去前台出示任命信，並領取我的識別證。 KAEDEN: You'll need that for the staffroom and other areas of the supermarket where shoppers aren't allowed. Kaeden：你需要那個才能進入員工休息室，以及超市裡其他顧客不能進入的區域。 So, after you've finished at the front desk, I'll take you to the staffroom. 所以你在前台辦完後，我會帶你去員工休息室。 Put your coat and rucksack in one of the lockers there. Take whichever one is free. 把你的外套和背包放進那裡的其中一個置物櫃。哪個空著就用哪個。 CHARLOTTE: Will I have a key? Charlotte：我會有鑰匙嗎？ KAEDEN: Yes. Try not to lose it. At the end of the day, leave it in the door for the next person to use. Kaeden：會的。盡量別弄丟。一天結束時，把鑰匙留在櫃門上，方便下一個人使用。 CHARLOTTE: Will do. Charlotte：好的。 KAEDEN: You also need to go to the HR department to see Tiffany. She's really helpful. Kaeden：你還需要去人力資源部找 Tiffany。她人很好，也很願意幫忙。 CHARLOTTE: I was told to bring my passport with me. HR need to take a note of the number in it. Charlotte：有人告訴我要帶護照。 人資部需要記下裡面的號碼。 KAEDEN: That's right. Or you can show your ID card. Kaeden：沒錯。或者你也可以出示身分證。 CHARLOTTE: I don't have one of those. Charlotte：我沒有身分證。 KAEDEN: OK. Tiffany will give you a uniform. Kaeden：好的。Tiffany 會給你一套制服。 They have lots in different sizes, so you just tell her what you need. 他們有很多不同尺寸，所以你只要告訴她你需要什麼尺碼就可以。 I won't come with you to HR – I've got to go and sort something else out. Problem with a bread slicer. 我不會陪你去人資部——我得去處理別的事情。麵包切片機出了點問題。 CHARLOTTE: Is the HR office near the staffroom? Charlotte：人資辦公室在員工休息室附近嗎？ KAEDEN: The staffroom's on the first floor, and HR are a couple of floors above that, on the third floor. There's a staircase outside the staffroom. Kaeden：員工休息室在一樓，人資部在上面幾層，也就是三樓。員工休息室外面有樓梯。 CHARLOTTE: OK. Charlotte：好的。 KAEDEN: When you've finished with HR, come and find me in the bakery section of the shop. Kaeden：你在人資部辦完後，就到店裡的烘焙區找我。 CHARLOTTE: I'm looking forward to getting started. Charlotte：我很期待開始工作。 KAEDEN: I'll just give you my phone number, in case you can't find me. Have you got your phone there? Kaeden：我把我的電話號碼給你， 以防你找不到我。你手機在身邊嗎？ CHARLOTTE: Yes... OK, ready. Charlotte：在……好了，準備好了。 KAEDEN: It's oh-four-one-two double-six-five nine-oh-three. Kaeden：是 0-4-1-2-6-6-5-9-0-3。 CHARLOTTE: OK, done. Charlotte：好的，記下了。 KAEDEN: So, Charlotte, your tasks today are in the bakery section, on the sushi counter, and on the meat and fish counters. Kaeden：那麼，Charlotte，你今天的工作會在烘焙區、壽司櫃台，以及肉類和魚類櫃台。 The first job is to check sell-by dates on the bread and cakes. 第一項工作是檢查麵包和蛋糕的銷售期限。 If any of the dates are today's, put a new price label on the packaging. 如果日期是今天，就在包裝上貼上新的價格標籤。 CHARLOTTE: What if any of the labels are yesterday's dates, or older? Charlotte：如果標籤上的日期是昨天或更早呢？ Do I throw those items away? 我要把那些商品丟掉嗎？ KAEDEN: Yes, but that shouldn't happen – we check the stock every day. Kaeden：是的，但那應該不會發生 ——我們每天都會檢查庫存。 When something needs a new price label, put a yellow one on the package, next to the original price. 如果商品需要新的價格標籤，就把黃色標籤貼在包裝上，放在原價旁邊。 CHARLOTTE: OK. Charlotte：好的。 KAEDEN: After that, you'll go to the sushi takeaway counter. Kaeden：之後，你會去壽司外帶櫃台。 CHARLOTTE: Will I be preparing boxes of food? Charlotte：我要準備盒裝食物嗎？ KAEDEN: For today, you'll just be helping the staff. Kaeden：今天你只需要協助其他員工。 CHARLOTTE: Yes, of course. Charlotte：好的，沒問題。 KAEDEN: You'll see lots of flat cardboard boxes at one end of the counter. Kaeden：你會在櫃台一端看到很多平放的紙盒。 Beneath those is where we keep the plastic boxes – we run out of those really quickly, so you should bring more from the storeroom. 那些下面放的是塑膠盒——我們很快就會用完，所以你需要從儲藏室多拿一些過來。 CHARLOTTE: Is that my only task on the sushi counter? Charlotte：那是我在壽司櫃台唯一的工作嗎？ KAEDEN: No. You also need to clean the area where they prepare the dishes. Kaeden：不是。你還需要清潔他們準備餐點的區域。 There are cloths and bottles of spray by the sink. Oh, and please make sure you clean that too. 水槽旁邊有抹布和噴霧瓶。哦，還有，也請務必把水槽清乾淨。 CHARLOTTE: Sure. That's important, isn't it? Charlotte：當然。那很重要，對吧？ KAEDEN: Absolutely. But you mustn't wash up knives. Kaeden：絕對重要。但你不能清洗刀具。 You have to do some training before you're allowed to touch sharp objects. 在你被允許接觸尖銳物品之前， 必須先接受一些訓練。 CHARLOTTE: What should I do if there are any? Charlotte：如果有刀具，我該怎麼辦？ KAEDEN: Ask someone to put them in the dishwasher. Kaeden：請別人把它們放進洗碗機。 CHARLOTTE: OK, thanks. I don't want to get anything wrong. Charlotte：好的，謝謝。我不想做錯任何事。 KAEDEN: Don't worry. You'll be fine. And I'll be around to help. Kaeden：別擔心。你會沒問題的。 我也會在附近幫忙。 CHARLOTTE: Right. Charlotte：好的。 KAEDEN: Finally, the meat and fish counters. Kaeden：最後是肉類和魚類櫃台。 You need to clean the area where staff serve customers, including wiping the weighing scales. 你需要清潔員工服務顧客的區域，包括擦拭秤重機。 CHARLOTTE: OK. Anything else? Charlotte：好的。還有別的嗎？ KAEDEN: The fish is laid on ice, but when that starts to melt, you'll need to get more from the cold-room. Kaeden：魚是放在冰上的，但當冰開始融化時，你需要從冷藏室再拿一些冰。 CHARLOTTE: I know the staff on the food counters wear a hat. Will that be the same for me? Charlotte：我知道食品櫃台的員工會戴帽子。我也需要嗎？ KAEDEN: You won't be serving customers directly, so no. Kaeden：你不會直接服務顧客，所以不用。 But make sure you put on thermal gloves when you take anything out of the cold-room. 但從冷藏室拿東西時，一定要戴上保暖手套。 The temperature's low enough in there to get frostbite from touching things. 裡面的溫度很低，碰到東西可能會凍傷。 CHARLOTTE: Understood. Charlotte：明白。

entries.title: Listening Practice 8
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11 and 12 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO problems with some training programmes for new runners does Liz mention? A. There is a risk of serious injury. B. They are unsuitable for certain age groups. C. They are unsuitable for people with health issues. D. It is difficult to stay motivated. E. There is a lack of individual support. Questions 13 and 14 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO tips does Liz recommend for new runners? A. doing two runs a week B. running in the evening C. going on runs with a friend D. listening to music during runs E. running very slowly Questions 15–18 What reason prevented each of the following members of the Compton Park Runners Club from joining until recently? Write the correct letter, A, B or C, next to Questions 15–18. Reasons A. a lack of confidence B. a dislike of running C. a lack of time Club members 15. Ceri __________ 16. James __________ 17. Leo __________ 18. Mark __________ Questions 19 and 20 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 19. What does Liz say about running her first marathon? A. It had always been her ambition. B. Her husband persuaded her to do it. C. She nearly gave up before the end. 20. Liz says new runners should sign up for a race A. every six months. B. within a few weeks of taking up running. C. after completing several practice runs. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO problems with some training programmes for new runners does Liz mention? There is a risk of serious injury. They are unsuitable for certain age groups. They are unsuitable for people with health issues. It is difficult to stay motivated. There is a lack of individual support. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO tips does Liz recommend for new runners? doing two runs a week running in the evening going on runs with a friend listening to music during runs running very slowly Ceri a lack of confidence a dislike of running a lack of time James a lack of confidence a dislike of running a lack of time Leo a lack of confidence a dislike of running a lack of time Mark a lack of confidence a dislike of running a lack of time What does Liz say about running her first marathon? It had always been her ambition. Her husband persuaded her to do it. She nearly gave up before the end. Liz says new runners should sign up for a race every six months. within a few weeks of taking up running. after completing several practice runs. My name's Liz Fuller and I'm a running coach with Compton Park Runners Club. 我叫 Liz Fuller，是 Compton Park Runners Club 的跑步教練。 Welcome to my podcast. If you're thinking about taking up running – I'm here to help. 歡迎收聽我的播客。如果你正在考慮開始跑步，我可以幫助你。 There are many training programmes available online which aim to help people build up to running 5 kilometres. 網路上有很多訓練計畫，目的是幫助人們逐步達到能跑 5 公里的程度。 Some of them are great and thousands of people of all ages are taking part in 5-kilometre races across the country as a result. 其中有些計畫很棒，也因此全國各地有成千上萬、各個年齡層的人參加 5 公里賽跑。 People like them because they're easy to follow and don't push them too hard. 人們喜歡這些計畫，因為它們容易遵循，也不會把人逼得太緊。 However, they don't work for everyone – especially if you suffer from something like a heart condition or asthma, because they're aimed at people with average fitness and running ability. 然而，它們並不適合所有人，尤其是如果你有心臟問題或氣喘之類的情況，因為這些計畫是針對體能和跑步能力一般的人設計的。 Another thing is that everyone is different – and if you have any specific questions related to your needs, there's no one to provide any answers. 另一點是，每個人都不同；如果你有和自身需求相關的具體問題，沒有人能提供答案。 I have a couple of simple tips I always give to new runners. 我有幾個簡單建議，總是會給剛開始跑步的人。 I expect you've been told to run very slowly until your fitness increases – well, I find that can prevent progress. 我猜你可能被建議在體能提升前要跑得非常慢——但我發現那反而可能阻礙進步。 You should run at a speed that feels comfortable, but time yourself and try to run a bit faster each time. 你應該以自己覺得舒服的速度跑，但要計時，並試著每次跑得稍微快一點。 Listening to music can be very helpful – it takes your mind off things and helps your body get into a rhythm. 聽音樂可能很有幫助——它能讓你轉移注意力，也幫助身體進入節奏。 I'd say that is better than running with a friend – especially as most people are competitive and that's not what you want when you're just starting. 我會說這比和朋友一起跑更好， 尤其是大多數人都有競爭心，而剛開始跑步時你並不需要那種壓力。 I don't think the time of day is especially important – some people are better in the evening, while others are morning people – but you need to be consistent, so aim to train regularly – twice a week is enough to begin with. 我不認為一天中的跑步時間特別重要——有些人晚上狀態更好，有些人則適合早上——但你需要保持規律，所以目標是定期訓練；一開始每週兩次就足夠了。 New members often say to me that they've been put off running either because they lack confidence, or they don't have time, or they think they dislike running. 新會員常對我說，他們以前不想跑步，要不是因為缺乏信心，就是沒有時間，或者以為自己不喜歡跑步。 Ceri, for example, joined the club two years ago at the age of 40. 例如，Ceri 兩年前在 40 歲時加入了俱樂部。 She'd always enjoyed running at school but wasn't sure if she'd be able to do it. 她上學時一直很喜歡跑步，但不確定自己是否還能做到。 She was worried about being left behind and being the slowest runner. 她擔心自己會落後，成為跑得最慢的人。 But she says she was made to feel so welcome she soon forgot all about that. 但她說大家讓她感到非常受歡迎，所以她很快就忘了那些擔心。 James had always hated the idea of running but a friend encouraged him to come along for a taster session and he hasn't looked back. James 一直討厭跑步這件事，但朋友鼓勵他來參加體驗課，之後他就一直跑了下去。 He never misses a training session despite having a really demanding job. 儘管工作非常忙碌，他從不缺席訓練。 Leo was worried about having to commit himself to training sessions every week and wasn't sure he'd be able to fit training into his busy schedule. Leo 擔心自己每週都得投入訓練，也不確定能否把訓練安排進繁忙的行程中。 But after experiencing a lot of stress at work he came along to us and gave it a go. 不過在工作壓力很大之後，他來到我們這裡並試了一下。 Now he says he feels much more relaxed and he looks forward to his weekly run. 現在他說自己放鬆多了，也很期待每週的跑步。 Mark is quite typical of our new members. Mark 是我們新會員中相當典型的一位。 He's never considered himself to be a sporty person and it was only when he retired that he decided to take up the challenge of trying to run 5 kilometres. 他從不認為自己是愛運動的人， 直到退休後才決定接受挑戰，嘗試跑 5 公里。 It took him months to find the courage to contact us but felt reassured immediately as there were other people his age who were only just taking up running for the first time. 他花了好幾個月才鼓起勇氣聯絡我們，但一來就放心了，因為還有其他和他年紀相仿、也是第一次開始跑步的人。 My own journey hasn't been easy. 我自己的跑步歷程也不容易。 I did my first marathon when I was 37, after having had two kids. 我在 37 歲時跑了第一場馬拉松，那時我已經有兩個孩子。 My husband had been running marathons for years, but I never dreamed I'd be doing one with him. 我丈夫已經跑馬拉松很多年了， 但我從沒想過自己會和他一起跑。 I managed to complete it in four hours, but I felt like giving up halfway through – it was only the support of the spectators that kept me going. 我最後用四小時完成了比賽，但中途我差點想放棄——是觀眾的支持讓我堅持下去。 I do think signing up for a race of whatever length is motivating – whether it's 5K or 25K – because it's good to have something to work towards and it gives you a sense of achievement. 我確實認為報名參加任何距離的比賽都很有激勵作用——不管是 5 公里還是 25 公里——因為有一個努力目標是很好的，也會帶來成就感。 I did my first 10K after only six months, which was certainly very challenging and not something I'd necessarily recommend. 我只訓練六個月就跑了第一場 10 公里，這當然非常有挑戰性， 也不一定是我會推薦的做法。 But after you've been training for a few weeks, it's worth putting your name down for a 5K – some people find they only need a few practice runs before taking part in a race, but I'd give yourself a couple of months at least. 但在你訓練幾週後，值得報名參加 5 公里賽。有些人發現參賽前只需要練跑幾次，但我會建議至少給自己幾個月時間。 Well, I hope that's given... 好，我希望這些已經讓你……

entries.title: Listening Practice 8
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–25 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 21. Kieran thinks the packing advice given by Jane’s grandfather is A. common sense. B. hard to follow. C. over-protective. 22. How does Jane feel about the books her grandfather has given her? A. They are not worth keeping. B. They should go to a collector. C. They have sentimental value for her. 23. Jane and Kieran agree that hardback books should be A. put out on display. B. given as gifts to visitors. C. more attractively designed. 24. While talking about taking a book from a shelf, Jane A. describes the mistakes other people make doing it. B. reflects on a significant childhood experience. C. explains why some books are easier to remove than others. 25. What do Jane and Kieran suggest about new books? A. Their parents liked buying them as presents. B. They would like to buy more of them. C. Not everyone can afford them. Questions 26–30 Where does Jane’s grandfather keep each of the following types of books in his shop? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 26–30. Location of books A. near the entrance B. in the attic C. at the back of the shop D. on a high shelf E. near the stairs F. in a specially designed space G. within the café Types of books 26. rare books __________ 27. children’s books __________ 28. unwanted books __________ 29. requested books __________ 30. coursebooks __________ Kieran thinks the packing advice given by Jane’s grandfather is common sense. hard to follow. over-protective. How does Jane feel about the books her grandfather has given her? They are not worth keeping. They should go to a collector. They have sentimental value for her. Jane and Kieran agree that hardback books should be put out on display. given as gifts to visitors. more attractively designed. While talking about taking a book from a shelf, Jane describes the mistakes other people make doing it. reflects on a significant childhood experience. explains why some books are easier to remove than others. What do Jane and Kieran suggest about new books? Their parents liked buying them as presents. They would like to buy more of them. Not everyone can afford them. rare books near the entrance in the attic at the back of the shop on a high shelf near the stairs in a specially designed space within the café children’s books near the entrance in the attic at the back of the shop on a high shelf near the stairs in a specially designed space within the café unwanted books near the entrance in the attic at the back of the shop on a high shelf near the stairs in a specially designed space within the café requested books near the entrance in the attic at the back of the shop on a high shelf near the stairs in a specially designed space within the café coursebooks near the entrance in the attic at the back of the shop on a high shelf near the stairs in a specially designed space within the café KIERAN: So Jane – you'll be off to Denmark soon to do your work placement. Kieran：Jane，你很快就要去丹麥實習了。 JANE: Yes, I'm really looking forward to it and I've just started packing up all my books to put in storage. Jane：是的，我真的很期待，而且我剛開始把所有書打包，準備放進倉庫。 KIERAN: Well, I hope they don't get spoilt. Kieran：嗯，希望它們不會被弄壞。 JANE: It's OK – my grandfather works in a bookshop and he told me how to pack them. Jane：沒事的。我爺爺在書店工作，他告訴我該怎麼打包。 KIERAN: Oh, that's helpful. Kieran：哦，那很有幫助。 JANE: He says you have to support the spine otherwise the paper can come away from the cover. Jane：他說一定要支撐書脊，否則書頁可能會從封面脫落。 KIERAN: Yeah – that's obvious. Kieran：是啊——這很明顯。 JANE: He also told me to pack them flat in the box not on their side – again because they can bend and if you leave them like that for, say, a year, it's quite hard to get them back to their normal shape. Jane：他還告訴我要把書平放在盒子裡，不要側放——同樣是因為它們會彎曲；如果像那樣放一年，就很難恢復原狀。 KIERAN: Well, it's pretty clear that ruins them, but a lot of people just can't be bothered to protect their books. Kieran：嗯，很明顯那會把書弄壞，但很多人就是懶得保護自己的書。 JANE: He always says it's such a shame that publishers don't use better-quality paper. Jane：他總說出版商不使用更高品質的紙張，真的很可惜。 KIERAN: It's the acid in the paper that causes the problem, isn't it? Kieran：問題是紙裡的酸性物質造成的，對吧？ JANE: Yeah – that's why old books go yellow. You know some of the books my grandfather's given me are like that already. Jane：是啊，這就是為什麼舊書會變黃。你知道我爺爺給我的一些書已經那樣了。 KIERAN: Oh... Kieran：哦…… JANE: I should dump them really if they're going to deteriorate further, but I'd feel bad. Jane：如果它們還會繼續變壞，我其實應該把它們丟掉，但我會覺得很難過。 They'll always remind me of him. He's quite a collector, you know. 它們總會讓我想起他。你知道， 他是個很愛收藏的人。 KIERAN: Well, if they're important to you... Kieran：嗯，如果它們對你很重要 …… JANE: Yeah – I'd regret just throwing them away. Jane：是啊，直接把它們丟掉我會後悔。 KIERAN: You know, maybe it's because I was taught to treasure books... but I hate seeing students force open the pages – of paperbacks. They press so hard they end up breaking the spine. Kieran：你知道，也許是因為我從小被教導要珍惜書吧……但我很討厭看到學生用力撐開平裝書的書頁。他們壓得太用力，最後把書脊弄斷。 JANE: I know, but unfortunately, paperbacks aren't designed to last a long time and people know that. Hardbacks aren't quite as weak. Jane：我知道，但不幸的是，平裝書本來就不是設計來長久保存的，大家也知道這點。精裝書就沒那麼脆弱。 KIERAN: Yeah, they're different, I suppose. But I still don't think people value hardbacks like they used to. Kieran：是啊，我想它們是不一樣的。不過我還是覺得人們不像以前那樣重視精裝書了。 JANE: Well, they aren't decorative, are they, like other objects. Plus, nowadays, people don't keep them out on shelves as much as they used to. Jane：嗯，它們不像其他物品那樣有裝飾性，不是嗎？而且現在人們也不像以前那樣把它們擺在書架上。 KIERAN: That's such a pity. When I visit someone – if they have, say, a colourful book on a table, it's the first thing I'm drawn to. Kieran：那真可惜。我去別人家拜訪時，如果他們桌上有一本色彩鮮豔的書，那一定是第一個吸引我的東西。 JANE: I agree – and book covers can be a work of art in themselves. Some are really eye-catching. Jane：我同意——書封本身也可以是一件藝術品。有些真的很吸引人。 KIERAN: I've always been taught to handle books carefully. If you watch someone take a book off a shelf, well, they usually do it wrong. Kieran：我一直被教導要小心拿書。如果你觀察別人從書架上拿書，嗯，他們通常都拿錯了。 JANE: Ah, my grandfather says, you should put your hand right over the top of the book... or if you can't do that, pull the other books on the shelf aside so that you can hold the whole cover. Jane：啊，我爺爺說，你應該把手直接放在書的上方……如果做不到，就把書架上的其他書挪開， 這樣才能握住整個封面。 KIERAN: When did you learn all this? Kieran：你什麼時候學會這些的？ JANE: He watched me pull a heavy book off the shelf when I was small, and it fell on the floor and broke apart. Jane：我小時候，他看到我從書架上拉下一本很重的書，結果書掉到地上散開了。 KIERAN: Oh dear! Kieran：天啊！ JANE: I can still remember it! Jane：我到現在還記得！ KIERAN: You know what I really like? Kieran：你知道我真的很喜歡什麼嗎？ JANE: What? Jane：什麼？ KIERAN: The smell of new books. Kieran：新書的味道。 JANE: Me too. Jane：我也是。 KIERAN: My parents used to laugh at me when I was a kid because I loved putting books up to my nose. Almost as much as reading them! Kieran：我小時候，我爸媽常笑我，因為我很喜歡把書拿到鼻子前聞。幾乎和我喜歡讀書一樣！ JANE: New books aren't cheap, though, are they? Jane：不過新書不便宜，對吧？ KIERAN: I guess we're lucky we can buy them. Kieran：我想我們能買得起已經很幸運了。 JANE: My grandfather stocks second-hand books as well as new ones and they don't smell quite as good. Jane：我爺爺店裡既有二手書也有新書，而二手書聞起來就沒那麼好。 KIERAN: I'd love to have a bookshop like your grandfather. What's it like? Kieran：我很想擁有一家像你爺爺那樣的書店。它是什麼樣子？ JANE: Well, it's quite big – it's got two floors and an attic, and he stocks all kinds of books really. Jane：嗯，它挺大的——有兩層樓和一個閣樓，而且他真的收藏各種書。 KIERAN: I guess he treasures things like first editions and other rare books. Kieran：我猜他很珍惜初版書和其他稀有書籍。 JANE: Yeah – you might think he'd keep those in the attic or somewhere. Jane：是啊——你可能會以為他把那些書放在閣樓或某個地方。 KIERAN: ...so they'd be hidden? Kieran：……所以它們會被藏起來？ JANE: Yeah. But he likes people to know that he has them. Jane：是啊。但他喜歡讓人知道他有那些書。 So, he puts them out in the shop but makes sure you need a ladder to get them. 所以他把它們放在店裡展示，但確保你需要梯子才能拿到。 KIERAN: Right. That would prevent any thefts! Kieran：對。那可以防止被偷！ JANE: Uhuh. Jane：嗯。 KIERAN: Does he stock books for children? Kieran：他有賣兒童書嗎？ JANE: He does. He particularly likes to encourage kids to read; he always says that he used to sit under the stairs as a child with a pile of books and read them all. Jane：有。他特別喜歡鼓勵孩子閱讀；他總說自己小時候常坐在樓梯下，抱著一堆書，把它們全讀完。 KIERAN: Is that where he keeps them, then? Kieran：那他現在也把兒童書放在那裡嗎？ JANE: Not exactly – he's got a dedicated area on the ground floor with cushions so that parents can enter with their toddlers, go there and spend some time reading to them. Jane：不完全是——他在一樓設了一個專門區域，有坐墊，讓家長可以帶幼兒進去，在那裡花時間讀書給他們聽。 KIERAN: Oh cool. Kieran：哦，真酷。 JANE: And then there's a place for pushchairs by the front door. And a café if anyone needs refreshments. Jane：前門旁邊還有放嬰兒推車的地方。如果有人需要飲料點心，也有咖啡館。 KIERAN: That's good to know. Kieran：知道這些真不錯。 JANE: As I said, it's a big shop and there's a storage area out the back as well. Jane：就像我說的，那是一家大書店，後面也有一個儲藏區。 KIERAN: Oh, what does he keep there? Books he wants to throw away? Kieran：哦，他在那裡放什麼？想丟掉的書嗎？ JANE: He hardly ever throws anything away – he just leaves unwanted books by the front door for customers to take. Jane：他幾乎從不丟任何東西—— 他只是把不需要的書放在前門旁，讓顧客自行拿走。 KIERAN: Well, that's very nice. Kieran：嗯，那真不錯。 JANE: Yeah – and books people or institutions have requested, they all go at the far end. Jane：是啊——人們或機構預訂的書，則都放在最裡面。 KIERAN: Oh. Kieran：哦。 JANE: He thinks it's best to keep these out of the main shopping area as they're boxed and new. Jane：他覺得最好不要把這些書放在主要購物區，因為它們都是裝箱的新書。 KIERAN: Did you get your coursebooks from him? Kieran：你的課本是從他那裡買的嗎？ JANE: Naturally. He stocks books for a lot of the colleges. Jane：當然。他為很多學院備有課本。 He used to keep these books on the first floor, but now there's a new university in my hometown, he's moved them downstairs to attract the students. 他以前把這些書放在一樓，但現在我家鄉有了一所新大學，所以他把它們搬到樓下，以吸引學生。 They're actually part of the coffee shop, on low shelves all around it. 它們其實就在咖啡店區域裡，放在咖啡店周圍的低書架上。 KIERAN: Pretty central then. You'll have to take me there some time! Kieran：那位置很中心。你改天一定要帶我去看看！

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Tree Planting Reforestation projects should: ● include a range of tree species ● not include invasive species because of possible 31 __________ with native species ● aim to capture carbon, protect the environment and provide sustainable sources of 32 __________ for local people ● use tree seeds with a high genetic diversity to increase resistance to 33 __________ and climate change ● plant trees on previously forested land which is in a bad condition, not select land which is being used for 34 __________ Large-scale reforestation projects ● Base planning decisions on information from accurate 35 __________. ● Drones are useful for identifying areas in Brazil which are endangered by keeping 36 __________ and illegal logging. Lampang Province, Northern Thailand ● A forest was restored in an area damaged by mining. ● A variety of native fig trees were planted, which are important for: ○ supporting many wildlife species ○ increasing the 37 __________ of recovery by attracting animals and birds, e.g. 38 __________ were soon attracted to the area. Involving local communities ● Destruction of mangrove forests in Madagascar made it difficult for people to make a living from 39 __________. ● The mangrove reforestation project: ○ provided employment for local people ○ restored a healthy ecosystem ○ protects against the higher risk of 40 __________ ● not include invasive species because of possible 31 __________ with sources of 32 __________ for local people ● use tree seeds with a high genetic diversity to increase resistance to 33 __________ and climate change select land which is being used for 34 __________ ● Base planning decisions on information from accurate 35 __________. keeping 36 __________ and illegal logging. ○ increasing the 37 __________ of recovery by attracting animals and birds, e.g. 38 __________ were soon attracted to the area. people to make a living from 39 __________. ○ protects against the higher risk of 40 __________ Tree planting now dominates political and popular agendas and is often presented as an easy answer to the climate crisis, as well as a way for business corporations to offset their carbon emissions. 植樹如今已成為政治和大眾議程中的重要議題，並常被呈現為應對氣候危機的簡單方法， 也是企業抵消碳排放的一種方式。 But unfortunately, tree planting isn't as straightforward as some people think. 但不幸的是，植樹並不像有些人想的那麼簡單。 When the wrong trees are planted in the wrong place, it can do considerably more damage than good, failing to help either people or the environment. 如果在錯誤的地方種下錯誤的樹，可能弊大於利，既無法幫助人類，也無法幫助環境。 Reforestation projects are currently being undertaken on a huge scale in many countries and it's crucial that the right trees are selected. 目前許多國家正在大規模推行再造林計畫，選擇正確的樹種至關重要。 A mix of species should always be planted, typical of the local natural forest ecosystem and including rare and endangered species in order to create a rich ecosystem. 應該始終種植多種樹種，包括當地自然森林生態系統中典型的樹種，以及稀有和瀕危物種，以建立豐富的生態系統。 It's important to avoid non-native species that could become invasive. 避免可能成為入侵物種的外來樹種非常重要。 Invasive species are a significant contributor to the current global biodiversity crisis and are often in competition with native species and may threaten their long-term survival. 入侵物種是當前全球生物多樣性危機的重要因素，它們經常與本土物種競爭，並可能威脅本土物種的長期生存。 Restoring biodiversity that will maximise carbon capture is key when reforesting an area, but ideally any reforestation project should have several goals. 在某個地區進行再造林時，恢復能最大化碳捕捉的生物多樣性是關鍵，但理想情況下，任何再造林計畫都應該有多個目標。 These could include selecting trees that can contribute to wildlife conservation, improve the availability of food for the local community and maintain the stability of soil systems. 這些目標可以包括選擇有助於野生動物保護的樹種、改善當地社區食物供應，以及維持土壤系統穩定。 Meeting as many of these goals as possible, whilst doing no harm to local communities, native ecosystems and vulnerable species, is the sign of a highly successful tree-planting scheme. 在不傷害當地社區、本土生態系統和脆弱物種的前提下，盡可能實現這些目標，是一個高度成功的植樹計畫標誌。 To ensure the survival and resilience of a planted forest, it's vital to use tree seeds with appropriate levels of genetic diversity: the amount of genetic variation found within a species essential for their survival. 為了確保人工林的存活率和韌性，使用具有適當遺傳多樣性的樹種種子非常重要；這指的是一個物種內對其生存至關重要的遺傳變異量。 Using seeds with low genetic diversity generally lowers the resilience of restored forests, which can make them vulnerable to disease and unable to adapt to climate change. 使用遺傳多樣性低的種子通常會降低復育森林的韌性，使其容易受到疾病侵害，也無法適應氣候變化。 Choosing the right location for reforestation projects is as important as choosing the right trees. 為再造林計畫選擇正確地點， 和選擇正確樹種一樣重要。 Ultimately, the best area for planting trees would be in formerly forested areas that are in poor condition. 歸根結底，最適合植樹的地點，是曾經是森林但目前狀況不佳的地區。 It's better to avoid non-forested landscapes such as natural grasslands, savannas or wetlands as these ecosystems already contribute greatly to capturing carbon. 最好避免在非森林地貌植樹， 例如天然草地、熱帶稀樹草原或濕地，因為這些生態系統本身已經對碳捕捉有很大貢獻。 It would also be advantageous to choose an area where trees could provide other benefits, such as recreational spaces. 選擇樹木能提供其他好處的地區也很有利，例如提供休閒空間。 Reforesting areas which are currently exploited for agriculture should be avoided as this often leads to other areas being deforested. 應避免在目前用於農業的地區進行再造林，因為這往往會導致其他地區被砍伐森林。 Large-scale reforestation projects require careful planning. 大規模再造林計畫需要仔細規劃。 Making the right decisions about where to plant trees depends on having the right information. 要正確決定在哪裡植樹，取決於是否掌握正確資訊。 Having detailed and up-to-date maps identifying high-priority areas for intervention is essential. 擁有詳細且最新的地圖，以辨識需要優先介入的地區，是非常必要的。 Drone technology is a useful tool in helping to prioritise and monitor areas of degraded forest for restoration. 無人機技術是一項有用工具， 可協助確定退化森林復育的優先順序並進行監測。 In Brazil, it's being used to identify and quantify how parts of the Amazon are being devastated by human activities such as rearing cattle and illegal logging. 在巴西，無人機被用來識別和量化亞馬遜部分地區如何受到人類活動破壞，例如養牛和非法伐木。 A good example of where the right trees were picked to achieve a restored forest is in Lampang Province in Northern Thailand. 選擇正確樹種來成功復育森林的一個好例子，是泰國北部的 Lampang Province。 A previously forested site which had been degraded through mining was reforested by a cement company together with Chiang Mai University. 一處原本是森林、後來因採礦而退化的地區，由一家水泥公司和清邁大學合作進行再造林。 After spreading 60 cm of topsoil, they planted 14 different native tree species which included several species of fig. 在鋪上 60 公分表土後，他們種植了 14 種不同的本土樹種，其中包括幾種無花果樹。 Figs are a keystone species because of the critical role they play in maintaining wildlife populations. 無花果是關鍵物種，因為它們在維持野生動物族群方面發揮重要作用。 They are central to tropical reforestation projects as they accelerate the speed of the recovery process by attracting animals and birds which act as natural seed dispersers. 它們是熱帶再造林計畫的核心，因為它們能吸引動物和鳥類，而這些動物和鳥類會自然散播種子，從而加快復育速度。 This helps to promote diversity through the healthy regrowth of a wide range of plant species. 這有助於透過多種植物的健康再生來促進多樣性。 Unlike the majority of fruit trees, figs bear fruit all year round, providing a reliable food source for many species. 與大多數果樹不同，無花果全年結果，為許多物種提供穩定的食物來源。 At this site, for example, after only three rainy seasons, monkeys started visiting to eat the fig fruits, naturally dispersing seeds through defecation. 例如在這個地點，僅僅三個雨季後，猴子就開始來吃無花果，並透過排便自然散播種子。 Reforestation projects should always aim to make sure that local communities are consulted and involved in the decision-making process. 再造林計畫應始終確保諮詢當地社區，並讓他們參與決策過程。 The restoration of mangrove forests in Madagascar is an example of a project which has succeeded in creating real benefits for the community. 馬達加斯加紅樹林復育是一個成功為社區創造實際利益的計畫案例。 Destruction of the mangrove forests had a terrible impact on plant and animal life, and also badly affected the fishing industry, which was a major source of employment for local people living in coastal areas. 紅樹林遭破壞對動植物生命造成嚴重影響，也嚴重打擊漁業，而漁業是沿海地區當地居民的主要就業來源。 The reforestation project involved hiring local people to plant and care for the new mangrove trees. 這項再造林計畫雇用當地人種植並照顧新的紅樹林。 Millions of mangrove trees have now been planted which has resulted in the return of a healthy aquatic ecosystem. 如今已有數百萬棵紅樹林被種下，健康的水生生態系統也因此恢復。 The mangroves also act as a defence against the increased threat of flooding caused by climate change. 紅樹林也能抵禦氣候變化導致的洪水風險增加。 What's more, the local economy is more stable and thousands more Madagascans are now able to send their children to school. 此外，當地經濟更加穩定，也有更多馬達加斯加人現在能送孩子上學。 One other important point to consider... 另一個需要考慮的重要點是 ……

entries.title: Listening Practice 9
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Part 1 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Transport Survey Name: Sadie Jones Year of birth: 1991 Postcode: 1 __________ Travelling by bus ● Date of bus journey: 2 __________ ● Reason for trip: shopping and visit to the 3 __________ ● Travelled by bus because cost of 4 __________ too high ● Got on bus at 5 __________ Street ● Complaints about bus service: ○ bus today was 6 __________ ○ frequency of buses in the 7 __________ Travelling by car ● Goes to the 8 __________ by car Travelling by bicycle ● Dislikes travelling by bike in the city centre because of the 9 __________ ● Doesn’t own a bike because of a lack of 10 __________ Postcode: 1 __________ ● Date of bus journey: 2 __________ ● Reason for trip: shopping and visit to the 3 __________ ● Travelled by bus because cost of 4 __________ too high ● Got on bus at 5 __________ Street ○ bus today was 6 __________ ○ frequency of buses in the 7 __________ ● Goes to the 8 __________ by car ● Dislikes travelling by bike in the city centre because of the 9 __________ ● Doesn’t own a bike because of a lack of 10 __________ MAN: Excuse me. Would you mind if I asked you some questions? 男士：不好意思。你介意我問你幾個問題嗎？ We’re doing a survey on transport. 我們正在做一項關於交通的調查。 SADIE: Yes, that’s OK. Sadie：可以，沒問題。 MAN: First of all, can I take your name? 男士：首先，可以請問你的姓名嗎？ SADIE: Yes. It’s Sadie Jones. Sadie：可以。我叫 Sadie Jones 。 MAN: Thanks very much. 男士：非常感謝。 And could I have your date of birth – just the year will do, actually. 可以請問你的出生日期嗎？ 其實只要年份就可以。 Is that all right? 這樣可以嗎？ SADIE: Yes, that’s fine. It’s 1991. Sadie：可以，沒問題。是 1991 年。 MAN: So next your postcode, please. 男士：接下來請告訴我你的郵遞區號。 SADIE: It’s DW30 7YZ. Sadie：是 DW30 7YZ。 MAN: Great. Thanks. Is that in Wells? 男士：太好了，謝謝。那是在 Wells 嗎？ SADIE: No, it’s actually in Harborne – Wells isn’t far from there, though. Sadie：不是，其實是在 Harborne，不過 Wells 離那裡不遠。 MAN: I really like that area. 男士：我很喜歡那一區。 My grandmother lived there when I was a kid. 我小時候，我祖母住在那裡。 SADIE: Yes, it is nice. Sadie：是啊，那裡很不錯。 MAN: Right, so now I want to ask you some questions about how you travelled here today. 男士：好的，現在我想問你一些關於今天怎麼來這裡的問題。 Did you use public transport? 你有使用公共交通嗎？ SADIE: Yes. I came by bus. Sadie：有。我是搭公車來的。 MAN: OK. And that was today. 男士：好的。那是今天。 It’s the 24th of April, isn’t it? 今天是 4 月 24 日，對吧？ SADIE: Isn’t it the 25th? Sadie：不是 25 日嗎？ No, actually, you’re right. 不，其實你是對的。 MAN: Ha ha. And what was the reason for your trip today? 男士：哈哈。那你今天出行的原因是什麼？ I can see you’ve got some shopping with you. 我看到你有買一些東西。 SADIE: Yes. I did some shopping but the main reason I came here was to go to the dentist. Sadie：是的。我買了些東西， 但我今天來這裡的主要原因是去看牙醫。 MAN: That’s not much fun. 男士：那可不太有趣。 Hope it was nothing serious. 希望不是什麼嚴重問題。 SADIE: No, it was just a check-up. It’s fine. Sadie：不是，只是例行檢查。 沒事。 MAN: Good. Do you normally travel by bus into the city centre? 男士：那就好。你平常也搭公車進市中心嗎？ SADIE: Yes. I stopped driving in ages ago because parking was so difficult to find and it costs so much. Sadie：是的。我很久以前就不開車進城了，因為停車位很難找，而且費用很高。 MAN: I see. 男士：我明白。 SADIE: The bus is much more convenient too. Sadie：公車也方便多了。 It only takes about 30 minutes. 只需要大約 30 分鐘。 MAN: That’s good. So where did you start your journey? 男士：那很好。那你今天是從哪裡開始搭車的？ SADIE: At the bus stop on Claxby Street. Sadie：在 Claxby Street 的公車站。 MAN: Is that C-L-A-X-B-Y? 男士：是 C-L-A-X-B-Y 嗎？ SADIE: That’s right. Sadie：沒錯。 MAN: And how satisfied with the service are you? 男士：那你對公車服務滿意嗎？ Do you have any complaints? 有什麼不滿嗎？ SADIE: Well, as I said, it’s very convenient and quick when it’s on time, but this morning it was late. Sadie：嗯，就像我說的，如果準時的話，它非常方便又快速，但今天早上它晚點了。 Only about 10 minutes, but still. 雖然只晚了大約 10 分鐘，但還是有點煩。 MAN: Yes, I understand that’s annoying. 男士：是的，我理解，那確實令人不快。 And what about the timetable? 那時刻表方面呢？ Do you have any comments about that? 你有什麼看法嗎？ SADIE: Mmm. I suppose I mainly use the bus during the day, but any time I’ve been in town in the evening – for dinner or at the cinema – I’ve noticed you have to wait a long time for a bus – there aren’t that many. Sadie：嗯。我主要是在白天搭公車，但只要晚上到城裡吃飯或看電影，我就發現要等很久才有公車，晚上班次不多。 MAN: OK, thanks. So now I’d like to ask you about your car use. 男士：好的，謝謝。那現在我想問你關於開車的情況。 SADIE: Well, I have got a car but I don’t use it that often. Sadie：嗯，我有車，但不常用。 Mainly just to go to the supermarket. But that’s about it really. 主要只是去超市時開，基本上就是這樣。 My husband uses it at the weekends to go to the golf club. 我丈夫週末會開它去高爾夫俱樂部。 MAN: And what about a bicycle? 男士：那自行車呢？ SADIE: I don’t actually have one at the moment. Sadie：我目前其實沒有自行車。 MAN: What about the city bikes you can rent? 男士：那可以租的城市自行車呢？ Do you ever use those? 你有用過嗎？ SADIE: No – I’m not keen on cycling there because of all the pollution. Sadie：沒有。我不太想在那裡騎車，因為污染太嚴重。 But I would like to get a bike – it would be good to use it to get to work. 不過我想買一輛自行車，用它上班應該不錯。 MAN: So why haven’t you got one now? 男士：那你為什麼現在還沒有呢？ SADIE: Well, I live in a flat – on the second floor and it doesn’t have any storage – so we’d have to leave it in the hall outside the flat. Sadie：嗯，我住在公寓二樓， 而且沒有儲藏空間，所以我們只能把自行車放在公寓外面的走廊。 MAN: I see. OK. Well, I think that’s all... 男士：我明白。好的，我想問題就到這裡……

entries.title: Listening Practice 9
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–13 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Becoming a Volunteer for ACE 11. Why does the speaker apologise about the seats? A. They are too small. B. There are not enough of them. C. Some of them are very close together. 12. What does the speaker say about the age of volunteers? A. The age of volunteers is less important than other factors. B. Young volunteers are less reliable than older ones. C. Most volunteers are about 60 years old. 13. What does the speaker say about training? A. It is continuous. B. It is conducted by a manager. C. It takes place online. Questions 14 and 15 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO issues does the speaker ask the audience to consider before they apply to be volunteers? A. their financial situation B. their level of commitment C. their work experience D. their ambition E. their availability Questions 16–20 What does the speaker suggest would be helpful for each of the following areas of voluntary work? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 16–20. Helpful things volunteers might offer A. experience on stage B. original, new ideas C. parenting skills D. an understanding of food and diet E. retail experience F. a good memory G. a good level of fitness Area of voluntary work 16. Fundraising __________ 17. Litter collection __________ 18. “Playmates” __________ 19. Story club __________ 20. First aid __________ Why does the speaker apologise about the seats? They are too small. There are not enough of them. Some of them are very close together. What does the speaker say about the age of volunteers? The age of volunteers is less important than other factors. Young volunteers are less reliable than older ones. Most volunteers are about 60 years old. What does the speaker say about training? It is continuous. It is conducted by a manager. It takes place online. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO issues does the speaker ask the audience to consider before they apply to be volunteers? their financial situation their level of commitment their work experience their ambition their availability Fundraising experience on stage original, new ideas parenting skills an understanding of food and diet retail experience a good memory a good level of fitness Litter collection experience on stage original, new ideas parenting skills an understanding of food and diet retail experience a good memory a good level of fitness “Playmates” experience on stage original, new ideas parenting skills an understanding of food and diet retail experience a good memory a good level of fitness Story club experience on stage original, new ideas parenting skills an understanding of food and diet retail experience a good memory a good level of fitness First aid experience on stage original, new ideas parenting skills an understanding of food and diet retail experience a good memory a good level of fitness Good evening, everyone. Let me start by welcoming you all to this talk and thanking you for taking the time to consider joining ACE voluntary organisation. 各位晚上好。首先歡迎大家來參加這場說明會，也感謝你們花時間考慮加入 ACE 志工組織。 ACE offers support to people and services in the local area and we’re now looking for more volunteers to help us do this. ACE 為當地居民和服務項目提供支援，我們現在正在尋找更多志工來協助這項工作。 By the way, I hope you’re all comfortable – we have brought in extra seats so that no one has to stand, but it does mean that the people at the back of the room may be a bit squashed. 順便說一下，希望大家都坐得舒服。我們加了額外座位，這樣就沒有人需要站著，但這也表示房間後面的人可能會有點擠。 We’ll only be here for about half an hour so, hopefully, that’s OK. 我們大概只會在這裡待半小時，所以希望這樣還可以。 One of the first questions we’re often asked is how old you need to be to volunteer. 我們經常被問到的第一個問題之一，就是志工需要幾歲。 Well, you can be as young as 16 or you can be 60 or over; it all depends on what type of voluntary work you want to do. 嗯，你可以年輕到 16 歲，也可以是 60 歲以上；這完全取決於你想做哪一類志工工作。 Other considerations, such as reliability, are crucial in voluntary work and age isn’t related to these, in our experience. 根據我們的經驗，其他因素，例如可靠性，在志工工作中非常重要，而年齡與這些因素並沒有直接關係。 Another question we get asked relates to training. 我們被問到的另一個問題和培訓有關。 Well, there’s plenty of that and it’s all face-to-face. 培訓很多，而且都是面對面進行。 What’s more, training doesn’t end when you start working for us – it takes place before, during and after periods of work. 更重要的是，培訓不會在你開始為我們工作後就結束；它會在工作前、工作期間和工作後持續進行。 Often, it’s run by other experienced volunteers as managers tend to prefer to get on with other things. 通常，培訓由其他有經驗的志工負責，因為經理通常更願意去處理其他事情。 Now, I would ask you to consider a couple of important issues before you decide to apply for voluntary work. 現在，在你決定申請志工工作之前，我想請你考慮幾個重要問題。 We don’t worry about why you want to be a volunteer – people have many different reasons that range from getting work experience to just doing something they’ve always wanted to do. 我們不會太在意你想成為志工的原因；人們有各種不同理由， 從想獲得工作經驗，到只是想做一直想做的事情都有。 But it is critical that you have enough hours in the day for whatever role we agree is suitable for you – if being a volunteer becomes stressful then it’s best not to do it at all. 但關鍵是，你每天必須有足夠時間投入我們認為適合你的角色；如果當志工變成壓力，那最好就不要做。 You may think that your income is important, but we don’t ask about that. 你可能認為收入很重要，但我們不會詢問這一點。 It’s up to you to decide if you can work without earning money. 是否能做無薪工作，由你自己決定。 What we value is dedication. 我們重視的是投入和奉獻。 Some of our most loyal volunteers earn very little themselves but still give their full energy to the work they do with us. 我們一些最忠誠的志工本身收入很少，但仍然全心投入與我們一起做的工作。 OK, so let’s take a look at some of the work areas that we need volunteers for and the sort of things that would help you in those. 好的，接下來我們看看一些需要志工的工作領域，以及哪些能力會對這些工作有幫助。 You may wish simply to help us raise money. 你可能只是想幫我們籌款。 If you have the creativity to come up with an imaginative or novel way of fundraising, we’d be delighted, as standing in the local streets or shops with a collection box can be rather boring! 如果你有創意，能想出有想像力或新穎的籌款方式，我們會非常高興，因為拿著募款箱站在當地街道或商店裡可能相當無聊！ One outdoor activity that we need volunteers for is litter collection and for this it’s useful if you can walk for long periods, sometimes uphill. 我們需要志工參與的一項戶外活動是撿拾垃圾；這項工作需要能長時間步行，有時還要走上坡。 Some of our regular collectors are quite elderly, but very active and keen to protect the environment. 我們一些固定參與撿垃圾的志工年紀較大，但非常活躍，也很熱心保護環境。 If you enjoy working with children, we have three vacancies for what are called “playmates”. 如果你喜歡和孩子一起工作， 我們有三個「玩伴」志工空缺。 These volunteers help children learn about staying healthy through a range of out-of-school activities. 這些志工會透過一系列課外活動，幫助孩子學習如何保持健康。 You don’t need to have children yourself, but it’s good if you know something about nutrition and can give clear instructions. 你自己不一定要有孩子，但如果你懂一些營養知識，並能清楚給出指示，那會很有幫助。 If that doesn’t appeal to you, maybe you would be interested in helping out at our story club for disabled children, especially if you have done some acting. 如果這不吸引你，也許你會對協助我們的身心障礙兒童故事俱樂部感興趣，尤其是如果你有表演經驗的話。 We put on three performances a year based on books they have read and we’re always looking for support with the theatrical side of this. 我們每年會根據孩子們讀過的書演出三場表演，因此一直在尋找能協助戲劇方面的人。 The last area I’ll mention today is first aid. 今天我要提到的最後一個領域是急救。 Volunteers who join this group can end up teaching others in vulnerable groups who may be at risk of injury. 加入這個小組的志工，最後可能會教導那些有受傷風險的弱勢群體。 Initially, though, your priority will be to take in a lot of information and not forget any important steps or details. 不過一開始，你的首要任務是吸收大量資訊，並且不要忘記任何重要步驟或細節。 Right, so does anyone have any questions… 好的，那麼有人有問題嗎……
