entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–26 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Talk on Jobs in Fashion Design 21. What problem did Chantal have at the start of the talk? A. Her view of the speaker was blocked. B. She was unable to find an empty seat. C. The students next to her were talking. 22. What were Hugo and Chantal surprised to hear about the job market? A. It has become more competitive than it used to be. B. There is more variety in it than they had realised. C. Some areas of it are more exciting than others. 23. Hugo and Chantal agree that the speaker’s message was A. unfair to them at times. B. hard for them to follow. C. critical of the industry. 24. What do Hugo and Chantal criticise about their school careers advice? A. when they received the advice B. how much advice was given C. who gave the advice 25. When discussing their future, Hugo and Chantal disagree on A. which is the best career in fashion. B. when to choose a career in fashion. C. why they would like a career in fashion. 26. How does Hugo feel about being an unpaid assistant? A. He is realistic about the practice. B. He feels the practice is dishonest. C. He thinks others want to change the practice. Questions 27 and 28 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO mistakes did the speaker admit she made in her first job? A. being dishonest to her employer B. paying too much attention to how she looked C. expecting to become well known D. trying to earn a lot of money E. openly disliking her client Questions 29 and 30 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO pieces of retail information do Hugo and Chantal agree would be useful? A. the reasons people return fashion items B. how much time people have to shop for clothes C. fashion designs people want but can’t find D. the best time of year for fashion buying E. the most popular fashion sizes What problem did Chantal have at the start of the talk? Her view of the speaker was blocked. She was unable to find an empty seat. The students next to her were talking. What were Hugo and Chantal surprised to hear about the job market? It has become more competitive than it used to be. There is more variety in it than they had realised. Some areas of it are more exciting than others. Hugo and Chantal agree that the speaker’s message was unfair to them at times. hard for them to follow. critical of the industry. What do Hugo and Chantal criticise about their school careers advice? when they received the advice how much advice was given who gave the advice When discussing their future, Hugo and Chantal disagree on which is the best career in fashion. when to choose a career in fashion. why they would like a career in fashion. How does Hugo feel about being an unpaid assistant? He is realistic about the practice. He feels the practice is dishonest. He thinks others want to change the practice. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO mistakes did the speaker admit she made in her first job? being dishonest to her employer paying too much attention to how she looked expecting to become well known trying to earn a lot of money openly disliking her client Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO pieces of retail information do Hugo and Chantal agree would be useful? the reasons people return fashion items how much time people have to shop for clothes fashion designs people want but can’t find the best time of year for fashion buying the most popular fashion sizes HUGO: Hi Chantal. What did you think of the talk, then? Hugo：嗨，Chantal。你覺得這場講座怎麼樣？ CHANTAL: Hi Hugo. I thought it was good once I’d moved seats. Chantal：嗨，Hugo。我換了座位之後覺得還不錯。 HUGO: Oh – were the people beside you chatting or something? Hugo：哦——你旁邊的人在聊天之類的嗎？ CHANTAL: It wasn’t that. Chantal：不是那樣。 I went early so that I’d get a seat and not have to stand, but then this guy sat right in front of me and he was so tall! 我很早就去了，這樣就能有座位、不用站著，但後來有個人坐在我正前方，而且他非常高！ HUGO: It’s hard to see through people’s heads, isn’t it? Hugo：要透過別人的頭看東西很難，對吧？ CHANTAL: Impossible! Anyway, to answer your question, I thought it was really interesting, especially what the speaker said about the job market. Chantal：根本不可能！不過回答你的問題，我覺得講座真的很有趣，尤其是講者談到就業市場的部分。 HUGO: Me too. I mean we know we’re going into a really competitive field so it’s obvious that we may struggle to get work. Hugo：我也是。我的意思是，我們知道自己要進入一個競爭非常激烈的領域，所以很明顯我們可能會很難找到工作。 CHANTAL: That’s right – and we know we can’t all have that “dream job”. Chantal：沒錯，而且我們也知道，不可能每個人都得到那份「夢想工作」。 HUGO: Yeah, but it looks like there’s a whole range of areas of work that we hadn’t even thought of – like fashion journalism, for instance. Hugo：是啊，但看起來有一整個範圍的工作領域是我們根本沒想過的，例如時尚新聞。 CHANTAL: Yeah – I wasn’t expecting so many career options. Chantal：是啊，我沒想到有這麼多職業選擇。 HUGO: Mmm. Overall, she had quite a strong message, didn’t she? Hugo：嗯。整體來說，她傳達的訊息相當強烈，不是嗎？ CHANTAL: She did. She kept saying things like “I know you all think this, but…” and then she’d tell us how it really is. Chantal：是的。她一直說像是「我知道你們都這麼想，但是……」然後就告訴我們實際情況是怎樣。 HUGO: Perhaps she thinks students are a bit narrow-minded about the industry. Hugo：也許她覺得學生對這個行業的看法有點狹隘。 CHANTAL: It was a bit harsh, though! Chantal：不過她說得有點嚴厲！ We know it’s a tough industry. 我們知道這是一個很艱難的行業。 HUGO: Yeah – and we’re only first years, after all. We’ve got a lot to learn. Hugo：是啊，而且畢竟我們才一年級。我們還有很多要學。 CHANTAL: Exactly. Do you think our secondary-school education should have been more career-focused? Chantal：正是如此。你覺得我們的中學教育應該更重視職業規劃嗎？ HUGO: Well, we had numerous talks on careers, which was good, but none of them were very inspiring. Hugo：嗯，我們當時有很多職業講座，這點很好，但沒有一場特別鼓舞人心。 They could have asked more people like today’s speaker to talk to us. 他們本可以請更多像今天這位講者一樣的人來跟我們談。 CHANTAL: I agree. We were told about lots of different careers – just when we needed to be, but not by the experts who really know stuff. Chantal：我同意。我們確實在需要的時候聽到了很多不同職業的介紹，但不是由真正懂這個行業的專家來講。 HUGO: So did today’s talk influence your thoughts on what career you’d like to take up in the future? Hugo：那今天的講座有影響你對未來想從事哪種職業的想法嗎？ CHANTAL: Well, I promised myself that I’d go through this course and keep an open mind till the end. Chantal：嗯，我答應過自己會完成這門課程，並一直保持開放心態直到最後。 HUGO: But I think it’s better to pick an area of the industry now and then aim to get better and better at it. Hugo：但我覺得最好現在就選定這個行業中的某個領域，然後努力在那方面越做越好。 CHANTAL: Well, I think we’ll just have to differ on that issue! Chantal：嗯，我想在這件事上我們只能保留不同看法了！ HUGO: One thing’s for certain, though. Hugo：不過有一件事是肯定的。 From what she said, we’ll be unpaid assistants in the industry for quite a long time. 按她所說，我們會在這個行業裡做很長一段時間的無薪助理。 CHANTAL: Mmm. Chantal：嗯。 HUGO: I’m prepared for that, aren’t you? Hugo：我已經做好準備了，你呢？ CHANTAL: Actually, I’m not going to accept that view. Chantal：其實，我不打算接受那種看法。 HUGO: Really? But she knows it’s the case – and everyone else says the same. Hugo：真的嗎？但她知道情況就是這樣，而且其他人也都這麼說。 CHANTAL: That doesn’t mean it has to be true for me. Chantal：那不代表對我來說也一定會是這樣。 HUGO: OK. Well – I hope you’re right! Hugo：好吧。嗯——希望你是對的！ CHANTAL: I thought the speaker’s account of her first job was fascinating. Chantal：我覺得講者講她第一份工作的經歷很吸引人。 HUGO: Yeah – she admitted she was lucky to get work being a personal dresser for a musician. Hugo：是啊，她承認自己很幸運，能得到一份為音樂家做私人造型師的工作。 She didn’t even apply for the job and there she was getting paid to choose all his clothes. 她甚至沒有申請那份工作，就這樣得到了替他挑選所有服裝並拿薪水的機會。 CHANTAL: It must have felt amazing – though she said all she was looking for back then was experience, not financial reward. Chantal：那感覺一定很棒，雖然她說當時自己追求的是經驗，而不是金錢回報。 HUGO: Mmm. And then he was so mean, telling her she was more interested in her own appearance than his! Hugo：嗯。然後他很刻薄，說她比起他的外表，更關心自己的外表！ CHANTAL: But – she did realise he was right about that, which really made me think. Chantal：但她確實意識到他在這點上是對的，這真的讓我思考很多。 I’m always considering my own clothes but now I can see you should be focusing on your client! 我總是在考慮自己的衣服，但現在我明白應該把注意力放在客戶身上！ HUGO: She obviously regretted losing the job. Hugo：她顯然很後悔失去那份工作。 CHANTAL: Well, as she said, she should have hidden her negative feelings about him, but she didn’t. Chantal：嗯，正如她所說，她本應隱藏自己對他的負面感受，但她沒有。 HUGO: It was really brave the way she picked herself up and took that job in retail. Hugo：她重新振作並接受零售工作的做法真的很勇敢。 Fancy working in a shop after that! 在那之後居然去商店工作！ CHANTAL: Yeah – well, she recommended we all do it at some point. Chantal：是啊，不過她建議我們每個人在某個階段都應該去做做看。 I guess as a designer you’d get to find out some useful information, like how big or small the average shopper is. 我想作為設計師，你能獲得一些有用資訊，例如一般顧客的身形大小。 HUGO: I think that’s an issue for manufacturers, not designers. Hugo：我認為那是製造商要考慮的問題，不是設計師。 However, it would be useful to know if there’s a gap in the market – you know, an item that no one’s stocking but that consumers are looking for. 不過，如果知道市場上有缺口會很有用——也就是某種消費者正在找、但沒有人供貨的商品。 CHANTAL: Yeah, people don’t give up searching. Chantal：是啊，人們不會放棄尋找。 They also take things back to the store if they aren’t right. 如果東西不合適，他們也會退回商店。 HUGO: Yeah. Imagine you worked in an expensive shop and you found out the garments sold there were being returned because they fell apart in the wash! Hugo：是啊。想像一下，如果你在一家高級商店工作，卻發現那裡賣的衣服因為洗了就散掉而被退回！ CHANTAL: Yeah, it would be good to know that kind of thing. Chantal：是啊，知道那種事情會很有用。 HUGO: Yeah. Hugo：是啊。

entries.title: Listening Practice 9
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Elephant Translocation Reasons for overpopulation at Majete National Park ● strict enforcement of anti-poaching laws ● successful breeding Problems caused by elephant overpopulation ● greater competition, causing hunger for elephants ● damage to 31 __________ in the park The translocation process ● a suitable group of elephants from the same 32 __________ was selected ● vets and park staff made use of 33 __________ to help guide the elephants into an open plain ● elephants were immobilised with tranquilisers: ○ this process had to be completed quickly to reduce 34 __________ ○ elephants had to be turned on their 35 __________ to avoid damage to their lungs ○ elephants’ 36 __________ had to be monitored constantly ○ tracking devices were fitted to the matriarchs ○ data including the size of their tusks and 37 __________ was taken ● elephants were taken by truck to their new reserve Advantages of translocation at Nkhotakota Wildlife Park ● 38 __________ opportunities ● a reduction in the number of poachers and 39 __________ ● an example of conservation that other parks can follow ● an increase in 40 __________ as a contributor to GDP ● damage to 31 __________ in the park ● a suitable group of elephants from the same 32 __________ was selected ● vets and park staff made use of 33 __________ to help guide the ○ this process had to be completed quickly to reduce 34 __________ ○ elephants had to be turned on their 35 __________ to avoid ○ elephants’ 36 __________ had to be monitored constantly ○ data including the size of their tusks and 37 __________ was ● 38 __________ opportunities ● a reduction in the number of poachers and 39 __________ ● an increase in 40 __________ as a contributor to GDP For my presentation today I want to tell you about how groups of elephants have been moved and settled in new reserves. 在今天的簡報中，我想介紹大象群是如何被遷移並安置到新的保護區的。 This is known as translocation and has been carried out in Malawi in Africa in recent years. 這被稱為遷地轉移，近年來已在非洲的馬拉威進行。 The reason this is being done is because of overpopulation of elephants in some areas. 進行這項工作的原因，是某些地區的大象數量過多。 Overpopulation is a good problem to have and not one we tend to hear about very often. 數量過多算是一種好問題，而且也不是我們經常聽到的問題。 In Malawi’s Majete National Park the elephant population had been wiped out by poachers, who killed the elephants for their ivory. 在馬拉威的 Majete National Park，大象族群曾被偷獵者消滅，他們為了象牙而獵殺大象。 But in 2003, the park was restocked and effective law enforcement was introduced. 但在 2003 年，公園重新引入大象，並實施了有效的執法措施。 Since then, not a single elephant has been poached. 從那以後，沒有一頭大象遭到偷獵。 In this safe environment, the elephant population boomed. 在這個安全的環境中，大象數量迅速增加。 Breeding went so well that there were more elephants than the park could support. 繁殖非常成功，以至於大象數量超過了公園能承載的範圍。 This led to a number of problems. 這導致了一些問題。 Firstly, there was more competition for food, which meant that some elephants were suffering from hunger. 首先，食物競爭變得更加激烈， 這意味著有些大象正在挨餓。 As there was a limit to the amount of food in the national park, some elephants began looking further afield. 由於國家公園內的食物有限， 一些大象開始到更遠的地方尋找食物。 Elephants were routinely knocking down fences around the park, which then had to be repaired at a significant cost. 大象經常撞倒公園周圍的圍欄，而這些圍欄之後必須花費大量資金修復。 To solve this problem, the decision was made to move dozens of elephants from Majete National Park to Nkhotakota Wildlife Park, where there were no elephants. 為了解決這個問題，人們決定將數十頭大象從 Majete National Park 遷移到沒有大象的 Nkhotakota Wildlife Park。 But, obviously, attempting to move significant numbers of elephants to a new home 300 kilometres away is quite a challenge. 但顯然，試圖把大量大象遷移到 300 公里外的新家，是一項相當大的挑戰。 So how did this translocation process work in practice? 那麼，這個遷地轉移過程實際上是如何運作的呢？ Elephants were moved in groups of between eight and twenty, all belonging to one family. 大象以 8 到 20 頭為一組進行遷移，且每組都屬於同一個家族。 Because relationships are very important to elephants, they all had to be moved at the same time. 因為關係對大象非常重要，所以牠們必須同時被轉移。 A team of vets and park rangers flew over the park in helicopters and targeted a group, which were rounded up and directed to a designated open plain. 一隊獸醫和公園巡護員乘坐直升機飛越公園，鎖定一組大象， 然後將牠們圍起來，引導到指定的開闊平原。 The vets then used darts to immobilise the elephants – this was a tricky manoeuvre, as they not only had to select the right dose of tranquiliser for different-sized elephants but they had to dart the elephants as they were running around. 接著獸醫使用飛鏢讓大象失去行動能力——這是一項棘手的操作，因為他們不僅要根據大象不同體型選擇合適的鎮靜劑劑量，還必須在大象四處奔跑時射中牠們。 This also had to be done as quickly as possible so as to minimise the stress caused. 這也必須盡快完成，以盡量減少造成的壓力。 As soon as the elephants began to flop onto the ground, the team moved in to take care of them. 大象一開始倒在地上，團隊就立刻靠近照料牠們。 To avoid the risk of suffocation, the team had to make sure none of the elephants were lying on their chests because their lungs could be crushed in this position. 為避免窒息風險，團隊必須確保沒有任何大象趴在胸部上， 因為這種姿勢可能會壓傷牠們的肺。 So all the elephants had to be placed on their sides. 因此所有大象都必須側躺。 One person stayed with each elephant while they waited for the vets to do checks. 在等待獸醫檢查時，每頭大象旁邊都有一個人陪著。 It was very important to keep an eye on their breathing – if there were fewer than six breaths per minute, the elephant would need urgent medical attention. 密切觀察牠們的呼吸非常重要 ——如果每分鐘少於六次呼吸，大象就需要緊急醫療處理。 Collars were fitted to the matriarch in each group so their movements could be tracked in their new home. 每組中的母象首領都被戴上項圈，這樣就可以追蹤牠們在新棲地中的活動。 Measurements were taken of each elephant’s tusks – elephants with large tusks would be at greater risk from poachers – and also of their feet. 工作人員測量了每頭大象的象牙，因為象牙較大的大象更容易遭到偷獵；同時也測量了牠們的腳。 The elephants were then taken to a recovery area before being loaded onto trucks and transported to their new home. 隨後，大象被帶到恢復區，然後裝上卡車，運往牠們的新家。 The elephants translocated to Nkhotakota settled in very well and the project has generally been accepted to have been a huge success – and not just for the elephants. 被遷移到 Nkhotakota 的大象適應得很好，而這個項目普遍被認為非常成功——而且不只是對大象而言。 Employment prospects have improved enormously, contributing to rising living standards for the whole community. 就業機會大幅改善，促進了整個社區生活水準的提高。 Poaching is no longer an issue, as former poachers are able to find more reliable sources of income. 偷獵不再是問題，因為過去的偷獵者現在能找到更可靠的收入來源。 In fact, many of them volunteered to give up their weapons, as they were no longer of any use to them. 事實上，他們當中許多人主動交出武器，因為那些武器對他們來說已經沒有用處。 More than two dozen elephants have been born at Nkhotakota since relocation. 自遷移以來，Nkhotakota 已有二十多頭大象出生。 With an area of more than 1,800 square kilometres, there’s plenty of space for the elephant population to continue to grow. 由於面積超過 1,800 平方公里， 這裡有足夠空間讓大象族群繼續增長。 Their presence is also helping to rebalance Nkhotakota’s damaged ecosystem and providing a sustainable conservation model, which could be replicated in other parks. 牠們的存在也有助於重新平衡 Nkhotakota 受損的生態系統， 並提供一種可持續的保育模式，可供其他公園借鑑。 All this has been a big draw for tourism, which contributes five times more than the illegal wildlife trade to GDP, and this is mainly because of the elephants. 這一切對旅遊業產生了巨大吸引力，而旅遊業對 GDP 的貢獻是非法野生動物貿易的五倍， 這主要是因為大象。 There’s also been a dramatic rise in interest... 人們對此的興趣也大幅增加……

entries.title: Listening Practice 10
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Part 1 Questions 1–5 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Working at Milo’s Restaurants Benefits ● 1 __________ provided for all staff ● 2 __________ during weekdays at all Milo’s Restaurants ● 3 __________ provided after midnight Person specification ● must be prepared to work well in a team ● must care about maintaining a high standard of 4 __________ ● must have a qualification in 5 __________ Practice 10, source question diagram/table, PDF page 5 ● 1 __________ provided for all staff ● 2 __________ during weekdays at all Milo’s Restaurants ● 3 __________ provided after midnight ● must care about maintaining a high standard of 4 __________ ● must have a qualification in 5 __________ Location: _____ Street Making sure _____ is clean Starting salary £ _____ per hour Maintaining stock and organising _____ No work on a _____ once a month WOMAN: So, I understand you're interested in restaurant work? 女士：好的，我了解到你對餐廳工作有興趣，對嗎？ MAN: Yes. I've got a bit of experience and I can provide references. 男士：是的。我有一些工作經驗，也可以提供推薦人資料。 WOMAN: That's good. I can check all that later. 女士：很好。那些我稍後可以再確認。 Now, Milo's Restaurants have some vacancies at the moment. 目前 Milo’s Restaurants 有一些職缺。 They're a really good company to work for. Lots of benefits. 他們是一家很好的公司，員工福利很多。 MAN: Oh right. 男士：哦，明白。 WOMAN: Yes. They've got a very good reputation for looking after staff. 女士：是的。他們在照顧員工方面口碑很好。 For example, all employees get training – even temporary staff. 例如，所有員工都會接受培訓，連臨時員工也包括在內。 MAN: Oh really? That's quite unusual, isn't it? 男士：真的嗎？那挺少見的， 不是嗎？ WOMAN: Certainly is. 女士：確實是。 MAN: And do staff get free uniforms too? 男士：那員工也會有免費制服嗎？ WOMAN: Um … you just need to wear a white T-shirt and black trousers, it says here. So I guess not … 女士：嗯……這裡寫著你只需要穿白色 T 恤和黑色長褲。所以我想應該沒有免費制服…… But another benefit of working for a big company like this is that you can get a discount at any of their restaurants. 不過，在這樣的大公司工作還有另一個好處，就是你可以在他們旗下任何一家餐廳享有折扣。 MAN: Even at weekends? 男士：週末也可以嗎？ WOMAN: No, but you'll be working then anyway. 女士：不行，不過反正你週末也會上班。 MAN: Oh yes. I suppose so. 男士：哦，是的。我想也是。 Most of their restaurants are in the city centre, aren't they? 他們大多數餐廳都在市中心， 對吧？ So, easy to get to by bus? 所以搭公車應該很方便？ WOMAN: Yes. That's right. 女士：是的，沒錯。 But if you have to do a late shift and finish work after midnight, the company will pay for you to get a taxi home. 但如果你上晚班，工作到午夜以後，公司會支付你搭計程車回家的費用。 MAN: I probably won't need one. 男士：我大概不需要。 I think I'd use my bike. 我想我會騎腳踏車。 WOMAN: OK. Now, they do have some quite specific requirements for the kind of person they're looking for. 女士：好的。現在，他們對想招聘的人確實有一些相當具體的要求。 Milo's is a young, dynamic company and they're really keen on creating a strong team. Milo’s 是一家年輕、有活力的公司，他們非常重視建立一支強大的團隊。 It's really important that you can fit in and get on well with everyone. 你能融入團隊並和大家相處融洽，這非常重要。 MAN: Yeah. I've got no problem with that. It sounds good, actually. 男士：可以。這方面我沒問題。 其實聽起來很不錯。 The last place I worked for was quite demanding too. 我上一份工作的地方要求也很高。 We had to make sure we gave a really high level of service. 我們必須確保提供非常高水準的服務。 WOMAN: That's good to hear because that will be equally important at Milo's. 女士：很高興聽你這麼說，因為這在 Milo’s 也同樣重要。 I know they want people who have an eye for detail. 我知道他們想要注重細節的人。 MAN: That's fine. I'm very used to working in that kind of environment. 男士：沒問題。我很習慣在那種環境中工作。 WOMAN: Perfect. So the only other thing that's required is good communication skills, so you'll need to have a certificate in English. 女士：太好了。唯一另一項要求是良好的溝通能力，所以你需要有英文證書。 MAN: Sure. 男士：好的。 WOMAN: OK. Let's have a look at the current job vacancies at Milo's. 女士：好。我們來看看 Milo’s 目前的職缺。 The first one is in Wivenhoe Street. 第一個在 Wivenhoe Street。 MAN: Sorry, where? 男士：抱歉，哪裡？ WOMAN: Wivenhoe. W-I-V-E-N-H-O-E. 女士：Wivenhoe， W-I-V-E-N-H-O-E。 It's quite central, just off Cork Street. 它位置很靠近市中心，就在 Cork Street 附近。 MAN: Oh right. 男士：哦，好的。 WOMAN: They're looking for a breakfast supervisor. 女士：他們正在招聘早餐主管。 MAN: That would be OK. 男士：那可以。 WOMAN: So you're probably familiar with the kind of responsibilities involved. 女士：那你可能熟悉這類工作的責任。 Obviously checking that all the portions are correct, etc., and then things like checking all the procedures for cleaning the equipment are being followed. 很明顯，要檢查所有餐點份量是否正確等等，還有確認設備清潔流程是否都有被遵守。 MAN: OK. And what about the salary? 男士：好的。薪水呢？ In my last job I was getting £9.50 per hour. 我上一份工作的時薪是 9.50 英鎊。 I was hoping to get a bit more than that. 我希望這次能比那個高一點。 WOMAN: Well, to begin with, you'd be getting £9.75 but that goes up to £11.25 after three months. 女士：嗯，一開始是每小時 9.75 英鎊，但三個月後會升到 11.25 英鎊。 MAN: That's not too bad. 男士：那還不錯。 And I suppose it's a very early start? 我想這份工作開始得很早吧？ WOMAN: Mmm. That's the only unattractive thing about this job. 女士：嗯。這是這份工作唯一不太吸引人的地方。 But then you have the afternoons and evenings free. 但這樣你下午和晚上就有空。 So the restaurant starts serving breakfast from 7 a.m. 餐廳早上 7 點開始供應早餐。 And you'd have to be there at 5.30 to set everything up. 你必須 5 點半到那裡，把一切準備好。 But you'd be finished at 12.30. 但你 12 點半就下班了。 MAN: Mmm. Well, as you say, there are advantages to that. 男士：嗯。就像你說的，那也有好處。 WOMAN: Now, you might also be interested in the job at the City Road branch. 女士：另外，你可能也會對 City Road 分店的工作感興趣。 That's for a junior chef, so again a position of responsibility. 那是初級廚師的職位，所以同樣是有責任的職位。 MAN: I might prefer that, actually. 男士：其實我可能更喜歡那個。 WOMAN: Right, well obviously this role would involve supporting the sous chef and other senior staff. 女士：好的，這個職位顯然需要協助副主廚和其他資深員工。 And you'd be responsible for making sure there's enough stock each week – and sorting out all the deliveries. 你還要負責確保每週庫存充足，並整理所有送貨。 MAN: I've never done that before, but I imagine it's fairly straightforward, once you get the hang of it. 男士：我以前沒做過這個，但我想一旦上手，應該相當簡單。 WOMAN: Yes, and you'd be working alongside more experienced staff to begin with, so I'm sure it wouldn't be a problem. 女士：是的，而且一開始你會和更有經驗的員工一起工作， 所以我相信這不會是問題。 The salary's slightly higher here. 這個職位的薪水稍微高一些。 It's an annual salary of £23,000. 年薪是 23,000 英鎊。 MAN: Right. 男士：好的。 WOMAN: I know that if they like you, it's likely you'll be promoted quite quickly. 女士：我知道如果他們欣賞你，你很可能很快會升職。 So that's worth thinking about. 所以這值得考慮。 MAN: Yes. It does sound interesting. 男士：是的。聽起來確實很有意思。 What are the hours like? 工作時間怎麼樣？ WOMAN: The usual, I think. 女士：我想是一般時間。 There's a lot of evening and weekend work, but they're closed on Mondays. 晚上和週末工作比較多，但他們星期一不營業。 But you do get one Sunday off every four weeks. 不過你每四週可以休一個星期天。 So would you like me to send off your … 那你要我幫你送出你的……

entries.title: Listening Practice 10
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11 and 12 Choose TWO letters, A–E. What are the TWO main reasons why this site has been chosen for the housing development? A. It has suitable geographical features. B. There is easy access to local facilities. C. It has good connections with the airport. D. The land is of little agricultural value. E. It will be convenient for workers. Questions 13 and 14 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO aspects of the planned housing development have people given positive feedback about? A. the facilities for cyclists B. the impact on the environment C. the encouragement of good relations between residents D. the low cost of all the accommodation E. the rural location Questions 15–20 Label the map below. Write the correct letter, A–I, next to Questions 15–20. 15. School __________ 16. Sports centre __________ 17. Clinic __________ 18. Community centre __________ 19. Supermarket __________ 20. Playground __________ Practice 10, source question diagram/table, PDF page 8 Choose TWO letters, A–E. What are the TWO main reasons why this site has been chosen for the housing development? It has suitable geographical features. There is easy access to local facilities. It has good connections with the airport. The land is of little agricultural value. It will be convenient for workers. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO aspects of the planned housing development have people given positive feedback about? the facilities for cyclists the impact on the environment the encouragement of good relations between residents the low cost of all the accommodation the rural location School A B C D E F G H I Sports centre A B C D E F G H I Clinic A B C D E F G H I Community centre A B C D E F G H I Supermarket A B C D E F G H I Playground A B C D E F G H I Hello everyone. 大家好。 It's good to see that so many members of the public have shown up for our presentation on the new housing development planned on the outskirts of Nunston. 很高興看到這麼多民眾來參加我們關於 Nunston 郊區新住宅開發計畫的介紹會。 I'm Mark Reynolds and I'm Communications Manager at the development. 我是 Mark Reynolds，是這個開發項目的傳訊經理。 I'll start by giving you a brief overview of our plans for the development. 我會先簡要介紹一下我們的開發計畫。 So one thing I'm sure you'll want to know is why we've selected this particular site for a housing development. 我相信你們一定想知道，我們為什麼選擇這個特定地點來做住宅開發。 At present it's being used for farming, like much of the land around Nunston. 目前這片土地和 Nunston 周圍許多土地一樣，被用於農業。 But because of the new industrial centre in Nunston, there's a lot of demand for housing for employees in the region, as many employees are having to commute long distances at present. 但由於 Nunston 新建了工業中心，該地區員工對住房有很大需求，因為目前許多員工不得不長距離通勤。 Of course, there's also the fact that we have an international airport just 20 minutes' drive away, but although that's certainly convenient, it wasn't one of our major criteria for choosing the site. 當然，這裡距離國際機場只有 20 分鐘車程，這確實很方便， 但那並不是我們選址的主要標準之一。 We were more interested in the fact that there's an excellent hospital just 15 kilometres away, and a large secondary school even closer than that. 我們更看重的是，距離這裡 15 公里處有一家很好的醫院，而且還有一所大型中學，距離更近。 One drawback to the site is that it's on quite a steep slope, but we've taken account of that in our planning so it shouldn't be a major problem. 這個地點的一個缺點是位於相當陡的斜坡上，但我們在規劃中已經考慮到這一點，所以應該不會是大問題。 We've had a lot of positive feedback about the plans. 我們收到了許多關於這些計畫的正面回饋。 People like the wide variety of accommodation types and prices, and the fact that it's only a short drive to get out into the countryside from the development. 人們喜歡住宿類型和價格的多樣性，也喜歡從開發區開車很短時間就能到鄉村。 We were particularly pleased that so many people liked the designs for the layout of the development. 我們特別高興有這麼多人喜歡開發區的布局設計。 The majority of people said it generally made a good impression and blended in well with the natural features of the landscape, with provision made for protecting trees and wildlife on the site. 大多數人表示，整體設計給人良好印象，並且與景觀的自然特色融合得很好，同時也規劃了保護場地內樹木和野生動物的措施。 Some people have mentioned that they'd like to see more facilities for cyclists, and we'll look at that. 有些人提到希望看到更多自行車相關設施，我們會考慮這一點。 But the overall feedback has been that the design and facilities of the development make it seem a place where people of all ages can live together happily. 不過整體回饋是，這個開發區的設計和設施讓它看起來像是一個各年齡層的人都能愉快共住的地方。 OK. So I'll put a map of the proposed development up on the screen. 好的。現在我會把擬議開發區的地圖放到螢幕上。 You'll see it's bounded on the south side by the main road, which then goes on to Nunston. 你們會看到，它南側以主路為界，而這條主路通往 Nunston 。 Another boundary is formed by London Road, on the western side of the development. 另一條邊界是 London Road， 位於開發區西側。 Inside the development there'll be about 400 houses and 3 apartment blocks. 開發區內將有大約 400 棟房屋和 3 棟公寓樓。 There'll also be a school for children up to 11 years old. 也會有一所供 11 歲以下兒童就讀的學校。 If you look at the South Entrance at the bottom of the map, there's a road from there that goes right up through the development. 如果你們看地圖底部的南入口，會看到有一條路從那裡一路向上穿過開發區。 The school will be on that road, at the corner of the second turning to the left. 學校會在那條路上，位於第二個左轉路口的角落。 A large sports centre is planned with facilities for indoor and outdoor activities. 我們計畫建一座大型運動中心，配備室內和戶外活動設施。 This will be on the western side of the development, just below the road that branches off from London Road. 它會位於開發區西側，就在從 London Road 分出來的道路下方。 There'll be a clinic where residents can go if they have any health problems. 這裡也會有一間診所，居民有健康問題時可以前往。 Can you see the lake towards the top of the map? 你們能看到地圖上方附近的湖嗎？ The clinic will be just below this, to the right of a street of houses. 診所就在湖的下方，位於一排房屋街道的右側。 There'll also be a community centre for people of all ages. 這裡也會有一座適合各年齡層使用的社區中心。 On the northeast side of the development, there'll be a row of specially designed houses specifically for residents over 65, and the community centre will be adjoining this. 在開發區東北側，會有一排專為 65 歲以上居民設計的房屋， 社區中心將與它相鄰。 We haven't forgotten about shopping. 我們也沒有忘記購物需求。 There'll be a supermarket between the two entrances to the development. 在開發區兩個入口之間會有一家超市。 We're planning to leave the three large trees near London Road, and it'll be just to the south of these. 我們計畫保留 London Road 附近的三棵大樹，而超市就在這些樹的南邊。 It's planned to have a playground for younger children. 我們也計畫設置一個給年幼兒童使用的遊樂場。 If you look at the road that goes up from the South Entrance, you'll see it curves round to the left at the top, and the playground will be in that curve, with nice views of the lake. 如果你們看從南入口向上延伸的那條路，會看到它在上方往左彎，遊樂場就在那個彎道裡，還可以看到很美的湖景。 OK, so now does anyone … 好的，那麼現在有人……

entries.title: Listening Practice 10
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–24 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 21. Why do the students think the Laki eruption of 1783 is so important? A. It was the most severe eruption in modern times. B. It led to the formal study of volcanoes. C. It had a profound effect on society. 22. What surprised Adam about observations made at the time? A. the number of places producing them B. the contradictions in them C. the lack of scientific data to support them 23. According to Michelle, what did the contemporary sources say about the Laki haze? A. People thought it was similar to ordinary fog. B. It was associated with health issues. C. It completely blocked out the sun for weeks. 24. Adam corrects Michelle when she claims that Benjamin Franklin A. came to the wrong conclusion about the cause of the haze. B. was the first to identify the reason for the haze. C. supported the opinions of other observers about the haze. Questions 25 and 26 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO issues following the Laki eruption surprised the students? A. how widespread the effects were B. how long-lasting the effects were C. the number of deaths it caused D. the speed at which the volcanic ash cloud spread E. how people ignored the warning signs Questions 27–30 What comment do the students make about the impact of the Laki eruption on the following countries? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 27–30. Comments A. This country suffered the most severe loss of life. B. The impact on agriculture was predictable. C. There was a significant increase in deaths of young people. D. Animals suffered from a sickness. E. This country saw the highest rise in food prices in the world. F. It caused a particularly harsh winter. Countries 27. Iceland __________ 28. Egypt __________ 29. UK __________ 30. USA __________ Why do the students think the Laki eruption of 1783 is so important? It was the most severe eruption in modern times. It led to the formal study of volcanoes. It had a profound effect on society. What surprised Adam about observations made at the time? the number of places producing them the contradictions in them the lack of scientific data to support them According to Michelle, what did the contemporary sources say about the Laki haze? People thought it was similar to ordinary fog. It was associated with health issues. It completely blocked out the sun for weeks. Adam corrects Michelle when she claims that Benjamin Franklin came to the wrong conclusion about the cause of the haze. was the first to identify the reason for the haze. supported the opinions of other observers about the haze. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO issues following the Laki eruption surprised the students? how widespread the effects were how long-lasting the effects were the number of deaths it caused the speed at which the volcanic ash cloud spread how people ignored the warning signs Iceland This country suffered the most severe loss of life. The impact on agriculture was predictable. There was a significant increase in deaths of young people. Animals suffered from a sickness. This country saw the highest rise in food prices in the world. It caused a particularly harsh winter. Egypt This country suffered the most severe loss of life. The impact on agriculture was predictable. There was a significant increase in deaths of young people. Animals suffered from a sickness. This country saw the highest rise in food prices in the world. It caused a particularly harsh winter. UK This country suffered the most severe loss of life. The impact on agriculture was predictable. There was a significant increase in deaths of young people. Animals suffered from a sickness. This country saw the highest rise in food prices in the world. It caused a particularly harsh winter. USA This country suffered the most severe loss of life. The impact on agriculture was predictable. There was a significant increase in deaths of young people. Animals suffered from a sickness. This country saw the highest rise in food prices in the world. It caused a particularly harsh winter. ADAM: So, Michelle, shall we make a start on our presentation? Adam：那麼，Michelle，我們開始準備簡報吧？ We haven't got that much time left. 我們剩下的時間不多了。 MICHELLE: No, Adam. But at least we've done all the background reading. Michelle：是啊，Adam。不過至少我們已經完成所有背景閱讀了。 I found it really interesting – I'd never even heard of the Laki eruption before this. 我覺得這真的很有趣，在這之前我甚至從沒聽過 Laki 火山噴發。 ADAM: Me neither. Adam：我也沒有。 I suppose 1783 is a long time ago. 我想 1783 年確實是很久以前了。 MICHELLE: But it was a huge eruption and it had such devastating consequences. Michelle：但那是一次巨大的噴發，而且造成了毀滅性的後果。 ADAM: I know. Adam：我知道。 It was great there were so many primary sources to look at. 有這麼多原始資料可以看，真的很不錯。 It really gives you a sense of how catastrophic the volcano was. 這真的讓人感受到那次火山噴發有多災難性。 People were really trying to make sense of the science for the first time. 人們當時第一次真正試圖理解其中的科學。 MICHELLE: That's right. Michelle：沒錯。 But what I found more significant was how it impacted directly and indirectly on political events, as well as having massive social and economic consequences. 但我覺得更重要的是，它如何直接和間接影響政治事件，同時也造成巨大的社會和經濟後果。 ADAM: I know. That should be the main focus of our presentation. Adam：我知道。那應該是我們簡報的重點。 MICHELLE: The observations made by people at the time were interesting, weren't they? Michelle：當時人們做出的觀察很有趣，不是嗎？ I mean, they all gave a pretty consistent account of what happened, even if they didn't always use the same terminology. 我的意思是，即使他們不一定使用相同術語，他們對發生的事情描述得相當一致。 ADAM: Yeah. I was surprised there were so many weather stations established by that time – so, you know, you can see how the weather changed, often by the hour. Adam：是啊。我很驚訝那時候已經建立了這麼多氣象站，所以你可以看到天氣如何變化， 而且常常是按小時記錄。 MICHELLE: Right. Writers at the time talked about the Laki haze to describe the volcanic fog that spread across Europe. Michelle：對。當時的作家用「 Laki haze」來形容蔓延到歐洲各地的火山霧。 They all realised that this wasn't the sort of fog they were used to – and of course this was in pre-industrial times – so they hadn't experienced sulphur-smelling fog before. 他們都意識到這不是他們習慣的普通霧，而且當時還是前工業時代，所以他們以前沒有經歷過帶硫磺味的霧。 ADAM: No, that's true. Adam：是啊，沒錯。 MICHELLE: Reports from the period blamed the haze for an increase in headaches, respiratory issues and asthma attacks. Michelle：當時的報告把頭痛、 呼吸系統問題和哮喘發作增加歸咎於這片霧霾。 And they all describe how it covered the sun and made it look a strange red colour. 他們也都描述它如何遮住太陽，讓太陽看起來呈現奇怪的紅色。 ADAM: Must have been very weird. Adam：那一定很詭異。 MICHELLE: It's interesting that Benjamin Franklin wrote about the haze. Michelle：有趣的是 Benjamin Franklin 也寫過這片霧霾。 Did you read that? 你有讀到嗎？ He was the American ambassador in Paris at the time. 他當時是美國駐巴黎大使。 ADAM: Yeah. At first no one realised that the haze was caused by the volcanic eruption in Iceland. Adam：有。起初沒有人意識到這片霧霾是由冰島火山噴發造成的。 MICHELLE: It was Benjamin Franklin who realised that before anyone else. Michelle：是 Benjamin Franklin 比任何人都先意識到這點。 ADAM: He's often credited with that, apparently. Adam：顯然，人們常把這個功勞歸給他。 But a French naturalist beat him to it – I can't remember his name. 但其實一位法國博物學家比他更早指出這點——我不記得那人的名字了。 I'd have to look it up. 我得查一下。 Then other naturalists had the same idea – all independently of each other. 後來其他博物學家也有相同想法，而且都是彼此獨立提出的。 MICHELLE: Oh right. We should talk about the immediate impact of the eruption, which was obviously enormous – especially in Iceland, where so many people died. Michelle：哦，對。我們應該談談火山噴發的直接影響，這顯然非常巨大，尤其是在冰島，那裡死了很多人。 ADAM: Mmm. You'd expect that – and the fact that the volcanic ash drifted so swiftly – but not that the effects would go on for so long. Adam：嗯。這一點可以預料， 還有火山灰迅速飄散也可以預料，但沒想到影響會持續那麼久。 Or that two years after the eruption, strange weather events were being reported as far away as North America and North Africa. 也沒想到噴發兩年後，遠至北美和北非都還有奇怪天氣事件的報告。 MICHELLE: No. I found all that hard to believe too. Michelle：是啊。我也覺得那些很難相信。 It must have been terrible – and there was nothing anyone could do about it, even if they knew the ash cloud was coming in their direction. 那一定很可怕，而且即使人們知道火山灰雲正朝他們的方向飄來，也完全無能為力。 MICHELLE: We should run through some of the terrible consequences of the eruption experienced in different countries. Michelle：我們應該快速梳理一下不同國家經歷的可怕後果。 There's quite a varied range. 影響範圍相當多樣。 ADAM: Starting with Iceland, where the impact on farming was devastating. Adam：先從冰島開始，那裡農業受到毀滅性打擊。 MICHELLE: Mmm. One of the most dramatic things there was the effect on livestock as they grazed in the fields. Michelle：嗯。那裡最劇烈的影響之一，是對在田野中吃草的牲畜造成的影響。 They were poisoned because they ate vegetation that had been contaminated with fluorine as a result of the volcanic fallout. 牠們中毒了，因為吃了被火山沉降物中的氟污染的植物。 ADAM: That was horrible. Adam：那太可怕了。 In Egypt, the bizarre weather patterns led to a severe drought and as a result the Nile didn't flood, which meant the crops all failed. 在埃及，異常天氣導致嚴重乾旱，結果尼羅河沒有氾濫，這表示農作物全部歉收。 MICHELLE: It's so far from where the eruption happened and yet the famine there led to more people dying than any other country. Michelle：埃及離火山噴發地那麼遠，但那裡的饑荒造成的死亡人數卻比任何其他國家都多。 It was worse than the plague. 情況比瘟疫還糟。 ADAM: OK. Then in the UK the mortality rate went up a lot – presumably from respiratory illnesses. Adam：好。接著在英國，死亡率大幅上升，推測是因為呼吸系統疾病。 According to one report it was about double the usual number and included an unusually high percentage of people under the age of 25. 根據一份報告，死亡人數約為平常的兩倍，而且 25 歲以下的人所占比例異常高。 MICHELLE: Mmm. I think people will be surprised to hear that the weather in the USA was badly affected too. Michelle：嗯。我想人們聽到美國天氣也受到嚴重影響時會很驚訝。 George Washington even makes a note in his diary that they were snowbound until March in Virginia. George Washington 甚至在日記中寫到，他們在 Virginia 一直被大雪困到三月。 That was before he became president. 那是在他成為總統之前。 ADAM: Yes, and there was ice floating down the Mississippi, which was unprecedented. Adam：是的，而且 Mississippi River 上還有浮冰，這是前所未有的。 MICHELLE: Astonishing, really. Anyway, what do you think … Michelle：真的很驚人。不管怎樣，你覺得……

entries.title: Listening Practice 10
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Pockets Reason for choice of subject ● They are 31 __________ but can be overlooked by consumers and designers. Pockets in men’s clothes ● Men started to wear 32 __________ in the 18th century. ● A 33 __________ sewed pockets into the lining of the garments. ● The wearer could use the pockets for small items. ● Bigger pockets might be made for men who belonged to a certain type of 34 __________. Pockets in women’s clothes ● Women’s pockets were less 35 __________ than men’s. ● Women were very concerned about pickpockets. ● Pockets were produced in pairs using 36 __________ to link them together. ● Pockets hung from the women’s 37 __________ under skirts and petticoats. ● Items such as 38 __________ could be reached through a gap in the material. ● Pockets, of various sizes, stayed inside clothing for many decades. ● When dresses changed shape, hidden pockets had a negative effect on the 39 __________ of women. ● Bags called “pouches” became popular, before women carried a 40 __________. ● They are 31 __________ but can be overlooked by consumers and ● Men started to wear 32 __________ in the 18th century. ● A 33 __________ sewed pockets into the lining of the garments. 34 __________. ● Women’s pockets were less 35 __________ than men’s. ● Pockets were produced in pairs using 36 __________ to link them ● Pockets hung from the women’s 37 __________ under skirts and ● Items such as 38 __________ could be reached through a gap in the 39 __________ of women. ● Bags called “pouches” became popular, before women carried a 40 __________. Good morning. 早安。 Now, we've been asked to choose an aspect of European clothing or fashion and to talk about its development over time. 我們被要求選擇歐洲服裝或時尚的一個方面，並談談它隨時間的發展。 I decided to focus on a rather small area of clothing and that's pockets. 我決定聚焦在服裝中一個相當小的部分，也就是口袋。 I chose pockets for two reasons, really. 我選擇口袋其實有兩個原因。 We all have them – in jeans, jackets, coats, for example – and even though we often carry bags or briefcases as well, nothing is quite as convenient as being able to pop your phone or credit card into your pocket. 我們都有口袋，例如牛仔褲、 夾克、外套上都有。即使我們也常常攜帶包包或公事包，但沒有什麼比把手機或信用卡直接放入口袋更方便。 Yet, I suspect that, other than that, people don't really think about pockets too much and they're rather overlooked as a fashion item. 然而，我認為除此之外，人們其實不太會特別思考口袋，而且口袋作為時尚元素也常被忽略。 It's certainly very interesting to go back in time and see how pockets developed for men and women. 回到過去看看男女服裝中口袋如何發展，確實非常有趣。 In the 18th century, fashions were quite different from the way they are now, and pockets were too. 在 18 世紀，時尚和現在非常不同，口袋也是如此。 If we think about male fashion first … that was the time when suits became popular. 如果我們先看男性時尚，那正是西裝開始流行的時期。 Trousers were knee-length only and referred to as ‘breeches’, the waistcoats were short and the jackets were long, but all three garments were lined with material and pockets were sewn into this cloth by whichever tailor the customer used. 當時褲子只到膝蓋，稱為 breeches；背心較短，外套較長，但這三種衣物都有內襯，而顧客所找的裁縫會把口袋縫進這些內襯布料中。 The wearer could then carry small objects such as pencils or coins on their person and reach them through a gap in the lining. 穿著者因此可以隨身攜帶鉛筆或硬幣等小物件，並透過內襯的開口拿取。 Coat pockets became increasingly decorative on the outside for men who wanted to look stylish. 對於想看起來時髦的男性來說，外套外側的口袋變得越來越具裝飾性。 But they were often larger but plainer if the wearer was someone with a profession who needed to carry medical instruments – a doctor or physician, for example. 但如果穿著者從事某種職業， 需要攜帶醫療器具，例如醫生或內科醫師，口袋通常會更大，但樣式更樸素。 The development of women's pockets was a little different. 女性口袋的發展則有些不同。 For one thing, they weren't nearly as visible or as easy to reach as men's. 首先，女性口袋遠不像男性口袋那樣明顯，也不如男性口袋那麼容易拿取。 In the 18th and 19th centuries, women carried numerous possessions on their person and some of these could be worth a lot of money. 在 18 和 19 世紀，女性會隨身攜帶許多物品，其中一些可能價值不菲。 Women were more vulnerable to theft and wealthy women, in particular, worried constantly about pickpockets. 女性更容易成為偷竊目標，尤其是富有女性，經常擔心扒手。 So – what they did was to have a pair of pockets made that were tied together with string. 所以她們會做一對口袋，並用繩子把它們連在一起。 The pockets were made of fabric, which might be recycled cloth if the wearer had little money or something more expensive, such as linen, sometimes featuring very delicate embroidery. 口袋由布料製成；如果穿著者經濟不寬裕，可能會使用回收布料，若較有錢則可能使用較昂貴的亞麻布，有時還會有非常精緻的刺繡。 Women tied the pockets around their waist so that they hung beneath their clothes. 女性會把口袋綁在腰間，讓它們垂掛在衣服下面。 Remember, skirts were long then and there was plenty of room to hide a whole range of small possessions between the layers of petticoats that were commonly worn. 要記得，當時裙子很長，而且常穿多層襯裙，因此有足夠空間在層層衣物之間藏放各種小物件。 They would have an opening in the folds of their skirts through which they could reach whatever they needed, like their perfume. 她們會在裙子的褶皺處留一個開口，透過那裡拿到需要的東西，例如香水。 Working women, of course, also needed to carry around items that they might use for whatever job or trade they were involved in. 當然，職業女性也需要隨身攜帶工作或生意中可能會用到的物品。 But their pairs of pockets still remained on the inside of their clothing, they just got bigger or longer – sometimes reaching down to their knees! 但她們的一對口袋仍然留在衣服內側，只是變得更大或更長，有時甚至垂到膝蓋！ So the tie-on pockets went well into the 19th century and only changed when fashion altered towards the end of that period. 因此，這種綁在身上的口袋一直延續到 19 世紀，直到該時期末期時尚發生變化才改變。 That's when dresses became tighter and less bulky, and the pairs of pockets became very noticeable – they stood out too much and detracted from the woman's image. 那時連身裙變得更貼身、不再那麼厚重，而成對口袋變得非常明顯，太過突出，影響了女性形象。 Women who had been used to carrying around a range of personal possessions – and still wanted to – needed somewhere to carry these items about their person. 已經習慣隨身攜帶各種私人物品，並且仍想繼續這樣做的女性，需要找到其他地方來攜帶這些物品。 That was when small bags, or pouches as they were known, came into fashion and, of course, they inevitably led on to the handbag of more modern times, particularly when fashion removed pockets altogether. 於是小包，也就是當時所稱的 pouches，開始流行起來；當然，尤其在時尚完全取消口袋之後，它們不可避免地發展成了更現代的手提包。

entries.title: Listening Practice 11
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Practice 11, source question diagram/table, PDF page 4 Practice 11, source question diagram/table, PDF page 4 Home address: 52 _____ Street, Peacetown Heard about us: from a _____ Question 3 — refer to the original question paper above. Type of membership: _____ membership (£30) Question 5 — refer to the original question paper above. Scene must show some _____ The _____ was wrong. ‘_____’ Scene must show _____ The photograph was too _____. BREDA: Hello, Wayside Camera Club, Breda speaking. Breda：您好，這裡是 Wayside Camera Club，我是 Breda。 DAN: Oh, hello, um, my name’s Dan and I’d like to join your club. Dan：哦，你好，嗯，我叫 Dan，我想加入你們的俱樂部。 BREDA: That’s great, Dan. Breda：太好了，Dan。 We have an application form – would you like to complete it over the phone, then you can ask any questions you might have? 我們有一份申請表——你想透過電話填寫嗎？這樣你有任何問題也可以順便問。 DAN: Oh, yes, thanks. Dan：哦，好的，謝謝。 BREDA: OK, so what’s your family name? Breda：好的，那你的姓氏是什麼？ DAN: It’s Green – Dan Green. Dan：是 Green，Dan Green。 BREDA: So – can I take your email address? Breda：那麼，可以告訴我你的電子郵件地址嗎？ DAN: Yes, it’s dan1068@market.com. Dan：可以，是 dan1068@market.com。 BREDA: Thanks. And what about your home address? Breda：謝謝。那你的住址呢？ DAN: Well, I’m about ten miles away from your club in Peacetown. Dan：嗯，我住在 Peacetown，離你們俱樂部大約十英里。 I live in a house there. 我住在那裡的一棟房子裡。 BREDA: OK, so what’s the house number and street? Breda：好的，那門牌號和街道是什麼？ DAN: It’s 52 Marrowfield Street. Dan：是 Marrowfield Street 52 號。 BREDA: Is that M-A double R-O-W-F-I-E-L-D? Breda：是 M-A，兩個 R， O-W-F-I-E-L-D 嗎？ DAN: That’s right. Dan：沒錯。 BREDA: … and that’s Peacetown, you said? Breda：……你剛才說是在 Peacetown ，對嗎？ DAN: Uhuh. Dan：嗯。 BREDA: So how did you hear about our club? Breda：那你是怎麼知道我們俱樂部的？ Did you look on the internet? 是在網路上看到的嗎？ DAN: I usually do that, but this time, well, I was talking to a relative the other day and he suggested it. Dan：我通常會上網查，但這次不是。前幾天我和一位親戚聊天，是他推薦的。 BREDA: Oh, is he a member too? Breda：哦，他也是會員嗎？ DAN: He belongs to another club – but he’d heard good things about yours. Dan：他是另一個俱樂部的會員，但他聽說你們俱樂部很不錯。 BREDA: OK. So what do you hope to get from joining? Breda：好的。那你希望加入後獲得什麼？ DAN: Well, one thing that really interests me is the competitions that you have. Dan：嗯，我很感興趣的一件事是你們舉辦的比賽。 I enjoy entering those. 我喜歡參加這類比賽。 BREDA: Right. Anything else? Breda：明白。還有其他原因嗎？ DAN: Well, I also like to socialise with other photographers. Dan：嗯，我也喜歡和其他攝影師交流。 BREDA: That’s great. So what type of membership would you like? Breda：很好。那你想申請哪一類會員？ DAN: What are the options? Dan：有哪些選項？ BREDA: It’s £30 a year for full membership or £20 a year if you’re an associate. Breda：正式會員一年 30 英鎊，準會員一年 20 英鎊。 DAN: I think I’ll go for the full membership, then. Dan：那我想我會選正式會員。 BREDA: That’s a good idea because you can’t vote in meetings with an associate membership. Breda：這是個好選擇，因為準會員在會議中不能投票。 BREDA: If I could just find out a bit more about you … Breda：如果可以的話，我想再多了解你一點…… DAN: OK. Dan：好的。 BREDA: So you said you wanted to compete – have you ever won any photography competitions? Breda：你剛才說你想參加比賽—— 你以前有贏過攝影比賽嗎？ DAN: Not yet, but I have entered three in the past. Dan：還沒有，但我過去參加過三次。 BREDA: Oh, that’s interesting. Breda：哦，那很有意思。 So why don’t you tell me something about those? 那你不妨跟我說說那些比賽。 Let’s start with the first one. 我們從第一個開始吧。 DAN: Well, the theme was entitled “Domestic Life”. Dan：嗯，主題叫做 “Domestic Life” 。 BREDA: I see – so it had to be something related to the home? Breda：我明白，所以必須是和家庭有關的內容？ DAN: Yeah. I chose to take a photo of a family sitting round the dinner table having a meal, and, um, I didn’t win, but I did get some feedback. Dan：是的。我選擇拍一家人圍坐在餐桌旁吃飯的照片，嗯，我沒有贏，但確實得到了一些回饋。 BREDA: Oh, what did the judges say? Breda：哦，評審怎麼說？ DAN: That it was too “busy” as a picture. Dan：他們說這張照片畫面太「雜亂」。 BREDA: Aha – so it was the composition of the picture that they criticised? Breda：啊哈，所以他們批評的是照片構圖？ DAN: That’s right – and once they’d told me that, I could see my mistake. Dan：沒錯。他們一說，我就看出自己的錯誤了。 BREDA: So what was the theme of the second competition? Breda：那第二次比賽的主題是什麼？ DAN: Well, my university was on the coast and that area gets a lot of beautiful sunsets, so that was the theme. Dan：嗯，我的大學在海邊，那一帶有很多美麗的日落，所以主題就是日落。 BREDA: Oh, sunsets, that’s a great theme. Breda：哦，日落，那是很棒的主題。 DAN: Yes. The instructions were to capture the clouds as well – it couldn’t just be blue sky and a setting sun. Dan：是的。規定還要求拍到雲，不能只有藍天和落日。 BREDA: Sure, cause they give you all those amazing pinks and purples. Breda：當然，因為雲會呈現那些很漂亮的粉色和紫色。 DAN: Yeah – and I thought I’d done that well, but the feedback was that I should have waited a bit longer to get the shot. Dan：是啊，我本來覺得自己做得不錯，但回饋說我應該再等久一點再拍。 BREDA: I see. So the timing wasn’t right. Breda：我明白。所以時機不太對。 DAN: Yes – I took it too soon, basically. Dan：是的，基本上就是我拍得太早了。 And then the third competition I entered was called “Animal Magic”. 然後我參加的第三個比賽叫做 “Animal Magic”。 BREDA: Well, that’s a difficult subject! Breda：嗯，那可是個困難的主題！ DAN: I know! I had to take hundreds of shots. Dan：我知道！我拍了好幾百張。 BREDA: I’m sure – because animals move all the time. Breda：我相信，因為動物一直在動。 DAN: That’s what we had to show – there had to be some movement in the scene. Dan：那正是我們必須呈現的內容 ——畫面中必須有某種動作。 I got a great shot of a fox in the end, but I took it at night and, well, I suspected that it was a bit dark, which is what I was told. 最後我拍到一張很棒的狐狸照片， 但那是在晚上拍的，而且我也懷疑它有點暗，結果評審也是這麼說的。 BREDA: Well Dan – you seem to be really keen and we’d be delighted to have you in our club. Breda：嗯，Dan，你看起來真的很熱衷攝影，我們會很高興你加入我們俱樂部。 I’m sure we can help with all those areas that you’ve outlined. 我相信我們可以幫助你改善剛才提到的那些方面。 DAN: Thanks, that’s great. Dan：謝謝，那太好了。

entries.title: Listening Practice 11
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11 and 12 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO warnings does Dan give about picking mushrooms? A. Don’t pick more than one variety of mushroom at a time. B. Don’t pick mushrooms near busy roads. C. Don’t eat mushrooms given to you. D. Don’t eat mushrooms while picking them. E. Don’t pick old mushrooms. Questions 13 and 14 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO ideas about wild mushrooms does Dan say are correct? A. Mushrooms should always be peeled before eating. B. Mushrooms eaten by animals may be unsafe. C. Cooking destroys toxins in mushrooms. D. Brightly coloured mushrooms can be edible. E. All poisonous mushrooms have a bad smell. Questions 15–20 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 15. What advice does Dan give about picking mushrooms in parks? A. Choose wooded areas. B. Don’t disturb wildlife. C. Get there early. 16. Dan says it is a good idea for beginners to A. use a mushroom app. B. join a group. C. take a reference book. 17. What does Dan say is important for conservation? A. selecting only fully grown mushrooms B. picking a limited amount of mushrooms C. avoiding areas where rare mushroom species grow 18. According to Dan, some varieties of wild mushrooms are in decline because there is A. a huge demand for them from restaurants. B. a lack of rain in this part of the country. C. a rise in building developments locally. 19. Dan says that when storing mushrooms, people should A. keep them in the fridge for no more than two days. B. keep them in a brown bag in a dark room. C. leave them for a period after washing them. 20. What does Dan say about trying new varieties of mushrooms? A. Experiment with different recipes. B. Expect some to have a strong taste. C. Cook them for a long time. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO warnings does Dan give about picking mushrooms? Don’t pick more than one variety of mushroom at a time. Don’t pick mushrooms near busy roads. Don’t eat mushrooms given to you. Don’t eat mushrooms while picking them. Don’t pick old mushrooms. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO ideas about wild mushrooms does Dan say are correct? Mushrooms should always be peeled before eating. Mushrooms eaten by animals may be unsafe. Cooking destroys toxins in mushrooms. Brightly coloured mushrooms can be edible. All poisonous mushrooms have a bad smell. What advice does Dan give about picking mushrooms in parks? Choose wooded areas. Don’t disturb wildlife. Get there early. Dan says it is a good idea for beginners to use a mushroom app. join a group. take a reference book. What does Dan say is important for conservation? selecting only fully grown mushrooms picking a limited amount of mushrooms avoiding areas where rare mushroom species grow According to Dan, some varieties of wild mushrooms are in decline because there is a huge demand for them from restaurants. a lack of rain in this part of the country. a rise in building developments locally. Dan says that when storing mushrooms, people should keep them in the fridge for no more than two days. keep them in a brown bag in a dark room. leave them for a period after washing them. What does Dan say about trying new varieties of mushrooms? Experiment with different recipes. Expect some to have a strong taste. Cook them for a long time. PRESENTER: This evening we’re delighted to welcome Dan Beagle, who’s just written a book on looking for and finding food in the wild. 主持人：今晚我們很高興歡迎 Dan Beagle，他剛寫了一本關於在野外尋找食物的書。 He’s going to tell us everything we need to know about picking wild mushrooms. 他將告訴我們採摘野生蘑菇需要知道的一切。 DAN: Thank you very much. Dan：非常感謝。 Well, I need to start by talking about safety. 嗯，我需要先從安全談起。 You really need to know what you’re doing because some mushrooms are extremely poisonous. 你真的需要知道自己在做什麼，因為有些蘑菇有劇毒。 Having said that, once you know what to look for, it’s really worth doing for the amazing variety of mushrooms available – which you can’t get in the shops. 話雖如此，一旦你知道該找什麼，這件事真的很值得做，因為野外有各式各樣令人驚喜的蘑菇，而這些在商店裡買不到。 But of course, you have to be very careful and that’s why I always say you should never consume mushrooms picked by friends or neighbours. 但當然，你必須非常小心，所以我總是說，絕對不要吃朋友或鄰居採來的蘑菇。 Always remember that some poisonous mushrooms look very similar to edible ones and it’s easy for people to get confused. 一定要記住，有些有毒蘑菇看起來和可食用蘑菇非常相似， 人們很容易混淆。 The other thing to avoid is mushrooms growing beside busy roads for obvious reasons. 另一件要避免的事，是採摘繁忙道路旁生長的蘑菇，原因很明顯。 But nothing beats the taste of freshly picked mushrooms – don’t forget that the ones in the shops are often several days old and past their best. 不過，新鮮採摘的蘑菇味道無可比擬。別忘了，商店裡的蘑菇通常已經放了好幾天，過了最佳狀態。 There are certain ideas about wild mushrooms that it’s important to be aware of. 有一些關於野生蘑菇的觀念很重要，大家需要了解。 Don’t listen to people who tell you that it’s only OK to eat mushrooms that are pale or dull – this is completely untrue. 如果有人告訴你只有顏色淡或暗沉的蘑菇才能吃，不要相信，這完全不正確。 Some edible mushrooms are bright red, for example. 例如，有些可食用蘑菇是鮮紅色的。 Personally, I prefer mushrooms cooked but it won’t do you any harm to eat them uncooked in salads – it’s not necessary to peel them. 就我個人而言，我比較喜歡吃煮熟的蘑菇，但把它們生吃放進沙拉裡也不會有害，而且不需要去皮。 Another thing you should remember is that you can’t tell if a mushroom is safe to eat by its smell. 你還應該記住另一點：不能靠氣味判斷蘑菇是否安全可食。 Some of the most deadly mushrooms have no smell and taste quite nice, apparently. 顯然，有些最致命的蘑菇沒有氣味，而且味道還相當不錯。 Finally, just because deer or squirrels eat a particular mushroom doesn’t mean that you can. 最後，鹿或松鼠能吃某種蘑菇，並不代表你也能吃。 Of course, mushroom picking is associated with the countryside but if you haven’t got a car, your local park can be a great place to start. 當然，採蘑菇通常讓人想到鄉村，但如果你沒有車，當地公園也可以是很好的起點。 There are usually a range of habitats where mushrooms grow, such as playing fields and wooded areas. 通常會有多種蘑菇生長的棲地，例如運動場和林地。 But you need to be there first thing in the morning, as there’s likely be a lot of competition – not just from people but wildlife too. 但你需要一大早就到，因為競爭可能很激烈，不只是人，還有野生動物。 The deer often get the best mushrooms in my local park. 在我當地的公園裡，最好的蘑菇常常被鹿吃掉。 If you’re a complete beginner, I wouldn’t recommend going alone or relying on photos in a book, even the one I’ve written! 如果你是完全的新手，我不建議你獨自前往，也不建議只依賴書上的照片，即使是我寫的那本書也一樣！ There are some really good phone apps for identifying mushrooms, but you can’t always rely on getting a good signal in the middle of a wood. 有些辨識蘑菇的手機應用程式真的很不錯，但你不能總是指望在樹林深處有良好訊號。 If possible, you should go with a group led by an expert – you’ll stay safe and learn a lot that way. 如果可能，你應該跟著由專家帶領的小組一起去，這樣既安全，也能學到很多。 Conservation is a really important consideration and you must follow a few basic rules. 保育是非常重要的考量，你必須遵守幾條基本規則。 You should never pick all the mushrooms in one area – collect only enough for your own needs. 你絕不應該把一個區域內的蘑菇全部採走，只採自己需要的量就好。 Be very careful that you don’t trample on young mushrooms or other plants. 要非常小心，不要踩到幼小蘑菇或其他植物。 And make sure you don’t pick any mushrooms that are endangered and protected by law. 也要確保不要採摘任何瀕危且受法律保護的蘑菇。 There’s been a decline in some varieties of wild mushrooms in this part of the country. 這個國家這一地區的一些野生蘑菇品種數量已經下降。 Restaurants are becoming more interested in locally sourced food like wild mushrooms, but the biggest problem is that so many new houses have been built in this area in the last ten years. 餐廳對野生蘑菇等本地食材越來越感興趣，但最大的問題是過去十年這一地區建了太多新房子。 And more water is being taken from rivers and reservoirs because of this, and mushroom habitats have been destroyed. 因此，更多水被從河流和水庫中取走，蘑菇棲地也遭到破壞。 Anyway, a word of advice on storing mushrooms. 無論如何，關於保存蘑菇，我有一點建議。 Collect them in a brown paper bag and as soon as you get home, put them in the fridge. 採摘時把它們放在棕色紙袋裡，一回到家就放進冰箱。 They’ll be fine for a couple of days, but it’s best to cook them as soon as possible – after washing them really carefully first, of course. 它們可以保存幾天，但最好盡快烹調，當然要先非常仔細地清洗。 So everybody knows what a mushroom tastes like, right? 大家都知道蘑菇是什麼味道， 對吧？ Well, you’ll be surprised by the huge variety of wild mushrooms there are. 嗯，野生蘑菇種類之多會讓你驚訝。 Be adventurous! They’re great in so many dishes – stir fries, risottos, pasta. 大膽嘗試吧！它們很適合做很多菜，例如炒菜、義式燉飯和義大利麵。 But just be aware that some people can react badly to certain varieties so it’s a good idea not to eat huge quantities to begin with. 但要注意，有些人可能會對某些品種有不良反應，所以一開始最好不要吃太多。 OK, so now I’m going to show you … 好的，那麼現在我要給大家看 ……

YOUNG MAN: That seminar yesterday on automation and the future of work was really good, wasn’t it? 男學生：昨天那場關於自動化和未來工作的研討會真的很棒，不是嗎？ Looking at the first industrial revolution in Britain in the 19th century and seeing how people reacted to massive change was a real eye-opener. 看看 19 世紀英國第一次工業革命，以及人們如何應對巨大變革，真的讓人大開眼界。 YOUNG WOMAN: Yes. It was interesting to hear how people felt about automation then and what challenges they faced. 女學生：是的。聽到當時人們如何看待自動化，以及他們面臨哪些挑戰，很有意思。 I didn’t know that first started with workers in the textile industry. 我以前不知道這最早是從紡織業工人開始的。 YOUNG MAN: With those protesting workers called the Luddites destroying their knitting machines because they were so worried about losing their jobs. 男學生：那些抗議的工人被稱為 Luddites，他們因為非常擔心失去工作，就摧毀自己的針織機。 YOUNG WOMAN: Yes, and ultimately, they didn’t achieve anything. 女學生：是的，而且最終他們什麼也沒達成。 And anyway, industrialisation created more jobs than it destroyed. 而且無論如何，工業化創造的工作比它摧毀的更多。 YOUNG MAN: Yes, that’s true – but it probably didn’t seem a positive thing at the time. 男學生：是的，這是真的，但在當時它大概看起來不是件好事。 I can see why the Luddites felt so threatened. 我能理解為什麼 Luddites 會覺得受到那麼大的威脅。 YOUNG WOMAN: I know. I’m sure I would have felt the same. 女學生：我知道。我相信我也會有同樣感受。 The discussion about the future of work was really optimistic for a change. 關於未來工作的討論這次難得很樂觀。 I like the idea that work won’t involve doing boring, repetitive tasks, as robots will do all that. 我喜歡那種未來工作不再包括無聊、重複性任務的想法，因為機器人會做那些事。 Normally, you only hear negative stuff about the future. 通常我們聽到的都是關於未來的負面內容。 YOUNG MAN: Bit too optimistic, don’t you think? 男學生：有點太樂觀了，你不覺得嗎？ For example, I can’t see how people are about to have more leisure time, when all the evidence shows people are spending longer than ever at work. 例如，所有證據都顯示人們花在工作上的時間比以往更長， 我看不出大家怎麼會突然有更多休閒時間。 YOUNG WOMAN: No – that’s true. 女學生：是啊，那是真的。 And what about lower unemployment? 那失業率降低呢？ I’m not so sure about that. 我對此也不太確定。 YOUNG MAN: Perhaps in the long term – but not in the foreseeable future. 男學生：也許長期來看會吧，但在可預見的未來不會。 YOUNG WOMAN: Mmm. And I expect most people will be expected to work until they’re much older – as everyone’s living much longer. 女學生：嗯。而且我預計大多數人會被要求工作到更老，因為大家壽命都變長了。 YOUNG MAN: That’s already happening. 男學生：這已經在發生了。 YOUNG WOMAN: I enjoyed all that stuff on how technology has changed some jobs and how they’re likely to change in the near future. 女學生：我很喜歡關於科技如何改變某些工作，以及這些工作在不久的將來可能如何改變的那些內容。 YOUNG MAN: Yeah, incredible. Like accountants. 男學生：是啊，很不可思議。像會計師。 You might think all the technological innovations would have put them out of a job, but in fact there are more of them than ever. 你可能會以為所有技術創新會讓他們失業，但事實上會計師的人數比以往更多。 They’re still really in demand and have become far more efficient. 他們仍然非常搶手，而且效率也高得多。 YOUNG WOMAN: Right. That was amazing. 女學生：對，這很驚人。 Twenty times more accountants in this country compared to the 19th century. 這個國家的會計師人數比 19 世紀多了 20 倍。 YOUNG MAN: I know. I’d never have thought that demand for hairdressing would have gone up so much in the last hundred years. 男學生：我知道。我從沒想過過去一百年裡，對美髮服務的需求會增加這麼多。 One hairdresser for every 287 people now, compared to one for over 1,500. 現在每 287 人就有一名美髮師，而以前是超過 1,500 人才有一名。 YOUNG WOMAN: Yeah because people’s earning power has gone up so they can afford to spend more on personal services like that. 女學生：是啊，因為人們的收入能力提高了，所以能花更多錢在這類個人服務上。 YOUNG MAN: But technology hasn’t changed the actual job that much. 男學生：但科技其實沒有太大程度改變這份工作的實際內容。 YOUNG WOMAN: No, they’ve got hairdryers, etc. but it’s one job where you don’t depend on a computer. 女學生：是的，他們有吹風機等等，但這是一份不依賴電腦的工作。 The kind of work that administrative staff do has changed enormously, thanks to technology. 由於科技發展，行政人員所做的工作已經有了巨大變化。 Even 20 years ago there were secretaries doing dictation and typing. 即使在 20 年前，仍有秘書負責聽寫和打字。 YOUNG MAN: Yes. Really boring compared to these days, when they’re given much more responsibility and higher status. 男學生：是的。和現在相比，那真的很無聊；現在他們被賦予更多責任，也有更高地位。 YOUNG WOMAN: Mmm. A lot of graduates go in for this kind of work now. 女學生：嗯。現在很多畢業生都投入這類工作。 I’d expected there to be a much bigger change in the number of agricultural workers in the 19th century. 我原本以為 19 世紀農業工人的人數變化會更大。 But the 1871 census showed that roughly 25% of the population worked on the land. 但 1871 年的人口普查顯示，大約 25% 的人口在土地上工作。 YOUNG MAN: Yeah, I’d have assumed it would be more than 50%. 男學生：是啊，我原本以為會超過 50%。 Now it’s less than 0.2%. 現在則不到 0.2%。 YOUNG WOMAN: What about care workers? 女學生：那照護工作者呢？ YOUNG MAN: They barely existed in the 19th century as people’s lifespan was so much shorter. 男學生：在 19 世紀幾乎沒有這類工作，因為人們壽命短得多。 But now of course this sector will see huge growth. 但現在這個行業當然會大幅成長。 YOUNG WOMAN: Yeah – and it’s hard enough to meet current demand. 女學生：是啊，而且目前需求已經很難滿足了。 The future looks quite bleak for bank clerks. 銀行櫃員的未來看起來相當黯淡。 They’ve been in decline since ATMs were introduced in the eighties. 自從 1980 年代自動提款機出現以來，這類工作就一直在減少。 YOUNG MAN: And technology will certainly make most of the jobs they do now redundant, I think. 男學生：我認為，科技肯定會讓他們現在做的大多數工作變得多餘。 YOUNG WOMAN: I agree, although the situation may change. 女學生：我同意，雖然情況也可能改變。 It’s very hard to predict what will happen. 很難預測會發生什麼。

entries.title: Listening Practice 11
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Space Traffic Management A Space Traffic Management system ● is a concept similar to Air Traffic Control, but for satellites rather than planes. ● would aim to set up legal and 31 __________ ways of improving safety. ● does not actually exist at present. Problems in developing effective Space Traffic Management ● Satellites are now quite 32 __________ and therefore more widespread, e.g. there are constellations made up of 33 __________ of satellites. ● At present, satellites are not required to transmit information to help with their 34 __________. ● There are few systems for 35 __________ satellites. ● Small pieces of debris may be difficult to identify. ● Operators may be unwilling to share details of satellites used for 36 __________ or commercial reasons. ● It may be hard to collect details of the object’s 37 __________ at a given time. ● Scientists can only make a 38 __________ about where the satellite will go. Solutions ● Common standards should be agreed on for the presentation of information. ● The information should be combined in one 39 __________. ● A coordinated system must be designed to create 40 __________ in its users. ● would aim to set up legal and 31 __________ ways of improving safety. ● Satellites are now quite 32 __________ and therefore more widespread, e.g. there are constellations made up of 33 __________ of satellites. with their 34 __________. ● There are few systems for 35 __________ satellites. ● Operators may be unwilling to share details of satellites used for 36 __________ or commercial reasons. ● It may be hard to collect details of the object’s 37 __________ at a given ● Scientists can only make a 38 __________ about where the satellite will ● The information should be combined in one 39 __________. ● A coordinated system must be designed to create 40 __________ in its In today’s astronomy lecture, I’m going to talk about the need for a system to manage the movement of satellites and other objects in orbit around the Earth. 在今天的天文學講座中，我要談談為什麼需要一套系統來管理地球軌道上衛星和其他物體的運行。 In other words, a Space Traffic Management system. 換句話說，就是太空交通管理系統。 We already have effective Air Traffic Control systems that are used internationally to ensure that planes navigate our skies safely. 我們已經有國際上使用的有效空中交通管制系統，以確保飛機能在天空中安全航行。 Well, Space Traffic Management is a similar concept, but focusing on the control of satellites. 太空交通管理是一個類似概念，但重點在於控制衛星。 The aim of such a system would be to prevent the danger of collisions in space between the objects in orbit around the Earth. 這類系統的目標，是防止地球軌道上的物體在太空中發生碰撞的危險。 In order to do this, we’d need to have a set of legal measures, and we’d also have to develop the technical systems to enable us to prevent such accidents. 為了做到這一點，我們需要一套法律措施，也必須發展技術系統，使我們能夠防止這類事故。 But unfortunately, at present we don’t actually have a Space Traffic Management system that works. 但不幸的是，目前我們其實還沒有一套有效運作的太空交通管理系統。 So why not? What are the problems in developing such a system? 那為什麼沒有呢？開發這樣的系統有什麼問題？ Well, for one thing, satellites are relatively cheap these days, compared with how they were in the past, meaning that more people can afford to put them into space. 首先，和過去相比，現在衛星相對便宜，這意味著更多人有能力把衛星送上太空。 So there’s a lot more of them out there, and people aren’t just launching single satellites but whole constellations, consisting of thousands of them designed to work together. 所以太空中的衛星數量多了很多，而且人們不只是發射單顆衛星，而是發射整個星座，由數千顆設計來協同工作的衛星組成。 So space is getting more crowded every day. 因此，太空每天都變得更加擁擠。 But in spite of this, one thing you may be surprised to learn is that you can launch a satellite into space and, once it’s out there, it doesn’t have to send back any information to Earth to allow its identification. 但儘管如此，你可能會驚訝地發現，人們可以把衛星發射到太空，而它一旦進入太空，就不必向地球傳回任何能識別其身份的資訊。 So while we have international systems for ensuring we know where the planes in our skies are, and to prevent them from colliding with one another, when it comes to the safety of satellites, at present we don’t have anything like enough proper ways of tracking them. 因此，雖然我們有國際系統確保知道天空中飛機的位置，並防止它們互相碰撞，但談到衛星安全時，目前我們還遠遠沒有足夠完善的追蹤方法。 And it isn’t just entire satellites that we need to consider. 而且我們需要考慮的不只是完整的衛星。 A greater threat is the huge amount of space debris in orbit around the Earth – broken bits of satellite and junk from space stations and so on. 更大的威脅是地球軌道上大量的太空碎片，例如衛星碎片和太空站垃圾等等。 And some of these are so small that they can be very hard to identify, but they can still be very dangerous. 其中一些碎片非常小，很難辨識，但仍然可能非常危險。 In addition, some operators may be unwilling to share information about the satellites they’ve launched. 此外，一些營運者可能不願分享他們發射衛星的資訊。 For example, a satellite may be designed for military purposes, or it may have been launched for commercial reasons, and the operators don’t want competitors to have information about it. 例如，一顆衛星可能是為軍事目的設計，或是因商業原因發射，而營運者不希望競爭對手掌握相關資訊。 And even if the operators are willing to provide it, the information isn’t easy to collect. 即使營運者願意提供資訊， 這些資訊也不容易收集。 Details are needed about the object itself, as well as about its location at a particular time. 我們需要關於物體本身的細節，也需要它在特定時間的位置資訊。 And remember that a satellite isn’t very big, and it’s likely to be moving at thousands of kilometres an hour. 而且要記住，衛星並不大， 並且可能以每小時數千公里的速度移動。 We don’t have any sensors that can constantly follow something moving so fast, so all that the scientists can do is to put forward a prediction concerning where the satellite is heading next. 我們沒有任何感測器能持續追蹤移動如此快速的物體， 所以科學家能做的只是預測衛星接下來會往哪裡去。 So those are some of the problems that we’re facing. 這些就是我們面臨的一些問題。 Let’s consider now some of the solutions that have been suggested. 現在我們來看看一些已被提出的解決方案。 One key issue is the way in which information is dealt with. 一個關鍵問題是資訊如何被處理。 We need more information, but it also needs to be accessible at a global level, so we need to establish shared standards that we can all agree on for the way in which this information is presented. 我們需要更多資訊，但這些資訊也必須能在全球層級被取得，因此我們需要建立大家都同意的共同標準，規範資訊呈現方式。 We already do this in other areas of science, so although this is a challenge, it’s not an impossible task. 我們在其他科學領域已經這樣做了，所以雖然這是一項挑戰，但並不是不可能完成的任務。 Then, as all this information’s collected, it needs to be put together so it can be used, and that will involve creating a single database on which it can be entered. 接著，當所有資訊被收集起來後，需要整合在一起以便使用，這將涉及建立一個可輸入資訊的單一資料庫。 As we continue to push forward new developments, congestion of the space environment is only going to increase. 隨著我們持續推動新的發展，太空環境的擁擠程度只會增加。 To cope with this, we need to develop a system like the one I’ve described to coordinate the work of the numerous spacecraft operators. 為了應對這種情況，我們需要開發一套像我所描述的系統，用來協調眾多太空器營運者的工作。 But it’s also essential that this system is one that establishes trust in the people that use it, both nationally and at a global level. 但同樣重要的是，這套系統必須能在使用者之間建立信任，無論是在國內還是全球層面。 One interesting development … 一項有趣的發展是……
