entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Buckworth Conservation Group Regular activities Beach ● making sure the beach does not have 1 __________ on it ● no 2 __________ Nature reserve ● maintaining paths ● nesting boxes for birds installed ● next task is taking action to attract 3 __________ to the place ● identifying types of 4 __________ ● building a new 5 __________ Forthcoming events Saturday ● meet at Dunsmore Beach car park ● walk across the sands and reach the 6 __________ ● take a picnic ● wear appropriate 7 __________ Woodwork session ● suitable for 8 __________ to participate in ● making 9 __________ out of wood ● 17th, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. ● cost of session, no camping: £10 __________ ● making sure the beach does not have 1 __________ on it ● no 2 __________ ● next task is taking action to attract 3 __________ to the place ● identifying types of 4 __________ ● building a new 5 __________ ● walk across the sands and reach the 6 __________ ● wear appropriate 7 __________ ● suitable for 8 __________ to participate in ● making 9 __________ out of wood ● cost of session, no camping: £10 __________ PETER: Hello? Peter：您好？ JAN: Oh hello. My name’s Jan. Jan：哦，你好。我叫 Jan。 Are you the right person to talk to about the Buckworth Conservation Group? 請問關於 Buckworth Conservation Group 的事情， 是找你嗎？ PETER: Yes, I’m Peter. I’m the secretary. Peter：是的，我是 Peter。我是秘書。 JAN: Good. I’ve just moved to this area, and I’m interested in getting involved. Jan：太好了。我剛搬到這個地區，很想參與你們的活動。 I was in a similar group where I used to live. 我以前住的地方也參加過類似的團體。 Could you tell me something about your activities, please? 你能介紹一下你們的活動嗎？ PETER: Of course. Well, we have a mixture of regular activities and special events. Peter：當然可以。我們有一些定期活動，也有一些特別活動。 One of the regular ones is trying to keep the beach free of litter. 其中一項定期活動是努力保持海灘沒有垃圾。 A few of us spend a couple of hours a month on it, and it’s awful how much there is to clear. 我們有幾個人每個月會花幾個小時清理，但要清掉的垃圾量實在很多，情況很糟。 I wish people would be more responsible and take it home with them. 我希望人們能更負責任，把垃圾帶回家。 JAN: I totally agree. I’d be happy to help with that. Jan：我完全同意。我很願意幫忙。 Is it OK to take dogs? 可以帶狗嗎？ PETER: I’m afraid not, as they’re banned from the beach itself. Peter：恐怕不行，因為海灘本身禁止狗進入。 You can take them along the cliffs, though. And children are welcome. 不過你可以帶牠們沿著懸崖走。孩子們也很歡迎。 JAN: Right. Jan：明白。 PETER: We also manage a nature reserve, and there’s a lot to do there all year round. Peter：我們也管理一個自然保護區，那裡全年都有很多工作要做。 For example, because it’s a popular place to visit, we spend a lot of time looking after the paths and making sure they’re in good condition for walking. 例如，因為那裡是很受歡迎的遊覽地點，我們花很多時間維護小路，確保它們適合步行。 JAN: I could certainly help with that. Jan：這方面我肯定可以幫忙。 PETER: Good. And we have a programme of creating new habitats there. Peter：很好。我們還有一個在那裡創造新棲地的計畫。 We’ve just finished making and installing nesting boxes for birds to use, and next we’re going to work on encouraging insects – they’re important for the biodiversity of the reserve. 我們剛完成鳥類巢箱的製作和安裝，接下來會努力吸引昆蟲，因為牠們對保護區的生物多樣性很重要。 JAN: They certainly are. Jan：牠們確實很重要。 PETER: Oh, and we’re also running a project to identify the different species of butterflies that visit the reserve. Peter：哦，我們還在進行一個項目，辨識來到保護區的不同蝴蝶種類。 You might be interested in taking part in that. 你可能會有興趣參加。 JAN: Sure. I was involved in something similar where I used to live, counting all the species of moths. Jan：當然。我以前住的地方也參加過類似活動，是統計所有蛾類種類。 I’d enjoy that. 我會很喜歡。 PETER: Another job we’re doing at the reserve is replacing the wall on the southern side, between the parking area and our woodshed. Peter：我們在保護區做的另一項工作，是更換南側停車區和木棚之間的牆。 It was badly damaged in a storm last month. 上個月暴風雨把它嚴重損壞了。 JAN: OK. Jan：好的。 PETER: Then as I said, we have a programme of events as well, both at the weekend, and during the week. Peter：然後，就像我說的，我們也有一系列活動，週末和平日都有。 JAN: Right. I presume you have guided walks? Jan：好的。我想你們有導覽步行活動吧？ I’d like to get to know the local countryside, as I’m new to the area. 我剛搬來這裡，所以想了解當地鄉村。 PETER: Yes, we do. The next walk is to Ruston Island, a week on Saturday. Peter：有的。下一次步行活動是去 Ruston Island，下週六舉行。 We’ll be meeting in the car park at Dunsmore Beach at low tide – that’s when the sands are dry enough for us to walk to the island without getting wet. 我們會在退潮時於 Dunsmore Beach 停車場集合，那時沙灘足夠乾，可以走到島上而不會弄濕。 JAN: Sounds good. Jan：聽起來不錯。 PETER: The island’s a great place to explore. Peter：那座島很適合探索。 It’s quite small, and it’s got a range of habitats. 它相當小，但有多種棲地。 It’s also an ideal location for seeing seals just off the coast, or even on the beach. 那裡也是觀察海豹的理想地點，可以看到牠們在近岸處， 甚至在海灘上。 JAN: OK. And is there anything we should bring, like a picnic, for instance? Jan：好的。那我們需要帶什麼嗎？比如野餐？ PETER: Yes, do bring one, as it’s a full-day walk. Peter：是的，請帶一份，因為這是一整天的步行活動。 And of course it’ll be wet walking across and back, so make sure your boots are waterproof. 當然，來回走過沙地時會濕， 所以一定要確保你的靴子防水。 JAN: I must buy a new pair – there’s a hole in one of my current ones! Jan：我得買一雙新的了——我現在這雙有一隻破了個洞！ Well, I’d definitely like to come on the walk. 不過，我肯定想參加這次步行活動。 PETER: Great. Then later this month we’re having a one-day woodwork session in Hopton Wood. Peter：太好了。本月晚些時候，我們會在 Hopton Wood 舉辦一天的木工課。 JAN: I’ve never tried that before. Jan：我以前從沒試過。 Is it OK for beginners to take part? 初學者可以參加嗎？ PETER: Definitely. There’ll be a couple of experts leading the session, and we keep the number of participants down, so you’ll get as much help as you need. Peter：當然可以。會有幾位專家帶領課程，而且我們會限制參加人數，所以你會得到足夠的協助。 JAN: Excellent! I’d love to be able to make chairs. Jan：太好了！我很想學會做椅子。 PETER: That’s probably too ambitious for one day! Peter：一天要做到那個可能太有野心了！ You’ll be starting with wooden spoons, and of course learning how to use the tools. 你們會從木勺開始做，當然也會學習如何使用工具。 And anything you make is yours to take home with you. 你做的任何東西都可以帶回家。 JAN: That sounds like fun. When is it? Jan：聽起來很有趣。什麼時候舉行？ PETER: It’s on the 17th, from 10 a.m. until 3. Peter：在 17 號，上午 10 點到下午 3 點。 There’s a charge of £35, including lunch, or £40 if you want to camp in the wood. 費用是 35 英鎊，包含午餐；如果你想在森林裡露營，則是 40 英鎊。 JAN: I should think I’ll come home the same day. Jan：我想我會當天回家。 Well, I’d certainly like to join the group. 總之，我確實很想加入這個團體。

entries.title: Listening Practice 12
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–14 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Boat Trip Round Tasmania 11. What is the maximum number of people who can stand on each side of the boat? A. 9 B. 15 C. 18 12. What colour are the tour boats? A. dark red B. jet black C. light green 13. Which lunchbox is suitable for someone who doesn’t eat meat or fish? A. Lunchbox 1 B. Lunchbox 2 C. Lunchbox 3 14. What should people do with their litter? A. take it home B. hand it to a member of staff C. put it in the bins provided on the boat Questions 15 and 16 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO features of the lighthouse does Lou mention? A. why it was built B. who built it C. how long it took to build D. who staffed it E. what it was built with Questions 17 and 18 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO types of creature might come close to the boat? A. sea eagles B. fur seals C. dolphins D. whales E. penguins Questions 19 and 20 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO points does Lou make about the caves? A. Only large tourist boats can visit them. B. The entrances to them are often blocked. C. It is too dangerous for individuals to go near them. D. Someone will explain what is inside them. E. They cannot be reached on foot. What is the maximum number of people who can stand on each side of the boat? 9 15 18 What colour are the tour boats? dark red jet black light green Which lunchbox is suitable for someone who doesn’t eat meat or fish? Lunchbox 1 Lunchbox 2 Lunchbox 3 What should people do with their litter? take it home hand it to a member of staff put it in the bins provided on the boat Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO features of the lighthouse does Lou mention? why it was built who built it how long it took to build who staffed it what it was built with Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO types of creature might come close to the boat? sea eagles fur seals dolphins whales penguins Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO points does Lou make about the caves? Only large tourist boats can visit them. The entrances to them are often blocked. It is too dangerous for individuals to go near them. Someone will explain what is inside them. They cannot be reached on foot. So, hello everyone. My name’s Lou Miller and I’m going to be your tour guide today as we take this fantastic boat trip around the Tasmanian coast. 大家好。我叫 Lou Miller，今天我會擔任你們的導遊，帶大家乘船遊覽塔斯馬尼亞海岸。 Before we set off, I just want to tell you a few things about our journey. 在我們出發前，我想先介紹幾件關於這趟旅程的事情。 Our boats aren’t huge as you can see. 如你們所見，我們的船並不大。 We already have three staff members on board and on top of that, we can transport a further fifteen people – that’s you – around the coastline. 船上已經有三名工作人員，除此之外還能再載十五名乘客， 也就是你們，沿著海岸航行。 But please note if there are more than nine people on either side of the boat, we’ll move some of you over, otherwise all eighteen of us will end up in the sea! 但請注意，如果船的任一側超過九個人，我們會請一些人移到另一邊，否則我們十八個人都會掉進海裡！ We’ve recently upgraded all our boats. 我們最近升級了所有船隻。 They used to be jet black, but our new ones now have these comfortable dark red seats and a light-green exterior in order to stand out from others and help promote our company. 以前它們是亮黑色的，但現在新船有舒適的深紅色座椅，外觀是淺綠色，這樣能和其他船區分開，也有助於宣傳公司。 This gives our boats a rather unique appearance, don’t you think? 這讓我們的船看起來相當獨特，你們不覺得嗎？ We offer you a free lunchbox during the trip and we have three types. 旅途中我們會提供免費午餐盒，共有三種。 Lunchbox 1 contains ham and tomato sandwiches. 第一種午餐盒有火腿番茄三明治。 Lunchbox 2 contains a cheddar cheese roll and Lunchbox 3 is salad-based and also contains eggs and tuna. 第二種有切達起司麵包卷，第三種以沙拉為主，還包含雞蛋和鮪魚。 All three lunchboxes also have a packet of crisps and chocolate bar inside. 三種午餐盒裡也都有一包洋芋片和一條巧克力棒。 Please let staff know which lunchbox you prefer. 請告訴工作人員你想要哪一種。 I’m sure I don’t have to ask you not to throw anything into the sea. 我相信我不必特別要求你們不要把任何東西丟進海裡。 We don’t have any bins to put litter in, but Jess, myself or Ray, our other guide, will collect it from you after lunch and put it all in a large plastic sack. 船上沒有垃圾桶，但午餐後 Jess、我或另一位導遊 Ray 會向你們收垃圾，然後全部放進一個大塑膠袋裡。 The engine on the boat makes quite a lot of noise so before we head off, let me tell you a few things about what you’re going to see. 船上的引擎聲相當大，所以在出發前，讓我先告訴你們幾件即將看到的事物。 This area is famous for its ancient lighthouse, which you’ll see from the boat as we turn past the first little island. 這個地區以古老燈塔聞名，當我們繞過第一座小島時，你們會從船上看到它。 It was built in 1838 to protect sailors as a number of shipwrecks had led to significant loss of life. 它建於 1838 年，目的是保護海員，因為當時多起船難造成了重大人員傷亡。 The construction itself was complicated as some of the original drawings kept by the local council show. 從地方議會保存的一些原始圖紙可以看出，建造本身相當複雜。 It sits right on top of the cliffs in a very isolated spot. 它位於懸崖頂端，位置非常偏僻。 In the nineteenth century there were many jobs there, such as polishing the brass lamps, chopping firewood and cleaning windows, that kept lighthouse keepers busy. 在 19 世紀，那裡有很多工作要做，例如擦亮銅燈、劈柴和擦窗戶，讓燈塔看守人非常忙碌。 These workers were mainly prison convicts until the middle of that century when ordinary families willing to live in such circumstances took over. 這些工作者主要是囚犯，直到 19 世紀中期，願意住在這種環境中的普通家庭才接手。 Some of you have asked me what creatures we can expect to see. 你們有些人問過我，我們可能會看到哪些生物。 I know everyone loves the penguins, but they’re very shy and, unfortunately, tend to hide from passing boats. 我知道大家都喜歡企鵝，但牠們非常害羞，很可惜，通常會躲避經過的船。 But you might see birds in the distance, such as sea eagles, flying around the cliff edges where they nest. 不過你們可能會看到遠處的鳥，例如海鵰，在牠們築巢的懸崖邊飛翔。 When we get to the rocky area inhabited by fur seals, we’ll stop and watch them swimming around the coast. 當我們到達海狗棲息的岩石區時，我們會停下來，看牠們在海岸附近游泳。 They’re inquisitive creatures so don’t be surprised if one pops up right in front of you. 牠們是好奇心很強的動物，所以如果有一隻突然出現在你面前，不要太驚訝。 Their predators, orca whales, hunt along the coastline too, but spotting one of these is rare. 牠們的捕食者虎鯨也會沿著海岸捕獵，但看到虎鯨的機會很少。 Dolphins, on the other hand, can sometimes approach on their own or in groups as they ride the waves beside us. 另一方面，海豚有時會單獨或成群靠近，在我們旁邊乘著海浪游動。 Lastly, I want to mention the caves. 最後，我想提一下洞穴。 Tasmania is famous for its caves and the ones we’ll pass by are so amazing that people are lost for words when they see them. 塔斯馬尼亞以洞穴聞名，我們會經過的那些洞穴非常壯觀， 人們看到時常常說不出話來。 They can only be approached by sea, but if you feel that you want to see more than we’re able to show you, then you can take a kayak into the area on another day and one of our staff will give you more information on that. 這些洞穴只能從海上接近；如果你們想看到比我們今天能展示的更多內容，可以改天划皮艇進入該區域，我們的工作人員會提供更多資訊。 What we’ll do is to go through a narrow channel, past some incredible rock formations and from there we’ll be able to see the openings to the caves, and at that point we’ll talk to you about what lies beyond. 我們會穿過一條狹窄水道，經過一些令人驚嘆的岩石構造， 然後從那裡看到洞穴入口，到時我們會向你們介紹洞穴深處有什麼。

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–26 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Work Experience for Veterinary Science Students 21. What problem did both Diana and Tim have when arranging their work experience? A. making initial contact with suitable farms B. organising transport to and from the farm C. finding a placement for the required length of time 22. Tim was pleased to be able to help A. a lamb that had a broken leg. B. a sheep that was having difficulty giving birth. C. a newly born lamb that was having trouble feeding. 23. Diana says the sheep on her farm A. were of various different varieties. B. were mainly reared for their meat. C. had better quality wool than sheep on the hills. 24. What did the students learn about adding supplements to chicken feed? A. These should only be given if specially needed. B. It is worth paying extra for the most effective ones. C. The amount given at one time should be limited. 25. What happened when Diana was working with dairy cows? A. She identified some cows incorrectly. B. She accidentally threw some milk away. C. She made a mistake when storing milk. 26. What did both farmers mention about vets and farming? A. Vets are failing to cope with some aspects of animal health. B. There needs to be a fundamental change in the training of vets. C. Some jobs could be done by the farmer rather than by a vet. Questions 27–30 What opinion do the students give about each of the following modules on their veterinary science course? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 27–30. Opinions A. Tim found this easier than expected. B. Tim thought this was not very clearly organised. C. Diana may do some further study on this. D. They both found the reading required for this was difficult. E. Tim was shocked at something he learned on this module. F. They were both surprised how little is known about some aspects of this. Modules on Veterinary Science course 27. Medical terminology __________ 28. Diet and nutrition __________ 29. Animal disease __________ 30. Wildlife medication __________ What problem did both Diana and Tim have when arranging their work experience? making initial contact with suitable farms organising transport to and from the farm finding a placement for the required length of time Tim was pleased to be able to help a lamb that had a broken leg. a sheep that was having difficulty giving birth. a newly born lamb that was having trouble feeding. Diana says the sheep on her farm were of various different varieties. were mainly reared for their meat. had better quality wool than sheep on the hills. What did the students learn about adding supplements to chicken feed? These should only be given if specially needed. It is worth paying extra for the most effective ones. The amount given at one time should be limited. What happened when Diana was working with dairy cows? She identified some cows incorrectly. She accidentally threw some milk away. She made a mistake when storing milk. What did both farmers mention about vets and farming? Vets are failing to cope with some aspects of animal health. There needs to be a fundamental change in the training of vets. Some jobs could be done by the farmer rather than by a vet. Medical terminology Tim found this easier than expected. Tim thought this was not very clearly organised. Diana may do some further study on this. They both found the reading required for this was difficult. Tim was shocked at something he learned on this module. They were both surprised how little is known about some aspects of this. Diet and nutrition Tim found this easier than expected. Tim thought this was not very clearly organised. Diana may do some further study on this. They both found the reading required for this was difficult. Tim was shocked at something he learned on this module. They were both surprised how little is known about some aspects of this. Animal disease Tim found this easier than expected. Tim thought this was not very clearly organised. Diana may do some further study on this. They both found the reading required for this was difficult. Tim was shocked at something he learned on this module. They were both surprised how little is known about some aspects of this. Wildlife medication Tim found this easier than expected. Tim thought this was not very clearly organised. Diana may do some further study on this. They both found the reading required for this was difficult. Tim was shocked at something he learned on this module. They were both surprised how little is known about some aspects of this. DIANA: So, Tim, we have to do a short summary of our work experience on a farm. Diana：Tim，我們需要簡短總結一下在農場的工作經驗。 TIM: Right. My farm was great, but arranging the work experience was hard. Tim：對。我去的農場很棒，但安排實習很困難。 One problem was it was miles away and I don’t drive. 一個問題是它離我很遠，而我不會開車。 And also, I’d really wanted a placement for a month, but I could only get one for two weeks. 另外，我本來很想實習一個月，但最後只能找到兩週的實習。 DIANA: I was lucky, the farmer let me stay on the farm so I didn’t have to travel. Diana：我很幸運，農場主讓我住在農場，所以我不用通勤。 But finding the right sort of farm to apply to wasn’t easy. 但要找到合適的農場申請並不容易。 TIM: No, they don’t seem to have websites, do they. Tim：是啊，他們好像沒有網站，對吧？ I found mine through a friend of my mother’s, but it wasn’t easy. 我是透過我母親的一位朋友找到的，但也不容易。 DIANA: No. Diana：確實不容易。 TIM: My farm was mostly livestock, especially sheep. Tim：我去的農場主要養牲畜，尤其是羊。 I really enjoyed helping out with them. 我真的很喜歡幫忙照顧牠們。 I was up most of one night helping a sheep deliver a lamb … 有一晚我幾乎整晚沒睡，在幫一隻母羊接生小羊…… DIANA: On your own? Diana：你自己一個人嗎？ TIM: No, the farmer was there, and he told me what to do. Tim：不是，農場主也在，他告訴我該怎麼做。 It wasn’t a straightforward birth, but I managed. 那次生產並不順利，但我應付過來了。 It was a great feeling to see the lamb stagger to its feet and start feeding almost straightaway, and to know that it was OK. 看到小羊搖搖晃晃地站起來，幾乎立刻開始吃奶，而且知道牠沒事，那感覺真的很好。 DIANA: Mm. Diana：嗯。 TIM: Then another time a lamb had broken its leg, and they got the vet in to set it, and he talked me through what he was doing. Tim：還有一次，一隻小羊摔斷了腿，他們請獸醫來接骨， 獸醫一邊做一邊向我解釋。 That was really useful. 那真的很有幫助。 DIANA: Yes, my farm had sheep too. Diana：是的，我的農場也有羊。 The farm was in a valley and they had a lowland breed called Suffolks, although the farmer said they’d had other breeds in the past. 農場在山谷裡，他們養的是一種低地品種，叫 Suffolks， 不過農場主說他們過去也養過其他品種。 TIM: So were they bred for their meat? Tim：所以牠們是為了肉而飼養的嗎？ DIANA: Mostly, yes. They’re quite big and solid. Diana：主要是的。牠們很大， 也很壯實。 TIM: My farm was up in the hills and they had a different breed of sheep, they were Cheviots. Tim：我的農場在山上，他們養的是另一種羊，叫 Cheviots 。 DIANA: Oh, I heard their wool’s really sought after. Diana：哦，我聽說牠們的羊毛很受歡迎。 TIM: Yes. It’s very hardwearing and they use it for carpets. Tim：是的。那種羊毛很耐用， 會用來做地毯。 DIANA: Right. Diana：明白。 TIM: I was interested in the amount of supplements they add to animals’ feed nowadays. Tim：我對現在他們在動物飼料中加入的補充劑數量很感興趣。 Like, even the chickens got extra vitamins and electrolytes in their feed. 比如，就連雞的飼料裡也有額外的維生素和電解質。 DIANA: Yes, I found that too. And they’re not cheap. Diana：是的，我也發現了。而且它們不便宜。 But my farmer said some are overpriced for what they are. 但我的農場主說，有些補充劑以實際效果來看價格過高。 And he didn’t give them as a matter of routine, just at times when the chickens seemed to particularly require them. 而且他不是例行性地給，而是在雞看起來特別需要時才給。 TIM: Yes, mine said the same. Tim：是的，我那邊的農場主也這麼說。 He said certain breeds of chickens might need more supplements than the others, but the cheap and expensive ones are all basically the same. 他說某些品種的雞可能比其他品種更需要補充劑，但便宜和昂貴的補充劑基本上都差不多。 DIANA: Mm. Diana：嗯。 TIM: So did your farm have any other livestock, Diana? Tim：Diana，那你的農場還有其他牲畜嗎？ DIANA: Yes, dairy cows. I made a really embarrassing mistake when I was working in the milk shed. Diana：有，乳牛。我在牛奶棚工作時犯了一個非常尷尬的錯誤。 Some cows had been treated with antibiotics, so their milk wasn’t suitable for human consumption, and it had to be put in a separate container. 有些牛接受過抗生素治療， 所以牠們的牛奶不適合人類飲用，必須放進單獨容器。 But I got mixed up, and I poured some milk from the wrong cow in with the milk for humans, so the whole lot had to be thrown away. 但我弄混了，把不該混進去的牛奶倒進了供人飲用的牛奶裡，所以整批牛奶都得丟掉。 The farmer wasn’t too happy with me. 農場主對我不太高興。 TIM: I asked my farmer how much he depended on the vet to deal with health problems. Tim：我問過我的農場主，他有多依賴獸醫處理動物健康問題。 I’d read reports that the livestock’s health is being affected as farmers are under pressure to increase production. 我讀過一些報告，說農民在增加產量的壓力下，牲畜健康受到影響。 Well, he didn’t agree with that, but he said that actually some of the stuff the vets do, like minor operations, he’d be quite capable of doing himself. 不過他不同意那種說法，但他說其實獸醫做的一些事情，例如小手術，他自己也完全有能力做。 DIANA: Yeah. My farmer said the same. Diana：是的，我的農場主也這麼說。 But he reckons vets’ skills are still needed. 但他認為獸醫的技術仍然是需要的。 DIANA: Now we’ve got to give a bit of feedback about last term’s modules – just short comments, apparently. Diana：現在我們還得對上學期的課程模組給一點回饋， 顯然只需要簡短評論。 Shall we do that now? 我們現在做嗎？ TIM: OK. So medical terminology. Tim：好。先說醫學術語。 DIANA: Well, my heart sank when I saw that, especially right at the beginning of the course. Diana：嗯，我一看到那個就心沉了下去，尤其是在課程剛開始的時候。 And I did struggle with it. 我確實學得很吃力。 TIM: I’d thought it’d be hard, but actually I found it all quite straightforward. Tim：我本來以為會很難，但實際上我覺得相當簡單。 What did you think about diet and nutrition? 你覺得飲食與營養怎麼樣？ DIANA: OK, I suppose. Diana：我想還可以吧。 TIM: Do you remember what they told us about pet food and the fact that there’s such limited checking into whether or not it’s contaminated? Tim：你還記得他們告訴我們關於寵物食品的事嗎？也就是對它是否受到污染的檢查非常有限。 I mean in comparison with the checks on food for humans – I thought that was terrible. 我的意思是，和人類食品檢查相比，我覺得那很糟。 DIANA: Mm. I think the module that really impressed me was the animal disease one, when we looked at domesticated animals in different parts of the world, like camels and water buffalo and alpaca. Diana：嗯。真正讓我印象深刻的是動物疾病那個模組， 當時我們研究了世界各地的家養動物，例如駱駝、水牛和羊駝。 The economies of so many countries depend on these, but scientists don’t know much about the diseases that affect them. 很多國家的經濟都依賴這些動物，但科學家對影響牠們的疾病了解並不多。 TIM: Yes, I thought they’d know a lot about ways of controlling and eradicating those diseases, but that’s not the case at all. Tim：是啊，我原以為他們會很了解如何控制和根除那些疾病，但事實完全不是這樣。 I loved the wildlife medication unit. 我很喜歡野生動物醫療那個單元。 Things like helping birds that have been caught in oil spills. 例如幫助被石油洩漏困住的鳥類。 That’s something I hadn’t thought about before. 那是我以前從沒想過的事情。 DIANA: Yeah, I thought I might write my dissertation on something connected with that. Diana：是啊，我想我可能會寫一篇和那相關的論文。 TIM: Right. So … Tim：好的。那麼……

entries.title: Listening Practice 12
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Labyrinths Definition ● a winding spiral path leading to a central area Labyrinths compared with mazes ● Mazes are a type of 31 __________ ○ 32 __________ is needed to navigate through a maze ○ the word “maze” is derived from a word meaning a feeling of 33 __________ ● Labyrinths represent a journey through life ○ they have frequently been used in 34 __________ and prayer Early examples of the labyrinth spiral ● Ancient carvings on 35 __________ have been found across many cultures ● The Pima, a Native American tribe, wove the symbol on baskets ● Ancient Greeks used the symbol on 36 __________ Walking labyrinths ● The largest surviving example of a turf labyrinth once had a big 37 __________ at its centre Labyrinths nowadays ● Believed to have a beneficial impact on mental and physical health, e.g. walking a maze can reduce a person’s 38 __________ rate ● Used in medical and health and fitness settings and also prisons ● Popular with patients, visitors and staff in hospitals: ○ patients who can’t walk can use “finger labyrinths” made from 39 __________ ○ research has shown that Alzheimer’s sufferers experience less 40 __________ ● Mazes are a type of 31 __________ ○ 32 __________ is needed to navigate through a maze ○ the word “maze” is derived from a word meaning a feeling of 33 __________ ○ they have frequently been used in 34 __________ and prayer ● Ancient carvings on 35 __________ have been found across many ● Ancient Greeks used the symbol on 36 __________ ● The largest surviving example of a turf labyrinth once had a big 37 __________ at its centre walking a maze can reduce a person’s 38 __________ rate ○ patients who can’t walk can use “finger labyrinths” made from 39 __________ ○ research has shown that Alzheimer’s sufferers experience less 40 __________ Labyrinths have existed for well over 4,000 years. 迷宮式螺旋路徑已存在超過 4000 年。 Labyrinths and labyrinthine symbols have been found in regions as diverse as modern-day Turkey, Ireland, Greece, and India. 在現今的土耳其、愛爾蘭、希臘和印度等不同地區，都發現了 labyrinth 及相關符號。 There are various designs of labyrinth but what they all have in common is a winding spiral path which leads to a central area. Labyrinth 有多種設計，但共同點是都有一條蜿蜒的螺旋路徑，通向中央區域。 There is one starting point at the entrance and the goal is to reach the central area. 入口處有一個起點，目標是到達中央區域。 Finding your way through a labyrinth involves many twists and turns, but it’s not possible to get lost as there is only one single path. 走過 labyrinth 會經歷許多彎曲轉折，但不可能迷路，因為只有一條單一路徑。 In modern times, the word labyrinth has taken on a different meaning and is often used as a synonym for a maze. 在現代，labyrinth 這個詞有了不同含義，常被用作 maze 的同義詞。 A maze is quite different as it is a kind of puzzle with an intricate network of paths. 但 maze 非常不同，因為它是一種由複雜路徑網絡構成的謎題。 Mazes became fashionable in the 15th and 16th centuries in Europe, and can still be found in the gardens of great houses and palaces. Maze 在 15 和 16 世紀的歐洲變得流行，至今仍可在大型宅邸和宮殿的花園中看到。 The paths are usually surrounded by thick, high hedges so that it’s not possible to see over them. 路徑通常被又厚又高的樹籬包圍，因此無法看越過去。 Entering a maze usually involves getting lost a few times before using logic to work out the pattern and find your way to the centre and then out again. 進入 maze 通常會先迷路幾次，然後運用邏輯推算路線模式，找到通往中心再出來的路。 There are lots of dead ends and paths which lead you back to where you started. 裡面有很多死路，也有一些路會把你帶回起點。 The word “maze” is believed to come from a Scandinavian word for a state of confusion. 據信，“maze” 這個詞來自一個斯堪的納維亞詞，意思是一種混亂狀態。 This is where the word “amazing” comes from. “amazing” 這個詞也源自於此。 Labyrinths, on the other hand, have a very different function. 另一方面，labyrinth 的功能非常不同。 Although people now often refer to things they find complicated as labyrinths, this is not how they were seen in the past. 雖然現在人們常把複雜事物稱為 labyrinth，但過去人們並不是這樣看待它們的。 The winding spiral of the labyrinth has been used for centuries as a metaphor for life’s journey. 幾個世紀以來，labyrinth 蜿蜒的螺旋路徑一直被用作人生旅程的隱喻。 It served as a spiritual reminder that there is purpose and meaning to our lives and helped to give people a sense of direction. 它是一種精神提醒，提醒人們生命有目的和意義，並幫助人們獲得方向感。 Labyrinths are thought to encourage a feeling of calm and have been used as a meditation and prayer tool in many cultures over many centuries. 人們認為 labyrinth 能帶來平靜感，幾個世紀以來，它在許多文化中被用作冥想和祈禱工具。 The earliest examples of the labyrinth spiral pattern have been found carved into stone, from Sardinia to Scandinavia, from Arizona to India to Africa. 最早的 labyrinth 螺旋圖案被發現刻在石頭上，分布地區從撒丁島到斯堪的納維亞，從亞利桑那到印度和非洲。 In Europe, these spiral carvings date from the late Bronze Age. 在歐洲，這些螺旋雕刻可追溯到青銅時代晚期。 The Native American Pima tribe wove baskets with a circular labyrinth design that depicted their own cosmology. 美洲原住民 Pima 部落會編織帶有圓形 labyrinth 圖案的籃子，用來描繪他們自己的宇宙觀。 In Ancient Greece, the labyrinth spiral was used on coins around four thousand years ago. 在古希臘，約四千年前， labyrinth 螺旋圖案被用在硬幣上。 Labyrinths made of mosaics were commonly found in bathhouses, villas and tombs throughout the Roman Empire. 在整個羅馬帝國，以馬賽克製成的 labyrinth 常見於浴場、別墅和陵墓中。 In Northern Europe, there were actual physical labyrinths designed for walking on. 在北歐，曾有真正可供行走的實體 labyrinth。 These were cut into the turf or grass, usually in a circular pattern. 這些通常被切割在草皮或草地上，形成圓形圖案。 The origin of these walking labyrinths remains unclear, but they were probably used for fertility rites which may date back thousands of years. 這些步行 labyrinth 的起源仍不清楚，但它們可能用於生育儀式，歷史或許可追溯到數千年前。 Eleven examples of turf labyrinths survive today, including the largest one at Saffron Walden, England, which used to have a large tree in the middle of it. 現今仍保留著 11 個草皮 labyrinth，其中最大的位於英格蘭 Saffron Walden，其中央曾有一棵大樹。 More recently labyrinths have experienced something of a revival. 近年來，labyrinth 又出現了一定程度的復興。 Some believe that walking a labyrinth promotes healing and mindfulness, and there are those who believe in its emotional and physical benefits, which include slower breathing and a restored sense of balance and perspective. 有些人相信走 labyrinth 能促進療癒和正念，也有人相信它對情緒和身體有益，包括放慢呼吸，並恢復平衡感和看待事物的角度。 This idea has become so popular that labyrinths have been laid into the floors of spas, wellness centres and even prisons in recent years. 這種想法變得非常流行，以至於近年來水療中心、健康中心，甚至監獄的地板上都設置了 labyrinth。 A pamphlet at Colorado Children’s Hospital informs patients that “walking a labyrinth can often calm people in the midst of a crisis”. Colorado Children’s Hospital 的一本小冊子告訴病人：「走 labyrinth 通常能讓處於危機中的人平靜下來」。 And apparently, it’s not only patients who benefit. 顯然，受益的不只是病人。 Many visitors find walking a labyrinth less stressful than sitting in a corridor or waiting room. 許多訪客發現，走 labyrinth 比坐在走廊或候診室裡壓力更小。 Some doctors even walk the labyrinth during their breaks. 甚至有些醫生會在休息時間去走 labyrinth。 In some hospitals, patients who can’t walk can have a paper “finger labyrinth” brought to their bed. 在一些醫院，不能行走的病人可以在床邊使用紙製的「手指 labyrinth」。 The science behind the theory is a little sketchy, but there are dozens of small-scale studies which support claims about the benefits of labyrinths. 這個理論背後的科學依據還不算充分，但已有數十項小規模研究支持 labyrinth 具有益處的說法。 For example, one study found that walking a labyrinth provided “short-term calming, relaxation, and relief from anxiety” for Alzheimer’s patients. 例如，一項研究發現，走 labyrinth 能為阿茲海默症患者帶來「短期平靜、放鬆和焦慮緩解」。 So, what is it about labyrinths that makes their appeal so universal? Well … 那麼，labyrinth 到底有什麼特質，讓它具有如此普遍的吸引力呢？嗯……

entries.title: Listening Practice 13
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Part 1 Questions 1–7 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Opportunities for Voluntary Work in Southoe Village Library ● Help with 1 __________ books, times to be arranged ● Help needed to keep 2 __________ of books up to date ● Library is in the 3 __________ Room in the village hall Lunch club ● Help by providing 4 __________ ● Help with hobbies such as 5 __________ Help for individuals needed next week ● Taking Mrs Carroll to 6 __________ ● Work in the 7 __________ at Mr Selsbury’s house Practice 13, source question diagram/table, PDF page 4 ● Help with 1 __________ books, times to be arranged ● Help needed to keep 2 __________ of books up to date ● Library is in the 3 __________ Room in the village hall ● Help by providing 4 __________ ● Help with hobbies such as 5 __________ ● Taking Mrs Carroll to 6 __________ ● Work in the 7 __________ at Mr Selsbury’s house Question 8 — refer to the original question paper above. checking _____ designing the _____ JANE: Hello, Jane Fairbanks speaking. Jane：你好，我是 Jane Fairbanks 。 FRANK: Oh, good morning. My name’s Frank Pritchard. I’ve just retired and moved to Southoe. Frank：哦，早安。我叫 Frank Pritchard。我剛退休，搬到了 Southoe。 I’d like to become a volunteer, and I gather you co-ordinate voluntary work in the village. 我想成為志工，而且我聽說你負責協調村裡的志願工作。 JANE: That’s right. Jane：沒錯。 FRANK: What sort of thing could I do? Frank：我可以做些什麼呢？ JANE: Well, we need help with the village library. Jane：嗯，我們需要人協助村圖書館的工作。 We borrow books from the town library, and individuals also donate them. 我們會從鎮圖書館借書，也會收到個人捐贈的書。 So, one thing you could do is get involved in collecting them – if you’ve got a car, that is. 所以你可以做的一件事是參與收書——前提是你有車。 FRANK: Yes, that’s no problem. Frank：有，沒問題。 JANE: The times are pretty flexible so we can arrange it to suit you. Jane：時間很彈性，所以我們可以依照你的時間安排。 Another thing is the records that we keep of the books we’re given, and those we borrow and need to return to the town library. 另一件事是我們需要保存書籍記錄，包括收到的書，以及從鎮圖書館借來、之後需要歸還的書。 It would be very useful to have another person to help keep them up to date. 如果能多一個人幫忙保持記錄更新，會非常有用。 FRANK: Right. I’m used to working on a computer – I presume they’re computerised? Frank：明白。我習慣用電腦工作 ——我想那些記錄是電腦化的吧？ JANE: Oh yes. Jane：哦，是的。 FRANK: Is the library purpose-built? Frank：圖書館是專門建造的嗎？ I haven’t noticed it when I’ve walked round the village. 我在村裡散步時沒有注意到它。 JANE: No, we simply have the use of a room in the village hall, the West Room. Jane：不是，我們只是使用村民大廳裡的一個房間，也就是 West Room。 It’s on the left as you go in. 你進去後左手邊就是。 FRANK: I must go and have a look inside the hall. Frank：我一定要去大廳裡看看。 JANE: Yes, it’s a nice building. Jane：是的，那是一棟漂亮的建築。 FRANK: Do you run a lunch club in the village for elderly people? Frank：你們村裡有為長者開設午餐俱樂部嗎？ I know a lot of places do. 我知道很多地方都有。 JANE: Yes, we have a very successful club. Jane：有的，我們的午餐俱樂部很成功。 FRANK: I could help with transport, if that’s of any use. Frank：如果有需要的話，我可以幫忙接送。 JANE: Ooo definitely. People come to the club from neighbouring villages, and we’re always in need of more drivers. Jane：哦，當然需要。有人會從鄰近村莊來參加，我們一直需要更多司機。 FRANK: And does the club have groups that focus on a particular hobby, too? Frank：那俱樂部也有專注於某些興趣的小組嗎？ I could get involved in one or two, particularly if there are any art groups. 我可以參與一兩個，尤其是如果有藝術小組的話。 JANE: Excellent. I’ll find out where we need help and get back to you. Jane：太好了。我會了解一下哪裡需要幫忙，然後再聯絡你。 FRANK: Fine. What about help for individual residents? Frank：好的。那對個別居民的幫助呢？ Do you arrange that at all? 你們也安排這類事情嗎？ JANE: Yes, we do it as a one-off. In fact, there’s Mrs Carroll. Jane：有，我們會安排一次性的幫助。事實上，現在就有 Carroll 太太需要幫忙。 She needs a lift to the hospital next week, and we’re struggling to find someone. 她下週需要有人載她去醫院，而我們正努力找人。 FRANK: When’s her appointment? Frank：她的預約是什麼時候？ JANE: On Tuesday. It would take the whole morning. Jane：星期二。會花整個上午。 FRANK: I could do that. Frank：我可以幫忙。 JANE: Oh, that would be great. Thank you. Jane：哦，那太好了。謝謝你。 And also, next week, we’re arranging to have some work done to Mr Selsbury’s house before he moves, as he isn’t healthy enough to do it himself. 另外，下週我們也在安排人在 Selsbury 先生搬家前幫他整理房子，因為他身體不太好，無法自己做。 We’ve got some people to decorate his kitchen, but if you could do some weeding in his garden, that would be wonderful. 我們已經找了人裝修他的廚房， 但如果你能幫他花園除草，那就太好了。 FRANK: OK. I’d enjoy that. And presumably the day and time are flexible. Frank：好的。我會很樂意。而且我想日期和時間應該很彈性吧。 JANE: Oh yes. Just say when would suit you best, and we’ll let Mr Selsbury know. Jane：哦，是的。你只要說什麼時間最方便，我們會通知 Selsbury 先生。 FRANK: Good. Frank：很好。 JANE: The volunteers group also organises monthly social events, which is a great way to meet other people, of course. Jane：志工團體也會每月舉辦社交活動，當然，這也是認識其他人的好方法。 FRANK: Uhuh. Frank：嗯。 JANE: So next month, on the 19th of October, we’re holding a quiz – a couple of residents are great at planning unusual ones, and we always fill the village hall. Jane：所以下個月 10 月 19 日， 我們會舉辦一場問答比賽。有幾位居民很擅長設計特別的題目， 而且每次村民大廳都會坐滿。 FRANK: That sounds like fun. Frank：聽起來很有趣。 Can I do anything to help? 我能幫什麼忙嗎？ JANE: Well, because of the number of people, we need plenty of refreshments for halfway through. Jane：嗯，因為人很多，中場時我們需要大量茶點。 So, if you could provide any, we’d be grateful. 所以如果你能提供一些，我們會很感激。 FRANK: I’m sure I could. I’ll think about what to make, and let you know. Frank：我應該可以。我會想想要做什麼，然後告訴你。 JANE: Thank you. Then on November the 18th, we’re holding a dance, also in the village hall. Jane：謝謝。接著 11 月 18 日，我們會舉辦舞會，也是在村民大廳。 We’ve booked a band that specialises in music of the 1930s – they’ve been before, and we’ve had a lot of requests to bring them back. 我們預訂了一支專門演奏 1930 年代音樂的樂隊。他們以前來過，而且很多人要求再請他們回來。 FRANK: I’m not really a dancer, but I’d like to do something to help. Frank：我不太會跳舞，但我想做點事情幫忙。 JANE: Well, we sell tickets in advance, and having an extra person to check them at the door, as people arrive, would be good – it can be quite a bottleneck if everyone arrives at once! Jane：嗯，我們會提前售票，如果有人能在大家到場時在門口查票會很好——如果大家同時到， 門口會很容易堵住！ FRANK: OK, I’m happy with that. Frank：好的，我很樂意。 JANE: We’re also arranging a New Year’s Eve party. Jane：我們也在安排跨年派對。 We’re expecting that to be a really big event, so instead of the village hall, it’ll be held in the Mountfort Hotel. 我們預計那會是一場很大的活動，所以不會在村民大廳，而會在 Mountfort Hotel 舉行。 FRANK: The …? Frank：什麼……？ JANE: Mountfort. M-O-U-N-T-F-O-R-T Hotel. Jane：Mountfort， M-O-U-N-T-F-O-R-T Hotel。 It isn’t in Southoe itself, but it’s only a couple of miles away. 它不在 Southoe 村裡，但只有幾英里遠。 The hotel will be providing dinner and we’ve booked a band. 飯店會提供晚餐，我們也預訂了樂隊。 The one thing we haven’t got yet is a poster. 目前唯一還沒有的是海報。 That isn’t something you could do, by any chance, is it? 你不會剛好能做這個吧？ FRANK: Well actually, yes. Before I retired I was a graphic designer, so that’s right up my street. Frank：其實可以。我退休前是平面設計師，所以這正是我擅長的。 JANE: Oh perfect! I’ll give you the details, and then perhaps you could send me a draft … Jane：哦，太好了！我會把細節給你，然後也許你可以寄一份草稿給我…… FRANK: Of course. Frank：當然。

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–14 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Oniton Hall 11. Many past owners made changes to A. the gardens. B. the house. C. the farm. 12. Sir Edward Downes built Oniton Hall because he wanted A. a place for discussing politics. B. a place to display his wealth. C. a place for artists and writers. 13. Visitors can learn about the work of servants in the past from A. audio guides. B. photographs. C. people in costume. 14. What is new for children at Oniton Hall? A. clothes for dressing up B. mini tractors C. the adventure playground Questions 15–20 Which activity is offered at each of the following locations on the farm? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 15–20. Activities A. shopping B. watching cows being milked C. seeing old farming equipment D. eating and drinking E. starting a trip F. seeing rare breeds of animals G. helping to look after animals H. using farming tools Locations on the farm 15. dairy __________ 16. large barn __________ 17. small barn __________ 18. stables __________ 19. shed __________ 20. parkland __________ Many past owners made changes to the gardens. the house. the farm. Sir Edward Downes built Oniton Hall because he wanted a place for discussing politics. a place to display his wealth. a place for artists and writers. Visitors can learn about the work of servants in the past from audio guides. photographs. people in costume. What is new for children at Oniton Hall? clothes for dressing up mini tractors the adventure playground dairy shopping watching cows being milked seeing old farming equipment eating and drinking starting a trip seeing rare breeds of animals helping to look after animals using farming tools large barn shopping watching cows being milked seeing old farming equipment eating and drinking starting a trip seeing rare breeds of animals helping to look after animals using farming tools small barn shopping watching cows being milked seeing old farming equipment eating and drinking starting a trip seeing rare breeds of animals helping to look after animals using farming tools stables shopping watching cows being milked seeing old farming equipment eating and drinking starting a trip seeing rare breeds of animals helping to look after animals using farming tools shed shopping watching cows being milked seeing old farming equipment eating and drinking starting a trip seeing rare breeds of animals helping to look after animals using farming tools parkland shopping watching cows being milked seeing old farming equipment eating and drinking starting a trip seeing rare breeds of animals helping to look after animals using farming tools Good morning, and welcome to Oniton Hall, one of the largest estates in the area. 早安，歡迎來到 Oniton Hall， 這是本地區最大的莊園之一。 My name’s Nick, and I’m one of the guides. 我叫 Nick，是導覽員之一。 I’ll give you a brief introduction to the estate while you’re sitting down, and then we’ll walk round. 在大家坐著休息時，我會先簡要介紹一下這座莊園，然後我們再四處參觀。 The estate consists of the house, gardens, parkland and farm, and it dates back to the fourteenth century. 這座莊園包括主屋、花園、公園綠地和農場，歷史可追溯到 14 世紀。 The original house was replaced in the late seventeenth century, and of course it has had a large number of owners. 原本的房子在 17 世紀末被替換，當然，它也曾有過許多主人。 Almost all of them have left their mark, generally by adding new rooms, like the ballroom and conservatory, or by demolishing others. 幾乎每位主人都留下了自己的痕跡，通常是增建新房間， 例如舞廳和溫室，或拆除其他房間。 The farm looks much as it’s always done, although the current owner has done a great deal of work to the flower beds. 農場看起來基本上和過去差不多，不過現任主人對花壇做了大量整理。 In the seventeenth century, the estate was owned by a very wealthy man called Sir Edward Downes. 在 17 世紀，這座莊園屬於一位非常富有的人，名叫 Sir Edward Downes。 His intention was to escape from the world of politics, after years as an active politician, and to build a new house worthy of his big collection of books, paintings and sculptures. 他多年來一直活躍於政壇，後來想遠離政治世界，並建造一座配得上他大量書籍、繪畫和雕塑收藏的新宅邸。 He broke off contact with his former political allies, and hosted meetings of creative and literary people, like painters and poets. 他與過去的政治盟友斷絕聯繫，轉而舉辦畫家、詩人等創意和文學人士的聚會。 Unusually for his time, he didn’t care whether his guests were rich or poor, as long as they had talent. 以他那個時代來說很特別的是，他不在乎客人貧富，只要他們有才華。 Big houses like Oniton had dozens of servants until the 1920s or 30s, and we’ve tried to show what their working lives were like. 像 Oniton 這樣的大宅一直到 1920 或 1930 年代都有數十名僕人，我們試圖展示他們當年的工作生活。 Photographs of course don’t give much of an idea, so instead, as you go round the house, you’ll see volunteers dressed up as nineteenth-century servants, going about their work. 當然，照片無法充分呈現，所以當你們參觀屋內時，會看到志工打扮成 19 世紀僕人的樣子，忙著做自己的工作。 They’ll explain what they’re doing, and tell you their recipes, or what tools they’re using. 他們會解釋自己在做什麼，並告訴你他們的食譜或正在使用的工具。 We’ve just introduced this feature to replace the audio guide we used to have available. 我們剛推出這項安排，用來取代以前提供的語音導覽。 I see there are a number of children here with you today. 我看到今天有不少孩子和你們一起來。 Well, we have several activities specially for children, like dressing up in the sorts of clothes that children wore in the past, and as it’s a fine day, some of you will probably want to play in the adventure playground. 我們有幾項專為孩子設計的活動，例如穿上過去兒童穿的服裝；而且今天天氣很好，你們有些人可能也會想去冒險遊樂場玩。 Our latest addition is child-sized tractors, that you can drive around the grounds. 我們最新增加的是兒童尺寸的小拖拉機，孩子們可以在場地裡駕駛。 We’ll also be going into the farm that’s part of the estate, where there’s plenty to do. 我們也會進入莊園內的農場， 那裡有很多活動。 Most of the buildings date from the eighteenth century, so you can really step back into an agricultural past. 大多數建築可追溯到 18 世紀，所以你可以真正走進過去的農業生活。 Until recently, the dairy was where milk from the cows was turned into cheese. 直到不久前，乳品房還是把牛奶製成起司的地方。 It’s now the place to go for lunch, or afternoon tea, or just a cup of coffee and a slice of homemade cake. 現在那裡成了吃午餐、下午茶，或喝杯咖啡配一片自製蛋糕的地方。 The big stone building that dominates the farm is the large barn, and in here is our collection of agricultural tools. 農場裡最醒目的大型石造建築是大穀倉，裡面收藏著我們的農具。 These were used in the past to plough the earth, sow seeds, make gates, and much more. 這些工具過去用來犁地、播種、製作大門等。 There’s a small barn, also made of stone, where you can groom the donkeys and horses, to keep their coats clean. 還有一座小穀倉，也是石造的，你們可以在那裡為驢子和馬梳理毛髮，保持牠們的皮毛乾淨。 They really seem to enjoy having it done, and children love grooming them. 牠們似乎真的很享受被梳理， 而孩子們也很喜歡幫牠們整理。 The horses no longer live in the stables, which instead is the place to go to buy gifts, books, our own jams and pickles, and clothes and blankets made of wool from our sheep. 馬廄裡現在不再養馬，而是成了購買禮物、書籍、自製果醬和醃菜，以及用本莊園羊毛製成的衣服和毯子的地方。 Outside the shed, which is the only brick building, you can climb into a horse-drawn carriage for a lovely, relaxing tour of the park and farm. 棚屋是唯一的磚造建築，在它外面，你可以登上一輛馬車， 輕鬆愉快地遊覽公園和農場。 The carriages are well over a hundred years old. 這些馬車已有一百多年歷史。 And finally, the parkland, which was laid out in the eighteenth century, with a lake and trees that are now well established. 最後是公園綠地，它於 18 世紀規劃而成，裡面有湖泊和如今已長得很成熟的樹木。 You’ll see types of cattle and sheep that are hardly ever found on farms these days. 你們會看到如今農場上幾乎見不到的牛羊品種。 We’re helping to preserve them, to stop their numbers falling further. 我們正在協助保護牠們，防止數量進一步下降。 OK, well if you’d like to come with me … 好的，如果大家願意跟我來 ……

entries.title: Listening Practice 13
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21 and 22 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO things do the students agree they need to include in their reviews of Romeo and Juliet? A. analysis of the text B. a summary of the plot C. a description of the theatre D. a personal reaction E. a reference to particular scenes Questions 23–27 Which opinion do the speakers give about each of the following aspects of The Emporium’s production of Romeo and Juliet? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 23–27. Opinions A. They both expected this to be more traditional. B. They both thought this was original. C. They agree this created the right atmosphere. D. They agree this was a major strength. E. They were both disappointed by this. F. They disagree about why this was an issue. G. They disagree about how this could be improved. Aspects of the production 23. the set __________ 24. the lighting __________ 25. the costume design __________ 26. the music __________ 27. the actors’ delivery __________ Questions 28–30 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 28. The students think the story of Romeo and Juliet is still relevant for young people today because A. it illustrates how easily conflict can start. B. it deals with problems that families experience. C. it teaches them about relationships. 29. The students found watching Romeo and Juliet in another language A. frustrating. B. demanding. C. moving. 30. Why do the students think Shakespeare’s plays have such international appeal? A. The stories are exciting. B. There are recognisable characters. C. They can be interpreted in many ways. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO things do the students agree they need to include in their reviews of Romeo and Juliet? analysis of the text a summary of the plot a description of the theatre a personal reaction a reference to particular scenes the set They both expected this to be more traditional. They both thought this was original. They agree this created the right atmosphere. They agree this was a major strength. They were both disappointed by this. They disagree about why this was an issue. They disagree about how this could be improved. the lighting They both expected this to be more traditional. They both thought this was original. They agree this created the right atmosphere. They agree this was a major strength. They were both disappointed by this. They disagree about why this was an issue. They disagree about how this could be improved. the costume design They both expected this to be more traditional. They both thought this was original. They agree this created the right atmosphere. They agree this was a major strength. They were both disappointed by this. They disagree about why this was an issue. They disagree about how this could be improved. the music They both expected this to be more traditional. They both thought this was original. They agree this created the right atmosphere. They agree this was a major strength. They were both disappointed by this. They disagree about why this was an issue. They disagree about how this could be improved. the actors’ delivery They both expected this to be more traditional. They both thought this was original. They agree this created the right atmosphere. They agree this was a major strength. They were both disappointed by this. They disagree about why this was an issue. They disagree about how this could be improved. The students think the story of Romeo and Juliet is still relevant for young people today because it illustrates how easily conflict can start. it deals with problems that families experience. it teaches them about relationships. The students found watching Romeo and Juliet in another language frustrating. demanding. moving. Why do the students think Shakespeare’s plays have such international appeal? The stories are exciting. There are recognisable characters. They can be interpreted in many ways. ED: Did you make notes while you were watching the performances of Romeo and Juliet, Gemma? Ed：Gemma，你看《Romeo and Juliet》演出時有做筆記嗎？ GEMMA: Yes, I did. I found it quite hard though. Gemma：有。不過我覺得挺難的。 I kept getting too involved in the play. 我一直太投入劇情。 ED: Me too. I ended up not taking notes. Ed：我也是。結果我最後沒有做筆記。 I wrote down my impressions when I got home. 我回家後才寫下自己的觀感。 Do you mind if I check a few things with you? 你介意我跟你確認幾件事嗎？ In case I’ve missed anything. 以防我漏掉什麼。 And I’ve also got some questions about our assignment. 而且我對作業也有一些問題。 GEMMA: No, it’s good to talk things through. Gemma：不介意，把事情討論清楚很好。 I may have missed things too. 我可能也漏掉了一些東西。 ED: OK great. So first of all, I’m not sure how much information we should include in our reviews. Ed：好，太好了。首先，我不確定評論裡應該包含多少資訊。 GEMMA: Right. Well, I don’t think we need to describe what happens. Gemma：對。嗯，我覺得我們不需要描述劇情發生了什麼。 Especially as Romeo and Juliet is one of Shakespeare’s most well-known plays. 尤其是《Romeo and Juliet》是莎士比亞最知名的劇作之一。 ED: Yeah, everyone knows the story. Ed：是啊，大家都知道故事。 In an essay we’d focus on the poetry and Shakespeare’s use of imagery etc., but that isn’t really relevant in a review. 如果是論文，我們會關注詩性語言和莎士比亞對意象的運用等，但那些在評論中不太相關。 We’re supposed to focus on how effective this particular production is. 我們應該聚焦在這個特定製作版本的效果如何。 GEMMA: Mmm. We should say what made it a success or a failure. Gemma：嗯。我們應該說明是什麼讓它成功或失敗。 ED: And part of that means talking about the emotional impact the performance had on us. Ed：而其中一部分就是談論這場演出對我們造成的情感影響。 I think that’s important. 我覺得那很重要。 GEMMA: Yes. And we should definitely mention how well the director handled important bits of the play – like when Romeo climbs onto Juliet’s balcony. Gemma：是的。我們也一定要提到導演如何處理劇中重要片段，例如 Romeo 爬上 Juliet 陽台那一幕。 ED: And the fight between Mercutio and Tybalt. Ed：還有 Mercutio 和 Tybalt 的打鬥。 GEMMA: Yes. It would also be interesting to mention the theatre space and how the director used it but I don’t think we’ll have space in 800 words. Gemma：是的。提到劇場空間以及導演如何運用空間也會很有趣，但我覺得 800 字裡寫不下。 ED: No. OK. That all sounds quite straightforward. Ed：是啊。好，那聽起來很清楚。 ED: So what about The Emporium Theatre’s production of the play? Ed：那 The Emporium Theatre 的這個版本怎麼樣？ GEMMA: I thought some things worked really well but there were some problems too. Gemma：我覺得有些地方效果很好，但也有一些問題。 ED: Yeah. What about the set, for example? Ed：是啊。例如布景呢？ GEMMA: I think it was visually really stunning. Gemma：我覺得它在視覺上真的很驚艷。 I’d say that was probably the most memorable thing about this production. 我會說那可能是這個製作版本最令人難忘的地方。 ED: You’re right. The set design was really amazing, but actually I have seen similar ideas used in other productions. Ed：你說得對。布景設計真的很棒，不過其實我在其他製作中也看過類似想法。 GEMMA: What about the lighting? Gemma：燈光呢？ Some of the scenes were so dimly lit it was quite hard to see. 有些場景光線太暗，很難看清。 ED: I didn’t dislike it. Ed：我倒不討厭。 It helped to change the mood of the quieter scenes. 它有助於改變較安靜場景的氛圍。 GEMMA: That’s a good point. Gemma：這是個好觀點。 ED: What did you think of the costumes? Ed：你覺得服裝怎麼樣？ GEMMA: I was a bit surprised by the contemporary dress, I must say. Gemma：我得說，我對現代服裝有點驚訝。 ED: Yeah – I think it worked well, but I had assumed it would be more conventional. Ed：是啊，我覺得效果不錯，但我原本以為會更傳統一些。 GEMMA: Me too. I liked the music at the beginning and I thought the musicians were brilliant, but I thought they were wasted because the music didn’t have much impact in Acts 2 and 3. Gemma：我也是。我喜歡開頭的音樂，也覺得樂手很出色，但我覺得他們沒有被充分利用，因為音樂在第二幕和第三幕中影響不大。 ED: Yes – that was a shame. Ed：是啊，那很可惜。 GEMMA: One problem with this production was that the actors didn’t deliver the lines that well. Gemma：這個製作版本的一個問題是演員台詞表現不太好。 They were speaking too fast. 他們說得太快了。 ED: It was a problem I agree, but I thought it was because they weren’t speaking loudly enough – especially at key points in the play. Ed：我同意那是個問題，但我覺得是因為他們聲音不夠大，尤其是在劇中的關鍵時刻。 GEMMA: I actually didn’t have a problem with that. Gemma：其實我倒沒有覺得那是問題。 ED: It’s been an interesting experience watching different versions of Romeo and Juliet, hasn’t it? Ed：觀看不同版本的《Romeo and Juliet》真是一次有趣的經驗，不是嗎？ GEMMA: Definitely. It’s made me realise how relevant the play still is. Gemma：絕對是。它讓我意識到這齣戲至今仍然很有現實意義。 ED: Right. I mean a lot’s changed since Shakespeare’s time, but in many ways nothing’s changed. Ed：對。我的意思是，自莎士比亞時代以來，很多事情都改變了，但在許多方面其實又沒有變。 There are always disagreements and tension between teenagers and their parents. 青少年和父母之間總是會有分歧和緊張關係。 GEMMA: Yes, that’s something all young people can relate to – more than the violence and the extreme emotions in the play. Gemma：是的，那是所有年輕人都能產生共鳴的部分，比劇中的暴力和極端情緒更貼近他們。 ED: How did you find watching it in translation? Ed：你覺得看翻譯版本怎麼樣？ GEMMA: Really interesting. I expected to find it more challenging, but I could follow the story pretty well. Gemma：很有趣。我原本以為會更有挑戰性，但我能很好地跟上故事。 ED: I stopped worrying about not being able to understand all the words and focused on the actors’ expressions. Ed：我不再擔心聽不懂所有詞， 而是專注於演員的表情。 The ending was pretty powerful. 結尾相當有感染力。 GEMMA: Yes. That somehow intensified the emotion for me. Gemma：是的。那不知怎麼讓我的情緒更強烈。 ED: Did you know Shakespeare’s been translated into more languages than any other writer? Ed：你知道莎士比亞作品被翻譯成的語言比任何其他作家都多嗎？ GEMMA: What’s the reason for his international appeal, do you think? Gemma：你覺得他具有國際吸引力的原因是什麼？ ED: I was reading that it’s because his plays are about basic themes that people everywhere are familiar with. Ed：我讀到過，原因是他的劇作涉及世界各地人們都熟悉的基本主題。 GEMMA: Yeah, and they can also be understood on different levels. Gemma：是啊，而且它們也可以在不同層次上被理解。 The characters have such depth. 角色非常有深度。 ED: Right – which allows directors to experiment and find new angles. Ed：對，這讓導演可以嘗試不同做法，找到新的角度。 GEMMA: That’s really important because … Gemma：這真的很重要，因為 ……
