JEANNE: Hi Thomas, how are you enjoying the course so far? Jeanne：嗨，Thomas，到目前為止你覺得這門課怎麼樣？ THOMAS: Yeah, I think it’s good. Thomas：嗯，我覺得不錯。 JEANNE: Remind me – why did you decide to study sports science? Jeanne：提醒我一下，你為什麼決定讀運動科學？ Didn’t you want to be a professional athlete when you were at school? 你上學時不是想成為職業運動員嗎？ THOMAS: Yeah – that was my goal, and all my classmates assumed I would achieve it; they thought I was brilliant. Thomas：是的，那曾是我的目標，而且所有同學都以為我會做到；他們覺得我很出色。 JEANNE: That must have been a nice feeling. Jeanne：那感覺一定很好。 THOMAS: Mm, I thought I could win anything. Thomas：嗯，我當時覺得自己什麼都能贏。 There was no one who could run faster than me. 沒有人跑得比我快。 JEANNE: Exactly – so what happened? Jeanne：正是如此，那後來發生了什麼？ Did your mum and dad want you to be more “academic”? 你爸媽希望你更專注於學業嗎？ THOMAS: Not at all. Perhaps they should have pushed me harder, though. Thomas：完全不是。不過也許他們當時應該更督促我。 JEANNE: What do you mean? Jeanne：你是什麼意思？ THOMAS: I think I should have practised more. Thomas：我覺得我應該練得更多。 JEANNE: What makes you say that? Jeanne：為什麼這麼說？ THOMAS: Well, I went out to Kenya for a couple of weeks to train … Thomas：嗯，我去肯亞訓練了幾週…… JEANNE: Really! I didn’t know that. Jeanne：真的！我不知道這件事。 THOMAS: I was chosen to go there out of loads of kids and run with some of the top teenage athletes in the world. Thomas：我是從很多孩子中被選出來去那裡，和世界上一些頂尖青少年運動員一起跑步。 And … I was so calm about it. 而且……我對這件事很冷靜。 I just kept thinking how fortunate I was. 我一直在想自己有多幸運。 What a great chance this was! 這是一個多麼好的機會！ Everyone back home was so proud of me. 家裡所有人都為我感到驕傲。 But once we started competing, I very quickly realised I wasn’t good enough. 但一開始比賽，我很快就意識到自己不夠好。 JEANNE: That must have been a huge shock. Jeanne：那一定是很大的打擊。 THOMAS: I thought “this can’t be happening”! Thomas：我當時想：「這不可能發生！」 I was used to winning. 我已經習慣贏了。 JEANNE: I’m sorry to hear that. Jeanne：聽到這件事我很遺憾。 THOMAS: It’s OK. I’m over it now and I think it’s much better to do a university course and this one has such a variety of sports-related areas. Thomas：沒事。我現在已經走出來了，而且我覺得讀大學課程更好，這門課涵蓋了很多和運動相關的領域。 It’s going to be good. 會很不錯的。 JEANNE: Oh, I agree – I chose it because of that. Jeanne：哦，我同意。我就是因為這點才選它的。 THOMAS: So Jeanne – have you thought of any ideas for the discussion session next week on technology and sport? Thomas：那麼 Jeanne，你有想到下週科技與運動討論課的任何想法嗎？ JEANNE: We have to cover more than one sport, don’t we? Jeanne：我們得涵蓋不只一項運動，對吧？ THOMAS: Yeah. Thomas：對。 JEANNE: You know – we always think technology is about the future, but we could gather some ideas about past developments in sport. Jeanne：你知道，我們總是覺得科技是關於未來的，但我們也可以整理一些過去運動發展中的科技變化。 THOMAS: Look at early types of equipment perhaps? Thomas：也許可以看看早期的運動器材？ Uh, I remember reading something about table tennis bats once – how they ended up being covered with pimpled rubber. 呃，我記得曾讀過一些關於乒乓球拍的內容，說它們最後是怎麼覆蓋上顆粒橡膠的。 JEANNE: Cos they were just wooden at first, I’d imagine. Jeanne：我想它們最早只是木製的吧。 THOMAS: Yeah. In about the 1920s, a factory was making rolls of the rubber in bulk for something like horse harnesses. Thomas：是的。大約在 1920 年代，有一家工廠大量生產成卷橡膠，好像是用於馬具之類的東西。 JEANNE: Really! Jeanne：真的嗎！ THOMAS: Yeah – and someone realised that it’d make a perfect covering for the wooden bats. Thomas：是啊，然後有人意識到這種橡膠非常適合覆蓋在木製球拍上。 JEANNE: So what about cricket – that’s had a few innovative changes. Jeanne：那板球呢？它也有一些創新變化。 Maybe the pads they wear on their legs? 也許是他們腿上戴的護墊？ THOMAS: I don’t think they’ve changed much but, I’m just looking on the internet … and it says that when the first cricket helmet came in, in 1978, the Australian batsman who first wore it was booed and jeered by people watching because it was so ugly! Thomas：我不覺得那些變化很大，但我正在網上看……這裡說第一頂板球頭盔在 1978 年出現時，第一位戴上它的澳洲擊球手被觀眾喝倒采和嘲笑，因為它太醜了！ JEANNE: Wow, players have to protect themselves from getting hurt! Jeanne：哇，球員必須保護自己不受傷啊！ I mean everyone wears one now. 我的意思是，現在大家都戴了。 THOMAS: Mm, unlike the cycle helmet. Thomas：嗯，不像自行車安全帽。 JEANNE: Well, unless you’re a professional, but you’re right, many ordinary bikers don’t wear a helmet. Jeanne：嗯，除非是職業選手， 不過你說得對，很多普通騎士不戴安全帽。 THOMAS: Hey, look at these pictures of original helmet designs. Thomas：嘿，看看這些早期安全帽設計的照片。 This one looks like an upside-down bowl! 這個看起來像倒扣的碗！ JEANNE: Yet, the woman’s laughing – she’s so proud to be wearing it! Jeanne：可是那位女士在笑，她戴著它看起來很驕傲！ THOMAS: It says serious cyclists ended up with wet hair from all the hard exercise. Thomas：這裡說，認真騎車的人因為大量運動，最後頭髮都濕了。 JEANNE: I guess that’s why they have large air vents in them now so that the skin can breathe more easily. Jeanne：我想這就是為什麼現在的安全帽有大通風孔，讓皮膚比較容易透氣。 THOMAS: OK, so we’ve done helmets. Thomas：好，安全帽我們說完了。 What about golf balls or better still golf clubs – they’ve changed a lot. 那高爾夫球呢，或者更好的是高爾夫球桿，它們變化很大。 JEANNE: Yeah – I remember my great grandfather telling me that because a club was made entirely of wood, it would easily break and players had to get another. Jeanne：是啊，我記得曾祖父告訴我，以前球桿完全由木頭製成，很容易斷，球員不得不換新的。 THOMAS: There’s no wood at all in them now, is there? Thomas：現在裡面完全沒有木頭了，對吧？ JEANNE: No – they’re much more powerful. Jeanne：沒有了，而且現在的球桿強度大得多。 THOMAS: The same must be true of hockey sticks. Thomas：曲棍球桿一定也是這樣。 JEANNE: I don’t think so because players still use wooden sticks today. Jeanne：我不這麼認為，因為球員現在仍然使用木製球桿。 What it does say here, though, is that when the game started you had to produce a stick yourself. 不過這裡說，這項運動剛開始時，球員必須自己製作球桿。 THOMAS: I guess they just weren’t being manufactured. Thomas：我想那時候還沒有大規模生產。 So, one more perhaps. What about football? 那再說一個吧。足球怎麼樣？ JEANNE: Well, I know the first balls were made of animal skin. Jeanne：嗯，我知道最早的足球是用動物皮做的。 THOMAS: Yeah, they covered them with pieces of leather that were stitched together, but … the balls let in water when it rained. Thomas：是的，球的外層是由縫在一起的皮革片覆蓋，但…… 下雨時球會進水。 JEANNE: Oh, that would have made them much heavier. Jeanne：哦，那會讓它們重很多。 THOMAS: That’s right. You can imagine the damage to players’ necks when the ball was headed. Thomas：沒錯。你可以想像球員頂球時，這對脖子造成多大傷害。 JEANNE: How painful that must have been! Jeanne：那一定很痛！ THOMAS: Yeah, well, I think we can put together some useful ideas … Thomas：是啊，嗯，我覺得我們可以整理出一些有用的想法 ……

entries.title: Listening Practice 15
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Maple Syrup What is maple syrup? ● made from the sap of the maple tree ● colour described as 31 __________ ● added to food or used in cooking ● very 32 __________ compared to refined sugar The maple tree ● has many species ● needs moist soil but does not need fertiliser as well ● needs sunny days and cool nights ● best growing conditions and 33 __________ are in Canada and North America ● maple leaf has been on the Canadian flag since 1964 Early maple sugar producers ● made holes in the tree trunks ● used tree bark to make containers for collection ● used hot 34 __________ to heat the sap ● sweetened food and drink with sugar Today’s maple syrup The trees ● Tree trunks may not have the correct 35 __________ until they have been growing for 40 years. ● The changing temperature and movement of water within the tree produces the sap. The production ● A tap is drilled into the trunk and a 36 __________ carries the sap into a bucket. ● Large pans of sap called evaporators are heated by means of a 37 __________. ● A lot of 38 __________ is produced during the evaporation process. ● “Sugar sand” is removed because it makes the syrup look 39 __________ and affects the taste. ● The syrup is ready for use. ● A huge quantity of sap is needed to make a 40 __________ of maple syrup. ● colour described as 31 __________ ● very 32 __________ compared to refined sugar ● best growing conditions and 33 __________ are in Canada and North ● used hot 34 __________ to heat the sap ● Tree trunks may not have the correct 35 __________ until they have ● A tap is drilled into the trunk and a 36 __________ carries the sap into ● Large pans of sap called evaporators are heated by means of a 37 __________. ● A lot of 38 __________ is produced during the evaporation process. ● “Sugar sand” is removed because it makes the syrup look 39 __________ ● A huge quantity of sap is needed to make a 40 __________ of maple Hello everyone. Today we’re going to look at another natural food product and that’s maple syrup. 大家好。今天我們要來看另一種天然食品，那就是楓糖漿。 What is this exactly? 它到底是什麼呢？ Well, maple syrup looks rather like clear honey, but it’s not made by bees; it’s produced from the plant fluid – or sap – inside the maple tree and that makes maple syrup a very natural product. 楓糖漿看起來有點像清澈的蜂蜜，但它不是由蜜蜂製成的；它是由楓樹內部的植物液，也就是樹液製成，因此楓糖漿是一種非常天然的產品。 Maple syrup is a thick, golden, sweet-tasting liquid that can be bought in bottles or jars and poured onto food such as waffles and ice cream or used in the baking of cakes and pastries. 楓糖漿是一種濃稠、金黃色、 味道甜美的液體，可以裝在瓶子或罐子裡購買，倒在鬆餅和冰淇淋等食物上，也可以用於烘焙蛋糕和糕點。 It contains no preservatives or added ingredients, and it provides a healthy alternative to refined sugar. 它不含防腐劑或添加成分，是精製糖較健康的替代品。 Let’s just talk a bit about the maple tree itself, which is where maple syrup comes from. 接著我們來談談楓糖漿來源的楓樹本身。 So, there are many species of maple tree, and they’ll grow without fertilizer in areas where there’s plenty of moisture in the soil. 楓樹有許多種類，只要土壤中水分充足，即使不施肥也能生長。 However, they’ll only do this if another important criterion is fulfilled, which is that they must have full or partial sun exposure during the day and very cool nights – and I’ll talk more about that in a minute. 不過，它們還需要滿足另一個重要條件，那就是白天必須有全日照或部分日照，夜晚則要非常涼爽——這點我稍後會再說明。 There are only certain parts of the world that provide all these conditions: one is Canada, and by that, I mean all parts of Canada, and the other is the north-eastern states of North America. 世界上只有某些地區能提供所有這些條件：其中一個是加拿大，我指的是加拿大各地；另一個是北美東北部各州。 In these areas, the climate suits the trees perfectly. 在這些地區，氣候非常適合楓樹。 In fact, Canada produces over two-thirds of the world’s maple syrup, which is why the five-pointed maple leaf is a Canadian symbol and has featured on the flag since 1964. 事實上，加拿大生產全球超過三分之二的楓糖漿，這也是為什麼五角楓葉是加拿大象徵， 並自 1964 年起出現在加拿大國旗上。 So how did maple syrup production begin? 那麼，楓糖漿的生產是如何開始的呢？ Well, long before Europeans settled in these parts of the world, the indigenous communities had started producing maple sugar. 早在歐洲人定居這些地區之前，原住民社群就已經開始製作楓糖。 They bored holes in the trunks of maple trees and used containers made of tree bark to collect the liquid sap as it poured out. 他們在楓樹樹幹上鑽孔，並用樹皮製成容器，收集流出的液態樹液。 As they were unable to keep the liquid for any length of time – they didn’t have storage facilities in those days – they boiled the liquid by placing pieces of rock that had become scorching hot from the sun into the sap. 由於他們無法長時間保存液體 ——當時沒有儲存設備——他們會把被太陽曬得滾燙的石塊放入樹液中，藉此將液體煮沸。 They did this until it turned into sugar, and they were then able to use this to sweeten their food and drinks. 他們反覆這樣做，直到樹液變成糖，然後就能用它來為食物和飲品增甜。 Since that time, improvements have been made to the process, but it has changed very little overall. 自那時起，製作流程雖然有一些改良，但整體變化很小。 So let’s look at the production of maple syrup today. 那麼我們來看看如今楓糖漿的生產方式。 Clearly, the maple forests are a valuable resource in many Canadian and North American communities. 顯然，楓樹林在許多加拿大和北美社區中都是寶貴資源。 The trees have to be well looked after and they cannot be used to make syrup until the trunks reach a diameter of around 25 centimetres. 這些樹必須受到良好照料，而且只有當樹幹直徑達到約 25 公分時，才能用來製作糖漿。 This can take anything up to 40 years. 這可能需要長達 40 年。 As I’ve already mentioned, maple trees need the right conditions to grow and also to produce sap. Why is this? 正如我已經提到的，楓樹需要合適條件才能生長並產生樹液。為什麼呢？ Well, what happens is that during a cold night, the tree absorbs water from the soil, and that rises through the tree’s vascular system. 情況是這樣的：在寒冷夜晚，樹木會從土壤中吸收水分，水分會透過樹的維管系統向上移動。 But then in the warmer daytime, the change in temperature causes the water to be pushed back down to the bottom of the tree. 但到了較溫暖的白天，溫度變化會使水分被推回樹的底部。 This continual movement – up and down – leads to the formation of the sap needed for maple syrup production. 這種上下來回的持續流動，促成了製作楓糖漿所需樹液的形成。 When the tree is ready, it can be tapped and this involves drilling a small hole into the trunk and inserting a tube into it that ends in a bucket. 當樹準備好後，就可以取樹液了；這需要在樹幹上鑽一個小孔，插入一根通向桶子的管子。 The trees can often take several taps, though the workers take care not to cause any damage to the healthy growth of the tree itself. 一棵樹通常可以插入幾個取液口，不過工人會小心避免損害樹木本身的健康生長。 The sap that comes out of the trees consists of 98 percent water and 2 percent sugar and other nutrients. 從樹中流出的樹液含有 98% 的水，以及 2% 的糖和其他營養物質。 It has to be boiled so that much of that water evaporates, and this process has to take place immediately, using what are called evaporators. 它必須被煮沸，讓大量水分蒸發，而且這個過程必須立即進行，使用所謂的蒸發器。 These are basically extremely large pans – the sap is poured into these, a fire is built and the pans are then heated until the sap boils. 這些基本上是非常大的鍋子； 樹液被倒入其中，然後生火加熱，直到樹液沸騰。 As it does this, the water evaporates, and the syrup begins to form. 在這個過程中，水分蒸發，糖漿開始形成。 The evaporation process creates large quantities of steam, and the sap becomes thicker and denser, and, at just the right moment, when the sap is thick enough to be called maple syrup, the worker removes it from the heat. 蒸發過程會產生大量蒸汽，樹液也會變得越來越濃稠；在恰當時刻，也就是樹液濃到可以稱為楓糖漿時，工人會把它從火上移開。 After this process, something called “sugar sand” has to be filtered out as this builds up during the boiling and gives the syrup a cloudy appearance and a slightly gritty taste. 之後，必須濾除一種叫做 “sugar sand” 的物質，因為它會在煮沸過程中形成，使糖漿看起來混濁，並帶有輕微沙粒感。 Once this has been done, the syrup is ready to be packaged so that it can be used for a whole variety of products. 完成這一步後，糖漿就可以包裝，並用於各式各樣的產品。 It takes 40 litres of sap to produce one litre of maple syrup so you can get an idea of how much is needed! 製作一公升楓糖漿需要 40 公升樹液，所以你可以想像所需的樹液量有多大！ So that’s the basic process. In places like Quebec where … 這就是基本流程。在 Quebec 這樣的地方……

entries.title: Listening Practice 16
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Children’s Engineering Workshops Tiny Engineers, ages 4–5 Activities ● Create a cover for an 1 __________ so they can drop it from a height without breaking it. ● Take part in a competition to build the tallest 2 __________. ● Make a 3 __________ powered by a balloon. Junior Engineers, ages 6–8 Activities ● Build model cars, trucks and 4 __________ and learn how to program them so they can move. ● Take part in a competition to build the longest 5 __________ using card and wood. ● Create a short 6 __________ with special software. ● Build, 7 __________ and program a humanoid robot. Cost for a five-week block: £50 Held on: 8 __________ from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. Location Building 10A, 9 __________ Industrial Estate, Grasford Plenty of 10 __________ is available. ● Create a cover for an 1 __________ so they can drop it from a height ● Take part in a competition to build the tallest 2 __________. ● Make a 3 __________ powered by a balloon. ● Build model cars, trucks and 4 __________ and learn how to program ● Take part in a competition to build the longest 5 __________ using ● Create a short 6 __________ with special software. ● Build, 7 __________ and program a humanoid robot. Held on: 8 __________ from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. Building 10A, 9 __________ Industrial Estate, Grasford Plenty of 10 __________ is available. SARAH: Hello. Children’s Engineering Workshops. Sarah：您好，這裡是 Children’s Engineering Workshops。 FATHER: Oh hello. I wanted some information about the workshops in the school holidays. Father：哦，你好。我想了解一下學校假期期間工作坊的資訊。 SARAH: Sure. Sarah：當然。 FATHER: I have two daughters who are interested. Father：我有兩個女兒，她們都很感興趣。 The younger one’s Lydia, she’s four – do you take children as young as that? 小女兒叫 Lydia，她四歲了—— 你們收這麼小的孩子嗎？ SARAH: Yes, our Tiny Engineers workshop is for four to five-year-olds. Sarah：收的。我們的 Tiny Engineers 工作坊就是為 4 到 5 歲孩子設計的。 FATHER: What sorts of activities do they do? Father：他們會做哪些活動呢？ SARAH: All sorts. For example, they work together to design a special cover that goes round an egg so that when it’s inside they can drop it from a height and it doesn’t break. Sarah：各式各樣的活動都有。 例如，他們會一起設計一種特殊保護套，把雞蛋包在裡面， 這樣從高處掉下來時雞蛋就不會破。 Well, sometimes it does break but that’s part of the fun! 當然，有時候還是會破，不過那也是樂趣的一部分！ FATHER: Right. And Lydia loves building things. Father：明白。Lydia 很喜歡搭建東西。 Is there any opportunity for her to do that? 她有機會做這類活動嗎？ SARAH: Well, they have a competition to see who can make the highest tower. Sarah：有的。他們會比賽，看誰能搭出最高的塔。 You’d be amazed how high they can go. 你會驚訝他們能搭得多高。 FATHER: Right. Father：明白。 SARAH: But they’re learning all the time as well as having fun. Sarah：不過他們在玩得開心的同時，也一直在學習。 For example, one thing they do is to design and build a car that’s attached to a balloon, and the force of the air in that actually powers the car and makes it move along. 例如，他們會設計並製作一輛連著氣球的小車，而氣球裡空氣的力量會推動小車前進。 They go really fast too. 而且小車跑得真的很快。 FATHER: OK, well, all this sounds perfect. Father：好的，這些聽起來都很棒。 FATHER: Now Carly, that’s my older daughter, has just had her seventh birthday, so presumably she’d be in a different group? Father：那 Carly，也就是我的大女兒，剛過七歲生日，所以她應該會在另一個組別吧？ SARAH: Yes, she’d be in the Junior Engineers. Sarah：是的，她會參加 Junior Engineers。 That’s for children from six to eight. 那是為 6 到 8 歲孩子設計的。 FATHER: And do they do the same sorts of activities? Father：他們做的活動也差不多嗎？ SARAH: Some are the same, but a bit more advanced. Sarah：有些相同，但會更進階一些。 So they work out how to build model vehicles, things like cars and trucks, but also how to construct animals using the same sorts of material and technique, and then they learn how they can program them and make them move. 他們會學習如何製作模型交通工具，例如汽車和卡車，也會用相同材料和技巧製作動物模型，然後學習如何為它們編程，讓它們動起來。 FATHER: So they learn a bit of coding? Father：所以他們會學一點編程？ SARAH: They do. They pick it up really quickly. Sarah：會的。而且他們學得很快。 We’re there to help if they need it, but they learn from one another too. 如果他們需要，我們會在旁協助，不過他們也會互相學習。 FATHER: Right. And do they have competitions too? Father：明白。那他們也有比賽嗎？ SARAH: Yes, with the Junior Engineers, it’s to use recycled materials like card and wood to build a bridge, and the longest one gets a prize. Sarah：有的。Junior Engineers 會使用卡紙和木頭等回收材料搭橋，最長的橋可以得獎。 FATHER: That sounds fun. I wouldn’t mind doing that myself! Father：聽起來很有趣。我自己都想試試！ SARAH: Then they have something a bit different, which is to think up an idea for a five-minute movie and then film it, using special animation software. Sarah：接著他們還會做一個有點不同的活動，就是構思一部五分鐘短片，然後用特殊動畫軟體把它拍出來。 You’d be amazed what they come up with. 你會驚訝他們能想出什麼點子。 FATHER: And of course, that’s something they can put on their phone and take home to show all their friends. Father：當然，他們可以把影片放到手機裡，帶回家給朋友看。 SARAH: Exactly. And then they also build a robot in the shape of a human, and they decorate it and program it so that it can move its arms and legs. Sarah：沒錯。然後他們還會製作一個人形機器人，裝飾它並為它編程，讓它的手臂和腿能動。 FATHER: Perfect. So, is it the same price as the Tiny Engineers? Father：太好了。那價格和 Tiny Engineers 一樣嗎？ SARAH: It’s just a bit more: £50 for the five weeks. Sarah：只貴一點，五週 50 英鎊。 FATHER: And are the classes on a Monday, too? Father：課程也是星期一嗎？ SARAH: They used to be, but we found it didn’t give our staff enough time to clear up after the first workshop, so we moved them to Wednesdays. Sarah：以前是，但我們發現第一個工作坊結束後，工作人員沒有足夠時間清理，所以改到星期三了。 The classes are held in the morning from ten to eleven. 課程時間是上午 10 點到 11 點。 FATHER: OK. That’s better for me actually. Father：好的。其實這對我更方便。 And what about the location? Where exactly are the workshops held? 那地點呢？工作坊具體在哪裡舉行？ SARAH: They’re in building 10A – there’s a big sign on the door, you can’t miss it, and that’s in Fradstone Industrial Estate. Sarah：在 10A 大樓，門上有很大的標誌，你不會錯過。地點是在 Fradstone Industrial Estate。 FATHER: Sorry? Father：抱歉，怎麼拼？ SARAH: Fradstone – that’s F-R-A-D-S-T-O-N-E. Sarah：Fradstone，拼作 F-R-A-D-S-T-O-N-E。 FATHER: And that’s in Grasford, isn’t it? Father：那是在 Grasford，對吧？ SARAH: Yes, up past the station. Sarah：是的，過了車站再往前。 FATHER: And will I have any parking problems there? Father：那裡停車會有問題嗎？ SARAH: No, there’s always plenty available. Sarah：不會，那裡一直有很多停車位。 So would you like to enrol Lydia and Carly now? 那你現在要幫 Lydia 和 Carly 報名嗎？ FATHER: OK. Father：好的。 SARAH: So can I have your full name … Sarah：那請問你的全名是……

entries.title: Listening Practice 16
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–14 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 11. Stevenson’s was founded in A. 1923. B. 1924. C. 1926. 12. Originally, Stevenson’s manufactured goods for A. the healthcare industry. B. the automotive industry. C. the machine tools industry. 13. What does the speaker say about the company premises? A. The company has recently moved. B. The company has no plans to move. C. The company is going to move shortly. 14. The programme for the work experience group includes A. time to do research. B. meetings with a teacher. C. talks by staff. Questions 15–20 Practice 16, source question diagram/table, PDF page 7 Label the map below. Write the correct letter, A–J, next to Questions 15–20. 15. coffee room __________ 16. warehouse __________ 17. staff canteen __________ 18. meeting room __________ 19. human resources __________ 20. boardroom __________ Stevenson’s was founded in 1923. 1924. 1926. Originally, Stevenson’s manufactured goods for the healthcare industry. the automotive industry. the machine tools industry. What does the speaker say about the company premises? The company has recently moved. The company has no plans to move. The company is going to move shortly. The programme for the work experience group includes time to do research. meetings with a teacher. talks by staff. coffee room A B C D E F G H I warehouse A B C D E F G H I staff canteen A B C D E F G H I meeting room A B C D E F G H I human resources A B C D E F G H I boardroom A B C D E F G H I Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Stevenson’s, one of the country’s major manufacturers of metal goods. 各位早安，歡迎來到 Stevenson’s，這是本國主要的金屬製品製造商之一。 Thank you for choosing us for your two weeks of work experience. 感謝你們選擇來我們這裡進行兩週的工作體驗。 My name is Julia Simmons, and since the beginning of this year I’ve been the managing director. 我叫 Julia Simmons，從今年年初開始擔任董事總經理。 Stevenson’s is quite an old company. Stevenson’s 是一家相當老牌的公司。 Like me, the founder, Ronald Stevenson, went into the steel industry when he left school – that was in 1923. 創辦人 Ronald Stevenson 和我一樣，離開學校後就進入鋼鐵業，那是在 1923 年。 He set up this company when he finished his apprenticeship, in 1926, although he actually started making plans two years earlier, in 1924. 他在 1926 年完成學徒訓練後創立了這家公司，雖然實際上他早在兩年前，也就是 1924 年，就開始規劃了。 He was a very determined young man! 他當時真是一位非常有決心的年輕人！ Stevenson’s long-term plan was to manufacture components for the machine tools industry – although in fact that never came about – and for the automotive industry, that is, cars and lorries. Stevenson’s 的長期計畫是為工具機產業製造零件，雖然那其實從未實現；另一個方向則是為汽車產業，也就是小汽車和卡車製造零件。 However, there was a delay of five years before that happened, because shortly before the company went into production, Stevenson was given the opportunity to make goods for hospitals and other players in the healthcare industry, so that’s what we did for the first five years. 不過，汽車產業的生產延後了五年，因為在公司投產前不久，Stevenson 得到機會為醫院和醫療保健產業的其他機構製造產品，所以公司最初五年做的是這方面業務。 Over the years, we’ve expanded the premises considerably – we were lucky that the site is big enough, so moving to a new location has never been necessary. 多年來，我們大幅擴建了廠區。幸運的是，這片場地足夠大，所以從未有必要搬到新地點。 However, the layout is far from ideal for modern machinery and production methods, so we intend to carry out major refurbishment of this site over the next five years. 不過，對現代機械和生產方式來說，這裡的布局遠非理想， 所以我們計畫在未來五年對這個廠區進行大規模翻修。 I’d better give you some idea of what you’ll be doing during your two weeks with us, so you know what to expect. 我最好先讓你們了解一下這兩週會做些什麼，這樣你們就知道會有哪些安排。 Most mornings you’ll have a presentation from one of the managers, to learn about their department, starting this morning with research and development. 大多數上午，你們會聽一位經理介紹自己的部門，從今天上午的研發部門開始。 And you’ll all spend some time in each department, observing what’s going on and talking to people – as long as you don’t stop them from doing their work altogether! 你們也會在每個部門待一段時間，觀察部門運作並和員工交流——只要不要完全妨礙他們工作就行！ In the past, a teacher from your school has come in at the end of each week to find out how the group were getting on, but your school isn’t able to arrange that this year. 過去，你們學校每週末都會有老師來了解大家的情況，但今年學校無法安排。 OK, now I’ll briefly help you to orientate yourselves around the site. 好的，現在我會簡單幫你們熟悉一下廠區方位。 As you can see, we’re in the reception area, which we try to make attractive and welcoming to visitors. 如你們所見，我們現在在接待區，這裡我們盡量布置得有吸引力，也讓訪客感到受歡迎。 There’s a corridor running left from here, and if you go along that, the door facing you at the end is the entrance to the coffee room. 從這裡往左有一條走廊，沿著走廊走到盡頭，正對著你的那扇門就是咖啡室入口。 This looks out onto the main road on one side, and some trees on the other, and that’ll be where you meet each morning. 咖啡室一側面向主路，另一側可以看到一些樹木，你們每天早上會在那裡集合。 The factory is the very big room on the far side of the site. 工廠是場地遠端那個非常大的空間。 Next to it is the warehouse, which can be accessed by lorries going up the road to the turning area at the end. 旁邊是倉庫，卡車可以沿道路開到盡頭的轉彎區進入。 You can get to the warehouse by crossing to the far side of the courtyard, and then the door is on your right. 你們可以穿過庭院到另一側， 然後倉庫門就在右手邊。 Somewhere you’ll be keen to find is the staff canteen. 你們肯定會想知道員工餐廳在哪裡。 This is right next to reception. 它就在接待區旁邊。 I can confidently say that the food’s very good, but the view isn’t. 我可以很有信心地說，那裡食物很好，但景觀不怎麼樣。 The windows on one side look onto a corridor and courtyard, which aren’t very attractive at all, and on the other onto the access road, which isn’t much better. 一側窗戶看出去是走廊和庭院，完全不吸引人；另一側看出去是通道道路，也好不到哪裡去。 You’ll be using the meeting room quite often, and you’ll find it by walking along the corridor to the left of the courtyard, and continuing along it to the end. 你們會經常使用會議室。從庭院左側的走廊往前走，一直走到盡頭就能找到。 The meeting room is the last one on the right, and I’m afraid there’s no natural daylight in the room. 會議室是右手邊最後一間，很遺憾，裡面沒有自然光。 Then you’ll need to know where some of the offices are. 接著你們需要知道一些辦公室的位置。 The human resources department is at the front of this building, so you head to the left along the corridor from reception, and it’s the second room you come to. 人力資源部在這棟建築的前方，所以從接待區沿走廊往左走，第二間房就是。 It looks out onto the main road. 它面向主路。 And finally, the boardroom, where you’ll be meeting sometimes. 最後是董事會會議室，你們有時會在那裡開會。 That has quite a pleasant view, as it looks out on to the trees. 那間房景觀相當不錯，因為窗外可以看到樹木。 Go along the corridor past the courtyard, right to the end. 沿著走廊走，經過庭院，一直走到盡頭。 The boardroom is on the left, next to the factory. 董事會會議室在左手邊，緊鄰工廠。 OK, now are there any questions before we … 好的，在我們開始之前，有沒有任何問題……

entries.title: Listening Practice 16
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21 and 22 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO parts of the introductory stage to their art projects do Jess and Tom agree were useful? A. the Bird Park visit B. the workshop sessions C. the Natural History Museum visit D. the projects done in previous years E. the handouts with research sources Questions 23 and 24 Choose TWO letters, A–E. In which TWO ways do both Jess and Tom decide to change their proposals? A. by giving a rationale for their action plans B. by being less specific about the outcome C. by adding a video diary presentation D. by providing a timeline and a mind map E. by making their notes more evaluative Questions 25–30 Which personal meaning do the students decide to give to each of the following pictures? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 25–30. Personal meanings A. a childhood memory B. hope for the future C. fast movement D. a potential threat E. the power of colour F. the continuity of life G. protection of nature H. a confused attitude to nature Pictures 25. Falcon — Landseer __________ 26. Fish hawk — Audubon __________ 27. Kingfisher — van Gogh __________ 28. Portrait of William Wells __________ 29. Vairumati — Gauguin __________ 30. Portrait of Giovanni de Medici __________ Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO parts of the introductory stage to their art projects do Jess and Tom agree were useful? the Bird Park visit the workshop sessions the Natural History Museum visit the projects done in previous years the handouts with research sources Choose TWO letters, A–E. In which TWO ways do both Jess and Tom decide to change their proposals? by giving a rationale for their action plans by being less specific about the outcome by adding a video diary presentation by providing a timeline and a mind map by making their notes more evaluative Falcon — Landseer a childhood memory hope for the future fast movement a potential threat the power of colour the continuity of life protection of nature a confused attitude to nature Fish hawk — Audubon a childhood memory hope for the future fast movement a potential threat the power of colour the continuity of life protection of nature a confused attitude to nature Kingfisher — van Gogh a childhood memory hope for the future fast movement a potential threat the power of colour the continuity of life protection of nature a confused attitude to nature Portrait of William Wells a childhood memory hope for the future fast movement a potential threat the power of colour the continuity of life protection of nature a confused attitude to nature Vairumati — Gauguin a childhood memory hope for the future fast movement a potential threat the power of colour the continuity of life protection of nature a confused attitude to nature Portrait of Giovanni de Medici a childhood memory hope for the future fast movement a potential threat the power of colour the continuity of life protection of nature a confused attitude to nature JESS: How are you getting on with your art project, Tom? Jess：Tom，你的藝術專題進展如何？ TOM: OK. Like, they gave us the theme of birds to base our project on, and I’m not really all that interested in wildlife. Tom：還可以。老師給我們的主題是鳥，要以此作為專題基礎，但我其實對野生動物不是很感興趣。 But I’m starting to get into it. 不過我開始慢慢投入了。 I’ve pretty well finished the introductory stage. 我基本上已經完成了引入階段。 JESS: So have I. Jess：我也是。 When they gave us all those handouts with details of books and websites to look at, I was really put off, but the more I read, the more interested I got. 當老師發給我們那些列著書籍和網站資料的講義時，我真的有點被嚇退，但我讀得越多，就越感興趣。 TOM: Me too. I found I could research so many different aspects of birds in art – colour, movement, texture. Tom：我也是。我發現可以從藝術角度研究鳥的很多不同面向，例如色彩、動作和質感。 So I was looking forward to the Bird Park visit. 所以我原本很期待去 Bird Park 參觀。 JESS: What a letdown! Jess：結果真讓人失望！ It poured with rain and we hardly saw a single bird. 當天大雨傾盆，我們幾乎一隻鳥都沒看到。 Much less use than the trip to the Natural History Museum. 遠不如去 Natural History Museum 那次有用。 TOM: Yeah. I liked all the stuff about evolution there. Tom：是啊。我很喜歡那裡關於演化的內容。 The workshop sessions with Dr Fletcher were good too, especially the brainstorming sessions. Fletcher 博士的工作坊也不錯， 尤其是腦力激盪環節。 JESS: I missed those because I was ill. Jess：我生病了，所以錯過了那些。 I wish we could’ve seen the projects last year’s students did. 我真希望我們能看到去年學生做的專題。 TOM: Mm. I suppose they want us to do our own thing, not copy. Tom：嗯。我想老師希望我們做自己的東西，而不是模仿。 JESS: Have you drafted your proposal yet? Jess：你的提案草稿寫好了嗎？ TOM: Yes, but I haven’t handed it in. Tom：寫好了，但還沒交。 I need to amend some parts. 我需要修改一些部分。 I’ve realised the notes from my research are almost all just descriptions. 我發現我的研究筆記幾乎全都是描述。 I haven’t actually evaluated anything. So I’ll have to fix that. 我其實沒有真正評估任何內容。 所以我得修改。 JESS: Oh, I didn’t know we had to do that. Jess：哦，我不知道我們還得那樣做。 I’ll have to look at that too. 我也得檢查一下。 Did you do a timeline for the project? 你做了專題時間表嗎？ TOM: Yes, and a mind map. Tom：做了，還有心智圖。 JESS: Yeah, so did I. I quite enjoyed that. Jess：嗯，我也做了。我還挺喜歡那部分。 But it was hard having to explain the basis for my decisions in my action plan. 但要在行動計畫裡解釋我做決定的依據，真的有點難。 TOM: What? Tom：什麼意思？ JESS: You know, give a rationale. Jess：就是給出理由依據。 TOM: I didn’t realise we had to do that. Tom：我不知道我們得做那個。 OK, I can add it now. 好，我現在可以補上。 And I’ve done the video diary presentation, and worked out what I want my outcome to be in the project. 我已經完成了影片日誌展示，也想好了專題的預期成果。 JESS: Someone told me it’s best not to be too precise about your actual outcome at this stage, so you have more scope to explore your ideas later on. Jess：有人告訴我，在這個階段最好不要把實際成果寫得太精確， 這樣後面才有更多空間探索想法。 So I’m going to go back to my proposal to make it a bit more vague. 所以我打算回去把提案改得稍微模糊一點。 TOM: Really? OK, I’ll change that too then. Tom：真的嗎？好，那我也改一下。 TOM: One part of the project I’m unsure about is where we choose some paintings of birds and say what they mean to us. Tom：這個專題有一部分我不太確定，就是我們要選一些鳥類畫作，然後說明它們對我們的意義。 Like, I chose a painting of a falcon by Landseer. 例如，我選了 Landseer 畫的一幅獵鷹。 I like it because the bird’s standing there with his head turned to one side, but he seems to be staring straight at you. 我喜歡它，因為那隻鳥站在那裡，頭轉向一邊，但又好像正直直盯著你。 But I can’t just say it’s a bit scary, can I? 但我不能只是說它有點可怕，對吧？ JESS: You could talk about the possible danger suggested by the bird’s look. Jess：你可以談談那隻鳥的眼神暗示的潛在危險。 TOM: Oh, OK. Tom：哦，好的。 JESS: There’s a picture of a fish hawk by Audubon I like. Jess：我喜歡 Audubon 的一幅魚鷹圖。 It’s swooping over the water with a fish in its talons, and with great black wings which take up most of the picture. 牠用爪子抓著一條魚，正掠過水面，巨大的黑色翅膀佔據了畫面大部分。 TOM: So you could discuss it in relation to predators and food chains? Tom：所以你可以從掠食者和食物鏈的角度來討論？ JESS: Well actually I think I’ll concentrate on the impression of rapid motion it gives. Jess：其實我想集中在它帶來的快速動作感。 TOM: Right. Tom：明白。 JESS: Do you know that picture of a kingfisher by van Gogh – it’s perching on a reed growing near stream. Jess：你知道 van Gogh 那幅翠鳥圖嗎？牠棲息在溪邊長出的蘆葦上。 TOM: Yes, it’s got these beautiful blue and red and black shades. Tom：知道，裡面有漂亮的藍色、 紅色和黑色調。 JESS: Mm hm. I’ve actually chosen it because I saw a real kingfisher once when I was little, I was out walking with my grandfather, and I’ve never forgotten it. Jess：嗯。我選它其實是因為我小時候曾經看過一隻真正的翠鳥。 當時我和祖父一起散步，我一直沒有忘記那一幕。 TOM: So we can use a personal link? Tom：所以我們可以用個人連結來解讀？ JESS: Sure. Jess：當然。 TOM: OK. There’s a portrait called William Wells, I can’t remember the artist but it’s a middle-aged man who’s just shot a bird. Tom：好。有一幅肖像畫叫 William Wells，我不記得畫家是誰，但畫中是一位剛射下一隻鳥的中年男子。 And his expression, and the way he’s holding the bird in his hand suggests he’s not sure about what he’s done. 他的表情，以及他手裡拿著鳥的方式，都暗示他不太確定自己剛做了什麼。 To me it’s about how ambiguous people are in the way they exploit the natural world. 對我來說，這幅畫是關於人類在利用自然世界時那種矛盾又混亂的態度。 JESS: Interesting. There’s Gauguin’s picture Vairumati. Jess：很有意思。還有 Gauguin 的畫作 Vairumati。 He did it in Tahiti. 他是在 Tahiti 創作這幅畫的。 It’s a woman with a white bird behind her that is eating a lizard, and what I’m interested in is what idea this bird refers to. 畫中是一名女子，身後有一隻正在吃蜥蜴的白鳥，而我感興趣的是這隻鳥象徵什麼。 Apparently, it’s a reference to the never-ending cycle of existence. 顯然，它指的是永無止境的生命循環。 TOM: Wow. I chose a portrait of a little boy, Giovanni de Medici. Tom：哇。我選了一幅小男孩 Giovanni de Medici 的肖像。 He’s holding a tiny bird in one fist. 他一隻手握著一隻小鳥。 I like the way he’s holding it carefully so he doesn’t hurt it. 我喜歡他小心握著牠的樣子，像是不想傷害牠。 JESS: Ah right. Jess：啊，明白。

entries.title: Listening Practice 16
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Stoicism Stoicism is still relevant today because of its 31 __________ appeal. Ancient Stoics ● Stoicism was founded over 2,000 years ago in Greece. ● The Stoics’ ideas are surprisingly well known, despite not being intended for 32 __________. Stoic principles ● Happiness could be achieved by leading a virtuous life. ● Controlling emotions was essential. ● Epictetus said that external events cannot be controlled but the 33 __________ people make in response can be controlled. ● A Stoic is someone who has a different view on experiences which others would consider as 34 __________. The influence of Stoicism ● George Washington organised a 35 __________ about Cato to motivate his men. ● The French artist Delacroix was a Stoic. ● Adam Smith’s ideas on 36 __________ were influenced by Stoicism. ● Some of today’s political leaders are inspired by the Stoics. ● Cognitive Behaviour Therapy, CBT: ○ the treatment for 37 __________ is based on ideas from Stoicism ○ people learn to base their thinking on 38 __________. ● In business, people benefit from Stoicism by identifying obstacles as 39 __________. Relevance of Stoicism ● It requires a lot of 40 __________, but Stoicism can help people to lead a good life. ● It teaches people that having a strong character is more important than anything else. Stoicism is still relevant today because of its 31 __________ appeal. for 32 __________. ● Epictetus said that external events cannot be controlled but the 33 __________ people make in response can be controlled. would consider as 34 __________. ● George Washington organised a 35 __________ about Cato to motivate ● Adam Smith’s ideas on 36 __________ were influenced by Stoicism. ○ the treatment for 37 __________ is based on ideas from Stoicism ○ people learn to base their thinking on 38 __________. ● In business, people benefit from Stoicism by identifying obstacles as 39 __________. ● It requires a lot of 40 __________, but Stoicism can help people to lead Ancient philosophy is not just about talking or lecturing, or even reading long, dense books. 古代哲學不只是談論、講授，甚至也不只是閱讀冗長艱深的書籍。 In fact, it is something people have used throughout history – to solve their problems and to achieve their greatest triumphs. 事實上，歷史上人們一直用它來解決問題，並取得最偉大的成就。 Specifically, I am referring to Stoicism, which, in my opinion, is the most practical of all philosophies and therefore the most appealing. 具體來說，我指的是 Stoicism；在我看來，它是所有哲學中最實用的一種，因此也最具吸引力。 Stoicism was founded in Ancient Greece by Zeno of Citium in the early 3rd century BC, but was practised by the likes of Epictetus, Cato, Seneca and Marcus Aurelius. Stoicism 由 Citium 的 Zeno 於西元前 3 世紀初在古希臘創立，而 Epictetus、Cato、Seneca 和 Marcus Aurelius 等人都實踐過這種哲學。 Amazingly, we still have access to these ideas, despite the fact that the most famous Stoics never wrote anything down for publication. 令人驚訝的是，儘管最著名的 Stoics 從未為出版目的寫下任何內容，我們今天仍能接觸到這些思想。 Cato definitely didn’t. Cato 肯定沒有。 Marcus Aurelius never intended his Meditations to be anything but personal. Marcus Aurelius 從未打算讓他的 《Meditations》成為私人記錄以外的東西。 Seneca’s letters were, well, letters and Epictetus’ thoughts come to us by way of a note-taking student. Seneca 的書信，嗯，就是書信；而 Epictetus 的思想則是透過一位做筆記的學生傳到我們這裡的。 Stoic principles were based on the idea that its followers could have an unshakable happiness in this life and the key to achieving this was virtue. Stoic 原則建立在一個理念上：追隨者可以在此生獲得不可動搖的幸福，而實現這一點的關鍵是美德。 The road to virtue, in turn, lay in understanding that destructive emotions, like anger and jealousy, are under our conscious control – they don’t have to control us, because we can learn to control them. 通往美德的道路，則在於理解破壞性情緒，例如憤怒和嫉妒，是可以受我們有意識控制的；它們不必控制我們，因為我們可以學會控制它們。 In the words of Epictetus: “external events I cannot control, but the choices I make with regard to them, I do control”. 用 Epictetus 的話說：「外在事件我無法控制，但我可以控制自己對它們所做的選擇。」 The modern day philosopher and writer Nassim Nicholas Taleb defines a Stoic as someone who has a different perspective on experiences which most of us would see as wholly negative. 現代哲學家兼作家 Nassim Nicholas Taleb 將 Stoic 定義為一種人：他們對大多數人視為完全負面的經歷有不同看法。 A Stoic “transforms fear into caution, pain into transformation, mistakes into initiation and desire into undertaking”. Stoic 會「將恐懼轉化為謹慎，將痛苦轉化為蛻變，將錯誤轉化為啟程，將欲望轉化為行動」。 Using this definition as a model, we can see that throughout the centuries Stoicism has been practised in more recent history by kings, presidents, artists, writers and entrepreneurs. 以這個定義為模型，我們可以看到，幾個世紀以來，在較近代歷史中，國王、總統、藝術家、作家和企業家都曾實踐 Stoicism。 The founding fathers of the United States were inspired by the philosophy. 美國開國元勳們也受到這種哲學啟發。 George Washington was introduced to Stoicism by his neighbours at age seventeen, and later, put on a play based on the life of Cato to inspire his men. George Washington 在 17 歲時由鄰居介紹接觸 Stoicism，後來還安排了一齣以 Cato 生平為基礎的戲劇來激勵他的士兵。 Thomas Jefferson kept a copy of Seneca beside his bed. Thomas Jefferson 在床邊放著一本 Seneca 的作品。 Writers and artists have also been inspired by the Stoics. 作家和藝術家也受到 Stoics 啟發。 Eugène Delacroix, the renowned French Romantic artist known best for his painting Liberty Leading the People, was an ardent Stoic, referring to it as his “consoling religion”. 著名法國浪漫主義畫家 Eugène Delacroix 以《Liberty Leading the People》最為人所知，他是一位熱切的 Stoic，並稱 Stoicism 為他的 「安慰宗教」。 The economist Adam Smith’s theories on capitalism were significantly influenced by the Stoicism that he studied as a schoolboy, under a teacher who had translated Marcus Aurelius’ works. 經濟學家 Adam Smith 關於資本主義的理論，深受他學生時代所學 Stoicism 的影響；當時他的老師曾翻譯 Marcus Aurelius 的作品。 Today’s political leaders are no different, with many finding their inspiration from the ancient texts. 今天的政治領袖也不例外，許多人從古代文本中獲得靈感。 Former US president Bill Clinton rereads Marcus Aurelius every single year, and many have compared former President Obama’s calm leadership style to that of Cato. 美國前總統 Bill Clinton 每年都會重讀 Marcus Aurelius，而許多人也將前總統 Obama 冷靜的領導風格比作 Cato。 Wen Jiabao, the former prime minister of China, claims that Meditations is one of two books he travels with and that he has read it more than one hundred times over the course of his life. 中國前總理 Wen Jiabao 表示，《 Meditations》是他旅行時隨身攜帶的兩本書之一，而且他一生中已讀過一百多遍。 Stoicism had a profound influence on Albert Ellis, who invented Cognitive Behaviour Therapy, which is used to help people manage their problems by changing the way that they think and behave. Stoicism 對 Albert Ellis 產生了深遠影響；他創立了認知行為療法，用來幫助人們透過改變思考和行為方式來管理問題。 It’s most commonly used to treat depression. 它最常用於治療憂鬱症。 The idea is that we can take control of our lives by challenging the irrational beliefs that create our faulty thinking, symptoms and behaviours by using logic instead. 其理念是，我們可以透過邏輯挑戰那些造成錯誤思維、症狀和行為的非理性信念，從而掌控自己的生活。 Stoicism has also become popular in the world of business. Stoicism 在商業世界中也變得很受歡迎。 Stoic principles can build the resilience and state of mind required to overcome setbacks because Stoics teach turning obstacles into opportunity. Stoic 原則能培養克服挫折所需的韌性和心態，因為 Stoics 教導人們把障礙轉化為機會。 A lesson every business entrepreneur needs to learn. 這是每一位企業家都需要學習的一課。 I would argue that studying Stoicism is as relevant today as it was 2,000 years ago, thanks to its brilliant insights into how to lead a good life. 我認為，研究 Stoicism 在今天和 2000 年前一樣具有現實意義，因為它對如何過上美好生活有深刻洞察。 At the very root of the thinking, there is a very simple way of living – control what you can and accept what you can’t. 在這種思想的根本處，有一種非常簡單的生活方式：控制你能控制的，接受你不能控制的。 This is not as easy as it sounds and will require considerable practice – it can take a lifetime to master. 這並不像聽起來那麼容易，而且需要大量練習；要真正掌握它， 可能需要一生。 The Stoics also believed the most important foundation for a good and happy life is not money, fame, power or pleasure, but having a disciplined and principled character – something which seems to resonate with many people today. Stoics 也相信，美好而幸福人生最重要的基礎不是金錢、名聲、 權力或享樂，而是擁有自律且有原則的品格——這一點似乎至今仍能引起許多人的共鳴。

entries.title: Listening Practice 17
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Copying Photos to Digital Format Name of company: Picturerep Requirements ● Maximum size of photos is 30 cm, minimum size 4 cm. ● Photos must not be in a 1 __________ or an album. Cost ● The cost for 360 photos is £2 __________, including one disk. ● Before the completed order is sent, 3 __________ is required. Services included in the price ● Photos can be placed in a folder, e.g. with the name 4 __________. ● The 5 __________ and contrast can be improved if necessary. ● Photos which are very fragile will be scanned by 6 __________. Special restore service, costs extra ● It may be possible to remove an object from a photo, or change the 7 __________. ● A photo which is not correctly in 8 __________ cannot be fixed. Other information ● Orders are completed within 9 __________. ● Send the photos in a box, not 10 __________. ● Photos must not be in a 1 __________ or an album. ● The cost for 360 photos is £2 __________, including one disk. ● Before the completed order is sent, 3 __________ is required. ● Photos can be placed in a folder, e.g. with the name 4 __________. ● The 5 __________ and contrast can be improved if necessary. ● Photos which are very fragile will be scanned by 6 __________. ● It may be possible to remove an object from a photo, or change the 7 __________. ● A photo which is not correctly in 8 __________ cannot be fixed. ● Orders are completed within 9 __________. ● Send the photos in a box, not 10 __________. EMPLOYEE: Hello, Picturerep. Can I help you? Employee：您好，這裡是 Picturerep。請問有什麼可以幫您？ WOMAN: Oh, hi. I saw your advertisement about copying pictures to disk and I’d like a bit more information about what you do. Woman：哦，你好。我看到你們關於把照片複製到光碟上的廣告， 想多了解一下你們的服務。 EMPLOYEE: Sure. What would you like to know? Employee：當然可以。您想知道哪方面？ WOMAN: Well, I’ve got a box full of old family photos that’s been up in the attic for years, some of them must be 50 or 60 years old, and I’d like to get them converted to digital format. Woman：嗯，我有一整箱舊家庭照片，一直放在閣樓裡很多年了，有些肯定有五六十年歷史，我想把它們轉成數位格式。 EMPLOYEE: Sure, we can do that for you. Employee：當然，我們可以為您處理。 WOMAN: Right. And what about size? Woman：好的。那尺寸方面呢？ The photos are all sorts of sizes – are there any restrictions? 這些照片大小不一，有什麼限制嗎？ EMPLOYEE: Well the maximum size of photo we can do with our normal service is 30 centimetres. Employee：普通服務能處理的照片最大尺寸是 30 公分。 And each picture must be at least 4 centimetres, that’s the minimum we can cope with. 每張照片至少要有 4 公分，這是我們能處理的最小尺寸。 WOMAN: That should be fine. Woman：那應該沒問題。 And some of them are in a frame – should I take them out before I send them? 其中有些放在相框裡，寄給你們之前需要取出來嗎？ EMPLOYEE: Yes please, we can’t copy them otherwise. Employee：是的，麻煩您取出來， 否則我們無法複製。 And also the photos must all be separate, they mustn’t be stuck into an album. 而且照片必須都是分開的，不能貼在相簿裡。 WOMAN: OK, that’s not a problem. Woman：好的，沒問題。 So can you give me an idea of how much this will cost? 那你能大概告訴我費用是多少嗎？ I’ve got about 360 photos I think. 我想我大約有 360 張照片。 EMPLOYEE: We charge £195 for 300 to 400 photos for the basic service. Employee：基本服務中，300 到 400 張照片的收費是 195 英鎊。 WOMAN: OK. And does that include the disk? Woman：好的。這包括光碟嗎？ EMPLOYEE: Yes, one disk – but you can get extra ones for £5 each. Employee：包括一張光碟，不過如果想加購，每張 5 英鎊。 WOMAN: That’s good. So do I need to pay when I send you the photos? Woman：很好。那我寄照片時需要付款嗎？ EMPLOYEE: No, we won’t need anything until we’ve actually copied the pictures. Employee：不用。我們實際複製完照片之前不需要付款。 Then we’ll let you know how much it is, and once we’ve received the payment, we’ll send the parcel off to you. 之後我們會通知您總費用，收到付款後，就會把包裹寄給您。 WOMAN: Right. Woman：好的。 EMPLOYEE: Is there anything else you’d like to ask about our services? Employee：關於我們的服務，您還有其他問題嗎？ WOMAN: Yes. I’ve roughly sorted out the photos into groups, according to what they’re about – so can you keep them in those groups when you copy them. Woman：有。我已經大致按照內容把照片分成幾組了，你們複製時可以保持這些分組嗎？ EMPLOYEE: Sure. We’ll save each group in a different folder on the disk and if you like, you can suggest a name for each folder. Employee：當然。我們會把每一組存在光碟上的不同資料夾裡。如果您願意，也可以為每個資料夾命名。 WOMAN: So I could have one called “Grandparents” for instance? Woman：例如我可以有一個資料夾叫 “Grandparents” 嗎？ EMPLOYEE: Exactly. Employee：正是如此。 WOMAN: And do you do anything besides scan the photos? Woman：除了掃描照片之外，你們還會做其他處理嗎？ Like, can you make any improvements? 比如可以改善照片品質嗎？ EMPLOYEE: Yes, in the standard service each photo is checked, and we can sometimes touch up the colour a bit, or improve the contrast – that can make a big difference. Employee：可以。標準服務中，每張照片都會被檢查，我們有時可以稍微修正色彩，或改善對比度，這可能會有很大差別。 WOMAN: OK. And some of the photos are actually quite fragile – they won’t get damaged in the process, will they? Woman：好的。有些照片其實相當脆弱，處理過程中不會損壞吧？ EMPLOYEE: No, if any look particularly fragile, we’d do them by hand. Employee：不會。如果有些看起來特別脆弱，我們會手工處理。 We do realise how precious these old photos can be. 我們很清楚這些舊照片可能有多珍貴。 WOMAN: Sure. Woman：好的。 EMPLOYEE: And another thing is we can make changes to a photo if you want – so if you want to remove an object from a photo, or maybe alter the background, we can do that. Employee：另外，如果您願意，我們也可以對照片做修改。例如， 如果您想從照片中移除某個物件，或改變背景，我們都可以做。 WOMAN: Really? I might be interested in that. Woman：真的嗎？我可能會對這項服務感興趣。 I’ll have a look through the photos and see. 我會先看看照片再決定。 Oh, and talking of fixing photos – I’ve got a few that aren’t properly in focus. 哦，說到修復照片，我有幾張照片沒有對好焦。 Can you do anything to make that better? 你們能改善這種問題嗎？ EMPLOYEE: No, I’m afraid that’s one thing we can’t do. Employee：很抱歉，這一點我們做不到。 WOMAN: OK. Woman：好的。 EMPLOYEE: Any other information I can give you? Employee：還有其他需要我提供的資訊嗎？ WOMAN: Er … oh, how long will it all take? Woman：呃……哦，整個過程需要多久？ EMPLOYEE: We aim to get the copying done in ten days. Employee：我們的目標是在十天內完成複製。 WOMAN: Fine. Right, well I’ll get the photos packed up in a box and post them off to you. Woman：好的。那我會把照片裝進盒子裡，寄給你們。 EMPLOYEE: Right. If you’ve got a strong cardboard box, that’s best. Employee：好的。如果您有堅固的紙板箱，那最好。 We’ve found that plastic ones sometimes break in the post. 我們發現塑膠箱有時會在郵寄途中破裂。 WOMAN: OK. Right, thanks for your help. Bye. Woman：好的。謝謝你的幫忙，再見。 EMPLOYEE: Bye. Employee：再見。

entries.title: Listening Practice 17
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–15 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 11. Dartfield House school used to be A. a tourist information centre. B. a private home. C. a local council building. 12. What is planned with regard to the lower school? A. All buildings on the main site will be improved. B. The lower school site will be used for new homes. C. Additional school buildings will be constructed on the lower school site. 13. The catering has been changed because of A. long queuing times. B. changes to the school timetable. C. dissatisfaction with the menus. 14. Parents are asked to A. help their children to decide in advance which serving point to use. B. make sure their children have enough money for food. C. advise their children on healthy food to eat. 15. What does the speaker say about the existing canteen? A. Food will still be served there. B. Only staff will have access to it. C. Pupils can take their food into it. Questions 16–18 What comment does the speaker make about each of the following serving points in the Food Hall? Choose THREE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–D, next to Questions 16–18. Comments A. pupils help to plan menus B. only vegetarian food C. different food every week D. daily change in menu Food available at serving points in Food Hall 16. World Adventures __________ 17. Street Life __________ 18. Speedy Italian __________ Questions 19 and 20 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO optional after-school lessons are new? A. swimming B. piano C. acting D. cycling E. theatre sound and lighting Dartfield House school used to be a tourist information centre. a private home. a local council building. What is planned with regard to the lower school? All buildings on the main site will be improved. The lower school site will be used for new homes. Additional school buildings will be constructed on the lower school site. The catering has been changed because of long queuing times. changes to the school timetable. dissatisfaction with the menus. Parents are asked to help their children to decide in advance which serving point to use. make sure their children have enough money for food. advise their children on healthy food to eat. What does the speaker say about the existing canteen? Food will still be served there. Only staff will have access to it. Pupils can take their food into it. World Adventures pupils help to plan menus only vegetarian food different food every week daily change in menu Street Life pupils help to plan menus only vegetarian food different food every week daily change in menu Speedy Italian pupils help to plan menus only vegetarian food different food every week daily change in menu Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO optional after-school lessons are new? swimming piano acting cycling theatre sound and lighting Good morning and thank you for coming here today. 早安，感謝大家今天來到這裡。 I’d like to bring you up to date with changes in the school that will affect your children. 我想向大家介紹學校最新的變化，這些變化會影響到你們的孩子。 As you know, the school buildings date from various times: some from the 1970s, some from the last five years, and of course Dartfield House is over a century old. 如你們所知，學校建築年代各不相同：有些建於 1970 年代， 有些是過去五年內建成的，當然 Dartfield House 已有一百多年歷史。 It was commissioned by a businessman, Neville Richards, and intended as his family home, but he died before it was completed. 它是由商人 Neville Richards 委託建造的，原本打算作為他的家庭住宅，但他在完工前去世了。 His heir chose to sell it to the local council, who turned it into offices. 他的繼承人選擇把它賣給地方議會，地方議會把它改成了辦公室。 A later plan to convert it into a tourist information centre didn’t come about, through lack of money, and instead it formed the nucleus of this school when it opened 40 years ago. 後來曾計畫把它改成遊客資訊中心，但因缺乏資金沒有實現；相反，40 年前學校開辦時，它成為了學校的核心建築。 The school has grown as the local population has increased, and I can now give you some news about the lower school site, which is separated from the main site by a road. 隨著當地人口增加，學校也不斷擴大。現在我可以告訴大家一些關於低年級校區的消息， 它與主校區隔著一條路。 Planning permission has been granted for development of both sites. 兩個校區的開發計畫都已獲得規劃許可。 The lower school will move to new buildings that will be constructed on the main site. 低年級學校將搬到主校區新建的建築裡。 Developers will construct houses on the existing lower school site. 開發商會在現有低年級校區上建造住宅。 Work on the new school buildings should start within the next few months. 新校舍工程應該會在接下來幾個月內開始。 A more imminent change concerns the catering facilities and the canteen. 一項更迫近的變化涉及餐飲設施和食堂。 The canteen is always very busy throughout the lunch period – in fact it’s often full to capacity, because a lot of our pupils like the food that’s on offer there. 午餐時間食堂一直非常忙，事實上經常滿座，因為許多學生喜歡那裡提供的食物。 But there’s only one serving point, so most pupils have to wait a considerable time to be served. 但那裡只有一個供餐點，所以大多數學生必須等很久才能取餐。 This is obviously unsatisfactory, as they may have hardly finished their lunch before afternoon lessons start. 這顯然不理想，因為下午課開始前，他們可能才剛吃完午餐。 So we’ve had a new Food Hall built, and this will come into use next week. 因此，我們建了一個新的 Food Hall，下週將投入使用。 It’ll have several serving areas, and I’ll give you more details about those in a minute. 那裡會有幾個供餐區，我稍後會提供更多細節。 But one thing we ask you to do, to help in the smooth running of the Food Hall, is to discuss with your children each morning which type of food they want to eat that day, so they can go straight to the relevant serving point. 不過為了幫助 Food Hall 順利運作，我們請各位每天早上和孩子討論當天想吃哪類食物， 這樣他們就可以直接前往相關供餐點。 There won’t be any junk food – everything on offer will be healthy – and there’s no change to the current system of paying for lunches by topping up your child’s electronic payment card online. 那裡不會有垃圾食品，所有提供的食物都會是健康的；午餐付款方式也不變，仍是透過線上為孩子的電子支付卡充值。 You may be wondering what will happen to the old canteen. 你們可能會想知道舊食堂會怎麼處理。 We’ll still have tables and chairs in there, and pupils can eat food from the Food Hall or lunch they’ve brought from home. 那裡仍會保留桌椅，學生可以在那裡吃從 Food Hall 買來的食物，或自己從家裡帶的午餐。 Eventually we may use part of the canteen for storage, but first we’ll see how many pupils go in there at lunchtime. 最終我們可能會把食堂的一部分用作儲藏空間，但會先觀察午餐時間有多少學生會去那裡。 OK, back to the serving points in the Food Hall, which will all have side dishes, desserts and drinks on sale, as well as main courses. 好，回到 Food Hall 的供餐點。 每個供餐點除了主菜，也會出售配菜、甜點和飲料。 One serving point we call World Adventures. 其中一個供餐點叫做 World Adventures。 This will serve a different country’s cuisine each day, maybe Chinese one day and Lebanese the next. 這裡每天會供應不同國家的菜餚，可能一天是中國菜，隔天是黎巴嫩菜。 The menus will be planned for a week at a time, so pupils will know what’s going to be available the whole of that week. 菜單會一次規劃一週，所以學生會知道整週有哪些選擇。 Street Life is also international, with food from three particular cultures. Street Life 也是國際化的，提供來自三種特定文化的食物。 We’ll ask pupils to make suggestions, so perhaps sometimes there’ll be food from Thailand, Ethiopia and Mexico, and then one of them will be replaced by Jamaican food for a week or two. 我們會請學生提出建議，所以有時可能會有泰國、衣索比亞和墨西哥食物，然後其中一種會被牙買加食物取代一兩週。 The Speedy Italian serving point will cater particularly for the many pupils who don’t eat meat or fish: they can be sure that all the food served there is suitable for them. Speedy Italian 供餐點會特別照顧許多不吃肉或魚的學生； 他們可以確定那裡提供的所有食物都適合他們。 There’ll be plenty of variety, so they shouldn’t get bored with the food. 菜色會很多樣，所以他們不應該會吃膩。 OK, that’s all on the new Food Hall. 好的，關於新的 Food Hall 就介紹到這裡。 Now after-school lessons. 接下來是課後課程。 These are very popular with pupils, particularly swimming – in fact there’s a waiting list for lessons. 這些課程很受學生歡迎，尤其是游泳課，事實上已經有候補名單。 Cycling is another favourite, and I’m delighted that dozens of pupils make use of the chance to learn to ride in off-road conditions. 騎自行車也是另一項熱門課程，我很高興有數十名學生利用這個機會學習在越野環境中騎車。 It means that more and more cycle to and from school every day. 這意味著每天有越來越多學生騎車上下學。 As you know, we have a well-equipped performance centre, and we’re going to start drama classes in there, too. 如你們所知，我們有一個設備完善的表演中心，也會在那裡開設戲劇課。 Pupils will be able to join in just for fun or work up to taking part in a play – we hope to put on at least one a year. 學生可以只是為了好玩而參加，也可以逐步準備參與戲劇演出；我們希望每年至少上演一齣戲。 We already teach a number of pupils to use the sound and lighting systems in the centre. 我們已經在教一些學生使用表演中心的音響和燈光系統。 And a former pupil has given a magnificent grand piano to the school, so a few pupils will be able to learn at the school instead of going to the local college, as many of them do at the moment. 另外，一位校友捐了一架漂亮的三角鋼琴給學校，所以少數學生可以在學校學鋼琴，而不用像目前許多人那樣去當地學院上課。

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21–24 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Assignment on Sleep and Dreams 21. Luke read that one reason why we often forget dreams is that A. our memories cannot cope with too much information. B. we might otherwise be confused about what is real. C. we do not think they are important. 22. What do Luke and Susie agree about dreams predicting the future? A. It may just be due to chance. B. It only happens with certain types of event. C. It happens more often than some people think. 23. Susie says that a study on pre-school children having a short nap in the day A. had controversial results. B. used faulty research methodology. C. failed to reach any clear conclusions. 24. In their last assignment, both students had problems with A. statistical analysis. B. making an action plan. C. self-assessment. Questions 25–30 Complete the flow chart below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Research Plan ● Decide on research question: relationship between hours of sleep and number of dreams. ● Choose participants from the 25 __________ department. ● Use 26 __________ questionnaires because participants will complete them just after waking. ● Check ethical guidelines because the experiment involves 27 __________. ● Make sure participants are not put under unnecessary 28 __________. ● Analyse the data and present the results in a 29 __________. ● Finally, 30 __________ the research. Luke read that one reason why we often forget dreams is that our memories cannot cope with too much information. we might otherwise be confused about what is real. we do not think they are important. What do Luke and Susie agree about dreams predicting the future? It may just be due to chance. It only happens with certain types of event. It happens more often than some people think. Susie says that a study on pre-school children having a short nap in the day had controversial results. used faulty research methodology. failed to reach any clear conclusions. In their last assignment, both students had problems with statistical analysis. making an action plan. self-assessment. ● Choose participants from the 25 __________ department. ● Use 26 __________ questionnaires because participants will complete ● Check ethical guidelines because the experiment involves 27 __________. ● Make sure participants are not put under unnecessary 28 __________. ● Analyse the data and present the results in a 29 __________. ● Finally, 30 __________ the research. SUSIE: So Luke, for our next psychology assignment we have to do something on sleep and dreams. Susie：Luke，我們下一個心理學作業要做和睡眠及夢有關的內容。 LUKE: Right. I’ve just read an article suggesting why we tend to forget most of our dreams soon after we wake up. Luke：對。我剛讀了一篇文章， 裡面說明為什麼我們醒來後很快會忘記大部分夢境。 I mean, most of my dreams aren’t that interesting anyway, but what it said was that if we remembered everything, we might get mixed up about what actually happened and what we dreamed. 我的意思是，反正我的大多數夢也沒那麼有趣；但文章說，如果我們記得所有夢境，可能會混淆實際發生的事和夢到的事。 So it’s a sort of protection. I hadn’t heard that idea before. 所以這是一種保護。我以前沒聽過這種說法。 I’d always assumed that it was just that we didn’t have room in our memories for all that stuff. 我一直以為只是因為我們的記憶沒有空間容納所有那些內容。 SUSIE: Me too. What do you think about the idea that our dreams may predict the future? Susie：我也是。你怎麼看夢可能預知未來這種想法？ LUKE: It’s a belief that you get all over the world. Luke：這是世界各地都有的一種信念。 SUSIE: Yeah, lots of people have a story of it happening to them, but the explanation I’ve read is that for each dream that comes true, we have thousands that don’t, but we don’t notice those, we don’t even remember them. Susie：是啊，很多人都有夢境成真的故事，但我讀到的解釋是， 每有一個夢成真，就有成千上萬個夢沒有成真，只是我們不注意那些，也根本不記得。 We just remember the ones where something in the real world, like a view or an action, happens to trigger a dream memory. 我們只記得那些現實世界中某個景象或動作剛好觸發夢境記憶的情況。 LUKE: Right. So it’s just a coincidence really. Luke：對。所以其實只是巧合。 Something else I read about is what they call segmented sleeping. 我還讀到另一個概念，叫分段睡眠。 That’s a theory that hundreds of years ago, people used to get up in the middle of the night and have a chat or something to eat, then go back to bed. So I tried it myself. 這個理論說，幾百年前，人們常常半夜起床聊聊天或吃點東西，然後再回去睡覺。所以我自己也試了一下。 SUSIE: Why? Susie：為什麼？ LUKE: Well it’s meant to make you more creative. Luke：嗯，據說這會讓人更有創造力。 I don’t know why. But I gave it up after a week. 我不知道為什麼。不過我一週後就放棄了。 It just didn’t fit in with my lifestyle. 它實在不適合我的生活方式。 SUSIE: But most pre-school children have a short sleep in the day don’t they? Susie：但大多數學齡前兒童白天都會小睡一下，對吧？ There was an experiment some students did here last term to see at what age kids should stop having naps. 上學期有些學生在這裡做了一個實驗，想看看孩子應該在幾歲停止午睡。 But they didn’t really find an answer. 但他們並沒有真正找到答案。 They spent a lot of time working out the most appropriate methodology, but the results didn’t seem to show any obvious patterns. 他們花了很多時間制定最合適的方法，但結果似乎沒有顯示出任何明顯模式。 LUKE: Right. Anyway, let’s think about our assignment. Luke：明白。不管怎樣，我們來想想自己的作業吧。 Last time I had problems with the final stage, where we had to describe and justify how successful we thought we’d been. 上次我在最後階段遇到問題， 就是我們必須描述並說明自己認為做得有多成功。 I struggled a bit with the action plan too. 行動計畫我也有點吃力。 SUSIE: I was OK with the planning, but I got marked down for the self-assessment as well. Susie：我在計畫部分還可以，但自我評估也被扣分了。 And I had big problems with the statistical stuff, that’s where I really lost marks. 而且我在統計部分遇到很大問題，那裡真的丟了很多分。 LUKE: Right. Luke：明白。 SUSIE: So shall we plan what we have to do for this assignment? Susie：那我們要不要規劃一下這次作業要做什麼？ LUKE: OK. Luke：好。 SUSIE: First, we have to decide on our research question. Susie：首先，我們要決定研究問題。 So how about “Is there a relationship between hours of sleep and number of dreams?” 那「睡眠時間和夢的數量之間是否有關係？」怎麼樣？ LUKE: OK. Then we need to think about who we’ll do the study on. About 12 people? Luke：可以。接著我們要想研究對象是誰。大約 12 個人？ SUSIE: Right. And shall we use other psychology students? Susie：對。那要用其他心理學學生嗎？ LUKE: Let’s use people from a different department. What about history? Luke：我們用其他系的人吧。歷史系怎麼樣？ SUSIE: Yes, they might have interesting dreams! Or literature students? Susie：可以，他們可能會做有趣的夢！或者文學系學生？ LUKE: I don’t really know any. Luke：我不太認識文學系的人。 SUSIE: OK, forget that idea. Susie：好，那就算了。 Then we have to think about our methodology. 接著我們要考慮研究方法。 So we could use observation, but that doesn’t seem appropriate. 我們可以用觀察法，但這似乎不太合適。 LUKE: No. It needs to be self-reporting I think. Luke：對。我覺得需要自我報告。 And we could ask them to answer questions online. 我們可以讓他們在線上回答問題。 SUSIE: But in this case, paper might be better as they’ll be doing it straight after they wake up … in fact while they’re still half-asleep. Susie：但這種情況下，紙本可能更好，因為他們會在剛醒來後立刻填寫……事實上，那時他們可能還半睡半醒。 LUKE: Right. And we’ll have to check the ethical guidelines for this sort of research. Luke：對。而且我們要查看這類研究的倫理準則。 SUSIE: Mm, because our experiment involves humans, so there are special regulations. Susie：嗯，因為我們的實驗涉及人類，所以有特殊規定。 LUKE: Yes, I had a look at those for another assignment I did. Luke：是的，我之前做另一個作業時看過那些。 There’s a whole section on risk assessment, and another section on making sure they aren’t put under any unnecessary stress. 裡面有一整節是關於風險評估，還有另一節是確保參與者不會承受任何不必要壓力。 SUSIE: Let’s hope they don’t have any bad dreams! Susie：希望他們不要做惡夢！ LUKE: Yeah. Luke：是啊。 SUSIE: Then when we’ve collected all our data we have to analyse it and calculate the correlation between our two variables, that’s time sleeping and number of dreams and then present our results visually in a graph. Susie：然後收集完所有資料後， 我們要分析它，計算兩個變項， 也就是睡眠時間和夢的數量之間的相關性，接著用圖表呈現結果。 LUKE: Right. And the final thing is to think about our research and evaluate it. Luke：對。最後一件事是思考我們的研究並進行評估。 So that seems quite straightforward. 這樣看起來相當清楚。 SUSIE: Yeah. So now let’s … Susie：是啊。那現在我們……
