entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Health Benefits of Dance Recent findings ● All forms of dance produce various hormones associated with feelings of happiness. ● Dancing with others has a more positive impact than dancing alone. ● An experiment on university students suggested that dance increases 31 __________. ● For those with mental illness, dance could be used as a form of 32 __________. Benefits of dance for older people ● accessible for people with low levels of 33 __________ ● reduces the risk of heart disease ● better 34 __________ reduces the risk of accidents ● improves 35 __________ function by making it work faster ● improves participants’ general well-being ● gives people more 36 __________ to take exercise ● can lessen the feeling of 37 __________, very common in older people Benefits of Zumba ● A study at The University of Wisconsin showed that doing Zumba for 40 minutes uses up as many 38 __________ as other quite intense forms of exercise. ● The American Journal of Health Behavior study showed that: ○ women suffering from 39 __________ benefited from doing Zumba. ○ Zumba became a 40 __________ for the participants. ● An experiment on university students suggested that dance increases 31 __________. ● For those with mental illness, dance could be used as a form of 32 __________. ● accessible for people with low levels of 33 __________ ● better 34 __________ reduces the risk of accidents ● improves 35 __________ function by making it work faster ● gives people more 36 __________ to take exercise ● can lessen the feeling of 37 __________, very common in older people minutes uses up as many 38 __________ as other quite intense forms of ○ women suffering from 39 __________ benefited from doing ○ Zumba became a 40 __________ for the participants. Dancing is something that humans do when they want to have a good time. 跳舞是人類想要享受愉快時光時會做的事情。 It’s a universal response to music, found in all cultures. 它是對音樂的一種普遍反應，存在於所有文化中。 But what’s only been discovered recently is that dancing not only makes us feel good, it’s also extremely good for our health. 但直到最近人們才發現，跳舞不僅讓我們感覺良好，對健康也非常有益。 Dancing, like other forms of exercise, releases hormones, such as dopamine, which make us feel relaxed and happy. 跳舞和其他運動形式一樣，會釋放多巴胺等荷爾蒙，使我們感到放鬆和快樂。 And it also reduces feelings of stress or anxiety. 它也能減少壓力或焦慮感。 Dancing is also a sociable activity, which is another reason it makes us feel good. 跳舞也是一種社交活動，這也是它讓我們感覺良好的另一個原因。 One study compared people’s enjoyment of dancing at home in front of a video with dancing in a group in a studio. 一項研究比較了人們在家跟著影片跳舞，以及在舞蹈教室集體跳舞時的愉悅感。 The people dancing in a group reported feeling happier, whereas those dancing alone did not. 集體跳舞的人表示感覺更快樂， 而獨自跳舞的人則沒有。 In another experiment, university researchers at York and Sheffield took a group of students and sent each of them into a lab where music was played for five minutes. 在另一項實驗中，York 和 Sheffield 的大學研究人員找了一組學生，讓每個人進入實驗室， 聽五分鐘音樂。 Each had to choose from three options: to sit and listen quietly to the music, to cycle on an exercise bike while they listened, or to get up and dance. 每個人必須從三個選項中選一個：坐著安靜聽音樂、一邊聽一邊騎健身車，或起身跳舞。 All were given cognitive tasks to perform before and after. 所有人在前後都要完成認知任務。 The result showed that those who chose to dance showed much more creativity when doing problem-solving tasks. 結果顯示，選擇跳舞的人在解決問題任務中展現出更多創造力。 Doctor Lovatt at the University of Hertfordshire believes dance could be a very useful way to help people suffering from mental health problems. Hertfordshire 大學的 Lovatt 博士認為，舞蹈可能是幫助有心理健康問題者的一種非常有用的方法。 He thinks dance should be prescribed as therapy to help people overcome issues such as depression. 他認為舞蹈應被作為一種治療方式，用來幫助人們克服憂鬱症等問題。 It’s well established that dance is a good way of encouraging adolescent girls to take exercise but what about older people? 眾所周知，舞蹈是鼓勵青春期女孩運動的好方法，那老年人呢？ Studies have shown that there are enormous benefits for people in their sixties and beyond. 研究顯示，舞蹈對 60 多歲及以上的人有巨大益處。 One of the great things about dance is that there are no barriers to participation. 舞蹈的一大優點是參與沒有門檻。 Anyone can have a go, even those whose standard of fitness is quite low. 任何人都可以嘗試，即使體能水準相當低的人也可以。 Dance can be especially beneficial for older adults who can’t run or do more intense workouts, or for those who don’t want to. 對無法跑步或做更高強度訓練的老年人，或不想做那些運動的人來說，舞蹈尤其有益。 One 2015 study found that even a gentle dance workout helps to promote a healthy heart. 一項 2015 年研究發現，即使是溫和的舞蹈運動，也有助於促進心臟健康。 And there’s plenty of evidence which suggests that dancing lowers the risk of falls, which could result in a broken hip, for example, by helping people to improve their balance. 還有大量證據表明，跳舞可以透過幫助改善平衡，降低跌倒風險，例如避免可能導致髖部骨折的跌倒。 There are some less obvious benefits of dance for older people too. 舞蹈對老年人也有一些不太明顯的益處。 One thing I hadn’t realised before researching this topic was that dance isn’t just a physical challenge. 在研究這個主題之前，我沒有意識到舞蹈不只是身體上的挑戰。 It also requires a lot of concentration because you need to remember different steps and routines. 它還需要大量專注力，因為你需要記住不同舞步和動作組合。 For older people, this kind of activity is especially important because it forces their brain to process things more quickly and to retain more information. 對老年人來說，這類活動尤其重要，因為它迫使大腦更快處理資訊，並保留更多資訊。 Current research also shows that dance promotes a general sense of well-being in older participants, which can last up to a week after a class. 目前研究也顯示，舞蹈能提升老年參與者的整體幸福感，而且這種感覺可在課後持續長達一週。 Participants report feeling less tired and having greater motivation to be more active and do daily activities such as gardening or walking to the shops or a park. 參與者表示自己感覺不那麼疲倦，也更有動力保持活躍，去做園藝、步行去商店或公園等日常活動。 Ballroom or country dancing, both popular with older people, have to be done in groups. 交誼舞或鄉村舞都很受老年人歡迎，而且都需要集體進行。 They require collaboration and often involve touching a dance partner, all of which encourages interaction on the dance floor. 這些舞蹈需要合作，也常涉及與舞伴的肢體接觸，這些都會促進舞池中的互動。 This helps to develop new relationships and can reduce older people’s sense of isolation, which is a huge problem in many countries. 這有助於發展新關係，並能減少老年人的孤立感，而這在許多國家都是嚴重問題。 I also looked at the benefits of Zumba. 我也研究了 Zumba 的益處。 Fifteen million people in 180 countries now regularly take a Zumba class, an aerobic workout based on Latin American dance moves. 現在 180 個國家有 1500 萬人定期上 Zumba 課，這是一種以拉丁美洲舞步為基礎的有氧運動。 John Porcari, a professor of exercise and sport science at the University of Wisconsin, analysed a group of women who were Zumba regulars and found that a class lasting 40 minutes burns about 370 calories. Wisconsin 大學運動與體育科學教授 John Porcari 分析了一組經常跳 Zumba 的女性，發現一堂 40 分鐘課大約能消耗 370 卡路里。 This is similar to moderately intense exercises like step aerobics or kickboxing. 這與踏板有氧或踢拳等中等偏高強度運動相似。 A study in the American Journal of Health Behavior showed that when women with obesity did Zumba three times a week for 16 weeks, they lost an average of 1.2 kilos and lowered their percentage of body fat by 1%. 《American Journal of Health Behavior》的一項研究顯示，患有肥胖症的女性每週做三次 Zumba、持續 16 週後，平均減重 1.2 公斤，體脂率下降 1%。 More importantly, the women enjoyed the class so much that they made it a habit and continued to attend classes at least once a week – very unusual for an aerobic exercise programme. 更重要的是，這些女性非常喜歡課程，以至於把它變成習慣，並繼續每週至少上一次課；這對有氧運動課程來說非常少見。 Dance is never going to compete with high-intensity workouts when it comes to physical fitness gains, but its popularity is likely to keep on rising because it’s such a fun way to keep fit. 在提升體能方面，舞蹈永遠不會與高強度訓練競爭，但它的受歡迎程度可能會持續上升，因為它是一種非常有趣的健身方式。

entries.title: Listening Practice 18
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Junior Cycle Camp The course focuses on skills and safety. ● Charlie would be placed in Level 5. ● First of all, children at this level are taken to practise in a 1 __________. Instructors ● Instructors wear 2 __________ shirts. ● A 3 __________ is required and training is given. Classes ● The size of the classes is limited. ● There are quiet times during the morning for a 4 __________ or a game. ● Classes are held even if there is 5 __________. What to bring ● a change of clothing ● a 6 __________ ● shoes, not sandals ● Charlie’s 7 __________ Day 1 ● Charlie should arrive at 9.20 a.m. on the first day. ● Before the class, his 8 __________ will be checked. ● He should then go to the 9 __________ to meet his class instructor. Cost ● The course costs $10 __________ per week. ● First of all, children at this level are taken to practise in a 1 __________. ● Instructors wear 2 __________ shirts. ● A 3 __________ is required and training is given. ● There are quiet times during the morning for a 4 __________ or a ● Classes are held even if there is 5 __________. ● a 6 __________ ● Charlie’s 7 __________ ● Before the class, his 8 __________ will be checked. ● He should then go to the 9 __________ to meet his class instructor. ● The course costs $10 __________ per week. JAKE: Hello, Junior Cycle camp, Jake speaking. Jake：您好，這裡是 Junior Cycle Camp，我是 Jake。 WOMAN: Hi. I’m calling for some information about the cycle camp – I’m thinking of sending my son. Woman：你好。我打電話是想了解一些關於自行車營的資訊，我正在考慮讓我兒子參加。 JAKE: Great. Well, it’s held every weekday morning over the summer vacation and we focus on basic cycling skills and safety. Jake：太好了。這個營隊在暑假期間每個工作日早上舉行，重點是基本騎車技巧和安全。 We have eight levels for children from three years upwards. 我們為三歲以上的孩子設有八個級別。 How old’s your son? 你兒子幾歲？ WOMAN: Charlie? He’s seven. Woman：Charlie 嗎？他七歲。 He can ride a bike, but he needs a little more training before he’s safe to go on the road. 他會騎自行車，但在能安全上路之前，還需要再多一些訓練。 JAKE: He’d probably be best in Level 5. Jake：他大概最適合 Level 5。 They start off practising on the site here, and we aim to get them riding on the road, but first they’re taken to ride in the park, away from the traffic. 他們一開始會在我們這裡的場地練習，我們的目標是讓他們能上路騎車，但首先會帶他們去公園騎，遠離車流。 WOMAN: Right. And can you tell me a bit about the instructors? Woman：好的。你能告訴我一些關於教練的情況嗎？ JAKE: Well, all our staff wear different coloured shirts. Jake：嗯，我們所有工作人員都穿不同顏色的襯衫。 So, we have three supervisors, and they have red shirts. 我們有三名主管，他們穿紅色襯衫。 They support the instructors, and they also stand in for me if I’m not around. 他們會支援教練，如果我不在，也會代替我處理事情。 Then the instructors themselves are in blue shirts, and one of these is responsible for each class. 教練本人則穿藍色襯衫，每個班都有一位教練負責。 WOMAN: OK. Woman：好的。 JAKE: In order to be accepted, all our instructors have to submit a reference from someone who’s seen them work with children – like if they’ve worked as a babysitter, for example. Jake：為了被錄用，我們所有教練都必須提交一封推薦信，推薦人要見過他們和孩子一起工作，例如曾經做過保姆。 Then they have to complete our training course, including how to do lesson plans, and generally care for the well-being of the kids in their class. 然後他們必須完成我們的培訓課程，包括如何制定課程計畫，以及如何全面照顧班上孩子的身心狀況。 They do a great job, I have to say. 我必須說，他們做得非常好。 WOMAN: Right. And tell me a bit about the classes. Woman：明白。那再跟我說說班級吧。 What size will Charlie’s class be? Charlie 的班會有多少人？ JAKE: We have a limit of eight children in each class, so their instructor really gets to know them well. Jake：每班最多八個孩子，所以教練真的能很好地了解每個孩子。 They’re out riding most of the time but they have quiet times too, where their instructor might tell them a story that’s got something to do with cycling, or get them to play a game together. 他們大部分時間都在外面騎車，但也會有安靜時間，教練可能會講一個和騎車有關的故事，或者讓他們一起玩遊戲。 It’s a lot of fun. 這很有趣。 WOMAN: It must be. Woman：一定很有趣。 Now, what happens if there’s rain? 那如果下雨怎麼辦？ Do the classes still run? 課程還會照常進行嗎？ JAKE: Oh yes. We don’t let that put us off – we just put on our waterproofs and keep cycling. Jake：會的。我們不會因為下雨就停下來，只會穿上防水衣繼續騎。 WOMAN: And is there anything special Charlie should bring along with him? Woman：那 Charlie 有什麼特別需要帶的東西嗎？ JAKE: Well, maybe some spare clothes, especially if the weather’s not so good. Jake：嗯，也許要帶一些備用衣服，尤其是天氣不太好的時候。 And a snack for break time. 還要帶一份休息時間吃的小點心。 WOMAN: How about a drink? Woman：飲料呢？ JAKE: No, we’ll provide that. Jake：不用，我們會提供。 And make sure he has shoes, not sandals. 還要確保他穿鞋子，不要穿涼鞋。 WOMAN: Sure. And just at present Charlie has to take medication every few hours, so I’ll make sure he has that. Woman：好的。目前 Charlie 每隔幾個小時就要服藥，所以我會確保他帶著藥。 JAKE: Absolutely. Just give us details of when he has to take it and we’ll make sure he does. Jake：沒問題。只要把他什麼時候需要服藥的細節告訴我們， 我們會確保他按時服用。 WOMAN: Thanks. Woman：謝謝。 JAKE: Now, there are a few things you should know about Day 1 of the camp. Jake：接下來，有幾件關於營隊第一天的事情你需要知道。 The classes normally start at 9.30 every morning, but on Day 1 you should aim to get Charlie here by 9.20. 課程通常每天早上 9:30 開始， 但第一天你應該盡量在 9:20 前把 Charlie 送到。 The finishing time will be 12.30 as usual. 結束時間和平常一樣，是 12:30。 We need the additional time because there are a few extra things to do. 我們需要額外時間，因為有幾件額外事情要做。 The most important is that we have a very careful check to make sure that every child’s helmet fits properly. 最重要的是，我們會非常仔細地檢查，確保每個孩子的頭盔都合適。 If it doesn’t fit, we’ll try to adjust it, or we’ll find him another one – but he must wear it all the time he’s on the bike. 如果不合適，我們會試著調整，或者給他找另一頂；但只要他在自行車上，就必須一直戴著。 WOMAN: Of course. Woman：當然。 JAKE: Then after that, all the instructors will be waiting to meet their classes, and they’ll meet up in the tent – you can’t miss it. Jake：之後，所有教練會等著和自己的班級見面，他們會在帳篷集合，你不會錯過的。 And each instructor will take their class away and get started. 然後每位教練會帶自己的班離開並開始活動。 WOMAN: OK. Well that all sounds good. Woman：好的，聽起來都很好。 Now can you tell me how much the camp costs a week? 那你能告訴我這個營隊每週費用是多少嗎？ JAKE: One hundred ninety-nine dollars. Jake：199 美元。 We’ve managed to keep the price more or less the same as last year – it was one hundred ninety then. 我們已經盡量讓價格和去年差不多，去年是 190 美元。 But the places are filling up quite quickly. 不過名額很快就會滿。 WOMAN: Right. OK, well I’d like to book for … Woman：明白。好的，那我想預訂……

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11 and 12 Choose TWO letters, A–E. According to Megan, what are the TWO main advantages of working in the agriculture and horticulture sectors? A. the active lifestyle B. the above-average salaries C. the flexible working opportunities D. the opportunities for overseas travel E. the chance to be in a natural environment Questions 13 and 14 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO of the following are likely to be disadvantages for people working outdoors? A. the increasing risk of accidents B. being in a very quiet location C. difficult weather conditions at times D. the cost of housing E. the level of physical fitness required Questions 15–20 What information does Megan give about each of the following job opportunities? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 15–20. Information A. not a permanent job B. involves leading a team C. experience not essential D. intensive work but also fun E. chance to earn more through overtime F. chance for rapid promotion G. accommodation available H. local travel involved Job opportunities 15. Fresh food commercial manager __________ 16. Agronomist __________ 17. Fresh produce buyer __________ 18. Garden centre sales manager __________ 19. Tree technician __________ 20. Farm worker __________ Choose TWO letters, A–E. According to Megan, what are the TWO main advantages of working in the agriculture and horticulture sectors? the active lifestyle the above-average salaries the flexible working opportunities the opportunities for overseas travel the chance to be in a natural environment Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO of the following are likely to be disadvantages for people working outdoors? the increasing risk of accidents being in a very quiet location difficult weather conditions at times the cost of housing the level of physical fitness required Fresh food commercial manager not a permanent job involves leading a team experience not essential intensive work but also fun chance to earn more through overtime chance for rapid promotion accommodation available local travel involved Agronomist not a permanent job involves leading a team experience not essential intensive work but also fun chance to earn more through overtime chance for rapid promotion accommodation available local travel involved Fresh produce buyer not a permanent job involves leading a team experience not essential intensive work but also fun chance to earn more through overtime chance for rapid promotion accommodation available local travel involved Garden centre sales manager not a permanent job involves leading a team experience not essential intensive work but also fun chance to earn more through overtime chance for rapid promotion accommodation available local travel involved Tree technician not a permanent job involves leading a team experience not essential intensive work but also fun chance to earn more through overtime chance for rapid promotion accommodation available local travel involved Farm worker not a permanent job involves leading a team experience not essential intensive work but also fun chance to earn more through overtime chance for rapid promotion accommodation available local travel involved Hello everyone. My name’s Megan Baker and I’m a recruitment consultant at AVT Recruitment specialists. 大家好。我叫 Megan Baker，是 AVT Recruitment specialists 的招聘顧問。 Now, our company specialises in positions that involve working in the agriculture and horticulture sectors, so that’s fresh food production, garden and park maintenance and so on. 我們公司專門招聘農業和園藝領域相關職位，也就是新鮮食品生產、花園和公園維護等等。 And these sectors do provide some very special career opportunities. 這些產業確實提供一些非常特別的職涯機會。 For a start, they often offer opportunities for those who don’t want to be stuck with a 40-hour week, but need to juggle work with other responsibilities such as child care – and this is very important for many of our recruits. 首先，它們常常為那些不想被固定 40 小時工時束縛、但又需要兼顧育兒等其他責任的人提供機會，而這對我們許多求職者來說非常重要。 Some people like working in a rural setting, surrounded by plants and trees instead of buildings, although we can’t guarantee that. 有些人喜歡在鄉村環境工作， 周圍是植物和樹木，而不是建築物，雖然我們不能保證每份工作都是如此。 But there are certainly health benefits, especially in jobs where you’re not sitting all day looking at a screen – a big plus for many people. 但這確實有健康益處，尤其是那些不需要整天坐著盯著螢幕的工作，對很多人來說是一大優點。 Salaries can sometimes be good too, although there’s a lot of variety here. 薪水有時也不錯，雖然差異很大。 And you may have the opportunity in some types of jobs for travel overseas, although that obviously depends on the job, and not everyone is keen to do it. 某些職位也可能有海外旅行機會，不過這顯然取決於工作內容，而且不是每個人都想這樣做。 Of course, working outdoors does have its challenges. 當然，戶外工作也有挑戰。 It’s fine in summer, but can be extremely unpleasant when it’s cold and windy. 夏天還好，但寒冷又多風時可能非常不舒服。 You may need to be pretty fit for some jobs, though with modern technology that’s not as important as it once was. 某些工作可能需要相當好的體能，不過有了現代科技，這點不像以前那麼重要。 And standards of health and safety are much higher now than they used to be, so there are fewer work-related accidents. 現在健康與安全標準比過去高很多，所以工作相關事故也更少。 But if you like a lively city environment surrounded by lots of people, these jobs are probably not for you – they’re often in pretty remote areas. 但如果你喜歡熱鬧、周圍有很多人的城市環境，這些工作可能不適合你，因為它們通常位於相當偏遠的地方。 And some people worry about finding a suitable place to live, but in our experience, this usually turns out fine. 有些人也會擔心找不到合適住所，但根據我們的經驗，通常最後都沒問題。 Now let me tell you about some of the exciting jobs that we have on our books right now. 現在讓我介紹一些目前我們手上令人興奮的職缺。 One is for a fresh food commercial manager. 其中一個是新鮮食品商務經理。 Our client here is a very large fresh food producer supplying a range of top supermarkets. 我們的客戶是一家大型新鮮食品生產商，為多家頂級超市供貨。 They operate in a very fast-paced environment with low profit margins – the staff there work hard, but they play hard as well, so if you’ve a sociable personality this may be for you. 他們在節奏很快、利潤率較低的環境中運作，員工工作很努力，但也很會享受生活；所以如果你個性外向，這可能適合你。 We have an exciting post as an agronomist advising farmers on issues such as crop nutrition, protection against pests, and the latest legislation on farming and agricultural practices. 我們還有一個令人期待的農藝師職位，需要就作物營養、病蟲害防治，以及最新農業法規和實務向農民提供建議。 There are good opportunities for the right person to quickly make their way up the career ladder, but a deep knowledge of the agricultural sector is expected of applicants. 對合適的人來說，這是快速晉升的好機會，但申請者需要對農業領域有深入了解。 A leading supermarket is looking for a fresh produce buyer who is available for a 12-month maternity cover contract. 一家大型超市正在尋找一位新鮮農產品採購員，職位是為期 12 個月的產假代職合約。 You need to have experience in administration, planning and buying in the fresh produce industry, and in return will receive a very competitive salary. 你需要具備新鮮農產品行業中的行政、規劃和採購經驗，而作為回報，你會獲得很有競爭力的薪資。 We have also received a request for a sales manager for a chain of garden centres. 我們也收到一家連鎖園藝中心招聘銷售經理的需求。 You will be visiting centres in the region to ensure their high levels of customer service are maintained. 你需要走訪該地區的各個中心，確保它們維持高水準的客戶服務。 This post is only suitable for someone who is prepared to live in the region. 這個職位只適合願意住在該地區的人。 There is also a vacancy for a tree technician to carry out tree cutting, forestry and conservation work. 另外還有一個樹木技術員空缺，需要進行樹木修剪、林業和保育工作。 Candidates must have a clean driving licence and have training in safety procedures. 申請者必須持有無違規紀錄的駕照，並接受過安全程序培訓。 A year’s experience would be preferred but the company might be prepared to consider someone who has just completed an appropriate training course. 有一年經驗者優先，但公司也可能考慮剛完成相關培訓課程的人。 Finally, we have a position for a farm worker. 最後，我們有一個農場工人的職位。 This will involve a wide range of farm duties including crop sowing and harvesting, machine maintenance and animal care. 這份工作涉及各種農場職責， 包括播種與收成、機器維護和動物照料。 Perks of the job include the possibility of renting a small cottage on the estate, and the chance to earn a competitive salary. 這份工作的福利包括有機會在農場租一間小屋，以及獲得具有競爭力薪資的機會。 A driving licence and tractor driving experience are essential. 駕照和拖拉機駕駛經驗是必要條件。

entries.title: Listening Practice 18
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 21 and 22 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO points does Adam make about his experiment on artificial sweeteners? A. The results were what he had predicted. B. The experiment was simple to set up. C. A large sample of people was tested. D. The subjects were unaware of what they were drinking. E. The test was repeated several times for each person. Questions 23 and 24 Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO problems did Rosie have when measuring the fat content of nuts? A. She used the wrong sort of nuts. B. She used an unsuitable chemical. C. She did not grind the nuts finely enough. D. The information on the nut package was incorrect. E. The weighing scales may have been unsuitable. Questions 25–30 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 25. Adam suggests that restaurants could reduce obesity if their menus A. offered fewer options. B. had more low-calorie foods. C. were organised in a particular way. 26. The students agree that food manufacturers deliberately A. make calorie counts hard to understand. B. fail to provide accurate calorie counts. C. use ineffective methods to reduce calories. 27. What does Rosie say about levels of exercise in England? A. The amount recommended is much too low. B. Most people overestimate how much they do. C. Women now exercise more than they used to. 28. Adam refers to the location and width of stairs in a train station to illustrate A. practical changes that can influence people’s behaviour. B. methods of helping people who have mobility problems. C. ways of preventing accidents by controlling crowd movement. 29. What do the students agree about including reference to exercise in their presentation? A. They should probably leave it out. B. They need to do more research on it. C. They should discuss this with their tutor. 30. What are the students going to do next for their presentation? A. prepare some slides for it B. find out how long they have for it C. decide on its content and organisation Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO points does Adam make about his experiment on artificial sweeteners? The results were what he had predicted. The experiment was simple to set up. A large sample of people was tested. The subjects were unaware of what they were drinking. The test was repeated several times for each person. Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO problems did Rosie have when measuring the fat content of nuts? She used the wrong sort of nuts. She used an unsuitable chemical. She did not grind the nuts finely enough. The information on the nut package was incorrect. The weighing scales may have been unsuitable. Adam suggests that restaurants could reduce obesity if their menus offered fewer options. had more low-calorie foods. were organised in a particular way. The students agree that food manufacturers deliberately make calorie counts hard to understand. fail to provide accurate calorie counts. use ineffective methods to reduce calories. What does Rosie say about levels of exercise in England? The amount recommended is much too low. Most people overestimate how much they do. Women now exercise more than they used to. Adam refers to the location and width of stairs in a train station to illustrate practical changes that can influence people’s behaviour. methods of helping people who have mobility problems. ways of preventing accidents by controlling crowd movement. What do the students agree about including reference to exercise in their presentation? They should probably leave it out. They need to do more research on it. They should discuss this with their tutor. What are the students going to do next for their presentation? prepare some slides for it find out how long they have for it decide on its content and organisation ADAM: OK Rosie, shall we try to get some ideas together for our presentation on diet and obesity? Adam：好，Rosie，我們要不要為飲食和肥胖的簡報整理一些想法？ ROSIE: Sure. Rosie：當然。 ADAM: I can talk about the experiment I did to see if people can tell the difference between real sugar and artificial sweeteners. Adam：我可以談談我做的實驗，看看人們是否能分辨真糖和人工甜味劑。 ROSIE: Where you gave people drinks with either sugar or artificial sweeteners and they had to say which they thought it was? Rosie：就是你給人們喝含糖或人工甜味劑的飲料，然後讓他們判斷是哪一種？ ADAM: Yeah. It took me ages to decide exactly how I’d organise it, especially how I could make sure that people didn’t know which drink I was giving them. Adam：是的。我花了很久才決定要怎麼安排，尤其是要如何確保他們不知道我給他們的是哪種飲料。 It was hard to keep track of it all, especially as I had so many people doing it – I had to make sure I kept a proper record of what each person had had. 要記錄所有內容很困難，尤其是參與的人很多；我必須確保正確記錄每個人喝過什麼。 ROSIE: So could most people tell the difference? Rosie：那大多數人能分辨出差別嗎？ ADAM: Yeah – I hadn’t thought they would be able to, but most people could. Adam：能。我原本以為他們做不到，但大多數人都能。 ROSIE: Then there’s that experiment I did measuring the fat content of nuts, to see if the nutritional information given on the packet was accurate. Rosie：然後還有我做的那個測量堅果脂肪含量的實驗，看看包裝上的營養資訊是否準確。 ADAM: The one where you ground up the nuts and mixed them with a chemical to absorb the fat? Adam：就是你把堅果磨碎，然後和一種化學物質混合，用來吸收脂肪的那個？ ROSIE: Yes. My results were a bit problematic – the fat content for that type of nut seemed much lower than it said on the package. Rosie：是的。我的結果有點問題，這種堅果的脂肪含量看起來比包裝上標示的低很多。 But I reckon the package information was right. 但我認為包裝資訊是正確的。 I think I should probably have ground up the nuts more than I did. 我覺得我可能應該把堅果磨得更細。 It’s possible that the scales for weighing the fat weren’t accurate enough, too. 也有可能稱脂肪的秤不夠精準。 I’d really like to try the experiment again some time. 我真的很想找時間再做一次這個實驗。 ADAM: So what can we say about helping people to lose weight? Adam：那我們可以怎麼談幫助人們減重呢？ There’s a lot we could say about what restaurants could do to reduce obesity. 關於餐廳可以如何降低肥胖率，我們可以談很多。 I read that the items at the start of a menu and the items at the end of a menu are much more likely to be chosen than the items in the middle. 我讀到，菜單開頭和結尾的菜品比中間的菜品更容易被選。 So, if you put the low-calorie items at the beginning and end of the menu, people will probably go for the food with fewer calories, without even realising what they’re doing. 所以如果把低熱量食物放在菜單開頭和結尾，人們可能會選擇熱量較低的食物，甚至沒有意識到自己這樣做了。 ROSIE: I think food manufacturers could do more to encourage healthy eating. Rosie：我覺得食品製造商可以做更多事來鼓勵健康飲食。 ADAM: How? Adam：怎麼做？ ROSIE: Well, when manufacturers put calorie counts of a food on the label, they’re sometimes really confusing and I suspect they do it on purpose. Rosie：嗯，製造商把食物熱量標示在標籤上時，有時真的很令人困惑，我懷疑他們是故意的。 Because food that’s high in calories tastes better, and so they’ll sell more. 因為高熱量食物味道更好，所以會賣得更多。 ADAM: Yeah, so if you look at the amount of calories in a pizza, they’ll give you the calories per quarter pizza and you think, oh that’s not too bad. Adam：是啊，如果你看一個披薩的熱量，他們會標示四分之一個披薩的熱量，你就會想， 哦，那還不算太糟。 But who’s going to eat a quarter pizza? 但誰會只吃四分之一個披薩？ ROSIE: Exactly. Rosie：正是。 ADAM: I suppose another approach to this problem is to get people to exercise more. Adam：我想解決這個問題的另一種方法是讓人們多運動。 ROSIE: Right. In England, the current guidelines are for at least 30 minutes of brisk walking, five days a week. Rosie：對。在英格蘭，目前的指引是每週五天、每天至少快走 30 分鐘。 Now when you ask them, about 40% of men and 30% of women say they do this, but when you objectively measure the amount of walking they do with motion sensors, you find that only 6% of men and 4% of women do the recommended amount of exercise. 當你問他們時，大約 40% 的男性和 30% 的女性說自己做到了；但如果用動作感測器客觀測量他們的步行量，你會發現只有 6% 的男性和 4% 的女性達到建議運動量。 ADAM: Mm, so you can see why obesity is growing. Adam：嗯，所以你可以看出為什麼肥胖率在上升。 ROSIE: So how can people be encouraged to take more exercise? Rosie：那要怎麼鼓勵人們多運動呢？ ADAM: Well, for example, think of the location of stairs in a train station. Adam：嗯，例如想想火車站裡樓梯的位置。 If people reach the stairs before they reach the escalator when they’re leaving the station, they’re more likely to take the stairs. 如果人們離開車站時先看到樓梯，然後才看到電扶梯，他們就更可能走樓梯。 And if you increase the width of the stairs, you’ll get more people using them at the same time. 如果增加樓梯寬度，也會有更多人同時使用樓梯。 It’s an unconscious process and influenced by minor modifications in their environment. 這是一種無意識過程，會受到環境中細微改變的影響。 ROSIE: Right. And it might not be a big change, but if it happens every day, it all adds up. Rosie：對。這也許不是很大的變化，但如果每天都發生，累積起來就會有效果。 ADAM: Yes. But actually, I’m not sure if we should be talking about exercise in our presentation. Adam：是的。不過其實我不確定我們是否應該在簡報裡談運動。 ROSIE: Well, we’ve done quite a bit of reading about it. Rosie：嗯，我們已經讀了不少相關資料。 ADAM: I know, but it’s going to mean we have a very wide focus, and our tutor did say that we need to focus on causes and solutions in terms of nutrition. Adam：我知道，但那會讓簡報範圍變得很廣，而且導師說我們需要從營養角度聚焦於原因和解決方案。 ROSIE: I suppose so. And we’ve got plenty of information about that. Rosie：我想也是。而且我們有很多這方面資料。 OK, well that will be simpler. 好吧，那樣會簡單一些。 ADAM: So what shall we do now? Adam：那我們現在要做什麼？ We’ve still got half an hour before our next lecture. 下一堂課前我們還有半小時。 ROSIE: Let’s think about what we’re going to include and what will go where. Rosie：我們來想想要包含哪些內容，以及各部分放在哪裡。 Then we can decide what slides we need. 然後再決定需要哪些投影片。 ADAM: OK, fine. Adam：好，沒問題。

entries.title: Listening Practice 18
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Hand Knitting Interest in knitting ● Knitting has a long history around the world. ● We imagine someone like a 31 __________ knitting. ● A 32 __________ ago, knitting was expected to disappear. ● The number of knitting classes is now increasing. ● People are buying more 33 __________ for knitting nowadays. Benefits of knitting ● gives support in times of 34 __________ difficulty ● requires only 35 __________ skills and little money to start ● reduces stress in a busy life Early knitting ● The origins are not known. ● Findings show early knitted items to be 36 __________ in shape. ● The first needles were made of natural materials such as wood and 37 __________. ● Early yarns felt 38 __________ to touch. ● Wool became the most popular yarn for spinning. ● Geographical areas had their own 39 __________ of knitting. ● Everyday tasks like looking after 40 __________ were done while knitting. ● We imagine someone like a 31 __________ knitting. ● A 32 __________ ago, knitting was expected to disappear. ● People are buying more 33 __________ for knitting nowadays. ● gives support in times of 34 __________ difficulty ● requires only 35 __________ skills and little money to start ● Findings show early knitted items to be 36 __________ in shape. ● The first needles were made of natural materials such as wood and 37 __________. ● Early yarns felt 38 __________ to touch. ● Geographical areas had their own 39 __________ of knitting. ● Everyday tasks like looking after 40 __________ were done while Good morning everyone. So today we’re going to look at an important creative activity and that’s hand knitting. 大家早安。今天我們要來看一項重要的創意活動，也就是手工編織。 Ancient knitted garments have been found in many different countries, showing that knitting is a global activity with a long history. 許多不同國家都發現了古代針織衣物，這顯示編織是一項歷史悠久的全球性活動。 When someone says the word “knitting” we might well picture an elderly person – a grandmother perhaps – sitting by the fire knitting garments for themselves or other members of the family. 當有人說到「編織」這個詞時，我們很可能會想像一位老人，也許是一位祖母，坐在火爐旁為自己或其他家人織衣服。 It’s homely image, but one that may lead you to feel that knitting is an activity of the past – and, indeed, during the previous decade, it was one of the skills that was predicted to vanish from everyday life. 這是一幅溫馨的家庭畫面， 但也可能讓你覺得編織是過去的活動；事實上，在前一個十年裡，它曾被預測為會從日常生活中消失的技能之一。 For although humans have sewn and knitted their own clothing for a very long time, many of these craft-based skills went into decline when industrial machines took over – mainly because they were no longer passed down from one generation to another. 雖然人類很久以來都會縫製和編織自己的衣物，但當工業機器取代手工後，許多這類手工技能開始衰退，主要是因為它們不再代代相傳。 However, that’s all changing and interest in knitting classes in many countries is actually rising, as more and more people are seeking formal instruction in the skill. 然而，這一切正在改變，許多國家對編織課的興趣實際上正在上升，因為越來越多人正在尋求正式教學。 With that trend, we’re also seeing an increase in the sales figures for knitting equipment. 隨著這股趨勢，我們也看到編織工具設備的銷售數字增加。 So why do people want to be taught to knit at a time when a machine can readily do the job for them? 那麼，在機器已能輕易替人完成這項工作的時代，為什麼人們還想學編織呢？ The answer is that knitting, as a handicraft, has numerous benefits for those doing it. 答案是，編織作為一種手工藝，對從事它的人有許多好處。 Let’s consider what some of these might be. 我們來看看其中一些好處。 While many people knitted garments in the past because they couldn’t afford to buy clothes, it’s still true today that knitting can be helpful if you’re experiencing economic hardship. 過去很多人編織衣物是因為買不起衣服，而今天如果你正經歷經濟困難，編織仍然可能很有幫助。 If you have several children who all need warm winter clothes, knitting may save you a lot of money. 如果你有幾個孩子都需要保暖冬衣，編織可以幫你省很多錢。 And the results of knitting your own clothes can be very rewarding, even though the skills you need to get going are really quite basic and the financial outlay is minimal. 而且自己織衣服的成果會非常有成就感，即使開始所需技能其實相當基礎，花費也很低。 But the more significant benefits in today’s world are to do with well-being. 但在今天，更重要的好處與身心健康有關。 In a world where it’s estimated that we spend up to nine hours a day online, doing something with our hands that is craft-based makes us feel good. 在一個據估計每天最多花九小時上網的世界裡，動手做一件手工藝活動會讓我們感覺很好。 It releases us from the stress of a technological, fast-paced life. 它讓我們從科技化、快節奏生活的壓力中釋放出來。 Now, let’s look back a bit to early knitting activities. 現在，讓我們回顧一下早期的編織活動。 In fact, no one really knows when knitting first began, but archaeological remains have disclosed plenty of information for us to think about. 事實上，沒有人真正知道編織最早何時開始，但考古遺跡已揭示了許多值得思考的資訊。 One of the interesting things about knitting is that the earliest pieces of clothing that have been found suggest that most of the items produced were round rather than flat. 關於編織有趣的一點是，目前發現的最早衣物顯示，大多數製成品是圓形的，而不是平面的。 Discoveries from the 3rd and 4th centuries in Egypt show that things like socks and gloves, that were needed to keep hands and feet warm, were knitted in one piece using four or five needles. 在埃及發現的 3、4 世紀物品顯示，襪子和手套等用來讓手腳保暖的物品，是用四五根針一次織成的。 That’s very different from most knitting patterns today, which only require two. 這和今天大多數只需要兩根針的編織方式非常不同。 What’s more, the very first needles people used were hand carved out of wood and other natural materials, like bone, whereas today’s needles are largely made of steel or plastic and make that characteristic clicking sound when someone’s using them. 此外，人們最早使用的針是用木頭和骨頭等天然材料手工雕刻而成，而今天的針大多由鋼或塑膠製成，使用時會發出特有的喀嗒聲。 Ancient people knitted using yarns made from linen, hemp, cotton and wool, and these were often very rough on the skin. 古人用亞麻、大麻、棉和羊毛製成的紗線編織，而這些紗線接觸皮膚時通常相當粗糙。 The spinning wheel, which allowed people to make finer yarns and produce much greater quantities of them, led to the dominance of wool in the knitting industry – often favoured for its warmth. 紡車讓人們能製作更細的紗線，並大量生產，這使羊毛在編織業中占據主導地位，而羊毛常因保暖性受到青睞。 Another interesting fact about knitting is that because it was practised in so many parts of the world for so many purposes, regional differences in style developed. 關於編織的另一個有趣事實是，由於世界許多地區都為不同目的進行編織，因此形成了地區性的風格差異。 This visual identity has allowed researchers to match bits of knitted clothing that have been unearthed over time to the region from which the wearer came or the job that he or she did. 這種視覺特徵讓研究人員能將出土的針織衣物碎片，與穿著者來自的地區或其從事的工作聯繫起來。 As I’ve mentioned, knitting offered people from poor communities a way of making extra money while doing other tasks. 正如我提到的，編織為貧困社群的人提供了一種在做其他事情時賺取額外收入的方法。 For many centuries, it seems, men, women and children took every opportunity to knit, for example, while watching over sheep, walking to market or riding in boats. 幾個世紀以來，男性、女性和兒童似乎都會利用一切機會編織，例如看羊、走路去市場或乘船時。 So, let’s move on to take a … 那麼，接下來我們來看看……

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 1–10 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Holiday Rental Owners’ names: Jack Fitzgerald and Shirley Fitzgerald Granary Cottage ● available for week beginning 1 __________ May ● cost for the week: £2 __________ 3 __________ Cottage ● cost for the week: £480 ● building was originally a 4 __________ ● walk through doors from living room into a 5 __________ ● several 6 __________ spaces at the front ● bathroom has a shower ● central heating and stove that burns 7 __________ ● views of old 8 __________ from living room ● view of hilltop 9 __________ from the bedroom Payment ● deposit: £144 ● deadline for final payment: end of 10 __________ ● available for week beginning 1 __________ May ● cost for the week: £2 __________ 3 __________ Cottage ● building was originally a 4 __________ ● walk through doors from living room into a 5 __________ ● several 6 __________ spaces at the front ● central heating and stove that burns 7 __________ ● views of old 8 __________ from living room ● view of hilltop 9 __________ from the bedroom ● deadline for final payment: end of 10 __________ SHIRLEY: Hello? Shirley：您好？ TOM: Oh hello. I was hoping to speak to Jack Fitzgerald about renting a cottage. Tom：哦，您好。我想找 Jack Fitzgerald 談談租小屋的事情。 SHIRLEY: I’m his wife, Shirley, and we own the cottages together, so I’m sure I can help you. Shirley：我是他的妻子 Shirley， 這些小屋是我們共同擁有的， 所以我相信我也可以幫你。 TOM: Great. My name’s Tom. Tom：太好了。我叫 Tom。 Some friends of ours rented Granary Cottage from you last year, and they thought it was great. 我們有些朋友去年向你們租了 Granary Cottage，他們覺得非常好。 So my wife and I are hoping to come in May for a week. 所以我和妻子希望五月來住一週。 SHIRLEY: What date did you have in mind? Shirley：你們想哪一天開始？ TOM: The week beginning the 14th, if possible. Tom：如果可以的話，從 14 日開始那一週。 SHIRLEY: I’ll just check … I’m sorry, Tom, it’s already booked that week. Shirley：我查一下……抱歉，Tom ，那一週已經被預訂了。 It’s free the week beginning the 28th, though, for seven nights. 不過從 28 日開始那一週還空著，可以住七晚。 In fact, that’s the only time you could have it in May. 事實上，那是五月唯一能訂到的時間。 TOM: Oh. Well, we could manage that, I think. Tom：哦。嗯，我想我們可以安排一下。 We’d just need to change a couple of things. 我們只需要調整幾件事情。 How much would it cost? 費用是多少？ SHIRLEY: That’s the beginning of high season, so it’d be £550 for the week. Shirley：那是旺季開始的時候， 所以一週是 550 英鎊。 TOM: Ah. That’s a bit more than we wanted to pay, I’m afraid. Tom：啊，恐怕這比我們想付的高了一點。 We’ve budgeted up to £500 for accommodation. 我們住宿預算最高是 500 英鎊。 SHIRLEY: Well, we’ve just finished converting another building into a cottage, which we’re calling Chervil Cottage. Shirley：嗯，我們剛把另一棟建築改造成小屋，叫做 Chervil Cottage。 TOM: Sorry? What was that again? Tom：抱歉？叫什麼？ SHIRLEY: Chervil. C-H-E-R-V for Victor I-L. Shirley：Chervil。C-H-E-R-V，V 是 Victor 的 V，I-L。 TOM: Oh, that’s a herb, isn’t it? Tom：哦，那是一種香草，對吧？ SHIRLEY: That’s right. It grows fairly wild around here. Shirley：沒錯。這附近到處都長著 Chervil。 You could have that for the week you want for £480. 你們想要的那一週可以租這間，價格是 480 英鎊。 TOM: OK. So could you tell me something about it, please? Tom：好的。可以請你介紹一下這間小屋嗎？ SHIRLEY: Of course. The building was built as a garage. Shirley：當然。這棟建築原本是車庫。 It’s a little smaller than Granary Cottage. 它比 Granary Cottage 小一點。 TOM: So that must sleep two people, as well? Tom：那它應該也能住兩個人吧？ SHIRLEY: That’s right. There’s a double bedroom. Shirley：沒錯。有一間雙人臥室。 TOM: Does it have a garden? Tom：有花園嗎？ SHIRLEY: Yes, you get to it from the living room through French doors, and we provide two deckchairs. Shirley：有，從客廳穿過法式玻璃門就能到花園，我們還提供兩張摺疊躺椅。 We hope to build a patio in the near future, but I wouldn’t like to guarantee it’ll be finished by May. 我們希望近期建一個露台，但我不能保證五月前會完工。 TOM: OK. Tom：好的。 SHIRLEY: The front door opens onto the old farmyard, and parking isn’t a problem – there’s plenty of room at the front for that. Shirley：前門通向舊農家院子， 停車不是問題，前面有很多空間可以停車。 There are some trees and potted plants there. 那裡還有一些樹和盆栽。 TOM: What about facilities in the cottage? Tom：小屋裡有哪些設施？ It has standard things like a cooker and fridge, I presume. 我想應該有爐具和冰箱這些基本設備吧。 SHIRLEY: In the kitchen area there’s a fridge-freezer and we’ve just put in an electric cooker. Shirley：廚房區有冷凍冷藏冰箱，我們也剛裝了一台電爐。 TOM: Is there a washing machine? Tom：有洗衣機嗎？ SHIRLEY: Yes. There’s also a TV in the living room, which plays DVDs too. Shirley：有。客廳裡還有電視， 也可以播放 DVD。 The bathroom is too small for a bath, so there’s a shower instead. 浴室太小，放不下浴缸，所以改成淋浴。 I think a lot of people prefer that nowadays, anyway. 不過我想現在很多人本來就比較喜歡淋浴。 TOM: It’s more environmentally friendly, isn’t it? Tom：這也比較環保，不是嗎？ Unless you spend half the day in it! 除非你在裡面洗上半天！ SHIRLEY: Exactly. Shirley：正是。 TOM: What about heating? Tom：暖氣怎麼樣？ It sometimes gets quite cool at that time of year. 那個時候有時候會挺冷。 SHIRLEY: There’s central heating, and if you want to light a fire, there’s a stove. Shirley：有中央暖氣，如果你想生火，也有火爐。 We can provide all the wood you need for it. 我們可以提供所有需要的木柴。 It smells so much nicer than coal, and it makes the room very cosy – we’ve got one in our own house. 它比煤聞起來好多了，也會讓房間非常舒適。我們自己家裡也有一個。 TOM: That sounds very pleasant. Tom：聽起來很舒服。 Perhaps we should come in the winter, to make the most of it! 也許我們應該冬天來，好好享受一下！ SHIRLEY: Yes, we find we don’t want to go out when we’ve got the fire burning. Shirley：是啊，我們發現火爐一燒起來，就不想出門了。 There are some attractive views from the cottage, which I haven’t mentioned. 小屋裡還能看到一些很迷人的景色，我剛才還沒提到。 There’s a famous stone bridge – it’s one of the oldest in the region, and you can see it from the living room. 有一座著名的石橋，是這個地區最古老的橋之一，從客廳就能看到。 It isn’t far away. 它離這裡不遠。 The bedroom window looks in the opposite direction, and has a lovely view of the hills and the monument at the top. 臥室窗戶朝另一個方向，可以看到美麗的山丘和山頂上的紀念碑。 TOM: Well, that all sounds perfect. Tom：嗯，聽起來都很完美。 I’d like to book it, please. 我想預訂這間。 Would you want a deposit? 需要付訂金嗎？ SHIRLEY: Yes, we ask for thirty percent to secure your booking, so that’ll be, um, £144. Shirley：是的，我們需要 30% 作為訂金來保留預訂，所以是，嗯，144 英鎊。 TOM: And when would you like the rest of the money? Tom：那剩下的錢什麼時候付？ SHIRLEY: You’re coming in May, so the last day of March, please. Shirley：你們五月來，所以請在三月最後一天前付清。 TOM: Fine. Tom：好的。 SHIRLEY: Excellent. Could I just take your details … Shirley：太好了。可以請你提供一下詳細資料嗎……

entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 11–14 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Local Council Report on Traffic and Highways 11. A survey found people’s main concern about traffic in the area was A. cuts to public transport. B. poor maintenance of roads. C. changes in the type of traffic. 12. Which change will shortly be made to the cycle path next to the river? A. It will be widened. B. It will be extended. C. It will be resurfaced. 13. Plans for a pedestrian crossing have been postponed because A. the Post Office has moved. B. the proposed location is unsafe. C. funding is not available at present. 14. On Station Road, notices have been erected A. telling cyclists not to leave their bikes outside the station ticket office. B. asking motorists to switch off engines when waiting at the level crossing. C. warning pedestrians to leave enough time when crossing the railway line. Questions 15–20 Label the map below. Write the correct letter, A–I, next to Questions 15–20. 15. New car park __________ 16. New cricket pitch __________ 17. Children’s playground __________ 18. Skateboard ramp __________ 19. Pavilion __________ 20. Notice board __________ Practice 19, source question diagram/table, PDF page 7 A survey found people’s main concern about traffic in the area was cuts to public transport. poor maintenance of roads. changes in the type of traffic. Which change will shortly be made to the cycle path next to the river? It will be widened. It will be extended. It will be resurfaced. Plans for a pedestrian crossing have been postponed because the Post Office has moved. the proposed location is unsafe. funding is not available at present. On Station Road, notices have been erected telling cyclists not to leave their bikes outside the station ticket office. asking motorists to switch off engines when waiting at the level crossing. warning pedestrians to leave enough time when crossing the railway line. New car park A B C D E F G H I New cricket pitch A B C D E F G H I Children’s playground A B C D E F G H I Skateboard ramp A B C D E F G H I Pavilion A B C D E F G H I Notice board A B C D E F G H I CHAIRPERSON: Right. Next on the agenda we have traffic and highways. Councillor Thornton. Chairperson：好的。下一項議程是交通與道路。請 Thornton 議員發言。 COUNCILLOR THORNTON: Thank you. Well, we now have the results of the survey carried out last month about traffic and road transport in the town. Councillor Thornton：謝謝。現在我們已經有了上個月關於本鎮交通和道路運輸調查的結果。 People were generally satisfied with the state of the roads. 人們整體上對道路狀況感到滿意。 There were one or two complaints about potholes which will be addressed, but a significant number of people complained about the increasing number of heavy vehicles using our local roads to avoid traffic elsewhere. 有一兩起關於路面坑洞的投訴，我們會處理；但相當多人抱怨越來越多重型車輛使用本地道路，以避開其他地方的交通。 We’d expected more complaints by commuters about the reduction in the train service, but it doesn’t seem to have affected people too much. 我們原本預期通勤者會對火車服務減少有更多投訴，但這似乎沒有對人們造成太大影響。 The cycle path that runs alongside the river is very well used by both cyclists and pedestrians since the surface was improved last year, but overtaking can be a problem so we’re going to add a bit on the side to make it wider. 沿河自行車道自去年改善路面後，騎車者和行人都很常使用， 但超車可能是個問題，所以我們打算在旁邊加寬一點。 At some stage, we’d like to extend the path so that it goes all the way through the town, but that won’t be happening in the immediate future. 在某個階段，我們希望把這條路延伸到穿過整個城鎮，但近期不會實施。 The plans to have a pedestrian crossing next to the Post Office have unfortunately had to be put on hold for the time being. 很遺憾，在郵局旁設置行人穿越道的計畫目前必須暫停。 We’d budgeted for this to be done this financial year, but then there were rumours that the Post Office was going to move, which would have meant there wasn’t really a need for a crossing. 我們原本已將這項工程列入本財政年度預算，但後來有傳聞說郵局要搬走，那樣就不一定需要穿越道了。 Now they’ve confirmed that they’re staying where they are, but the Highways Department have told us that it would be dangerous to have a pedestrian crossing where we’d originally planned it as there’s a bend in the road there. 現在郵局已確認會留在原地， 但道路部門告訴我們，在原本計畫的位置設置行人穿越道會很危險，因為那裡有彎道。 So that’ll need some more thought. 所以這還需要進一步考慮。 On Station Road near the station and level crossing, drivers can face quite long waits if the level crossing’s closed, and we’ve now got signs up requesting them not to leave their engines running at that time. 在車站和鐵路平交道附近的 Station Road，如果平交道關閉，司機可能要等很久；我們現在已設置標誌，要求他們等待時不要讓引擎持續運轉。 This means pedestrians waiting on the pavement to cross the railway line don’t have to breathe in car fumes. 這樣在人行道上等著穿越鐵路線的行人就不用吸入汽車廢氣。 We’ve had some problems with cyclists leaving their bikes chained to the railings outside the ticket office, but the station has agreed to provide bike racks there. 我們曾遇到一些問題，騎車者把自行車鎖在售票處外的欄杆上，但車站已同意在那裡提供自行車架。 CHAIRPERSON: So next on the agenda is “Proposals for improvements to the recreation ground”. Councillor Thornton again. Chairperson：下一項議程是「改善休閒運動場的提案」。再次請 Thornton 議員發言。 COUNCILLOR THORNTON: Well, since we managed to extend the recreation ground, we’ve spent some time talking to local people about how it could be made a more attractive and useful space. Councillor Thornton：嗯，自從我們成功擴建休閒運動場後， 我們花了一些時間和當地居民討論如何讓它變得更有吸引力，也更實用。 If you have a look at the map up on the screen, you can see the river up in the north, and the Community Hall near the entrance from the road. 如果大家看螢幕上的地圖，可以看到北邊有河流， Community Hall 靠近道路入口。 At present, cars can park between the Community Hall and that line of trees to the east, but this is quite dangerous for pedestrians so we’re suggesting a new car park on the opposite side of the Community Hall, right next to it. 目前，車輛可以停在 Community Hall 和東邊那排樹之間，但這對行人很危險，所以我們建議在 Community Hall 的另一側、緊鄰它的位置設置新停車場。 We also have a new location for the cricket pitch. 我們也為板球場選定了新位置。 As we’ve now purchased additional space to the east of the recreation ground, beyond the trees, we plan to move it away from its current location, which is rather near the road, into this new area beyond the line of trees. 由於我們現在已購買休閒運動場東側、樹木之外的額外土地， 所以計畫把板球場從目前靠近道路的位置，移到樹線之外的新區域。 This means there’s less danger of stray balls hitting cars or pedestrians. 這表示偏離方向的球擊中車輛或行人的風險會降低。 We’ve got plans for a children’s playground which will be accessible by a footpath from the Community Hall and will be alongside the river. 我們計畫設置一個兒童遊樂場，可以從 Community Hall 經由人行道到達，位置會在河邊。 We’d originally thought of having it close to the road, but we think this will be a more attractive location. 我們原本想把它設在靠近道路的地方，但現在認為河邊會是更吸引人的位置。 The skateboard ramp is very popular with both younger and older children – we had considered moving this up towards the river, but in the end we decided to have it in the southeast corner near the road. 滑板坡道很受年紀較小和較大的孩子歡迎。我們曾考慮把它移到靠近河邊的位置，但最後決定把它設在靠近道路的東南角。 The pavilion is very well used at present by both football players and cricketers. 目前，足球員和板球員都經常使用這座涼亭。 It will stay where it is now – to the left of the line of trees and near to the river – handy for both the football and cricket pitches. 它會保留在原處，也就是那排樹的左側、靠近河流的位置，對足球場和板球場都很方便。 And finally, we’ll be getting a new notice board for local information, and that will be directly on people’s right as they go from the road into the recreation ground. 最後，我們會設置一個新的本地資訊公告板，位置就在大家從道路進入休閒運動場時右手邊。

JAKE: Now that we’ve done all the research into bike-sharing schemes in cities around the world, we need to think about how we’re going to organise our report. Jake：既然我們已經完成了對世界各城市共享單車計畫的研究，現在需要思考如何組織報告。 AMY: Right. I think we should start by talking about the benefits. Amy：對。我覺得我們應該先談好處。 I mean it’s great that so many cities have introduced these schemes where anyone can pick up a bike from dozens of different locations and hire it for a few hours. 我的意思是，很多城市都推出了這類計畫，任何人都可以從許多不同地點取車，租用幾個小時，這很棒。 It makes riding a bike very convenient for people. 這讓人們騎自行車變得非常方便。 JAKE: Yes, but the costs can add up and that puts people on low incomes off in some places. Jake：是的，但費用累積起來也不少，在某些地方會讓低收入者卻步。 AMY: I suppose so, but if it means more people in general are cycling rather than driving, then because they’re increasing the amount of physical activity they do, it’s good for their health. Amy：我想也是。不過如果這意味著整體上更多人騎自行車而不是開車，那他們的身體活動量就增加了，對健康有好處。 JAKE: OK. But isn’t that of less importance? Jake：好。但那不是比較次要嗎？ I mean, doesn’t the impact of reduced emissions on air pollution have a more significant effect on people’s health? 我的意思是，減少排放對空氣污染的影響，對人們健康不是更重要嗎？ AMY: Certainly, in some cities bike-sharing has made a big contribution to that. Amy：當然，在一些城市，共享單車在這方面貢獻很大。 And also helped to cut the number of cars on the road significantly. 而且也顯著減少了道路上的汽車數量。 JAKE: Which is the main point. Jake：這才是重點。 AMY: Exactly. But I’d say it’s had less of an impact on noise pollution because there are still loads of buses and lorries around. Amy：沒錯。不過我會說，它對噪音污染的影響比較小，因為路上仍然有很多公車和卡車。 JAKE: Right. Jake：對。 AMY: Shall we quickly discuss the recommendations we’re going to make? Amy：我們要不要快速討論一下要提出的建議？ JAKE: In order to ensure bike-sharing schemes are successful? Jake：為了確保共享單車計畫成功？ AMY: Yes. Amy：是的。 JAKE: OK. Well, while I think it’s nice to have really state-of-the art bikes with things like GPS, I wouldn’t say they’re absolutely necessary. Jake：好的。雖然我覺得有配備 GPS 等先進功能的自行車很好，但我不會說這是絕對必要的。 AMY: But some technical things are really important – like a fully functional app – so people can make payments and book bikes easily. Amy：但有些技術方面真的很重要，例如功能完整的應用程式，這樣人們才能輕鬆付款和預訂自行車。 Places which haven’t invested in that have really struggled. 沒有在這方面投資的地方確實遇到了很大困難。 JAKE: Good point … Some people say there shouldn’t be competing companies offering separate bike-sharing schemes, but in some really big cities, competition’s beneficial and anyway one company might not be able to manage the whole thing. Jake：有道理……有些人說不應該有競爭公司提供各自的共享單車計畫，但在一些非常大的城市裡，競爭是有益的，而且一家公司可能也無法管理整個系統。 AMY: Right. Deciding how much to invest is a big question. Amy：對。要投資多少是一個大問題。 Cities which have opened loads of new bike lanes at the same time as introducing bike-sharing schemes have generally been more successful – but there are examples of successful schemes where this hasn’t happened … 那些在推出共享單車計畫的同時開闢大量新自行車道的城市通常更成功，但也有一些成功案例並沒有這樣做…… What does matter though – is having a big publicity campaign. 不過真正重要的是要有大規模宣傳活動。 JAKE: Definitely. If people don’t know how to use the scheme or don’t understand its benefits, they won’t use it. Jake：絕對是。如果人們不知道如何使用這個計畫，或不了解它的好處，就不會使用。 People need a lot of persuasion to stop using their cars. 要讓人們停止開車，需要大量說服。 AMY: Shall we look at some examples now? Amy：我們現在來看看一些例子吧？ And say what we think is good or bad about them. 然後說說我們覺得它們好在哪裡或不好在哪裡。 JAKE: I suppose we should start with Amsterdam as this was one of the first cities to have a bike sharing scheme. Jake：我想我們應該從 Amsterdam 開始，因為它是最早擁有共享單車計畫的城市之一。 AMY: Yes. There was already a strong culture of cycling here. Amy：是的。那裡本來就有很強的自行車文化。 In a way it’s strange that there was such a demand for bike-sharing because you’d have thought most people would have used their own bikes. 從某種程度上說，共享單車需求這麼大有點奇怪，因為你會以為大多數人會用自己的自行車。 JAKE: And yet it’s one of the best-used schemes … Jake：然而它卻是使用率最高的計畫之一…… Dublin’s an interesting example of a success story. Dublin 是一個有趣的成功例子。 AMY: It must be because the public transport system’s quite limited. Amy：那一定是因為公共交通系統很有限。 JAKE: Not really – there’s no underground, but there are trams and a good bus network. Jake：不完全是。那裡沒有地鐵，但有電車和良好的公車網絡。 I’d say price has a lot to do with it. 我會說價格和成功很有關係。 It’s one of the cheapest schemes in Europe to join. 它是歐洲加入費用最低的計畫之一。 AMY: But the buses are really slow – anyway the weather certainly can’t be a factor! Amy：但公車真的很慢。不管怎樣，天氣肯定不是因素！ JAKE: No – definitely not. The London scheme’s been quite successful. Jake：對，絕對不是。London 的計畫相當成功。 AMY: Yes – it’s been a really good thing for the city. Amy：是的，這對城市來說是件很好的事。 The bikes are popular and the whole system is well maintained but it isn’t expanding quickly enough. 自行車很受歡迎，整個系統維護得很好，但擴張速度不夠快。 JAKE: Basically, not enough’s been spent on increasing the number of cycle lanes. Jake：基本上，在增加自行車道數量方面投入還不夠。 Hopefully that’ll change. 希望之後會改變。 AMY: Yes. Now what about outside Europe? Amy：是的。那歐洲以外呢？ JAKE: Well bike-sharing schemes have taken off in places like Buenos Aires. Jake：共享單車計畫在 Buenos Aires 這類地方已經發展起來。 AMY: Mmm. They built a huge network of cycle lanes to support the introduction of the scheme there, didn’t they? Amy：嗯。他們建了一個龐大的自行車道網絡來支持這個計畫的引入，對吧？ It attracted huge numbers of cyclists where previously there were hardly any. 它吸引了大量騎車者，而以前那裡幾乎沒有人騎車。 JAKE: An example of good planning. Jake：這是良好規劃的例子。 AMY: Absolutely. New York is a good example of how not to introduce a scheme. Amy：完全同意。New York 則是如何不應該推行計畫的好例子。 When they launched it, it was more than ten times the price of most other schemes. 他們推出時，價格是大多數其他計畫的十倍以上。 JAKE: More than it costs to take a taxi. Crazy. Jake：比搭計程車還貴，太瘋狂了。 I think the organisers lacked vision and ambition there. 我覺得那裡的組織者缺乏遠見和企圖心。 AMY: I think so too. Amy：我也這麼覺得。 Sydney would be a good example to use. Sydney 也是可以使用的一個好例子。 I would have expected it to have grown pretty quickly here. 我原本以為它在那裡會發展得很快。 JAKE: Yes. I can’t quite work out why it hasn’t been an instant success like some of the others. Jake：是啊。我不太明白為什麼它沒有像其他一些城市那樣立刻成功。 It’s a shame really. 真的很可惜。 AMY: I know. OK so now we’ve thought about … Amy：我知道。好，那現在我們已經想過……

entries.title: Listening Practice 19
entries.text: Answer the questions using the instructions in the original question paper below. 請按下方原題的字數限制及指示作答；錄音稿提供中英對照。 Questions 31–40 Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. The Extinction of the Dodo Bird The dodo was a large flightless bird which used to inhabit the island of Mauritius. History ● 1507 — Portuguese ships transporting 31 __________ stopped at the island to collect food and water. ● 1638 — The Dutch established a 32 __________ on the island. ● They killed the dodo birds for their meat. ● The last one was killed in 1681. Description ● The only record we have is written descriptions and pictures, possibly unreliable. ● A Dutch painting suggests the dodo was very 33 __________. ● The only remaining soft tissue is a dried 34 __________. ● Recent studies of a dodo skeleton suggest the birds were capable of rapid 35 __________. ● It’s thought they were able to use their small wings to maintain 36 __________. ● Their 37 __________ was of average size. ● Their sense of 38 __________ enabled them to find food. Reasons for extinction ● Hunting was probably not the main cause. ● Sailors brought dogs and monkeys. ● 39 __________ also escaped onto the island and ate the birds’ eggs. ● The arrival of farming meant the 40 __________ was destroyed. ● 1507 — Portuguese ships transporting 31 __________ stopped at the ● 1638 — The Dutch established a 32 __________ on the island. ● A Dutch painting suggests the dodo was very 33 __________. ● The only remaining soft tissue is a dried 34 __________. 35 __________. ● It’s thought they were able to use their small wings to maintain 36 __________. ● Their 37 __________ was of average size. ● Their sense of 38 __________ enabled them to find food. ● 39 __________ also escaped onto the island and ate the birds’ eggs. ● The arrival of farming meant the 40 __________ was destroyed. One of the most famous cases of extinction is that of a bird known as the dodo. 最著名的滅絕案例之一，是一種名為 dodo 的鳥。 In fact there’s even a saying in English, “as dead as the dodo”, used to refer to something which no longer exists. 事實上，英語裡甚至有一句說法 “as dead as the dodo”，用來形容已經不存在的事物。 But for many centuries the dodo was alive and well, although it could only be found in one place, the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean. 但在許多世紀裡，dodo 曾經生存得很好，雖然它只存在於一個地方，也就是印度洋上的 Mauritius 島。 It was a very large bird, about one metre tall, and over the centuries it had lost the ability to fly, but it survived happily under the trees that covered the island. 它是一種非常大的鳥，約一公尺高。數百年間，它失去了飛行能力，但仍在覆蓋島嶼的樹木下安然生存。 Then in the year 1507 the first Portuguese ships stopped at the island. 後來，在 1507 年，第一批葡萄牙船隻停靠在這座島上。 The sailors were carrying spices back to Europe, and found the island a convenient stopping place where they could stock up with food and water for the rest of the voyage, but they didn’t settle on Mauritius. 水手們正把香料運回歐洲，發現這座島是方便停靠的地方， 可以為接下來的航程補充食物和水，但他們沒有在 Mauritius 定居。 However, in 1638 the Dutch arrived and set up a colony there. 然而，1638 年荷蘭人抵達，並在那裡建立了殖民地。 These first human inhabitants of the island found the dodo birds a convenient source of meat, although not everyone liked the taste. 這些島上最早的人類居民發現 dodo 是方便取得的肉類來源， 雖然不是每個人都喜歡它的味道。 It’s hard to get an accurate description of what the dodo actually looked like. 要準確描述 dodo 真正的樣子很困難。 We do have some written records from sailors, and a few pictures, but we don’t know how reliable these are. 我們確實有一些水手留下的文字記錄和幾幅圖畫，但不知道它們有多可靠。 The best-known picture is a Dutch painting in which the bird appears to be extremely fat, but this may not be accurate – an Indian painting done at the same time shows a much thinner bird. 最著名的是一幅荷蘭畫作，畫中的鳥看起來非常肥胖，但這可能不準確；同時期的一幅印度畫則畫出一隻瘦得多的鳥。 Although attempts were made to preserve the bodies of some of the birds, no complete specimen survives. 雖然有人曾試圖保存一些 dodo 的屍體，但沒有任何完整標本留存下來。 In the early 17th century four dried parts of a bird were known to exist – of these, three have disappeared, so only one example of soft tissue from the dodo survives, a dodo head. 在 17 世紀初，人們知道曾有四塊乾燥的 dodo 身體部位存在；其中三塊已經消失，因此目前唯一留下的 dodo 軟組織是一顆 dodo 頭部。 Bones have also been found, but there’s only one complete skeleton in existence. 人們也發現了一些骨頭，但現存完整骨架只有一副。 This single dodo skeleton has recently been the subject of scientific research which suggests that many of the earlier beliefs about dodos may have been incorrect. 這副唯一完整的 dodo 骨架最近成為科學研究對象，研究顯示許多早期關於 dodo 的觀點可能是錯誤的。 For example, early accounts of the birds mention how slow and clumsy it was, but scientists now believe the bird’s strong knee joints would have made it capable of movement which was not slow, but actually quite fast. 例如，早期記載提到這種鳥行動緩慢又笨拙，但科學家現在認為，dodo 強壯的膝關節使牠能夠快速移動，而不是緩慢移動。 In fact, one 17th century sailor wrote that he found the birds hard to catch. 事實上，一位 17 世紀水手曾寫道，他覺得這些鳥很難捕捉。 It’s true that the dodo’s small wings wouldn’t have allowed it to leave the ground, but the scientists suggest that these were probably employed for balance while going over uneven ground. 的確，dodo 的小翅膀無法讓牠離地飛行，但科學家認為，這些翅膀可能用來在不平地面上移動時保持平衡。 Another group of scientists carried out analysis of the dodo’s skull. 另一組科學家對 dodo 的頭骨進行了分析。 They found that the reports of the lack of intelligence of the dodo were not borne out by their research, which suggested the bird’s brain was not small, but average in size. 他們發現，關於 dodo 缺乏智力的說法並未得到研究支持； 研究顯示牠的大腦並不小，而是平均大小。 In fact, in relation to its body size, it was similar to that of the pigeon, which is known to be a highly intelligent bird. 事實上，相對於身體大小， dodo 的大腦比例和鴿子相似， 而鴿子是已知非常聰明的鳥類。 The researchers also found that the structure of the bird’s skull suggested that one sense which was particularly well-developed was that of smell. 研究人員還發現，這種鳥的頭骨結構顯示，牠特別發達的一種感官是嗅覺。 So the dodo may also have been particularly good at locating ripe fruit and other food in the island’s thick vegetation. 因此，dodo 可能也特別擅長在島上茂密植被中尋找成熟水果和其他食物。 So it looks as if the dodo was better able to survive and defend itself than was originally believed. 因此，看起來 dodo 比人們最初認為的更能生存和保護自己。 Yet less than 200 years after Europeans first arrived on the island, they had become extinct. 然而，在歐洲人首次抵達這座島後不到 200 年，牠們就滅絕了。 So what was the reason for this? 那麼原因是什麼呢？ For a long time, it was believed that the dodos were hunted to extinction, but scientists now believe the situation was more complicated than this. 很長一段時間，人們認為 dodo 是被獵殺到滅絕的，但科學家現在認為情況比這更複雜。 Another factor may have been the new species brought to the island by the sailors. 另一個因素可能是水手們帶到島上的新物種。 These included dogs, which would have been a threat to the dodos, and also monkeys, which ate the fruit that was the main part of the dodos’ diet. 其中包括狗，牠們會威脅 dodo ；還有猴子，牠們會吃 dodo 主要食物來源中的水果。 These were brought to the island deliberately, but the ships also brought another type of creature – rats, which came to land from the ships and rapidly overran the island. 這些動物是被刻意帶到島上的，但船隻也帶來了另一種生物 ——老鼠；牠們從船上下到陸地，很快遍布整座島。 These upset the ecology of the island, not just the dodos but other species too. 這些老鼠破壞了島上的生態， 不只是 dodo，其他物種也受到影響。 However, they were a particular danger to the dodos because they consumed their eggs, and since each dodo only laid one at a time, this probably had a devastating effect on populations. 然而，老鼠對 dodo 特別危險， 因為牠們會吃 dodo 的蛋；而每隻 dodo 一次只下一顆蛋，這很可能對族群造成毀滅性影響。 However, we now think that probably the main cause of the birds’ extinction was not the introduction of non-native species, but the introduction of agriculture. 不過，我們現在認為，這種鳥滅絕的主要原因可能不是外來物種的引入，而是農業的引入。 This meant that the forest that had once covered all the island, and that had provided a perfect home for the dodo, was cut down so that crops such as sugar could be grown. 這意味著曾經覆蓋整座島、為 dodo 提供完美棲地的森林被砍伐，以便種植甘蔗等作物。 So although the dodo had survived for thousands of years, suddenly it was gone. 所以，儘管 dodo 已經生存了數千年，卻突然消失了。
